nfl.off_epa.label: Offensive EPA/play, opponent-adjusted, recency-weighted
nfl.off_epa.mechanism: Per-play expected-points added measures how much each snap moves scoring expectation; adjusting for defenses faced isolates the offense's own repeatable efficiency, which drives points per drive and therefore margin and totals.
nfl.off_epa.rationale: EPA/play is the best single public descriptor of offensive efficiency and predicts future points better than points or yards, but it is noisy early in the season (~17 games) and dominated by QB and a few explosive plays. Naive averages double-count weak schedules; the subtle part is separating QB-driven from scheme/OL-driven EPA when the QB changes.
nfl.off_epa.measurement: From play_by_play (pass/run, no kneels/spikes, win-prob 5-95% filter optional): team offense EPA/play by game. Opponent-adjust with a ridge regression (offense effect + defense effect + home + intercept) fitted on rolling windows; exponential recency decay (half-life ~6-8 games) blended with a prior from last season regressed ~35-50% toward league mean, weight on prior shrinking with games played. Compute separately for pass (per dropback) and rush, and condition on the QB actually starting.

nfl.def_epa.label: Defensive EPA/play allowed, opponent-adjusted
nfl.def_epa.mechanism: Defensive EPA/play allowed is the opponent-adjusted rate at which a defense prevents expected points; it sets the baseline for what any offense (and any individual passer/rusher/receiver) will achieve against it.
nfl.def_epa.rationale: Defense is less stable than offense year to year and more sensitive to injuries to a few pass rushers/corners, so season-long averages lag true current strength; split pass versus rush defense because the two have different stabilization speeds and different relevance to QB versus RB markets.
nfl.def_epa.measurement: Same ridge adjusted-EPA framework as offense but on the defensive effect, split into pass EPA/dropback allowed and rush EPA/rush allowed. Recency-weight and shrink toward a preseason prior built from returning defensive snaps and last-year ratings. Re-weight for current injury-absent lineup using snap-weighted player contributions when available.
free_sources: nflverse pfr_advstats (pass, rush, rec, def weekly)

nfl.success_rate.label: Success rate and early-down efficiency
nfl.success_rate.mechanism: Success rate (share of plays with positive EPA, early-down emphasis) measures consistency of staying on schedule, which controls drive sustainment and penalizes explosive-play dependence.
nfl.success_rate.rationale: Offenses that lean on explosive plays have high EPA but low success rate and are volatile; success rate is more stable and complements EPA for totals and team totals because sustained drives shape plays per game and clock. It is also less sensitive to a single long TD.
nfl.success_rate.measurement: Per game: share of plays with EPA>0 on 1st/2nd down, and separately third-down conversion over expected given distance. Opponent-adjust with the same ridge approach; recency-weight; report the gap between EPA rank and success-rate rank as an explosiveness-dependence flag.

nfl.ratings.label: Power ratings and market-implied team strength history
nfl.ratings.mechanism: Closing lines embed injury news, weather and sharp information; the rating implied by spread history is the strongest prior on team quality and encodes information not visible in box scores.
nfl.ratings.rationale: Any model of NFL results must beat or at least calibrate against market-implied strength; the real use is as a prior or control so residual inputs add information instead of re-deriving what the line already contains. Subtle: lines move for QB/injury news, so ratings must be keyed to the lineup the line assumed, not the season average.
nfl.ratings.measurement: Benchmark only (not a model input): for each season fit a ridge Bradley-Terry model of closing spread (home perspective, spread points only) on team indicators plus home constant over games up to the as-of week, with weights exp(-ln2 x games_ago/10) and ridge lambda 1; output team rating in points. Track kickoff-time rating and opening-to-closing change in rating. Label the output market-derived; the market-free counterpart is the points rating of nfl.own_team_rating_market_free.

nfl.ratings.market_note: Inverts closing spreads, totals and moneylines, so every output is market-derived; usable as a benchmark/comparison column only. A market-free rating is nfl.own_team_rating_market_free.

nfl.roster_continuity.label: Offseason roster turnover, returning production and age curve
nfl.roster_continuity.mechanism: Share of last year's snaps and production that returns (and the age profile of the core) determines how much last year's ratings carry into this year, which dominates season-level markets and early-season game priors.
nfl.roster_continuity.rationale: Early-season game markets and season win totals depend on how much to trust last season; free agency, retirements, coordinator departures and aging curves create predictable regression. The subtle part is weighting by position value: QB and OL/pass rush turnover matters more than WR3 turnover.
nfl.roster_continuity.measurement: From rosters and snap_counts compute returning snap share by unit (QB, OL, DL/EDGE, secondary, skill) and value-weight by position (QB highest). Add age-weighted aging curve by position and expected improvement of young starters (years 2-3). Regress prior-season rating toward mean with shrinkage coefficient fitted on rolling train years as a function of returning share.

nfl.rush_efficiency.label: Rush efficiency, yards before contact and run-block quality
nfl.rush_efficiency.mechanism: Team rushing success depends on the OL run-block, scheme (zone/gap), box counts faced, and RB creation; yards before contact separate line/scheme production from back creation.
nfl.rush_efficiency.rationale: Rushing yards props and team rush totals need volume (script) times yards per carry; YPC is noisy and heavily driven by a few long runs, while rush EPA, success rate and yards before contact are more stable and attribute credit between OL and RB.
nfl.rush_efficiency.measurement: From play_by_play and PFR/NGS rushing: rush success rate, EPA/rush, yards before contact per attempt, yards after contact per attempt, stuff rate and explosive-run rate (10+). Opponent-adjust versus defense rush EPA allowed and box counts; recency-weight and shrink individual RB values toward team level.
free_sources: nflverse pfr_advstats (pass, rush, rec, def weekly)

nfl.pass_efficiency.label: Team pass efficiency: EPA/dropback, ANY/A, CPOE, air-yards profile
nfl.pass_efficiency.mechanism: Passing efficiency combines QB accuracy and decision-making, receiver quality, protection and scheme; it drives passing yards, TDs and scoring.
nfl.pass_efficiency.rationale: ANY/A and EPA/dropback bundle sacks and interceptions, while CPOE and air yards isolate accuracy and aggressiveness; combining them with opponent pass-defense quality gives expected efficiency for yardage and TD props. Early-season values need heavy shrinkage.
nfl.pass_efficiency.measurement: From play_by_play: EPA/dropback, ANY/A, completion % over expected (CPOE), average depth of target (aDOT), air-yards per attempt, sack rate, INT rate, YAC share. Opponent-adjust with ridge using opposing pass-defense factors; for a specific QB use career-weighted prior (more weight on prior when <300 dropbacks) and recent 6-8 game window.
free_sources: nflverse pfr_advstats (pass, rush, rec, def weekly)

nfl.qb_efficiency.label: QB-specific efficiency prior (EPA+CPOE, career-regressed)
nfl.qb_efficiency.mechanism: The starting QB explains the largest share of team offensive variance; a QB-level efficiency prior built from career and recent play predicts passing production beyond team averages.
nfl.qb_efficiency.rationale: Teams change QBs often (injury, benching), so team-level stats misprice backups and returning starters; career-regressed estimates avoid overreacting to 3-game hot streaks, while recency captures real changes in health, supporting cast and scheme. Rookies and journeymen need position-appropriate priors (draft slot, college efficiency).
nfl.qb_efficiency.measurement: Per QB: EPA/dropback, CPOE, sack rate, INT rate, designed/scramble rush EPA, computed from play_by_play with opponent and receiver-quality adjustment; Bayesian shrinkage with prior weight ~200-300 dropbacks centered on a draft-slot/experience-based mean; blend with last-8-game window. Flag small samples.

nfl.explosive.label: Explosive-play rate and chunk-yard dependence
nfl.explosive.mechanism: Offense/defense explosive-play rates (20+ pass, 10+ run) shape scoring variance and drive length; explosive-heavy teams score fast with fewer plays.
nfl.explosive.rationale: Explosiveness is partly skill (vertical passing game, speed) and partly luck; it matters for totals variance, for tail outcomes (long TDs for yardage-ladder tails) and for first-TD timing. Defensive explosives allowed regress strongly.
nfl.explosive.measurement: Share of offensive plays gaining 10+ rushing/20+ passing, opponent-adjusted; and the same rate allowed. Compute expected explosive rate from air yards/depth profile and separate persistent skill (aDOT, speed receivers) from residual luck; shrink residuals toward zero.

nfl.redzone.label: Red-zone and goal-to-go TD conversion
nfl.redzone.mechanism: Finishing drives (TD versus FG) turns yards into points; red-zone TD rate has a skill component (scheme, goal-line personnel, QB mobility) and a large luck component.
nfl.redzone.rationale: Points per drive is the final link from yardage to scoring: teams with high yard efficiency but low red-zone TD rate are expected to regress upward in points, and vice versa. Separating persistent red-zone play-calling from noise protects against chasing outliers.
nfl.redzone.measurement: Red-zone (inside 20) and goal-to-go TD rate, success rate and pass/run split, opponent-adjusted. Shrink toward league average (prior ~40-60 red-zone trips) with additional weight to yards-based expected TD rate (from field-position-based expected points). Track separately for 4th-down go rate inside the 5.

nfl.turnovers.label: Turnover rate and takeaway luck regression
nfl.turnovers.mechanism: Turnovers swing possession counts and field position; offensive giveaway rates are mostly QB-driven and persistent in part, while defensive takeaways (especially fumble recoveries and INTs) regress heavily.
nfl.turnovers.rationale: Forecasting should use expected turnovers from process (pressure, tipped balls, aggressive throws, ball security) rather than realized takeaways; realized takeaway differential is a notorious regressor that markets sometimes overreact to.
nfl.turnovers.measurement: Offensive giveaways per play (INT rate with QB prior, fumble rate) and defensive takeaways per play; decompose INT into turnover-worthy/pressure/deflection and fumbles into forced vs recovered; regress recovered-fumble share to 50%; use opponent-adjusted rates with long half-life. Compare realized to expected from pressure and QB aggressiveness.
free_sources: nflverse pfr_advstats (pass, rush, rec, def weekly)

nfl.fumble_luck.label: Fumble recovery luck
nfl.fumble_luck.mechanism: Roughly half of all fumbles are recovered by each side irrespective of team skill, so team and player fumbles-lost outcomes are mostly random and mean-revert.
nfl.fumble_luck.rationale: Fumbles lost are a major swing factor in single-game outcomes and in season-level takeaway/turnover counts; a team that has been lucky recovering fumbles is overrated by raw turnover differential, and a player with several fumbles lost is not as likely to repeat.
nfl.fumble_luck.measurement: Count fumbles (forced and unforced) and recoveries by team and player; compute expected lost fumbles = fumbles x ~0.5 (position-specific adjustment: QB sacks/strips, RB, special teams); luck = realized lost minus expected; apply shrinkage to zero for forward projections; use fumble rate (not lost rate) as the repeatable component.

nfl.td_luck.label: Touchdown luck and yards-to-points regression
nfl.td_luck.mechanism: Touchdowns per yard or per target for a player or team above/below the expected rate given field position and usage are largely noise, producing regression in subsequent games and in season totals.
nfl.td_luck.rationale: TD props and totals are repriced on a recent hot streak; the true expectation depends on opportunity (red-zone touches, targets inside the 10) not on realized TDs. Subtle: some players (large TE/QB sneakers) have persistently higher TD rates than yardage implies.
nfl.td_luck.measurement: TD over expected = actual TDs minus expected TDs from carry/target location (yard line, game state), using expected points/TD models (ff_opportunity expected TD fields). Shrink luck to zero (e.g. 70-85% regression) and keep a smaller persistent player/role residual estimated across seasons.

nfl.pythag_luck.label: Close-game record and Pythagorean luck
nfl.pythag_luck.mechanism: Win-loss records in one-score games and points-versus-expected wins are noisy; teams with large positive close-game luck typically regress, affecting season win totals, playoff odds and futures.
nfl.pythag_luck.rationale: Season-level markets (wins, division, playoffs) are anchored by past records; Pythagorean/EPA-based wins and one-score-game luck give a better estimate of true talent than actual wins; the subtlety is the part of one-score success that is genuinely skill (QB late game, kicker, clock).
nfl.pythag_luck.measurement: Pythagorean expectation (points^2.37 form) and EPA-based expected wins; compute record in games decided by one score or less and the deficit versus expected; regress ~80-90% of close-game luck to zero; adjust using kicker/late-game QB prior.
free_sources: nflverse games.csv (spread_line, total_line, moneylines, roof, surface, temp, wind, rest, referee, coaches, starting QBs)

nfl.points_vs_expected.label: Points per drive versus drive-efficiency expectation (finishing luck)
nfl.points_vs_expected.mechanism: Points scored differ from points expected from yards and field position because of sequencing luck, FG variance, and turnover timing; this gap reverts toward zero.
nfl.points_vs_expected.rationale: A team that has scored much more than its yardage/EPA implies is expected to score less going forward; totals and team-total markets that follow recent scores can be mispriced by this sequencing noise.
nfl.points_vs_expected.measurement: For each team-game: actual points minus expected points from drive-level expected-points models (starting field position, yards gained) or EPA-based points; accumulate with recency weights; project regress to zero; track with decay so that real changes in finishing ability (kicker, QB) are slowly incorporated.

nfl.field_pos.label: Starting field position, special teams and return units
nfl.field_pos.mechanism: Average starting field position affects drive length and scoring probability (about 3 points per 10 yards of field position equivalent), determined by punting, returns, kickoffs, turnover spots and penalties.
nfl.field_pos.rationale: Special teams is a persistent but underweighted edge in game spread and totals; the 2024 kickoff rules changed touchback rates and return value, so older seasons need adjustment. Subtle: starting position also correlates with defensive quality via drive starts.
nfl.field_pos.measurement: Average starting yard line by team (own drives and opponent drives) separate from turnover-spot effect; net punt, kickoff return EPA, touchback rate by kicker; use rule-regime indicator for kickoff rules by season; shrink rate by games played.

nfl.kicker.label: Kicker accuracy by distance and effective range, kickoff touchback rate
nfl.kicker.mechanism: Kicker make probability by distance and weather determines the points value of drives that stall, FG attempt aggressiveness (range), and kickoff touchback probability.
nfl.kicker.rationale: Because roughly one-third of NFL scoring is FG/XP, kicker quality shifts team totals, kicker props and FG-versus-go decisions. Small samples demand shrinkage; wind and altitude interact strongly with long-range makes.
nfl.kicker.measurement: Logistic make probability vs distance with kicker random effect (Bayesian shrinkage with prior ~100+ attempts), stadium/altitude/wind/temp covariates; effective range = max distance with make prob >~50%; kickoff touchback rate by kicker and rule regime.

nfl.penalties.label: Team penalty rates and flag-driven drive effects
nfl.penalties.mechanism: Penalties move down-and-distance and field position; offensive holding/false starts depress EPA, defensive pass interference/holding extend drives. Team rates are partly persistent (discipline) and partly crew-driven.
nfl.penalties.rationale: Penalty-driven yardage can matter for team totals and for QB/receiver props via DPI yards; the crew effect (see officials) separates from team discipline. Registry notes it is currently not collected, so this is a hypothesis input.
nfl.penalties.measurement: Per game: accepted penalties and yards by type for offense/defense, opponent-adjusted; decompose into team-driven and referee-driven by mixed model with team and crew effects; include DPI per pass attempt.

nfl.officials_crew.label: Officiating crew penalty and call tendencies
nfl.officials_crew.mechanism: Referee crews differ in flag rates (holding, DPI, illegal contact) which affects drive length, scoring and pace; crews are announced weekly.
nfl.officials_crew.rationale: Penalty-heavy crews lengthen games and change efficiency; the effect is modest and noisy, so it needs shrinkage, but it is knowable pregame and may interact with pass-heavy offenses and DPI-heavy yardage props.
nfl.officials_crew.measurement: From nflverse officials and play_by_play, compute crew-level penalties per game, DPI per game and home-flag differential with random-effects shrinkage; control for the teams involved; map crew assignment to game (announced around Thursday of game week).
free_sources: nflverse games.csv (spread_line, total_line, moneylines, roof, surface, temp, wind, rest, referee, coaches, starting QBs)

nfl.pace.label: Neutral-situation pace and plays per game
nfl.pace.mechanism: Seconds per play in neutral situations (score within a window, first three quarters) and no-huddle usage set total offensive plays, which scales every counting stat and total points.
nfl.pace.rationale: Pace is a stable team trait strongly tied to coach and QB; it is partially offset by opponent (a slow opponent reduces possessions) and by game state. Because totals and props scale linearly with plays, pace misestimation of even 3-4 plays matters; remember run-heavy teams burn clock.
nfl.pace.measurement: Neutral-situation seconds per play (win prob 20-80%, quarters 1-3) per team; combine offense and opponent defense/time-of-possession style by additive model; compute expected plays = f(pace_off, pace_def, pass rate (clock stoppage), expected script). Recency-weight, shrink toward league; flag coaching/QB changes.

nfl.drives.label: Expected drives per team and clock-killing style
nfl.drives.mechanism: The number of possessions per team is the true volume unit: more drives means more scoring chances; it depends on pace, turnover rate, punts, and clock use.
nfl.drives.rationale: Drives per game is more directly tied to scoring than plays per game and is correlated across both teams, so game totals should be modeled as drives times points per drive with opponent adjustment; lopsided scripts reduce drives for the leading team late.
nfl.drives.measurement: Drives per game (excluding kneel-downs/end-of-half) per team and for games involving it; opponent-adjusted; project via plays/drive and drive-count model with script; include expected number of kneel/end-of-half possessions.

nfl.proe.label: Pass rate over expected, neutral and script-adjusted
nfl.proe.mechanism: Pass rate over expected measures a team's tendency to pass beyond what down, distance, field position and score predict; it is mainly coach/coordinator and QB-driven and sets pass attempts, hence passing yards and target volume.
nfl.proe.rationale: PROE separates scheme from game script so that expected attempts can be forecast jointly with the spread: pass-heavy teams hold volume in neutral scripts and inflate when trailing; run-heavy teams suppress passing yardage regardless of QB quality. Coordinator changes or QB injuries shift it.
nfl.proe.measurement: Fit an expected-pass model (logistic on down, distance, yard line, score diff, time, timeouts, shotgun) on league data; PROE = mean(actual - expected) over neutral plays per team; recency weighted with coordinator/QB regime flags; then forecast attempts = expected plays x (expected pass rate given forecast score distribution + PROE).

nfl.two_minute_tempo.label: Two-minute drill and hurry-up tempo
nfl.two_minute_tempo.mechanism: End-of-half and trailing hurry-up possessions inflate pass attempts, yards and quick scoring; teams differ in two-minute efficiency and willingness to hurry.
nfl.two_minute_tempo.rationale: First-half and quarter totals and receiving props include a lot of end-of-half mass; the opposite, kneel-downs and clock killing, suppress scoring. Coaches' timeout and clock behavior makes this partly knowable.
nfl.two_minute_tempo.measurement: Per team: points, plays and pass rate in the last two minutes of each half, share of end-of-half possessions with points; opponent-adjusted; timeouts retained; QB prior in two-minute drill; combine with lead/trail states from the own-model margin distribution (nfl.model_team_points_mean and nfl.heteroskedastic_margin_sd), not from betting spreads or totals.

nfl.garbage_time.label: Garbage-time and blowout script mass
nfl.garbage_time.mechanism: In lopsided games the trailing team passes more, the leader runs, and backups play; this redistributes yardage and creates tail outcomes for props.
nfl.garbage_time.rationale: Garbage-time inflates stats of trailing teams' receivers/QBs and deflates the leader's passing yardage; its probability is a function of the spread and team quality and should be modelled, not ignored, for yardage ladders.
nfl.garbage_time.measurement: Estimate probability of a 14+ point lead in Q4 from spread/total and score-difference distribution; measure each team/player stat split by garbage-time vs non-garbage-time (win probability <5% or >95%); add team tendency for starters leaving; combine into expected garbage mass for each prop.
free_sources: nflverse games.csv (spread_line, total_line, moneylines, roof, surface, temp, wind, rest, referee, coaches, starting QBs)

nfl.script.label: Game-script lattice: pass rate, pace and efficiency conditional on lead or trail
nfl.script.mechanism: Teams pass more and play faster when trailing and run and slow down when leading; the expected game script from the own-model expected margin (not the betting spread) therefore determines volume splits between passing and rushing props.
nfl.script.rationale: Because props are priced off a spread-and-total-derived script, the model must integrate over the score-state distribution rather than use a single average; teams differ in how strongly pass rate responds to score (coaching), making the lattice team-specific.
nfl.script.measurement: From play_by_play estimate pass rate, seconds/play, rush attempts and efficiency as a function of score differential bins and time remaining; simulate or integrate with the distribution of game states implied by the market-free margin and total distributions of nfl.model_team_points_mean and nfl.heteroskedastic_margin_sd (e.g., a Gaussian or t margin around the own-model mean margin); betting spreads and totals are not used; team-specific slope with shrinkage to league.
free_sources: nflverse games.csv (spread_line, total_line, moneylines, roof, surface, temp, wind, rest, referee, coaches, starting QBs)

nfl.opening_possession.label: Opening possession and coin-toss deferral behavior
nfl.opening_possession.mechanism: Which team gets the first possession (and the second-half kickoff) changes first-quarter scoring and first TD scorer/team probabilities.
nfl.opening_possession.rationale: Coin toss is random but teams' defer rates are coach-specific; first-scoring markets are partially a function of who has the ball first. After the second-half kickoff, the deferring team opens the half, shifting second-half timing.
nfl.opening_possession.measurement: Team and coach defer rate by season (post-2008 rule), by weather and by game importance; hazard model of first score timing by possession order; unknown at market time unless the market settles after the coin toss; adjust probabilities as 50/50 prior with a team-defer-rate mixture.

nfl.opening_script.label: Opening-drive play-calling and first-drive outcomes
nfl.opening_script.mechanism: Scripted opening drives show team-specific tendencies (pass/run split, tempo, TD rate on first drive) that influence first-quarter and first-TD markets.
nfl.opening_script.rationale: The first 15 plays are pre-scripted and differ from the rest of the game; the chance of an opening-drive TD for either team determines first-TD team/time and early race-to-N markets. Small samples require shrinkage.
nfl.opening_script.measurement: For each team: share of opening drives (first drive of game and of second half) ending in TD/FG/punt/turnover, plays per drive, pass rate vs expected; first-play targets; shrink to league mean with prior ~30 drives; adjust for QB/coordinator changes.

nfl.q_scoring.label: Historical scoring by quarter and half, opponent-adjusted
nfl.q_scoring.mechanism: Scoring is unevenly distributed through the game: first-quarter scripted drives, end-of-half drives, and second-half game-state adjustments cause quarter-specific scoring rates for each team.
nfl.q_scoring.rationale: Quarter/half total and spread markets need period scoring distributions rather than scaled game totals; end-of-half possessions and halftime adjustments make second half scoring different, and team styles (slow starters, strong two-minute offense) are persistent in part.
nfl.q_scoring.measurement: Per team: points and plays by quarter/half, opponent-adjusted; compute the team's share of expected game points scored in each period; shrink to league period shares (Q1 lower, Q2 and Q4 higher); combine team and opponent scoring shares with the game total from market.

nfl.qb.label: Starting QB status and QB-specific regime
nfl.qb.mechanism: The starting QB is the single biggest swing factor in team strength; moves between starter and backup shift the spread by ~3-10 points and change pass volume, efficiency and scoring.
nfl.qb.rationale: QB status resolves late (practice reports, game-time decision, Sunday inactives about 90 min before kickoff), so markets close before the QB is known and must hedge a mixture; the realized starter is not pregame-knowable until inactive list, while practice participation and beat reporting provide partial information.
nfl.qb.measurement: Probability distribution over starting QB from practice participation (DNP/limited/full), team designation, coach statements and history of QBs with similar injuries; QB value in points (starter minus replacement) estimated from own-model team ratings with and without the quarterback (nfl.own_team_rating_market_free), not from betting line moves; map to team ratings under each scenario and mix by probability; timestamp each information vintage.

nfl.injuries_pit.label: Injury report with practice status, timestamped vintages
nfl.injuries_pit.mechanism: Official practice participation (DNP/limited/full) and game designation (Out/Doubtful/Questionable) give early signals about player availability and effectiveness.
nfl.injuries_pit.rationale: Pregame-knowable info is timestamped: Wednesday and Thursday estimates, Friday final designation, and Sunday inactive list. Using the final vintage retroactively leaks information; the vintage at market time must be used and the probability of playing for Questionable players should be calibrated by position and practice pattern.
nfl.injuries_pit.measurement: Ingest injury reports with timestamps; map practice status sequences (e.g. DNP-limited-limited-Questionable) to play probability by calibrating on history (status to played) and by position; weights each player by snap/impact; note that the nflverse injuries file records final weekly status so true vintage requires own capture.

nfl.depth_chart_pit.label: Depth chart vintages (starter/rotation)
nfl.depth_chart_pit.mechanism: Depth charts reveal starters and role ordering (WR1/2/3, RB1/2, slot) that determine snap and target allocation, though they lag changes and are not official on many teams.
nfl.depth_chart_pit.rationale: Role certainty drives volume; a promoted WR2 gets targets only if depth charts or beat reports indicate the role change before the market closes. Because depth charts are team-reported and loosely maintained, snap/route data are a better realized-role signal than depth listing.
nfl.depth_chart_pit.measurement: Daily/weekly depth chart snapshots; compute changes in starter, RB1/RB2 and WR order versus last week; reconcile with snap_counts and routes from last games to estimate role stability; weight changes confirmed by injury report.

nfl.inactives_pit.label: Game-day inactive list (about 90 minutes before kickoff)
nfl.inactives_pit.mechanism: The inactive list definitively removes players from a game, collapsing uncertainty about starters, backups and role; it is posted about 90 minutes pregame.
nfl.inactives_pit.rationale: For markets that stay open until kickoff, the inactives announcement is the largest information event; markets settled before it face a mixture. Knowing the timing helps decide when information is knowable and prevents look-ahead.
nfl.inactives_pit.measurement: Capture official inactive lists with timestamp (ESPN game summary or NFL.com) and compare with pre-announcement probabilities; compute price reaction windows; use for belief updating of team ratings under the lineup realized.

nfl.ol.label: Offensive-line continuity, pass-block/pressure rates, run-block
nfl.ol.mechanism: The line governs time to throw, pressure and sack rates, and run-blocking yards before contact; continuity (same five starters) improves communication and pass-pro performance.
nfl.ol.rationale: OL injuries are underweighted by box score stats but matter for QB sacks, completions and rush yards; individual pass-block win rates are noisy and subject to scheme; replacement-level OL quality and tackle injuries matter more than guards for sacks.
nfl.ol.measurement: Compute games started together by projected five; team pressure rate allowed, sack rate, pressure-to-sack conversion, run-block EPA from play_by_play/participation with opponent pass-rush adjustment; individual OL pressures allowed from PFR; adjust team pass-block rating by (replacement - starter) value of absent players weighted by position.

nfl.skill_avail.label: WR/TE/RB availability and replacement quality
nfl.skill_avail.mechanism: Absence of a primary receiver or back redistributes targets and carries to replacements with different efficiency, altering both the team ceiling and individual prop expectations.
nfl.skill_avail.rationale: Vacated target share is only partly absorbed by the next man up; some goes to other positions (TE/RB), and efficiency drops because replacements are lower quality or face tougher coverage. Chemistry/QB-WR correlation changes the mix.
nfl.skill_avail.measurement: Compute vacated target share, air yards and red-zone targets of unavailable players; allocate by teammates' historical share when the absent player is out (with-or-without-you splits, shrinkage); adjust efficiency by replacement quality; update opponent coverage assumptions.

nfl.def_personnel.label: Defensive injuries and coverage scheme
nfl.def_personnel.mechanism: Missing pass rushers, corners or safeties changes the defense's pressure and coverage quality, shifting pass efficiency, yards and scoring allowed; scheme (zone/man, blitz) determines which receivers benefit.
nfl.def_personnel.rationale: Defensive stat lines are driven by a few top players (EDGE, CB1, FS); the market reacts to star injuries but depth-level injuries are underpriced; coverage scheme changes with personnel (e.g. a shutdown corner out moves coverage to zone).
nfl.def_personnel.measurement: Weight defensive snaps and pressure contributions by player; compute expected change in pressure rate and coverage EPA when absent; coverage scheme shares from participation data (man/zone, single-high/two-high); replace with replacement-level estimate; update opponent-adjusted defensive rating.

nfl.limited_player_discount.label: Efficiency discount for players returning or playing through injury
nfl.limited_player_discount.mechanism: A player listed Questionable/limited or returning from injury plays through reduced speed, snap counts and efficiency; the performance and volume are lower than healthy baseline.
nfl.limited_player_discount.rationale: Binary available/unavailable misses the larger middle group; a limited-practice QB may be mobile-restricted, a returning WR may be on a snap count, a banged-up RB less explosive; props over such players are often priced as if healthy.
nfl.limited_player_discount.measurement: Estimate snap-share and efficiency ratios for players in the first 1-3 games back or with limited practice labels relative to their healthy baseline using historical with/without samples by position and injury type (when disclosed); apply shrunken discount factor; keep uncertainty wide.
free_sources: nflverse injuries (weekly practice and game status)

nfl.in_game_exit_risk.label: In-game injury exit risk and snap ceiling
nfl.in_game_exit_risk.mechanism: Players can leave mid-game due to injury, ejection or blowout management, truncating counting stats; the risk is higher for players on the report and for high-contact positions.
nfl.in_game_exit_risk.rationale: Counting-stat props and anytime TD markets assume a full game; the exit probability is a hidden haircut, especially for RBs, QBs and players with prior injury history; this is a variance source not visible in the mean.
nfl.in_game_exit_risk.measurement: Estimate probability of missing >25% of expected snaps using position-specific historical in-game exit rate, adjusted by injury report status and prior-week snaps; apply to expected volume as a mixture; use blowout probability for starter rest.
free_sources: nflverse injuries (weekly practice and game status)

nfl.news.label: Beat-writer and news events (suspensions, trades, retirement, roles)
nfl.news.mechanism: Non-report information such as suspensions, trades, contract disputes, playing-time announcements and coaching statements changes player availability and team context.
nfl.news.rationale: News is the primary source for off-field and role-change markets; it is timestamped and noisy, so provenance (team site, beat reporters, league insiders) needs source weighting and reaction-time analysis.
nfl.news.measurement: Collect headlines with timestamp from ESPN news feed and team releases; classify event type (suspension, trade, injury, role) and credibility tier; link to player/team; measure the price reaction window; build features like days since news, number of independent sources.

nfl.pressure_qb.label: QB pressure/sack rate faced and time to throw
nfl.pressure_qb.mechanism: Pressure shortens time to throw, lowers completion and EPA, increases sacks and INTs; the QB's pressure rate faced is a product of opponent pass rush and own OL, modulated by QB time-to-throw and scrambling.
nfl.pressure_qb.rationale: The interaction is key: a quick-release QB neutralizes pass rush, while a slow-to-throw QB behind a weak OL amplifies it. Pressure is partially opponent-driven (stable) and partially play-call/QB-driven; pressure-to-sack conversion varies by QB.
nfl.pressure_qb.measurement: Team pressure rate allowed (OL+QB) and rate generated by opposing defense (from participation was_pressure, PFR), average time to throw (NGS), blitz rate faced, pressure-to-sack conversion, EPA/dropback under pressure vs clean; adjust by opponent: expected pressure = f(own OL, opp pass rush, QB time to throw) with recency and shrinkage.
free_sources: nflverse participation (pbp_participation: personnel, coverage type, man/zone, pressure, time to throw)
nflverse pfr_advstats (pass, rush, rec, def weekly)

nfl.pass_rush.label: Defensive pass rush: pressure rate, sack rate, edge quality
nfl.pass_rush.mechanism: A defense that generates pressure with four rushers reduces opposing passing efficiency and volume (more sacks, shorter drives) without blitz risk.
nfl.pass_rush.rationale: Pass rush is the most predictive defensive unit for pass efficiency; individual edge players (a few) drive it, so injuries to EDGE players are decisive. Sack totals regress; pressure rate is more stable.
nfl.pass_rush.measurement: Team pressure rate, sack rate and blitz-adjusted pressure rate, opponent-adjusted for OL quality faced; player-level pressures via PFR and snap-weighted contribution; expected sacks = dropbacks x pressure rate x pressure-to-sack conversion with shrinkage.
free_sources: nflverse participation (pbp_participation: personnel, coverage type, man/zone, pressure, time to throw)

nfl.coverage_scheme.label: Defensive coverage shell and man/zone rates
nfl.coverage_scheme.mechanism: Coverage type (man vs zone, single-high vs two-high, blitz frequency) determines which targets are open, expected aDOT, YAC and who sees the targets, and thus QB, WR and TE yardage distributions.
nfl.coverage_scheme.rationale: Offenses and receivers have coverage-specific splits (e.g. slot WRs vs man, TEs vs zone, deep threats vs two-high shells); a defense's tendencies shift with personnel and game state, so matching offense's performance vs man/zone to the defense's rates creates matchup edge.
nfl.coverage_scheme.measurement: From participation and FTN: defense man/zone rate, single-high/two-high rate, blitz rate, by down and distance; offense EPA and target distribution versus man and zone; expected EPA = weights x coverage-specific offense efficiency; shrink small samples.
free_sources: nflverse participation (pbp_participation: personnel, coverage type, man/zone, pressure, time to throw)

nfl.cb_coverage_matchup.label: Receiver versus cornerback matchup (shadow coverage, alignment)
nfl.cb_coverage_matchup.mechanism: When a defense assigns a top corner to a primary receiver, that receiver's target volume and efficiency fall, while others see more targets; slot and outside matchups differ.
nfl.cb_coverage_matchup.rationale: Shadow usage is scheme-specific and visible only from tracking-like data; most teams play sides/zone, so the effect is limited to teams that travel CBs. Matchup uncertainty is high and the market often ignores it, but evidence is noisy.
nfl.cb_coverage_matchup.measurement: Estimate CB shadow rates from participation/alignment (primary coverage assignments are not public; use route alignment vs defender side proxies) and receiver yards per route run vs top CB; apply an adjustment only when the defense has demonstrated travel patterns; shrink strongly.

nfl.run_defense.label: Run defense: box counts, stuff rate, front quality
nfl.run_defense.mechanism: Run-defense strength and defensive front personnel set rush efficiency and RB volume; light boxes make runs efficient but pass-leaning defenses concede rushing yards.
nfl.run_defense.rationale: Opponent rush adjustment must combine front quality (DL/LB injuries), box count tendencies and the offense's run scheme; rush yardage props depend jointly on efficiency and script, so a defense that is bad against the run in neutral situations may still see fewer rushes when trailing.
nfl.run_defense.measurement: Rush EPA allowed, stuff rate, yards before contact allowed, explosive-run rate allowed, box count (7-, 8+ men) rates from FTN/participation; opponent adjust; weight injuries to DL/LBs via snap shares; combine with expected rushes from script.

nfl.dvp.label: Defense versus position (RB/WR/TE) opponent-adjusted yields
nfl.dvp.mechanism: Position-specific yards, receptions and TDs allowed per target/carry (adjusted for opponents faced) summarize how a defense funnels production to a position (e.g. soft vs TEs).
nfl.dvp.rationale: Raw defense-vs-position (DvP) is dominated by who the defense has faced; the right measure is opponent-adjusted per-opportunity efficiency and share of targets, which is stable only with heavy shrinkage. It is a coverage/personnel scheme proxy rather than a causal force.
nfl.dvp.measurement: Per defense: target share and yards/target to RB/WR/TE and to alignment (slot, wide), adjusted for opposing offense quality with ridge fits; compute expected player yards = player target share x defense-specific yards-per-target with shrinkage to league; recency weighted and injury-adjusted.

nfl.coaching.label: Coach and coordinator tendencies (4th-down aggression, tempo, run/pass)
nfl.coaching.mechanism: Coaches determine pace, play-calling, 4th-down and 2-point aggression, and in-game timeout behavior, all of which change volume, points and distribution.
nfl.coaching.rationale: Coaching regimes persist across rosters and move with coordinator changes; a new play-caller can shift PROE and tempo; aggressive 4th-down teams alter FG vs TD mix and drive length, important for totals and TD markets. Tenure matters for sample size.
nfl.coaching.measurement: Regime-labeled stats by head coach and offensive/defensive coordinator: neutral pass rate, tempo, 4th-down go rate over expected (fourth-down model), 2-point attempt rate, challenge/timeout usage; shrink new-coach priors using previous stops; mark regime break dates.

nfl.formation.label: Formation/personnel groupings, motion and play-action rates
nfl.formation.mechanism: Personnel (11/12/21) and play-action/motion usage determine which skill players are on the field, target distribution and pass-run balance.
nfl.formation.rationale: Role allocation depends on personnel: a TE plays more in 12 personnel; RPO and play action raise efficiency; defensive personnel responses (base vs nickel) set run box and coverage; FTN charting gives rates but only from 2022.
nfl.formation.measurement: FTN: share of plays with 11/12/13/21 personnel, motion rate, play-action rate, screen rate, RPO; offense performance by formation; join with defensive personnel (nickel/dime rates) to estimate formation mix for the game.

nfl.ngs.label: Next Gen metrics: separation, cushion, YAC over expected, CPOE
nfl.ngs.mechanism: Tracking-derived separation, cushion and YAC over expected capture receiver skill and QB accuracy beyond box score outcomes.
nfl.ngs.rationale: These metrics help distinguish receiver-created production from QB or scheme-created production; they are more stable than counting stats but only available as aggregate weekly/season tables.
nfl.ngs.measurement: Weekly NGS tables: average separation, cushion, target share, YAC above expected, rushing yards over expected, time to throw, aggressiveness; shrink with prior ~ target counts; use as covariates in per-target yardage models.

nfl.target_competition.label: Target competition and teammate quality within the passing game
nfl.target_competition.mechanism: A receiver's target share depends on the quality and availability of teammates competing for the same targets, not just on his own skill.
nfl.target_competition.rationale: Adding or losing a WR1/TE1/RB receiver reallocates target share non-linearly; role specificity (slot, deep, red zone) means partial substitution; incorrectly assuming vacated targets are spread proportionally misprices props.
nfl.target_competition.measurement: With-or-without-you target share splits for each player given presence/absence of key teammates (shrunk); Dirichlet/multinomial target allocation model with covariates; vacated mass redistributed by role similarity.

nfl.snaps.label: Snap share and role by game state
nfl.snaps.mechanism: Snap share bounds opportunity: players on the field more get more touches; rotations and game-state-driven usage (passing downs, trailing, short yardage) determine realized volume.
nfl.snaps.rationale: Snap share is more stable than touches and anchors usage models, but changes with injuries, game script and returns from injury; snap counts for the upcoming game are not known pregame, only expectations.
nfl.snaps.measurement: Rolling snap share by down/distance/score state from snap_counts and participation; project expected snaps given game script and injury; separate rotational vs three-down role; shrink toward depth-chart-based prior.

nfl.routes.label: Route participation and alignment
nfl.routes.mechanism: Routes run (share of dropbacks) measure how often a receiver actually runs a pattern; targets per route run (TPRR) and yards per route run (YPRR) are the cleanest efficiency/usage decomposition.
nfl.routes.rationale: Targets alone mix opportunity and skill; route participation separates snap and blocking role from target earning; slot/wide alignment affects matchups. Route data requires participation/charting; sample sizes small early.
nfl.routes.measurement: Route participation rate = routes/dropbacks; TPRR; YPRR; slot/wide/inline alignment shares and aDOT, from participation and FTN; prior regressed to position; combine with expected pass attempts.

nfl.targets.label: Target share, air-yards share, TPRR and aDOT
nfl.targets.mechanism: Target volume and depth determine receptions and receiving yards; target share times expected team pass attempts gives expected targets, and aDOT shapes catch probability and yards per reception.
nfl.targets.rationale: Receiving ladders map directly to targets x catch rate x yards per catch; target share is persistent but moves with roster changes, game script and coverage; aDOT interacts with wind and QB arm; regression needed on small samples.
nfl.targets.measurement: Rolling target share, air yards share, TPRR, aDOT and WOPR-style composites from play_by_play; per-game targets forecast = team attempts forecast x share (shrunk with prior and updated for teammates absent); catch rate model with depth/QB covariates.

nfl.carries.label: Carry share, goal-line and passing-down role
nfl.carries.mechanism: RB carries depend on role in the committee, game script, and goal-line/short-yardage usage; passing-down role determines receptions.
nfl.carries.rationale: Rushing yards props are volume driven; committee share changes with injuries and efficiency. Goal-line role has large TD implications but small yardage; passing-down backs add receiving volume not rushing.
nfl.carries.measurement: Rolling carry share, inside-10 carry share, rushing attempts per game conditional on lead/trail, RB passing-down snap share; expected carries = team rush attempts forecast x share; injuries/hot-hand adjustment with shrinkage.

nfl.rz_share.label: Red-zone and goal-line usage shares
nfl.rz_share.mechanism: Players who receive carries/targets near the goal line carry the TD equity; usage shares inside the 10 and 5 predict TD probability better than yards.
nfl.rz_share.rationale: Anytime and first TD markets are about opportunity concentration: a goal-line back with few yards can have higher TD odds than a star WR. Roles change with injuries and play-calling; opposing defense (red-zone vulnerability) modifies.
nfl.rz_share.measurement: Red-zone target/carry share, inside-5 carry share, end-zone targets; team red-zone trip forecast x share x conversion rate; blend with prior from role (QB sneaks, TE); update for injuries.

nfl.td_rates.label: Anytime and first-TD scoring rates by role
nfl.td_rates.mechanism: Per-game probability of scoring is a function of expected team TDs, the player's share of scoring opportunities, and the correlation of scoring across teammates; first-TD adds a timing component.
nfl.td_rates.rationale: Anytime TD probability should be built from a team TD expectation and player share (Poisson/multinomial) rather than a flat historical rate; first-TD markets additionally weigh which team scores first and the player share of first-possession usage.
nfl.td_rates.measurement: Expected team touchdowns = (team total - FG expectation)/7 approximately; allocate by player share of expected TDs (red-zone/goal-line role and receiving usage), calibrate shares with shrinkage; first-TD = P(team first) x player share of that team's first TDs.

nfl.air_yards_adot.label: Air yards, aDOT and deep-target rate
nfl.air_yards_adot.mechanism: Depth of target controls both the average yards per catch and the catch probability; deep-target-heavy players have boom-bust yardage distributions and exposure to wind and QB arm.
nfl.air_yards_adot.rationale: Receiving yards ladders require the distribution, not only the mean; aDOT and deep share set variance, while slot underneath roles have high floors. The QB's deep ball accuracy changes realized yards.
nfl.air_yards_adot.measurement: Player aDOT, air-yards share, deep target share (20+), contested-catch rate from play_by_play and NGS; combine with QB deep-completion rate and weather (wind); model yards per target as mixture by depth bins.

nfl.catch_rate_oe.label: Catch rate over expected, drops and YAC over expected
nfl.catch_rate_oe.mechanism: Receivers who consistently catch more than expected based on target difficulty and generate YAC produce more yards per target.
nfl.catch_rate_oe.rationale: Catch rate over expected separates receiver skill from QB accuracy; YAC over expected is a stable skill; these affect yards per reception and reception props, but need shrinkage due to small target counts.
nfl.catch_rate_oe.measurement: Catch rate over expected using target depth, location, pressure and coverage; YAC over expected from NGS/PFR; shrink towards position average with prior of ~80-100 targets.
free_sources: nflverse pfr_advstats (pass, rush, rec, def weekly)

nfl.rb_efficiency.label: RB efficiency: rush yards over expected, yards after contact, receiving role
nfl.rb_efficiency.mechanism: Backs differ in creation of yardage beyond blocking (rush yards over expected, elusiveness), affecting yards per carry and explosive runs; passing-down backs differ in receiving usage.
nfl.rb_efficiency.rationale: RB yards per carry is a noisy mix of OL, box count, and RB; yards over expected stabilizes more slowly than team-level stats; use shrinkage and team-level prior; also relevant for fumble and injury-prone RBs.
nfl.rb_efficiency.measurement: NGS rush yards over expected per attempt, yards after contact, broken tackles/attempt from PFR; shrink to team YPC prior; recency-weighted; combine with opponent run defense.
free_sources: nflverse pfr_advstats (pass, rush, rec, def weekly)

nfl.qb_rushing.label: QB scramble and designed-run usage
nfl.qb_rushing.mechanism: Mobile QBs add rushing yards and TDs and avoid sacks; designed QB runs near the goal line also raise their TD probability and the team's red-zone conversion.
nfl.qb_rushing.rationale: QB rushing props and anytime TD for QBs depend on scheme and health; mobility drops with injury; rushing volume is partially game-script dependent (scrambles when pressured).
nfl.qb_rushing.measurement: QB designed runs and scrambles per game, goal-line QB sneak rate, rushing EPA; condition on pressure rate and opponent contain; adjust with injury status (limited mobility); shrink to career prior.

nfl.int_rate.label: QB interception rate decomposition and regression
nfl.int_rate.mechanism: Interceptions depend on QB decision-making and aggressiveness, pressure, throw depth, and large amounts of luck (tipped balls, defender hands); INT rate regresses substantially.
nfl.int_rate.rationale: INT props are priced on recent realized rates; the repeatable component is turnover-worthy throw rate and aggressiveness, while interception conversion of those plays by defenders is noisy; opponent ball-hawk skill adds small persistent effect.
nfl.int_rate.measurement: INT per attempt shrunk with prior; decomposition: turnover-worthy throw rate (PFR bad-throw/ pressure), tipped/deflected INT share, defense INT rate over expected; expected INTs = attempts x blended rate with opponent and pressure adjustments.
free_sources: nflverse pfr_advstats (pass, rush, rec, def weekly)

nfl.player_stat_variance.label: Player-stat distribution shape and boom-bust variance
nfl.player_stat_variance.mechanism: The dispersion of a player's stat around his mean (driven by role, depth of target, script, injury risk) determines probabilities of exceeding each ladder threshold even if the mean is correct.
nfl.player_stat_variance.rationale: Threshold markets are priced off the whole distribution: boom-bust deep receivers have fat right tails and more median-below-mean mass; QBs have game-script-induced variance; ignoring shape yields consistent miscalibration at rung extremes.
nfl.player_stat_variance.measurement: Fit game-level distributions (negative binomial or lognormal-zero-inflated by stat) using residuals around expected values; estimate dispersion by player role with shrinkage and mixture for injury exit and garbage time; compute exceedance probabilities by rung via simulation or analytic mixture.

nfl.weather_pit.label: Kickoff-hour weather forecast vintages (wind, temp, precipitation)
nfl.weather_pit.mechanism: Wind, rain, snow and cold reduce passing efficiency, deep passing, kicking accuracy and scoring, and raise run share; forecasts update through game week.
nfl.weather_pit.rationale: Weather effects are non-linear: wind above ~15 mph sharply cuts deep-ball and FG efficiency, while temperature has small effects unless extreme; roofs neutralize them. Using realized weather leaks information; forecast vintages at market time are required.
nfl.weather_pit.measurement: Store forecasts (wind speed/gust, temperature, precipitation probability) at fixed lead times before kickoff for open-air stadiums; map to stadium coordinates and kickoff hour; ignore for domes; compute wind component along field (cross vs head); calibrate effect on totals, pass rate and FG make rates.
free_sources: nflverse games.csv (spread_line, total_line, moneylines, roof, surface, temp, wind, rest, referee, coaches, starting QBs)

nfl.venue.label: Roof, surface, altitude and home-field effect
nfl.venue.mechanism: Venue properties modify weather exposure (dome vs open), surface speed, altitude (Denver) and crowd noise (false starts), shaping pace, totals and home advantage.
nfl.venue.rationale: Home-field advantage has declined and varies by team and crowd noise; domes lift passing and totals; turf vs grass affects injuries and speed; these are stable context variables but small and partly already in the line.
nfl.venue.measurement: Stadium table: roof type, surface, elevation, historical home margin and total residual with shrinkage; team-specific HFA in rating model; neutral-site indicator (international games, Super Bowl).

nfl.rest_travel.label: Rest, bye week, short week and travel/time zone
nfl.rest_travel.mechanism: Rest days and travel (time-zone change, short weeks after Thursday/Monday games) affect performance and injury risk; post-bye teams have extra preparation.
nfl.rest_travel.rationale: Effects are modest but systematic: Thursday road teams on short rest, west-to-east travel for early games, and international trips; the market already prices part of it, so any signal is small and conditional.
nfl.rest_travel.measurement: From schedule: days of rest for each team, bye indicator, miles/time-zone shifts, kickoff time relative to body clock, consecutive road games, international game flag; regress margin and total residuals on these with team and season effects.

nfl.divisional_familiarity.label: Divisional familiarity and rematch dynamics
nfl.divisional_familiarity.mechanism: Division opponents play twice a year with extensive scouting familiarity; games tend to be closer and lower scoring than team-quality alone predicts.
nfl.divisional_familiarity.rationale: Underdog cover rates and total residuals in divisional games may differ from non-division ones; this is a hypothesis with small effect and large noise; second meetings within a season include learned information.
nfl.divisional_familiarity.measurement: Division indicator, first vs second meeting, margin of first meeting; regress residual vs spread/total on these with shrinkage; interact with spread size.

nfl.motivation_seeding.label: Seeding stakes, clinching, tanking and starter rest

nfl.score_resid.label: Score residual distribution around market lines and key numbers
nfl.score_resid.mechanism: Final margin and total relative to the market line are not Gaussian: scores cluster on key numbers (3, 7, 6, 10) and totals on typical combinations, so probabilities at push-adjacent lines differ from normal approximations.
nfl.score_resid.rationale: Spread and total markets at half-point lines or ladder rungs need a lattice distribution: P(margin = k) differs sharply by k; empirical residual distribution conditional on the line (and scale with total) gives better-calibrated probabilities than a Gaussian with fixed SD.
nfl.score_resid.measurement: Estimate empirical distribution of (final margin - closing spread) and (total - closing total) using historical games, with kernel smoothing and key-number mass; scale SD with total; separate home/away; use for converting rating differences to rung probabilities.

nfl.ot_model.label: Overtime and tie model
nfl.ot_model.mechanism: Overtime frequency, the overtime rule set in force that season and tie probability determine settlement of regulation-only versus including-OT markets. (Rule history as stated in the original draft and NOT verified from a primary rulebook in this round; treat as unverified secondary information.) From 2025 the regular-season overtime is a single 10-minute period in which both teams get a possession (an opening-drive touchdown no longer ends the game), then sudden death; the game is a tie if the period expires level. Seasons 2017-2024 used the 10-minute first-possession-touchdown-wins format; the playoffs have no time limit.
nfl.ot_model.rationale: OT adds scoring and changes winner markets; in nflverse regular-season data (2012-2025, n=3,784, figures from the original draft and not re-checked here) about 6% of games were tied after regulation and went to overtime, but only about 0.4% ended tied, so markets that settle on regulation carry meaningful tie mass while including-OT markets almost none; ties count 0.5 in standings. The overtime rule set changes by season and must be read from each contract's rules text, not assumed. Market wording must be matched to the model.
nfl.ot_model.measurement: P(tie after 60 min) from the model margin lattice mass at 0 (nfl.model_margin_lattice, own means, no betting lines). Overtime: drive simulation under the rule era of the season (2017-2024: first-possession TD wins, 10 min; 2025+: both teams possess unless the first drive consumes the full 10 minutes and scores, then sudden death, 10 min; playoffs: both possess, untimed). Per drive, outcome rates (TD, FG, punt/turnover, safety) and drive duration from the two teams' own drive model by field position, shrunk to league with k=150 drives. A TD that wins outright ends the game with no try; a try follows only a TD that does not end it (first-possession TD, or a second-team TD that ties or trails), with the extra-point versus two-point choice by coach and score state. Resulting final margins: 6 or 3 for a second-team TD or FG after nothing/FG; 3, 4, 5 for a FG answered against a TD+try of 6, 7, 8; 1 or 2 after a matching TD and try; 6-8 for an unanswered TD; sudden death 3 (FG), 6 (TD), 2 (safety). Output P(OT), P(win | OT) per team, the OT points distribution, and P(level after OT) per game, refitted by era (2012-2016, 2017-2024, 2025+); use settlement wording to decide which components to include.

nfl.corr.label: Within-game correlations across stats and teams

nfl.team_total_split.label: Team-points share model (implied total and spread to team means)
nfl.team_total_split.mechanism: The game total and spread jointly imply each team's expected points: team A = (total + spread-to-A)/2; team totals markets depend on this split and on variance of each team separately.
nfl.team_total_split.rationale: Team total and combined markets must be consistent with the game market; the split depends on spread and total only if the market is efficient; deviations signal mispricing; allowing for scoring styles (high-variance team) matters.
nfl.team_total_split.measurement: Benchmark only: with spread_line s defined as nflverse (positive = home favored by s) and total T, implied home mean = (T + s)/2, implied away mean = (T - s)/2. Compare to quoted team totals Q_home, Q_away: inconsistency = (Q_home + Q_away) - T and (Q_home - Q_away) - s. Adjust each mean for key-number mass by shifting to the nearest of the discrete means in nfl.team_score_pmf_own_mean using the own-mean pmf as a likelihood ratio. Label output as market-derived; use nfl.model_team_points_mean for market-free analysis.

nfl.leader_order_statistic.label: League/week leader as max-of-N order statistic
nfl.leader_order_statistic.mechanism: Leader markets resolve to the maximum across many players with correlated outcomes; the probability that a given player leads depends on the top-end distribution of competitors, not just his own mean. Use by archetype: in statistical-leader markets this is the winner rule (Monte Carlo P(max)); in vote-based award markets (season_awards) it is only a production-rank feature that feeds ballot placement in nfl.vote_outcome_model and is not the winner rule.
nfl.leader_order_statistic.rationale: The favorite's probability is bounded by variance of many near contenders; per-game weekly leaders (e.g. most receiving yards) are far more random than season leaders; pricing should use simulation of the whole field with correlations.
nfl.leader_order_statistic.measurement: Simulate distributions for each contender (using player_stat_variance and games_played_dist) and compute P(max) by Monte Carlo; for weekly leaders include all players on the slate; calibrate against historical leader frequencies. For vote-based awards, output only each candidate's simulated production rank among peers as a feature of the ballot model; the winner there is decided by simulated ranked-ballot points.

nfl.fantasy_points_model.label: Fantasy-points translation (PPR component model)
nfl.fantasy_points_model.mechanism: Fantasy-point season/week markets are linear combinations of yards, receptions and TDs with positional baselines; the component correlations and volume determine outcomes.
nfl.fantasy_points_model.rationale: Because TDs are noisy and yardage/receptions are role-driven, projections should be built bottom-up; expected fantasy points from opportunity (ff_opportunity) are better predictors than realized points.
nfl.fantasy_points_model.measurement: Bottom-up expected fantasy points = sum of expected rushing/receiving yards, receptions, TDs weighted by scoring settings; use ff_opportunity expected points as baseline; simulate with correlation and games played.

nfl.award_stats.label: Award-candidate production and voting narrative
nfl.award_stats.mechanism: Season awards (MVP, OPOY, DPOY, ROY) are determined by voters who weigh production, team success, narrative and position bias (QBs for MVP).
nfl.award_stats.rationale: Statistical output alone underpredicts winners; voting patterns favor team success and recent performance; early-season narrative is volatile and late-season games weigh heavily; unusual feats and ESPN/NFL Honors narratives matter.
nfl.award_stats.measurement: Candidate features: EPA, yards, TDs, team wins, rank among peers; historical winner models using logistic regression on past awards (QB bias, team record threshold); track media poll mentions (not betting or prediction-market odds); update weekly.

nfl.award_voting_mechanics.label: Award voter pool, timing and tie rules

nfl.draft_board.label: Draft order, prospect rankings and team needs

m.combo_pricing.label: Combo/parlay price versus correlated-leg product
m.combo_pricing.mechanism: A combo's fair price equals the joint probability of legs; naive product of marginals ignores correlation, so a quoted combo price relative to joint model estimate reveals mispricing.
m.combo_pricing.rationale: Combos amplify errors: positively correlated legs (team win and over) are worth more than the product; negatively correlated worth less; also fees and liquidity are larger for combos.
m.combo_pricing.measurement: For a combo of legs L1..Ln at snapshot time t: p_joint = mean over 20,000 joint simulations using game-level dependence from nfl.corr and nfl.leg_dependence_by_model_regime (legs in different games independent unless nfl.cross_game_leg_dependence rho differs from 0). Executable cost c = best ask for YES plus Kalshi taker fee at that price; edge = p_joint - c, in probability points, with 90% interval from simulation seed variance plus leg-model uncertainty. Use the rules text version captured at t to apply void/push handling per nfl.leg_void_push_matrix; if any leg rule is unresolved, report edge under each variant. Price is read only as the comparison target, never as a model input.

m.stat_correction_risk.label: Official stat correction and settlement-source lag risk
m.stat_correction_risk.mechanism: Player and team stats can be corrected after the game by the league stat crew, and the settlement source may update at different times, creating tail risk for close thresholds.
m.stat_correction_risk.rationale: Contracts settled at a threshold within a yard or one reception are sensitive to stat revisions and source choice (official NFL vs ESPN); knowing which source and when it locks is important.
m.stat_correction_risk.measurement: For each stat type (rushing/receiving/passing yards, receptions, TDs, sacks) over seasons where own snapshots exist, compute revision rate r = share of player-games whose value at T+7d differs from the value at game end by >=1 unit, and revision size distribution; also source disagreement rate between ESPN and the contract's named settlement source at T+1d. For a threshold K, correction risk = P(|true revision| >= distance of projected value to K) approximated by r times P(realized stat within 1 unit of K) from the player distribution. Output probability in points; as-of before kickoff using rates from prior seasons only. No contract price is used; ladder strikes only supply K.

nfl.offfield_base_rate.label: Reference-class base rates for NFL off-field events
nfl.offfield_base_rate.mechanism: Each off-field series is priced from a named reference class of comparable past events with its historical frequency by calendar window: head-coach exits and hires, trades, retirements and roster events from the transaction history, cross-sport athletes linked to an NFL signing for the celebrity series, and announced international games for the game-location series.
nfl.offfield_base_rate.rationale: Off-field markets are not game-model problems; the prior is the historical frequency of a defined class conditional on record, contract and calendar, updated by dated official reporting. Classes must be declared per series: a celebrity-signing market has almost no successes in its class, so the prior is near zero and dominated by verified tryout or signing news, while ownership-stake and stadium-completion series are out of scope and excluded rather than given an invented prior.
nfl.offfield_base_rate.measurement: Per series reference class, window and estimator. (1) Coach exit/hire (KXNFLCOACHOUT, KXNFLNEXTCOACHOUT, KXNFLHIRECOACH): head-coach seasons 2000-2025, event by calendar week, conditioned on win% bin and tenure, Gamma-Poisson shrinkage (prior shape 2, rate 4 team-years). (2) Trades, next team, retirement, 53-man (KXNFLTRADE, KXNFLNEXTTEAM, KXNFLRETIRE, KXNFL53MAN): transaction log 2010-2025 by type and week, conditioned on contract year and age, same shrinkage. (3) Cross-sport athlete signing or snap (KXNFLHKANE, KXNFLCOMPETE): class = non-NFL athletes publicly reported as working out for or negotiating with an NFL team 2000-2025 (International Player Pathway rugby and other athletes, soccer and track converts, celebrities); success = official signing (HKANE) or a recorded snap (COMPETE) within the contract window; Beta(0.5, 0.5) prior updated by class counts, then multiplied by 0.1 when no credible tryout or negotiation report exists for the named person. (4) International game venue retention (KXNFLGAMELOCATION): announced international regular-season games 2007-2025, share played in the announced city by the announced date, Beta(1,1) prior. Excluded: KXNFLOWNERSTAKE and KXNFLSTADIUM, re-filed OUT_OF_SCOPE in the final series assignment. Store each event's official announcement timestamp; as-of quote time.
