nfl.leg_dependence_by_model_regime.label: Leg-pair dependence by model margin and total regime
nfl.leg_dependence_by_model_regime.mechanism: Cross-leg dependence (favourite cover with QB yards, total over with rusher yards) changes sign between competitive, blowout and shootout regimes; the regime must be assigned from the model's own pregame expectation.
nfl.leg_dependence_by_model_regime.rationale: One correlation coefficient averages positive shootout dependence with negative blowout dependence. Assigning regimes by the betting spread would make the combo price depend on the market line; using the model margin keeps the input market-free and lets the model disagree with the line.
nfl.leg_dependence_by_model_regime.measurement: For each leg-type pair (about 30 types), estimate Kendall tau or tetrachoric correlation of the two leg indicators within bins of the as-of pregame model expected margin from nfl.model_team_points_mean (|m|<3, 3-7, >7 points) and terciles of the model expected total, on 2015+ player-games with the model means re-computed point-in-time; shrink each bin toward the pooled estimate with k=150 games, require 400+ games per cell, report standard errors; as-of end of previous week. Closing spreads and totals are excluded and used only to benchmark.
raw_data: point-in-time model expected margin and total

nfl.cross_league_futures_leg.label: Cross-league futures leg marginal and dependence
nfl.cross_league_futures_leg.mechanism: A cross-league championship combo is the product of an NFL title probability and another league's title probability, adjusted for any shared dependence (near zero) and for the different resolution dates.
nfl.cross_league_futures_leg.rationale: The NFL leg comes from the season simulation, but the other leg (NBA champion) is outside every NFL input; without an explicit import of that sport's model output, with its own as-of time, the combo cannot be priced. Dependence between the legs is close to independence but resolution timing makes early NO paths matter for mark-to-market.
nfl.cross_league_futures_leg.measurement: P(combo) = P_NFL(team wins Super Bowl) x P_other(team wins title) x (1 + rho_adj), with P_NFL from nfl.standings_sim playoff simulation (20,000 seasons) and P_other the other sport's catalog championship model output taken as-of the same timestamp; rho_adj set to 0 unless a shared-owner or shared-market effect is shown (test: correlation of preseason title probabilities across leagues by metro 2000-2025, expected near 0). Record both legs' as-of times and the date each leg can first resolve NO.

nfl.cross_game_leg_dependence.label: Residual dependence between win legs of different games on one slate
nfl.cross_game_leg_dependence.mechanism: Correlation between the outcomes of different games after conditioning on each game's model win probability, arising from shared model error, shared weather fronts and league-wide officiating trends.
nfl.cross_game_leg_dependence.rationale: Multi-game moneyline parlays are priced as a product of legs; if residual outcome correlation is non-zero (e.g. the model systematically overrates favourites in one week or one weather regime), the product misprices the parlay. Expected to be near zero, but must be measured rather than assumed because errors compound across 3 legs.
nfl.cross_game_leg_dependence.measurement: For every pair of games in the same week 2012-2025 (regular season and playoffs separately), compute residuals e_g = 1{home win} - p_model_g using point-in-time model win probabilities from nfl.model_margin_lattice (OT included, ties scored 0.5); estimate the pooled pairwise correlation of e_g within week, and conditional on both games outdoor with forecast wind >15 mph and on both favourites p>0.7; shrink toward 0 with a prior of n0=2000 pairs; output rho and its standard error per regime, as-of previous season.

nfl.halftime_margin_scoring_model.label: Second-half scoring by halftime margin with model-based state weights
nfl.halftime_margin_scoring_model.mechanism: Q3 and Q4 scoring depend on the halftime margin and each team's script response; pregame 3Q, 4Q and 2H contracts are mixtures over halftime states.
nfl.halftime_margin_scoring_model.rationale: The same team scores differently leading by 14 than trailing by 3. The mixture weights must come from the model's own pregame margin so period prices are not anchored to the betting spread; second-half markets that include overtime also need the tie branch.
nfl.halftime_margin_scoring_model.measurement: Condition historical Q3 and Q4 team points on halftime margin bins (<=-10, -9..-4, -3..+3, +4..+9, >=+10) and on the point-in-time model expected full-game margin from nfl.model_team_points_mean (bins |m|<3, 3-7, >7); kernel-weight by halftime margin (bandwidth 3 points) and shrink to team second-half scoring with k=15 games; pregame mixture weights over halftime states from the first-half projection of nfl.model_margin_lattice; 2009+ pbp; as-of start of week. Spreads and totals excluded, used only as benchmarks.

nfl.quarter_total_order_statistics.label: Joint four-quarter total distribution: argmax quarter (with dead-heat share) and P(minimum quarter = 0)
nfl.quarter_total_order_statistics.mechanism: Simulated joint distribution of the four regulation quarter totals from drive allocation and period-specific per-drive scoring, summarised as P(quarter q is the unique or shared maximum, weighted 1/N) and P(any quarter total = 0).
nfl.quarter_total_order_statistics.rationale: Highest-scoring-quarter and scoreless-quarter contracts depend on order statistics of four dependent, lumpy totals; marginal quarter totals cannot price them because ties at the top and zero atoms dominate, and Q2/Q4 two-minute effects make the quarters non-exchangeable.
nfl.quarter_total_order_statistics.measurement: Run >=20,000 drive-level simulations per game using period drive counts (nfl.drive_clock_allocation), period per-drive TD/FG/safety rates (nfl.period_drive_scoring_rates) and the halftime-state mixture for Q3/Q4; for each draw compute T_q (combined points, regulation only, OT excluded), payout_q = 1{T_q = max}/#{argmax}, and 1{min_q T_q = 0}; average. Calibrate against 2012-2025 empirical frequencies by expected-total decile (isotonic on P(min=0) and on Q2/Q4 argmax shares). As-of: inputs frozen at the Friday injury report plus kickoff weather forecast.

nfl.pro_bowl_flag_roster_strength.label: Pro Bowl flag-football conference roster strength (actual participants)
nfl.pro_bowl_flag_roster_strength.mechanism: Conference win probability in the Pro Bowl flag game as a function of the quarterbacks and skill players who actually participate after opt-outs and replacements.
nfl.pro_bowl_flag_roster_strength.rationale: The exhibition removes line play and contact, so passing accuracy and open-field speed of the participants decide most scoring; the official roster changes repeatedly after selection (injuries, Super Bowl teams), so only the final participant list is informative and the format history is tiny.
nfl.pro_bowl_flag_roster_strength.measurement: For each conference, take the final participant list at game time; compute QB score = mean regular-season completion percentage over expected and EPA/dropback of participating QBs (weighted by expected snaps, equal split if unknown) and skill score = mean of participating WR/TE/RB yards per route run, standardised across all participants; logit P(NFC) = b*(QB_diff + 0.5*skill_diff) with b shrunk toward 0 (prior sd 0.3) because only a handful of flag-format games exist; as-of the final roster announcement.

nfl.player_trade_hazard.label: Named-player trade hazard before a date
nfl.player_trade_hazard.mechanism: Probability that a named player is traded (officially processed) within a window, from team contention status, contract structure and reported availability.
nfl.player_trade_hazard.rationale: Trades cluster before the trade deadline and in the offseason; most players have near-zero hazard, so team context and contract terms (dead cap, years of control) separate candidates, and reports of shopping are the strongest signal.
nfl.player_trade_hazard.measurement: Discrete-time weekly logistic hazard trained on 2010-2025 player-weeks: covariates = team win% minus preseason model expectation, weeks to trade deadline (indicator of final 2 weeks), dead cap if traded / cap hit, years of control remaining, age, positional value tier, credible-report flag (from nfl.insider_report_conversion); P(trade before date) = 1 - prod(1 - h_w) over weeks to the date; base-rate shrinkage toward position-season frequency with k=500 player-seasons; as-of each week.

nfl.player_destination_choice.label: Next-team categorical choice for a named player (incl. current team and retire/no team)
nfl.player_destination_choice.mechanism: Distribution over the player's team on a date: remain with current team, each other team, or retire/unsigned, from contract status, team cap space and positional need.
nfl.player_destination_choice.rationale: Next-team markets list every candidate team plus the current team and a residual; the current team often carries most mass (contract, tag, extension), and other teams are ranked by cap space, need and reported interest, not by quality alone.
nfl.player_destination_choice.measurement: Stage 1: P(move) = logistic on 2012-2025 veteran offseasons (contract expired or released) with features years remaining, franchise-tag eligibility flag, age, prior-season snap share, retirement-eligible age; ridge lambda by CV. Stage 2: conditional multinomial logit over 31 other teams with features (i) team cap space on the as-of date from a dated OTC snapshot, (ii) starter gap = team's best current starter's EPA-or-grade percentile at the player's position minus the player's, floored at 0, (iii) draft capital spent at the position in the last 2 drafts, (iv) 1[head coach or coordinator previously coached player], (v) 1[prior-team-of-record tie]; drop the subjective 'reported interest' flag unless captured with timestamp (own_capture). P(retire/no team) from age-position base rate. Shrink utilities with Dirichlet alpha=1. As-of timestamped snapshot before the decision window.
raw_data: team cap space by date (vintage snapshots)
depth charts / starter value by position

nfl.contract_value_comps.label: Positional contract value comps scaled by cap growth
nfl.contract_value_comps.mechanism: Expected new-contract value (APY and total) for a player from recent comparable contracts at the position, scaled to the projected salary cap.
nfl.contract_value_comps.rationale: Next-contract-size markets depend on how the market for the position has moved; the most recent top contract at the position resets the scale and cap growth shifts all values, while age and injury discount it.
nfl.contract_value_comps.measurement: For position p, take contracts signed in the last 24 months, express APY as % of the cap in the signing year; fit a quantile regression of APY%cap on player value (prior 2-season EPA or PFF-free equivalent production metrics), age and contract-year status; predicted APY = quantiles x projected cap of the signing year; report the distribution of total value = APY x expected years; as-of market time.
raw_data: contracts: player, position, sign date, years, total, APY, guarantees

nfl.coach_exit_competing_order.label: Competing-risk probability that a named coach is the next head coach out
nfl.coach_exit_competing_order.mechanism: Probability that coach i's departure occurs before every other permanent head coach's, from all 32 coaches' time-varying exit hazards.
nfl.coach_exit_competing_order.rationale: Next-coach-out pays on order, not occurrence: a coach's chance of being first depends on how hot the other seats are and on when each hazard spikes (in-season vs Black Monday), so per-coach probabilities from nfl.coach_exit_hazard must be combined in a competing-risk calculation.
nfl.coach_exit_competing_order.measurement: Using weekly hazards h_j(t) from nfl.coach_exit_hazard for all 32 coaches from issuance to Feb 15, 2027, compute P(i first) = sum_t h_i(t) prod_j S_j(t-1) prod_{j!=i}(1-h_j(t)) with simultaneous Black Monday exits split by announcement timestamp order (empirical tie-break by time of announcement); residual 'none before deadline' = prod_j S_j(T); recompute weekly as standings update.
raw_data: weekly coach hazards for all 32 teams

nfl.coach_candidate_hire_model.label: Named-candidate coaching hire probability
nfl.coach_candidate_hire_model.mechanism: Probability that a named candidate is hired as a coach before a date, from the number of expected vacancies, the candidate's profile and interest, and ties to decision-makers with openings.
nfl.coach_candidate_hire_model.rationale: Hire markets depend first on how many jobs open (from exit hazards) and then on candidate share; former head coaches returning, coordinators and media figures have very different conversion rates, and reported interviews are the strongest signal.
nfl.coach_candidate_hire_model.measurement: Expected vacancies V = sum of exit probabilities from nfl.coach_exit_hazard before the date (plus coordinator openings if the contract counts them); candidate share from a conditional logit over 2005-2025 hiring cycles with features: prior head-coach experience and record, years out of coaching, current role, age, number of reported interviews, prior ties to the hiring GM/owner; P(hire) = 1 - exp(-V x share); as-of market time.

nfl.weather_delay_hazard.label: Game weather-delay hazard (lightning and severe weather)
nfl.weather_delay_hazard.mechanism: Probability of any official weather delay (pre-start or in-game) for a scheduled game, from roof type, location climatology, month, kickoff hour and the thunderstorm forecast.
nfl.weather_delay_hazard.rationale: Weather delays are almost always lightning within the stadium's radius at open-air venues in early-season afternoon or evening games; fixed domes are near zero and retractable roofs depend on roof policy, so a generic weather input does not capture the event.
nfl.weather_delay_hazard.measurement: Logistic model on 2010-2025 games (outcome: any weather delay from game books/news): features = roof (open/retractable/dome), month, kickoff local hour, regional climatological thunderstorm-day frequency for the month (NOAA), and at forecast time the NWS thunderstorm probability for the kickoff window +/- 3 hours; shrink venue effects toward roof-type means with k=40 games; as-of the 24h and 3h forecast vintages.

nfl.weekly_qb_depth_slot_model.label: Weekly QB depth-chart slot probabilities (QB1, QB2) per team
nfl.weekly_qb_depth_slot_model.mechanism: Probability that each of a team's quarterbacks is listed QB1 or QB2 on the week's official depth chart, propagating QB1 changes down the chart.
nfl.weekly_qb_depth_slot_model.rationale: Starter and backup designation markets are coupled: a QB1 change promotes the QB2 and opens the QB2 slot, and teams differ in chart policy (co-starters, injured players kept listed), so a slot-level model is needed rather than a starter hazard alone.
nfl.weekly_qb_depth_slot_model.measurement: For each team-week, start from the previous chart order; apply P(QB1 changes) from nfl.qb_change_hazard and injury status; conditional on a change, assign the new QB1 by challenger rank (nfl.qb_challenger_prior); QB2 = highest-ranked remaining QB with rank score from draft capital, preseason snaps with the first and second team, contract APY and coach statements (logit fit on 2016-2025 chart snapshots); injured-but-listed retained per team policy (team fixed effect for keeping injured QBs listed, shrunk k=20 weeks); as-of the latest published chart before close.

QB draft slot and contract APY

nfl.season_participation_streak_hazard.label: Weekly miss hazard compounded over a season (every-week participation)
nfl.season_participation_streak_hazard.mechanism: Probability that a player takes a snap in every team game of a season, from a weekly hazard of missing a game through injury, rest or benching.
nfl.season_participation_streak_hazard.rationale: Every-week participation is a long product of weekly survivals; a weekly miss rate that looks small compounds to large season-level failure probability, and missed games cluster after injuries, so independence understates the streak's survival among durable players and overstates it for injury-prone ones.
nfl.season_participation_streak_hazard.measurement: Discrete-time logistic hazard of missing week w given active-roster membership, trained on 2012-2025 player-weeks: covariates = position, age, prior-season games missed, current injury designation, snaps per game (exposure), week >= 17 x team clinched flag; include a frailty term (player random effect, shrinkage from 3 prior seasons); P(streak) = prod_w (1 - h_w) over remaining scheduled games via simulation that carries injury state forward; as-of market time.

nfl.qb_completion_count_model.label: QB completion-count model: expected completion probability by attempt mix with accuracy over expected (market-free)
nfl.qb_completion_count_model.mechanism: Converts a forecast attempt distribution into a completions distribution using per-attempt expected completion probability (target depth, pressure, receiver separation) plus the QB's shrunk completion-over-expected.
nfl.qb_completion_count_model.rationale: Completion rungs settle on a thinned count; raw completion percentage confounds the QB's accuracy with his offence's target-depth mix and the opponent's coverage, and is noisy over a few games. Separating expected completion probability (scheme and matchup) from completion over expected (QB skill, heavily regressed) is what moves a 25+ completions rung when attempts are fixed.
nfl.qb_completion_count_model.measurement: Per QB-offence: xComp per attempt = mean nflfastR cp (completion probability) over the last 16 games with half-life 8 games; completion over expected = mean cpoe shrunk toward 0 with k=300 attempts; opponent factor = opponent's allowed (complete_pass - cp) over the last 12 games, shrunk with k=250 attempts; p = xComp + cpoe_shrunk + opp_factor (all on the probability scale, clipped to [0.35, 0.85]) with a wind >15 mph adjustment of -2 percentage points. Completions | attempts ~ beta-binomial(attempts, p, rho), rho estimated from 2018-2025 QB-games (about 0.01-0.02). Mixed over the nfl.qb_attempt_forecast distribution. As-of: end of the previous game.

nfl.game_receiving_leader_field_sim.label: Game receiving-yards leader: joint simulation of every pass catcher in one game
nfl.game_receiving_leader_field_sim.mechanism: Simulates receiving yards for all pass catchers of both teams from one shared game state so the maximum, its ties and a named player's chance of being the maximum are read jointly.
nfl.game_receiving_leader_field_sim.rationale: KXNFLMOSTRECYDS pays only if the named player beats every other catcher in the game, including the opponent's top receiver, and gives No to a non-participant. Teammates share one target pool (negative dependence) while both offences rise together in a shootout (positive dependence), so a product of marginals misprices the favourite and the long shot.
nfl.game_receiving_leader_field_sim.measurement: Per game: list every WR, TE and RB with snap share >=10 percent over the last 4 games (as-of the inactive list). Draw a shared game state (plays and pass rate per team from nfl.own_rating_game_state_prior-style own ratings, no market lines), split each team's targets by Dirichlet shares centred on target share over the last 8 games (half-life 4, shrink to role prior with k=40 targets), then yards per target from nfl.player_reception_length_distribution. 20,000 simulations; P(max) with 1/N tie credit; inactive players fixed at No. Units: probability; as-of kickoff minus 90 minutes.

nfl.game_rushing_leader_field_sim.label: Game rushing-yards leader: joint carry and yardage simulation for all ball carriers
nfl.game_rushing_leader_field_sim.mechanism: Draws one game script per simulation and allocates both teams' carries among backs and quarterbacks, so the game's rushing maximum and each named runner's chance of holding it are computed jointly.
nfl.game_rushing_leader_field_sim.rationale: KXNFLMOSTRSHYDS is lost if the opposing lead back or a scrambling QB out-rushes the named player. Carries are zero-sum within a backfield and the winning side's script adds late carries to its lead back, so the leader is concentrated on the projected winner's workhorse; independent marginals overstate committee backs and understate the favourite's lead back.
nfl.game_rushing_leader_field_sim.measurement: Per game: rushers with carry share >=8 percent over the last 4 games plus both starting QBs. Each simulation draws a final margin from own ratings (no spread), sets team rush attempts by the score-state run-rate surface (nfl.script response with own margin), splits carries by Dirichlet shares (last 6 games, half-life 3, shrink to depth-chart role with k=30 carries) and draws per-carry yards from nfl.rush_yardage_tail. 20,000 simulations; P(max) with 1/N tie credit; inactive named player fixed at No. As-of the inactive list.

nfl.hof_finalist_progression_history.label: Hall of Fame candidate progression: years as semifinalist and finalist, category and class cap
nfl.hof_finalist_progression_history.mechanism: Hall of Fame induction is a committee vote in which candidates usually advance from semifinalist to finalist over several years and the modern-era class is capped, so the candidate's place in that queue predicts selection.
nfl.hof_finalist_progression_history.rationale: Career statistics are fixed long before the vote; what changes year to year is the candidate's standing with the selectors (consecutive finalist years, first-ballot status of competing candidates at the same position) and the class cap, so a resume-only model misses the queue that decides KXNFLHALLOFFAME.
nfl.hof_finalist_progression_history.measurement: For each candidate and year 2000-2026: category (modern-era, seniors, coach/contributor), years eligible, count of prior semifinalist and finalist years, whether a first-year-eligible candidate at the same position is on the finalist list, and the modern-era class size. Logistic model of induction among finalists with candidate random effect, shrinkage to the category base rate with k=10 finalist-years; output P(inductee) as-of the finalist announcement and again after the class announcement date is known.

nfl.executive_move_attribution.label: Executive of the Year attribution: win surprise explained by front-office moves
nfl.executive_move_attribution.mechanism: Scores each team's general manager by the team's wins above its own pre-season expectation, weighted by the share of that surprise attributable to new acquisitions, the draft class and a new head coach.
nfl.executive_move_attribution.rationale: The PFWA executive vote rewards a visible turnaround that writers credit to roster building; a team that over-performs on luck or an incumbent star does not earn the same credit, so win surprise alone over-predicts and the attribution share is the subtle part.
nfl.executive_move_attribution.measurement: For each team-season: win surprise = actual wins minus own pre-season expected wins (from nfl.coach_surprise_vs_own_prior's prior); acquisition share = snap-weighted approximate value (PFR AV) of players new to the roster this season (trades, free agents, rookies) divided by total team AV; new-coach flag. Score = win surprise x (0.5 + acquisition share) + 1.0 x new-coach flag; softmax over teams with temperature fitted to PFWA winners 2000-2025, candidate shrinkage k=5 seasons. As-of each week; final as-of end of regular season.

nfl.wpmoty_nominee_profile.label: Walter Payton Man of the Year nominee profile: community record, prior nominations and visibility
nfl.wpmoty_nominee_profile.mechanism: Ranks the 32 team nominees by indicators the selection panel uses: scale and tenure of the nominee's charitable work, prior nominations, veteran status and media visibility of the cause.
nfl.wpmoty_nominee_profile.rationale: The award ignores on-field statistics beyond standing; repeat nominees, long-running foundations and veterans near retirement win disproportionately. There is no structured data on charitable work, so the input is a hand-coded profile with a strong prior on repeat nominees.
nfl.wpmoty_nominee_profile.measurement: For each nominee-year 2010-2025: number of prior nominations, years in the league, Pro Bowl count (standing proxy), foundation existence and age in years, count of national news articles on the charity in the 12 months before announcement (manual or news-API count). Multinomial logit over the year's 32 nominees fitted to past winners with ridge penalty; shrink coefficients toward equal probability with k=8 award-years. As-of nominee announcement (December).

nfl.ol_individual_protection_record.label: Offensive-lineman protection record: pressures and sacks allowed per pass-block snap
nfl.ol_individual_protection_record.mechanism: Measures an offensive lineman's pass protection (pressures and sacks allowed per pass-block snap, penalties), games started and team context, the evidence a Protector of the Year vote would reward.
nfl.ol_individual_protection_record.rationale: Linemen have no counting statistics in box scores, so voters lean on charting grades, reputation (prior All-Pro/Pro Bowl) and team sack rate; the individual pressure-allowed rate is paid charting data and team sack rate confounds the quarterback's habits, which is the subtle part.
nfl.ol_individual_protection_record.measurement: Per lineman-season to date: pressures allowed and sacks allowed per 100 pass-block snaps (PFF or SIS charting), penalties per 100 snaps, starts, and team sack rate adjusted for QB time to throw; shrink each rate toward position mean with k=300 pass-block snaps; composite z-score plus prior-honour indicator (All-Pro or Pro Bowl in last 2 seasons). As-of each week; final as-of end of regular season.

nfl.career_record_chase_survival.label: Career record chase: seasons remaining, age decline and retirement hazard
nfl.career_record_chase_survival.mechanism: A career rung set one unit above the all-time record is reached only if the player keeps playing enough seasons at a sufficient rate, so the forecast is a survival-weighted sum over future seasons.
nfl.career_record_chase_survival.rationale: Career contracts in this archetype (passing, receiving, rushing) need the gap to the record, the per-season output path by age and the probability the player retires, is released or is injured out first; a single-season model gives zero information about year three, and the retirement announcement ends the contract.
nfl.career_record_chase_survival.measurement: Gap = rung minus career regular-season total as of the last game. Per future season s: P(active in s) from a discrete-time retirement and release hazard by position and age fitted on 1990-2025 players with at least 5 seasons (logit on age, prior-season games and output percentile, k=20 player-seasons shrinkage); output in s = current rate x position aging curve (estimated from 2000-2025 same-position players, ratio by age) x expected games (nfl.games_played_dist). Simulate 20,000 career paths; P(cumulative >= gap before retirement and before the contract expiry). As-of the latest game.

nfl.individual_defender_sack_int_accrual.label: Individual defender sack and interception accrual (season totals and leaders)
nfl.individual_defender_sack_int_accrual.mechanism: A defender's season sacks or interceptions are his snaps times pass-rush or coverage opportunity times a low conversion rate that regresses strongly, accumulated over the remaining games.
nfl.individual_defender_sack_int_accrual.rationale: KXNFLSZNRECORD (rookie sack record 14.5, must be broken) and KXNFLLEADERPINT (interceptions leader) depend on individual defensive counts that none of the offence inputs describe; sacks are a noisy fraction of pressures and interceptions an even noisier fraction of targets, so pressure and target rates predict the rest of season better than banked counts.
nfl.individual_defender_sack_int_accrual.measurement: Per defender: pass-rush snaps per game (last 6 games, half-life 3) x pressure rate per rush snap (season to date shrunk to position prior with k=150 rush snaps) x sack-per-pressure (shrunk hard to the league rate of about 0.15 with k=60 pressures); interceptions = targets in coverage per game x INT per target (shrunk to about 0.03 with k=150 targets). Remaining-season totals simulated over games played (nfl.games_played_dist), banked counts added; for records require strictly greater than the record; for leaders take the max over all defenders. As-of the latest game.

nfl.team_season_stat_accrual.label: Team season-statistic accrual for non-points team totals (net passing, rushing yards) and late-season rest scaling
nfl.team_season_stat_accrual.mechanism: Projects a team's final regular-season net passing or rushing yards as banked total plus a simulated sum over its remaining games, and applies Weeks 17-18 starter-rest scaling to every team-season total; season points for/against are taken from nfl.team_points_for_against_rates, not recomputed.
nfl.team_season_stat_accrual.rationale: Team extremes and team specials settle on season totals, so a per-game rating is not enough: byes, the remaining opponents' defences or offences, late-season starter rest and the sack deduction in net passing yards change the remaining sum. The extreme over teams then needs every team's total jointly simulated with shared rating uncertainty.
nfl.team_season_stat_accrual.measurement: Points for/against: use the season-total simulation of nfl.team_points_for_against_rates unchanged (its banked-plus-remaining draws and 1/N extreme rule), only multiplying Weeks 17-18 expected scores by the starter-rest factor from nfl.clinched_rest_starter_probability. Net passing yards per remaining game g = expected team dropbacks (nfl.pace x nfl.proe) x [(1 - sack rate) x gross yards per attempt - sack rate x mean sack yards (about 6.5)], with sack rate = team sack rate allowed x opponent pressure factor, gross yards per attempt opponent-adjusted over the last 17 games (half-life 8 games, shrink to league mean with k=6 games); rushing yards analogously from rush attempts x opponent-adjusted yards per carry. Per-game sd from 2012-2025 residuals (about 70 net passing yards); team strength errors are the same per-simulation draw used by the points model (nfl.rating_uncertainty_shared_error), not an extra one. Sum over remaining games plus banked total; 20,000 simulations. As-of the latest completed game.

nfl.multi_season_playoff_drought_hazard.label: Multi-season playoff-appearance hazard (season of next playoff appearance)
nfl.multi_season_playoff_drought_hazard.mechanism: The season in which a team next makes the playoffs is a first-passage time of a mean-reverting team-strength process over several seasons, with jumps from quarterback and coaching changes.
nfl.multi_season_playoff_drought_hazard.rationale: KXNFLENDSTREAK pays on the specific future season of the next playoff appearance; this year's standings simulation answers only the current season, while later seasons depend on how fast NFL ratings revert (roughly one third per year), draft capital from bad seasons and the chance of a new starting quarterback, which a one-season model cannot give.
nfl.multi_season_playoff_drought_hazard.measurement: Year-end own rating (nfl.own_team_rating_market_free) evolves as r_{t+1} = 0.67 r_t + e, e ~ N(0, sd fitted on 2002-2025 year-to-year changes, about 4.5 points), with an added jump term when the starting QB changes (probability from contract year, age and draft capital; size from nfl.qb_scenario_rating_drop). P(playoffs | rating) per season from the standings simulation calibrated on 14-team formats (2020+). Simulate 20,000 paths of 6 seasons; P(first appearance in season s); apply the franchise-continuity clause as a negligible hazard. As-of the latest game.

nfl.game_fantasy_max_field_sim.label: Single-game fantasy maximum: joint simulation of both rosters under ESPN PPR scoring
nfl.game_fantasy_max_field_sim.mechanism: Simulates every relevant player's ESPN-PPR fantasy score in one game jointly (shared drives, touchdown attribution between passer and receiver, script) and reads the probability each player has the maximum.
nfl.game_fantasy_max_field_sim.rationale: A game-most contract is not a per-player threshold: it depends on the whole field of both teams and on the strong positive correlation between a quarterback and his receivers, which makes stacking players on one offence crowd the top. ESPN scoring weights differ from Sleeper's in places, so the per-player model must be re-scored on ESPN settings before the maximum is taken.
nfl.game_fantasy_max_field_sim.measurement: For each game: draw team drives and touchdowns from the team scoring model, attribute each touchdown to passer/receiver or rusher by player share (targets, carries, red-zone share over last 8 games, half-life 4), draw yards and receptions conditional on attributed plays from player component models (nfl.fantasy_component_and_stack_covariance), score each player with ESPN default PPR weights (1 per reception, 0.1 per rushing/receiving yard, 0.04 per passing yard, 4 per passing TD, 6 per rush/receiving TD, -2 per interception and lost fumble under ESPN defaults, to be verified); 20,000 simulations; P(max) per player with 1/N for exact ties. As-of kickoff with final inactives.
raw_data: player shares: targets, carries, red-zone opportunities

nfl.score_path_sequence_sim.label: Drive-sequence score-path simulation: largest lead, lead changes and comeback events
nfl.score_path_sequence_sim.mechanism: Simulates the alternating drive sequence of both teams with per-drive outcomes and point values, recording the full in-game margin path so path functionals (maximum lead, lead changes, minimum margin of the eventual winner) can be read.
nfl.score_path_sequence_sim.rationale: Final-score models cannot price path contracts: two games with the same final margin can have zero or eight lead changes. The path depends on drive-outcome probabilities by team, on the alternation of possessions, on state-dependent play calling (trailing teams pass and go for it, leaders run clock) and on point values (7, 3, 8, 6, 2), so a simulation that conditions each drive on the current score state is required.
nfl.score_path_sequence_sim.measurement: For each game: possessions alternate starting from the coin-toss winner; drive outcome multinomial (TD, FG, turnover, punt, safety, end of half) from team offence vs opposing defence rates (nfl.drive_outcome_by_index style, opponent-adjusted, last 16 games with half-life 8, shrink k=150 drives) modified by score state (lead or trail by 0-8, 9-16, 17+) and time remaining using 2012-2025 state multipliers; points per TD from nfl.scoring_event_point_values; 20,000 simulated games; outputs per game: distribution of max |margin|, number of lead changes (excluding first score), P(eventual winner trailed by >=24), calibrated against 2012-2025 realised frequencies by own-rating expected-margin and expected-total bucket (nfl.own_rating_game_state_prior; no sportsbook spread or total). As-of kickoff.

nfl.trick_play_and_goal_line_pass_events.label: Rare play-call events: non-QB pass attempts and pass attempts from the 1-yard line
nfl.trick_play_and_goal_line_pass_events.mechanism: Per-team rates of non-quarterback pass attempts (trick plays, fake punts) and of pass calls on snaps from on or inside the opponent's 1, combined with the expected number of snaps from the 1.
nfl.trick_play_and_goal_line_pass_events.rationale: Both contracts are low-rate Bernoulli events whose base rate differs strongly by coach and personnel (for example a former-quarterback receiver, or a team that favours quarterback sneaks at the 1; both are hypotheses to test, not measured facts); league averages mislead, but team samples are tiny, so heavy shrinkage toward the league rate is essential and stakes may raise trick-play frequency.
nfl.trick_play_and_goal_line_pass_events.measurement: Non-QB pass: count of pass attempts by players whose roster position is not QB per team-game over the last 3 seasons, shrunk to league rate (about 0.15 per game, to recompute) with k=40 team-games, coach random effect; P(any in game) = 1 - exp(-(rate_A + rate_B)). Pass from the 1: expected snaps with yardline_100 <= 1 per team-game (from drives reaching the 1, last 2 seasons, shrink k=30) x team pass share on those snaps (shrink to league about 0.35 with k=25 snaps) counting official forward pass attempts only; sacks, scrambles and runs must be excluded explicitly (whether the nflverse pass_attempt flag already excludes sacks, how no_play rows are treated and how spikes are flagged are UNVERIFIED); P(at least one) by Poisson. As-of kickoff with the active roster.
raw_data: pbp: game_id, posteam, passer_player_id, pass_attempt, sack, qb_scramble, yardline_100, down

nfl.own_one_yard_line_snap_rate.label: Own-one-yard-line snap rate (offence backed up at its own 1)
nfl.own_one_yard_line_snap_rate.mechanism: An offensive scrimmage gain can be at most 99 yards and only from a snap at the offence's own 1-yard line, so the count of such snaps is the exposure for the offensive route to a 99+ yard play.
nfl.own_one_yard_line_snap_rate.rationale: Snaps from the 1 are produced by punts downed or fumbled at the 1, goal-line stands that end in a turnover on downs, and penalties walking the ball back; they are rare, clustered in a few team-games and not stable team traits. The contract is therefore a Poisson-thinning problem whose rate is this count, not any player's long-run yardage.
nfl.own_one_yard_line_snap_rate.measurement: Per team-game, count snaps with yardline_100 = 99 (offence at own 1) from nflverse play-by-play, excluding kneels. Fit a negative-binomial rate on opponent-adjusted punting (inside-10 rate, net punt), defence goal-line stand rate and team penalty profile with 3-season pooling and shrinkage toward the league mean (about 30 team-games of prior weight). Output expected count for each remaining game; as-of = last completed game before the forecast.

nfl.backed_up_breakaway_conversion.label: Backed-up breakaway conversion (P(99-yard TD | snap from own 1))
nfl.backed_up_breakaway_conversion.mechanism: Conditional probability that a snap taken from the own 1 becomes a full-field touchdown, produced by deep-pass completions behind a single-high or man-coverage defence or by an untouched run.
nfl.backed_up_breakaway_conversion.rationale: The defence is in a compressed field and often in short-yardage or goal-line personnel, which makes a defender-free deep route more plausible on play action, but any penalty (holding, intentional grounding in the end zone) or safety is far likelier than the breakaway. The league sample of true 99-yard plays is a handful in 60 seasons, so the rate must be extrapolated, not counted.
nfl.backed_up_breakaway_conversion.measurement: Estimate with a hierarchical logistic tail model on all snaps from yardline_100 >= 90 with outcome yards_gained >= 60, then extrapolate to >= 99 with a generalized Pareto tail anchored on the historical 99-yard plays and 80+ yard gains from deep starts; covariates: pass-rush pressure rate, QB deep-ball rate, defence two-high rate, offence tempo; 5-season window, half-life 2 seasons for scheme, shrinkage constant 25 deep-start snaps to the league mean.
free_sources: nflverse participation and FTN charting (free, limited seasons)

nfl.kicker_ceiling_range_tail.label: Kicker ceiling range tail (make probability at 66-75 yards)
nfl.kicker_ceiling_range_tail.mechanism: Per-kicker make probability beyond the demonstrated range, driven by leg speed, ball strike and launch angle, which pooled accuracy-by-distance tables cannot resolve.
nfl.kicker_ceiling_range_tail.rationale: Existing long-kick models cover 50+ and 60+ yard attempts; a 70+ make lies beyond the regular-season record (68 yards, 2025, end of first half, indoors; previous record 66). Kickoff depth was a clean leg proxy only before the 2024 dynamic kickoff; since then (touchback to the 35 in 2025) depth is a strategic choice, so it is used only within one rule era and down-weighted, with preseason long makes as direct ceiling evidence.
nfl.kicker_ceiling_range_tail.measurement: Per kicker, fit a logistic make curve over distance on all regular-season attempts from 45 yards (era fixed effect from nfl.kicking_ball_and_fg_rule_era), with a kicker range term from career max make, 60+ attempt history and preseason makes of 60+ yards (nfl.preseason_long_kick_evidence, down-weighted 0.5 per attempt); pre-2024 kickoff distance enters only as a prior for kickers with that history. Shrink toward the position pool with 40 attempts of prior weight; adjust for roof, altitude and wind. Output P(make | attempt at 66, 68, 70, 72 yards, neutral and favourable conditions); as-of = last game before forecast.

nfl.long_fg_end_of_half_attempt_hazard.label: Long field-goal attempt hazard at end of half and game
nfl.long_fg_end_of_half_attempt_hazard.mechanism: Number of snaps per season where the clock and score make a 65+ yard attempt the best option over a Hail Mary or punt, set by coach choice, timeouts and the kicker's stated range.
nfl.long_fg_end_of_half_attempt_hazard.rationale: A 70+ attempt almost never occurs in normal play because a punt wins field position; it occurs with 0-5 seconds left in a half or game when only a kick keeps points alive. Whether a coach sends the kicker for 68 or throws a Hail Mary is a policy that varies by coach and by whether the kicker has shown the range.
nfl.long_fg_end_of_half_attempt_hazard.measurement: From play-by-play, count snaps with kick_distance >= 60 or qualifying situations (game_seconds_remaining in half <= 6, offence between own 40 and opponent 50, trailing by <= 3 or tied at the half) and estimate P(attempt | situation) by head coach with a hierarchical logit (coach, kicker max make, wind, roof, timeouts, rule era, low-leverage first-half flag for record-chasing). 4-season window; shrink coach rates toward the league with 15 qualifying situations of prior weight. Output expected 65+, 68+, 70+ yard attempts for the remaining schedule.
free_sources: nflverse play_by_play (qtr, game_seconds_remaining, timeout counts, kick_distance)
NFL gamebook text for coach statements (free, scrape)
raw_data: pbp: game_seconds_remaining, half_seconds_remaining, posteam_timeouts_remaining, score_differential, kick_distance, play_type

nfl.play_length_evt_tail_fit.label: Extreme-value tail fit for play length (long plays and long kicks)
nfl.play_length_evt_tail_fit.mechanism: Generalized Pareto or Gumbel-type fit to the upper tail of scrimmage-play and kick lengths, giving return levels for the league-wide season maximum.
nfl.play_length_evt_tail_fit.rationale: The contract is a threshold on a maximum, so only the extreme tail matters. A bulk model (mean yards per play) is nearly irrelevant, and the cap of 99 yards plus the finite number of own-goal-line snaps means a bounded-tail fit with exposure weighting is required. Few historical points mean parameter uncertainty must be carried into the probability.
nfl.play_length_evt_tail_fit.measurement: Using all regular-season plays since 1999, fit a peaks-over-threshold model (threshold 60 yards for plays, 56 yards for kick distance) with Poisson exceedance rate per 1,000 snaps by start-yardline bucket and an era term (pre-2024, 2024, 2025+ kicking rules) on the kick tail; fit offensive gains and turnover-return lengths separately so either contract reading can be priced; propagate parameter uncertainty by posterior or bootstrap; output P(max >= 99) and P(max kick >= 70) for N remaining games with the running maximum to date as the as-of state.
free_sources: Pro-Football-Reference longest-play and longest-FG record lists (free, scrape)

nfl.td_play_length_by_source.label: Touchdown play length by source (scrimmage, interception, fumble, kick and punt return, missed-FG return)
nfl.td_play_length_by_source.mechanism: Distribution of touchdown lengths split by scoring route, because returns can exceed 99 yards and short touchdowns come from goal-line runs and sneaks.
nfl.td_play_length_by_source.rationale: The single-game TD-length buckets read official play-by-play distances and do not exclude returns, so the route mix matters: return TDs reach 100-109 yards, while fumbles recovered in the end zone give 0-yard TDs that can set the minimum. Season-wide the minimum is almost always 0-1 yards, but per game it depends on how many TDs are scored and how.
nfl.td_play_length_by_source.measurement: From 1999-2026 regular-season plays with a touchdown, assign route: scrimmage (pass or rush; length = yards_gained), interception return, fumble return, kickoff return, punt return, missed/blocked FG return (length = return_yards, kick returns measured from the receiving spot as yardline of catch to goal). Tabulate counts per season and route, per-season maximum and minimum, and rate per 1,000 snaps of that route type (kicks per team kick). Fit per route a generalized Pareto above its 80th percentile length (peaks-over-threshold as in nfl.play_length_evt_tail_fit). Output both aggregates with and without return TDs so either contract reading can be priced.

nfl.scrimmage_turnover_return_long_tail.label: Long turnover-return tail on scrimmage downs (99+ yard INT, fumble, blocked/missed-FG returns)
nfl.scrimmage_turnover_return_long_tail.mechanism: Interceptions and fumbles in the defence's own red zone, and missed or blocked field goals fielded in the end zone, can be returned 99-109 yards on a play that began as a scrimmage down.
nfl.scrimmage_turnover_return_long_tail.rationale: If Kalshi counts these as plays from scrimmage, they are a more frequent route to 99+ yards than offensive gains from the own 1 and the own-1 exposure is no longer a bound. Exposure is opponent red-zone and goal-line pass attempts and long FG attempts, not own-1 snaps.
nfl.scrimmage_turnover_return_long_tail.measurement: Per team-game, rate of returns >= 99 yards on interceptions, fumbles and missed/blocked FGs from nflverse pbp (return_yards, play_type, interception, fumble_lost, field_goal_result) since 1999; exposure = opponent snaps with yardline_100 <= 10 plus FG attempts of 50+ yards; hierarchical Poisson with team takeaway rate shrunk to league (40 team-games prior); output expected count for remaining games.

nfl.kicking_ball_and_fg_rule_era.label: Kicking-ball and field-goal rule era (K-ball preparation, fair-catch kick, kickoff regime)
nfl.kicking_ball_and_fg_rule_era.mechanism: Rule changes may alter ball flight and attempt opportunities: a 2025 rule letting kickers prepare kicking balls is reported (secondary news only; primary rulebook not fetched; UNVERIFIED) to have been followed by a jump in 60+ yard makes, and the fair-catch free kick is described as allowing an unrushed attempt scored as a field goal (UNVERIFIED).
nfl.kicking_ball_and_fg_rule_era.rationale: A tail fit pooled over 1999-2024 understates the current 70+ rate unless an era term is added; the post-2025 sample is small, so the era effect must be estimated with a prior and carried as uncertainty.
nfl.kicking_ball_and_fg_rule_era.measurement: Era indicator per season (pre-2024, 2024 dynamic kickoff, 2025+ K-ball preparation and touchback-to-35); estimate era-specific 60+ attempt rate per team-game and make rate by distance from pbp with a hierarchical prior centred on the previous era (half the era difference as prior sd); flag fair-catch free kicks separately from scrimmage FGs; as-of = league rulebook for the season.
free_sources: NFL rulebook and competition committee announcements (free)

nfl.preseason_long_kick_evidence.label: Preseason and warm-up long-kick evidence (60+ yard makes outside the regular season)
nfl.preseason_long_kick_evidence.mechanism: Preseason makes and reported warm-up distances reveal a kicker's ceiling without the regular-season attempt selection that hides it.
nfl.preseason_long_kick_evidence.rationale: Only a handful of regular-season attempts exceed 65 yards, so the leg ceiling is nearly unidentified from settlement-scope data; a 70-yard preseason make (2025) is the only direct evidence a 70 is reachable. Preseason kicks are out of scope for settlement but in scope as an input.
nfl.preseason_long_kick_evidence.measurement: Per kicker, list preseason FG attempts of 55+ yards with result, venue, roof and wind from preseason play-by-play (seasons 2015+), plus beat-reported warm-up makes with date; summarise as max make and makes at 60+ and 65+; feed to the ceiling tail at half weight per attempt; as-of = last preseason game or report timestamp.
free_sources: nflverse play_by_play preseason games (season_type PRE, coverage unverified)

sources.name: nflverse pbp (preseason coverage)
sources.note: preseason games not in standard nflverse pbp

nfl.game_td_length_order_stats.label: Single-game touchdown-length order statistics (P(max >= k), P(min in band), P(no TD))
nfl.game_td_length_order_stats.mechanism: The longest and shortest TD of a game are the max and min of N TD lengths, N random per game and each length drawn from a route mixture (goal-line, red-zone pass, explosive scrimmage, return or recovery).
nfl.game_td_length_order_stats.rationale: Bucket markets need the whole distribution of the max and min, not a mean: the count N moves the two tails in opposite directions, zero TDs is a NO for all buckets, and integer yards with inclusive bounds create discreteness at 5/6 and 10/11 yards.
nfl.game_td_length_order_stats.measurement: For each team, N_TD ~ negative binomial with mean from nfl.model_team_td_mean (market-free) and dispersion fit on 2015+ games; per TD, route probabilities from goal-to-go share (nfl.redzone, nfl.goal_line_personnel) and non-offensive TD hazard (nfl.dst_td_hazard); length per route from the empirical 2015+ distribution of official TD distances shrunk to league with 30 TDs per team prior. Simulate 20,000 games; output bucket probabilities and P(N=0).

nfl.player_longest_reception_max_model.label: Player single-game longest reception model (max of K catches vs strike)
nfl.player_longest_reception_max_model.mechanism: P(longest reception > strike | plays) = 1 - E[F(strike)^K], where K is the number of receptions and F the player's per-catch length CDF in this matchup.
nfl.player_longest_reception_max_model.rationale: The contract ignores total yards: one long catch settles YES and zero catches settles NO, so volume enters through K and the upper tail of per-catch length matters more than the mean. Active-no-play settles at the fair price, so the forecastable part is conditional on a live snap.
nfl.player_longest_reception_max_model.measurement: K ~ negative binomial: targets forecast (nfl.targets) times catch probability (nfl.catch_rate_oe), dispersion fit on last 2 seasons; per-catch length = air yards (nfl.air_yards_adot, depth mixture) plus YAC, from the player's last 24 games with half-life 8 games, shrunk to position-role with 60 catches prior, adjusted by coverage matchup; compute 1 - sum_k P(K=k) F(s)^k at each strike; multiply by 1 - P(no live snap | active).
free_sources: nflverse play_by_play (receiver_player_id, complete_pass, yards_gained, air_yards, yards_after_catch)

nfl.draft_order_rules_engine.label: Draft order rules engine (season result to overall slot)
nfl.draft_order_rules_engine.mechanism: Deterministic mapping from final standings, playoff results and tiebreakers to round-one overall slots 1-32 (champion 32, Super Bowl loser 31), repeated in each round; compensatory picks and later rounds are handled by nfl.full_draft_order_compensatory_picks.
nfl.draft_order_rules_engine.rationale: Slot ownership before the draft is not a model output but a rules calculation on results that are still uncertain in November: non-playoff teams are ordered by record then strength of schedule, playoff teams by round exited, so the 32nd pick equals the Super Bowl winner. Forfeitures can shorten a round and shift overall numbering.
nfl.draft_order_rules_engine.measurement: Implement league draft-order rules: non-playoff teams ascending by win percentage, ties broken by strength of schedule then divisional and conference tiebreakers; picks 19-24 wild card losers, 25-28 divisional losers, 29-30 conference-final losers, 31 Super Bowl loser, 32 champion; apply the league's list of forfeited picks. Run on simulated seasons from the season simulation to give the slot distribution per team; as-of = latest game result and the official pick-transaction list.

nfl.draft_pick_ownership_trade_graph.label: Draft pick ownership and trade graph (who holds each slot, trade-up hazard)
nfl.draft_pick_ownership_trade_graph.mechanism: Current owner of each first-round pick, the set of future-pick bundles, and the chance a slot changes hands before or on draft night.
nfl.draft_pick_ownership_trade_graph.rationale: Contracts settle on the team that ultimately makes the pick and on pick-order outcomes, so ownership at the moment of selection is the relevant variable. Trade-ups for a quarterback, by a team that holds a later pick, are the main way that consensus order is broken, and there is a documented pre-draft window when picks are exchanged.
nfl.draft_pick_ownership_trade_graph.measurement: Maintain a table of pick-by-pick ownership for all seven rounds with transaction timestamps; estimate P(slot k traded before selection) with a logistic on slot, consensus gap between the top prospects, holder's quarterback need and asset stock, fitted on the last 15 drafts with shrinkage toward the empirical draft-wide trade rate for the same slot band (estimated, no fixed prior asserted); as-of = the latest official trade list.
free_sources: Over The Cap / Spotrac pick ownership (free_limited)

nfl.prospect_slot_dispersion_model.label: Prospect slot dispersion model (consensus rank to realized pick distribution)
nfl.prospect_slot_dispersion_model.mechanism: Empirical distribution of realized pick minus consensus rank by rank band and position, giving heavy-tailed, skewed slot distributions that vary by position premium.
nfl.prospect_slot_dispersion_model.rationale: Consensus boards give a central ranking, but markets ask for ordinal events (1st overall, top 5, before pick N, 3rd quarterback). The spread of realized slot around consensus grows with rank, is asymmetric for quarterbacks (they are taken early) and depends on how close the point-in-time board was to the draft.
nfl.prospect_slot_dispersion_model.measurement: From 2010-2026 drafts (seven rounds) join consensus rank (mean of public big boards dated 90, 30 and 1 days before the draft; exclude mock drafts and any source that cites sportsbook odds) to realized pick. Fit ordinal logistic regression of draft-pick bucket (1-32 by pick, then round buckets) plus an undrafted category on log(rank), position (QB, EDGE, OT, other) and days-to-draft, with spread parameter rising with rank; shrink thin positions toward the pooled model with weight 20 draftees. Output a slot PMF over picks 1-257 + undrafted per prospect; cross-prospect order statistics by sampling slots sequentially without replacement. As-of the board vintage date.
free_sources: NFL Mock Draft Database (free, scrape; historical vintage needs own capture)
raw_data: consensus rank by date (90, 30, 1 days pre-draft)

nfl.team_positional_need_and_qb_regime.label: Team positional need and quarterback regime (who needs what at their slot)
nfl.team_positional_need_and_qb_regime.mechanism: A per-team, per-position need score from starters' age, contract end, production and offseason moves, plus a quarterback state (franchise QB, bridge, none, draft-and-develop).
nfl.team_positional_need_and_qb_regime.rationale: Slot buyers choose among a handful of boards; need breaks ties between near-equal prospects and sets quarterback pressure: a top-3 holder without a franchise QB faces a qualitatively different incentive than a holder with a long-term deal. Free agency and trades before the draft shift need so a stale vintage is wrong.
nfl.team_positional_need_and_qb_regime.measurement: Need score per team-position = 0.30 x starter age percentile above position median (0-1) + 0.25 x [years remaining <= 1] + 0.25 x (1 - last-season EPA-based percentile of the starter at the position from nflverse, no PFF) + 0.20 x depth gap (1 if no starter-grade player is under contract after free agency). QB regime codes: 0 = long-term starter (guarantees through next 2 seasons), 1 = bridge/short deal, 2 = no starter-grade QB, plus a flag for QB drafted in rounds 1-2 within 2 years. Shrink position-group means with weight 10 team-years. Weights are assumptions to be fit by regression on historical first-round position choices. Refresh weekly until the draft; as-of last transaction.
free_sources: nflverse rosters, depth charts and contracts (free)
raw_data: roster and depth chart by position

nfl.prospect_declaration_eligibility_med.label: Prospect declaration, eligibility and medical status
nfl.prospect_declaration_eligibility_med.mechanism: Whether a named prospect enters the draft pool at all, remains draft-eligible, and passes medicals, testing and character gates before the draft.
nfl.prospect_declaration_eligibility_med.rationale: A named-prospect contract resolves NO if the player returns to college, is ruled ineligible or falls to a medical and disciplinary red flag. In November the declaration is still months away, the NCAA season is in progress and injuries during the college season change draft value; the deadline for underclassmen is known but the choices are not.
nfl.prospect_declaration_eligibility_med.measurement: P(declare) per underclass prospect by logistic regression on early-entry outcomes of 2021-2026 classes (NIL era, fitted separately from 2010-2020) with features class year, position, consensus round bucket (1, 2-3, 4-7, undrafted) from nfl.prospect_slot_dispersion_model, consensus-rank percentile, and an injury flag = 1 if the player missed 4+ games in either of the last two seasons from team injury reports or beat reports; ridge lambda by CV. Add post-combine/pro-day update: replace round bucket by the updated consensus rank. P(in pool) = P(declare) for eligible players, 1 for exhausted-eligibility seniors. As-of the last official list or the player's dated statement; no market data.

nfl.gm_draft_behavior_history.label: General manager and head coach draft behavior history
nfl.gm_draft_behavior_history.mechanism: Per decision-maker record of trading down, trading up for quarterbacks, positional reaches versus consensus, and tenure resets when GM or coach changes.
nfl.gm_draft_behavior_history.rationale: The picks are made by a small number of people with persistent habits: some GMs trade down 40 percent of the time, others take the best available; a new GM or coach resets need and scheme (4-3 versus 3-4 edge definition). Reaches above consensus rank are a stable personal trait.
nfl.gm_draft_behavior_history.measurement: For each GM and head coach, compute (a) trade-down and trade-up frequency by round, (b) mean reach versus consensus rank by position in rounds 1-3, (c) positions drafted by round including late-round special-teams and positional-value habits, using their past 5 drafts with tenure weighting and shrinkage to the league mean with 3 drafts of prior weight; flag new decision makers and set a new-regime weight to the franchise's last regime at 50 percent.

nfl.draft_position_label_governance.label: Draft position label governance (official position classification)
nfl.draft_position_label_governance.mechanism: Mapping from a prospect to the position label that settles contracts (QB, RB, WR, TE, OL, DL, EDGE, LB, DB), including how the governing league and source agencies label hybrid players.
nfl.draft_position_label_governance.rationale: Position-drafted and Nth-at-position contracts depend on labels, and the rules text states that if positions differ across source agencies the Governing League's position is used. Edge rushers, hybrid linebackers and safeties-cornerbacks and tackle-guard swaps are exactly where labels diverge.
nfl.draft_position_label_governance.measurement: Build a label table from the league's draft tracker position at the time of selection and compare with the college and consensus-board labels for the last 10 classes; compute the disagreement rate by position pair (EDGE versus DL versus LB, S versus CB, OT versus OG) and carry it as probability mass into Nth-at-position markets; as-of = each pick announcement.

nfl.supplemental_draft_mechanics.label: Supplemental Draft mechanics (eligibility petition, tiered lottery order, bid cost)
nfl.supplemental_draft_mechanics.mechanism: Supplemental Draft eligibility via petition, an order set by a lottery within record-based tiers (non-playoff teams grouped by wins, then playoff teams), and the bid rule that costs a team its same-round pick in the next regular draft.
nfl.supplemental_draft_mechanics.rationale: This draft is held rarely and picks only the few players the league declares eligible; whether a named player is selected depends on whether any team will pay a future pick, so the key variables are eligibility ruling, the player's expected round and team needs, not consensus board ranking.
nfl.supplemental_draft_mechanics.measurement: Count Supplemental Draft years with and without picks over 1977-2026 for a base rate; model P(selected) per eligible player from projected round (a bid costs the same-round pick next year, so teams bid only if the player is worth it), team round-pick inventory, and the league ruling date; as-of = league announcement of eligibility and the date of the draft.

nfl.full_draft_order_compensatory_picks.label: Full seven-round draft order with compensatory picks (who holds each of about 257 selections)
nfl.full_draft_order_compensatory_picks.mechanism: Round-by-round order repeats the round-one order, with compensatory selections (awarded in March under the free-agency formula and special minority-hiring picks) appended at the ends of rounds 3-7 and forfeitures removed; the last of these is the final selection.
nfl.full_draft_order_compensatory_picks.rationale: The last-pick, school-count, rounds 1-3 and pick-64 series settle beyond round one, where ownership depends on compensatory awards and late trades. Before March the number and placement of compensatory picks are uncertain, so the identity and team of the last pick is a distribution.
nfl.full_draft_order_compensatory_picks.measurement: Build rounds 1-7 from the rules engine order; forecast compensatory picks per team from net free-agent losses and the public compensatory formula projections until the official March release, then use the official list; apply forfeits and traded-pick ownership; output, per slot, the holding team distribution and the overall pick number of round boundaries (end of round 2, end of round 3) and of the final selection.
free_sources: NFL official compensatory pick release (free, March)
Over The Cap compensatory pick projections (free_limited)
raw_data: official seven-round order with compensatory flags

nfl.prospect_eligibility_clock_and_nil_e.label: Prospect eligibility clock, NCAA eligibility case status and NIL-era declare incentive
nfl.prospect_eligibility_clock_and_nil_e.mechanism: The league requires three seasons since high school graduation; NCAA eligibility waivers and litigation can grant extra college seasons; NIL and revenue-sharing pay raise the value of returning, strongest for quarterbacks.
nfl.prospect_eligibility_clock_and_nil_e.rationale: For early enrollees and reclassified prospects the league clock can bar entry regardless of talent, and pending eligibility rulings decide whether a player stays in college; a pre-NIL declare base rate overstates entry for top underclass QBs. These gates dominate named-prospect 2027 markets in November.
nfl.prospect_eligibility_clock_and_nil_e.measurement: Per prospect compute first eligible draft year = year in which three full seasons have elapsed since high-school graduation. Eligibility flag E = 1 if first eligible year <= target draft year. Extra-year risk X = P(player receives additional college eligibility via waiver or court ruling) = 1 if ruling announced, else base rate from 2021-2026 cases (decided cases won / filed, Beta(1,1) prior) when a case is pending, else 0. P(in pool) = E x (1 - X) x P(declare | NIL era, position, consensus round) from nfl.prospect_declaration_eligibility_medical's model. As-of: timestamp of latest ruling, statement or early-entry list.
raw_data: high school graduation and college enrolment dates
NCAA eligibility rulings and case dockets

nfl.school_draftable_prospect_pool.label: School draftable-prospect pool (eligible players by school with projected round)
nfl.school_draftable_prospect_pool.mechanism: Count and quality of each school's draft-eligible players (seniors, declared underclassmen, transfers listed under the school the league uses) with per-player probability of being drafted and of going in rounds 1-3.
nfl.school_draftable_prospect_pool.rationale: School count and school argmax series are sums over many prospects, including late-round players that national boards barely rank; transfer-portal moves change the classification school, and the league's college label settles the count.
nfl.school_draftable_prospect_pool.measurement: Per school S: for each eligible prospect i, P(drafted_i) and P(round<=3_i) from nfl.prospect_slot_dispersion_model; prospects outside the top 300 of the consensus board get position-specific base rates by school tier (power-conference top-25, other power, group of five, FCS) from 2015-2026 drafts. Simulate 20,000 classes: draw one school-level shock z_S ~ N(0, 0.35^2) on the logit of each prospect's probability (sd refit so the cross-school variance of round-1-3 counts matches 2015-2026), then draw selections independently; output P(count >= N) and P(school has max rounds 1-3 count, ties by 1/k split). As-of latest early-entry list.
free_sources: NFL Mock Draft Database consensus boards (free_scrape)
raw_data: prospect list by school and class
historical draftees by school and round

nfl.sb_neutral_site_matchup_win_prob.label: Super Bowl neutral-site matchup win probability (market-free)
nfl.sb_neutral_site_matchup_win_prob.mechanism: Win probability for each possible pair of conference champions at a neutral site after a two-week break, from full-strength lineups and the playoff overtime rule, then weighted by the chance each pair meets.
nfl.sb_neutral_site_matchup_win_prob.rationale: MVP probability for a player is P(his team reaches the game) times P(wins) times P(he is chosen given a win), so the first two factors are team-level quantities fixed by path and matchup. The full-strength rating, not the season average, applies because injured starters return or are lost in the two weeks and home advantage is absent.
nfl.sb_neutral_site_matchup_win_prob.measurement: For finalists A,B: margin mean = rating_A - rating_B (nfl.lineup_adjusted_team_rating at the latest injury report, shrunk to league mean with weight n/(n+10) games), home-field = 0, rest edge = 0 (both teams have a two-week gap); P(A wins) = Phi(mean/13.0). Pregame of the conference championships: sum P(pair) x P(A beats B) over the four possible championship outcomes, with each championship game using its own host-field constant (about 1.5 points) and rest-edge term of +0.5 points for the team coming off a bye. As-of latest game result and injury vintage; no betting spread, total or moneyline used.
