nfl.sb_mvp_winner_conditional_credit.label: Winning-team credit allocation (P(MVP | team wins) by player and unit)
nfl.sb_mvp_winner_conditional_credit.mechanism: Model of how credit divides among the winner's players: quarterback line, receivers, running backs, pass rushers, defensive scorers and returners, given the game script that leads to a win.
nfl.sb_mvp_winner_conditional_credit.rationale: Voters pick from the winning team (a single non-winner exception exists), so what matters is which unit posts the visible highlights. A high-passing quarterback line, a defensive touchdown or a decisive turnover can overrule season reputation; the mechanism is a function of in-game box score not season stats, so season-stat awards inputs are weak here.
nfl.sb_mvp_winner_conditional_credit.measurement: Fit a multinomial or conditional logit on all Super Bowls since 1967 (and playoff winners as extra data) with in-game player covariates: passing yards and TDs, rush and receiving yards, total TDs, defensive TDs and takeaways, game-winning play indicator and position dummy; sacks enter only for 1982+ games (official since 1982) with a missing indicator before, and tackles are excluded as unofficial. Add a QB-premium intercept with a hierarchical prior; predict on simulated box scores from the winner's player projection. Output P(player MVP | team wins) and position aggregates.
free_sources: Pro-Football-Reference Super Bowl box scores and MVP list (free, scrape)
raw_data: Super Bowl box scores by player

nfl.sb_mvp_historical_position_base_rate.label: Super Bowl MVP historical base rates by position, team result and era
nfl.sb_mvp_historical_position_base_rate.mechanism: Long-run shares of the award by position (QB, RB, WR, defence, special teams), incidence of losing-team and co-winners, and drift by era.
nfl.sb_mvp_historical_position_base_rate.rationale: With about 60 events the position shares are the only data for position and non-QB contracts, so they must be handled as shrinkage priors rather than hard frequencies; the quarterback share, the mix of defensive winners and cases of unusual winners (a returner, a losing-team defender, co-MVPs) shape tails.
nfl.sb_mvp_historical_position_base_rate.measurement: Tabulate winners by position, winning-team flag and era (1967-1990, 1991-2008, 2009-2026) from the official list; compute position shares with Beta shrinkage (prior weight 10 events) and incidence of losing-team and co-MVP outcomes; estimate drift with an era-weighted exponential decay (half-life 20 seasons) and use it as the prior intercept for the conditional-credit model.
raw_data: MVP list with position and team

nfl.sb_defender_highlight_hazard.label: Defender highlight hazard in a Super Bowl (sacks, takeaways, defensive TDs by player)
nfl.sb_defender_highlight_hazard.mechanism: Per-defender expected sacks, takeaways and defensive touchdowns in a game, weighted by pressure rate and the opponent's turnover tendency.
nfl.sb_defender_highlight_hazard.rationale: A defensive MVP needs an outlier game (several sacks, a pick-six or a strip-sack that changes the game); these are rare, high-variance events concentrated among a few edge rushers and ball-hawks and amplified in low-scoring wins. The opponent's offensive-line and quarterback sack and interception rates set the opportunity.
nfl.sb_defender_highlight_hazard.measurement: Per defender: sack rate per team pass-rush snap and per opponent dropback over the last 3 seasons (regular season + playoffs), shrunk to position mean with weight 12 games; expected sacks in the game = player rate x opponent expected dropbacks (nfl.pace x nfl.proe) x opponent sack-rate-allowed ratio vs league. Takeaway rate analogously from interceptions + forced fumbles recovered. Defensive TD hazard per team = takeaways x 0.06 league conversion rate (refit 2000-2025). P(2+ sacks) = 1 - P(0) - P(1) under Poisson; P(any defensive TD for player) from the share of team takeaways; combine with outcome sim from the matchup model. As-of week-of-game injury report.
free_sources: Pass-rush win-rate provider (paid, ESPN or PFF)

nfl.sb_mvp_live_ballot_state.label: Live Super Bowl ballot state (score, win probability and running player lines at ballot time)
nfl.sb_mvp_live_ballot_state.mechanism: During the game the MVP probability is driven by the current leader in visible production on the team that is ahead, evaluated at the time ballots close (fan vote in the fourth quarter).
nfl.sb_mvp_live_ballot_state.rationale: If the markets keep trading into the game, pre-game projections are quickly superseded; the right features are the in-game box score and a market-free win probability from score, time and field position, with a discount for plays after the ballot cut.
nfl.sb_mvp_live_ballot_state.measurement: From live play-by-play, compute every minute: market-free win probability from score differential, time remaining, possession and field position (nflverse-style WP model, no betting lines), and each player's running line; feed to the conditional-credit model with a time-to-ballot-close weight; as-of = play timestamp, never later than the decision time.
free_sources: NFL GameCenter live play-by-play (free_scrape, latency unverified)
nflverse WP model code (free, applied to live data)

nfl.sb_mvp_depth_chart_position_map.label: Super Bowl MVP depth-chart position map (candidate to position strikes)
nfl.sb_mvp_depth_chart_position_map.mechanism: Maps each candidate to the position(s) listed on the league depth chart at game time; a player with two listings (e.g. WR and returner) satisfies both strikes.
nfl.sb_mvp_depth_chart_position_map.rationale: KXNFLSBMVPPOS settles on depth-chart positions, not on the roster or fantasy label, and allows multiple strikes, so position probabilities are sums over a many-to-many map and need not add to one.
nfl.sb_mvp_depth_chart_position_map.measurement: Capture the league-published depth chart for both finalists in Super Bowl week (latest vintage before kickoff) and record every position listing per player; P(strike) = sum over candidates of P(MVP) x 1[candidate listed at strike]; flag hybrid listings and compare with roster positions for the last 10 finals.
free_sources: nflverse depth_charts (free, coverage of game-week vintage unverified)
raw_data: depth chart listings per player at game time

nfl.combine_invite_pool_position_mix.label: Combine invite pool size and position mix (aggregate of per-prospect priors, used as a covariate)
nfl.combine_invite_pool_position_mix.mechanism: The invite list fixes the field over which the fastest 40 and longest jump are taken. Candidates for the extreme come from any position with a fast prior (WR, CB, S, RB, and also edge, LB, TE for the jump), so the pool is filtered by prior, not by listed position.
nfl.combine_invite_pool_position_mix.rationale: Yearly extremes vary with class composition: a class heavy in undersized receivers and corners produces more sub-4.35 runs and 11-foot jumps. Non-invited small-school prospects cannot settle the contract even if faster, so the invite list, not the draft class, defines the field.
nfl.combine_invite_pool_position_mix.measurement: From the official invite list as of release date: counts by listed position, and for each drill the number of invitees whose nfl.prospect_pre_combine_athletic_prior is faster than 4.40 s (40) or longer than 130 inches (broad), regardless of position. Derived aggregate of the per-prospect prior: in the per-prospect simulation it adds no information, and it is used only as the log(participants) covariate of the historical GEV fit in nfl.combine_drill_extreme_history. Compare to 2006-2025 classes as z-scores. As-of: invite release, refreshed with late additions.
free_sources: NFL.com official Combine invite list release
nflverse combine data (load_combine, sourced from Pro-Football-Reference)

nfl.combine_drill_participation_hazard.label: Combine drill opt-in probability per invitee and drill
nfl.combine_drill_participation_hazard.mechanism: Each invitee independently decides whether to perform each drill in Indianapolis; skipping is driven by injury, draft-stock risk and preference for a pro-day surface.
nfl.combine_drill_participation_hazard.rationale: Opt-out is non-random: projected top picks and injured players skip more, and the fastest players sometimes run anyway to set records. Because the 40 contract is an argmax, a single opt-out of the best prior moves several percent of probability to each remaining contender.
nfl.combine_drill_participation_hazard.measurement: Logistic model of P(performed drill | invited) by drill, fit on 2010-2025 Combine data (missing value with player present = skip): covariates projected draft round from consensus board at invite date, injury reported in prior 60 days (yes/no), position, prior 40 tier; shrink team-agency effects with 20 prospects of prior weight. Update to 0 or 1 on credible reports in the final week; as-of each report timestamp.
raw_data: combine drill null flags by player
archived consensus board rank at invite date

sources.name: Archived mock draft / big board snapshots
Insider/beat reports, X and NFL Network archives

nfl.prospect_pre_combine_athletic_prior.label: Pre-Combine athletic prior (expected 40 time and broad jump per prospect)
nfl.prospect_pre_combine_athletic_prior.mechanism: Each prospect's expected best Combine 40 and broad jump predicted from sprint and jump history, body mass and height before he tests.
nfl.prospect_pre_combine_athletic_prior.rationale: College track results (60 m, 100 m, long jump), verified in-season GPS top speed when reported, and mass predict Combine times with an error of a few hundredths; heavier players with the same top speed run slower 40s because of acceleration. A prior is needed because the argmax is decided among a handful of prospects with similar reputations.
nfl.prospect_pre_combine_athletic_prior.measurement: Regression of official Combine 40 (seconds) and broad jump (inches) on: best collegiate 60 m and 100 m (FAT, wind-legal), long jump, reported GPS max mph (flag source), weight and height, position; train on 2010-2025 participants with both measures; missing-track prospects get a position-weight prior; shrinkage toward position-weight mean with weight equal to 3 track races. Output mean and sd per prospect; as-of day before testing.
raw_data: reported GPS top speed with source and date

nfl.combine_attempt_noise_best_of_k.label: Within-prospect attempt noise and best-of-attempts uplift
nfl.combine_attempt_noise_best_of_k.mechanism: The recorded value is the best of a prospect's attempts, so the expected recorded extreme exceeds his mean by an amount that rises with attempt variance and attempt count.
nfl.combine_attempt_noise_best_of_k.rationale: Attempt-to-attempt 40 variation (start reaction, stumbles, hamstring tightness) is roughly a few hundredths (unsourced estimate until fitted); best-of-two shifts the expected best by roughly 0.56 sd. For a record-break threshold or a close argmax, this variance matters as much as the mean.
nfl.combine_attempt_noise_best_of_k.measurement: From seasons where both 40 attempts and all jump attempts are published, estimate within-prospect sd by drill and position via random-effects model; where only best marks exist, infer sd from the gap between Combine and pro-day results for prospects who ran both (sd_attempt = sd_gap / sqrt(2) after removing a mean surface effect). Output sd and expected best-of-k uplift; units seconds and inches.
free_sources: Pro-Football-Reference pro-day and combine pages (free, scrape)
raw_data: combine attempt-level forty_1, forty_2 when published

nfl.combine_drill_extreme_history.label: Yearly Combine best marks by drill (40, broad jump, vertical, bench reps) and record tail
nfl.combine_drill_extreme_history.mechanism: Distribution of the yearly fastest 40, longest broad jump, highest vertical and most bench-press reps across classes, used to calibrate the extreme-value tail of each drill and the chance of breaking its record.
nfl.combine_drill_extreme_history.rationale: The 148-inch strike exceeds the 147-inch record, so the per-class probability is a record-exceedance tail that cannot be read from typical yearly bests; the era trend (training specialisation) and the number of participants shift the location.
nfl.combine_drill_extreme_history.measurement: From nflverse Combine data 2006-2025 (fixed window; earlier timing regime excluded), take each year's best 40 time (minimum), broad jump (maximum, inches), vertical (maximum, inches) and bench press (maximum reps at 225 lb) among participants. For the three continuous drills fit a GEV to the 20 yearly maxima (sign-flipped for the 40) with location mu = a + b x (season-2006) + c x ln(number of participants who recorded the drill); shape by maximum likelihood with a Normal(0, 0.15) prior. For bench reps (integer) fit the same GEV to yearly maxima and discretise by rounding with continuity correction. Parametric bootstrap 2,000 draws for intervals. Output P(max >= x) for any strike and the distribution of the winning mark per drill. As-of before testing, using the forecast participant count per drill.
raw_data: combine.season, player, pos, forty, broad_jump, vertical, bench
participant counts by drill, position and year

nfl.combine_timing_protocol_and_venue.label: Combine timing protocol, track surface and unofficial-to-official revision
nfl.combine_timing_protocol_and_venue.mechanism: How the recorded number is produced: electronic start and finish timing, indoor track surface, attempt rules, and the revision of broadcast unofficial times to official times.
nfl.combine_timing_protocol_and_venue.rationale: Unofficial broadcast times and official results can differ by a few hundredths, and timing-system changes across years shift the whole distribution; both matter for an argmax among sprinters separated by 0.01-0.03 s and for comparing a record across eras.
nfl.combine_timing_protocol_and_venue.measurement: For each Combine since 2015: document timing system and start method from league releases; compute mean and sd of (official minus first-displayed unofficial) 40 times from captured broadcast or tracker snapshots; flag years with a declared timing or surface change as regime breaks; output revision distribution in seconds and a regime indicator.
free_sources: league press releases on Combine format
raw_data: tracker snapshot player, drill, value, official flag, timestamp

nfl.slate_running_extreme_state.label: Running season extreme to date and remaining eligible games
nfl.slate_running_extreme_state.mechanism: For season-maximum contracts, the realised largest margin, total and single-game rushing yards so far, whether the rung is already cleared, and the list of remaining regular-season games define the live state.
nfl.slate_running_extreme_state.rationale: A season threshold is a first-passage event: once cleared it is YES, otherwise probability decays with each completed game. The relevant remaining exposure is not uniform: late-season weeks with rested starters and eliminated teams carry more blowout potential than mid-season weeks.
nfl.slate_running_extreme_state.measurement: After each completed game g update running maxima: M_margin = max |home-away|, M_total = max (home+away, OT included), M_rush = max player rushing yards (single game). For each rung r: cleared_r = 1[M >= r]. For remaining games compute p_g(r) from nfl.deep_tail_margin_model, nfl.total_distribution_tail and nfl.player_single_game_yardage_extreme_rate respectively, using the shared team-rating draw (nfl.rating_uncertainty_shared_error) in 20,000 simulations rather than an analytic product. P(YES at rung r) = 1 if cleared_r else share of simulations where any remaining game reaches r. As-of the final official score of the last completed game; remaining list with week and kickoff.

nfl.player_single_game_yardage_extreme_r.label: Player-game probability of a 200/225/250+ single-game rushing total
nfl.player_single_game_yardage_extreme_r.mechanism: Per player-game probability that rushing yards reach a high rung (200, 225, 250) from the compound of carry count and heavy-tailed per-carry yards, conditioned on script and opponent.
nfl.player_single_game_yardage_extreme_r.rationale: Mean-based projections put no back near 225 yards; the event, which recurs across seasons (record 296 yards), comes from a lead back getting 30 carries in a lopsided win against a poor run defence and breaking two long runs. The compound distribution, not the mean, decides, and quarterbacks with designed runs are a second, smaller contributor.
nfl.player_single_game_yardage_extreme_r.measurement: For each rusher-game: carries ~ NB with mean = player carry share (last 8 games, half-life 4, shrink to depth-slot prior with k=3 games) x team rush attempts, where team attempts are a function of own-model expected margin (nfl.own_team_rating_market_free, no betting spread) fitted on 2015-2025 team-games; per-carry yards drawn from the discrete tail of nfl.rush_yardage_tail with the opponent explosive-allowed adjustment; in simulated paths where the team leads by 28+ in Q4 cap the rusher's remaining carries at 2. Report P(yards >= 200/225/250). Calibrate by comparing simulated count of 200+ games per season with the 2000-2025 empirical frequency per season (scale intercept only). As-of start of week.
raw_data: team rush attempts, own-model expected margin

nfl.blowout_continuation_policy.label: Leader's scoring behaviour after the game is decided
nfl.blowout_continuation_policy.mechanism: Points the leading team keeps adding once the lead exceeds about 35 points, set by the head coach's run-it-up versus kneel tendency, backup quarterback play-calling and whether the trailing team concedes effort.
nfl.blowout_continuation_policy.rationale: A 52-point margin almost never arises from starters alone; it needs fourth-quarter scoring with backups. Coaches differ: some keep throwing and go for it on fourth down, others run the clock. The existing starter-pull input caps starters but says nothing about points scored after the pull.
nfl.blowout_continuation_policy.measurement: From 2000-2025 pbp, select game states with lead >= 28 in the third or fourth quarter; per head coach, compute points per remaining drive and pass rate versus league expectation for that state; shrink to league mean with 15 drives prior weight; output expected additional points and their distribution per remaining minute. As-of start of week with current coach.

nfl.weekly_slate_composition.label: Weekly slate size, byes and game windows
nfl.weekly_slate_composition.mechanism: Which teams and games are in the week's slate: byes remove teams, Week 18 includes all 32, and international or Thursday games are part of the same week; the game count N of the slate is the exposure of weekly count and maximum contracts.
nfl.weekly_slate_composition.rationale: The slate size N (about 13 to 16 games and 26 to 32 teams per week) is the exposure of weekly count and weekly maximum contracts, and a team on bye contributes no game, which a market text may not say explicitly.
nfl.weekly_slate_composition.measurement: From the official schedule as of the week's first kickoff: list of games, teams on bye, kickoff windows, roof status; N_games, N_teams; flag postponed or relocated games and their week assignment. Recompute after any schedule change; units counts.
raw_data: schedules.game_id, week, gameday, home_team, away_team, roof

nfl.slate_max_tie_mass.label: Probability and size of ties at the weekly maximum
nfl.slate_max_tie_mass.mechanism: Probability that two or more games (or teams) share the highest total (or team score) in a week, and the expected payout under the $1/N rounded-down rule.
nfl.slate_max_tie_mass.rationale: Team scores cluster on key values (17, 20, 24, 27, 31, 34) so ties at the top among 26-32 teams are common enough to change expected value; game-total ties at the maximum are rarer but not negligible. The dead-heat rule makes a tied favourite worth well below 1.
nfl.slate_max_tie_mass.measurement: Empirical 2002-2025: share of weeks with a tied maximum team score and tied maximum game total, by number of teams playing; model: simulate integer team-score PMFs per team-game (from nfl.team_score_pmf_own_mean, the catalog key-number PMF input), compute P(tie at max) and expected payout floor(100/N)/100 per named team; calibrate simulated tie rates to the empirical share. As-of week start.

nfl.season_extreme_era_base_rate.label: Era-adjusted historical distribution of season maxima (margin, total, rushing yards)
nfl.season_extreme_era_base_rate.mechanism: Per-season maxima of game margin, game total and single-game rushing yards over past regular seasons, adjusted for the scoring environment and number of games.
nfl.season_extreme_era_base_rate.rationale: Rungs differ in rarity: the 109.5 total lies beyond the post-merger record (about 106), the 51.5 margin has been exceeded at least five times since the merger (59, 54, 59, 55 and 58 points in 1976, 1989, 2009, 2011 and 2012), roughly once a decade, and 225+ rushing yards recurs across seasons. Base rates are therefore set separately per rung: seasons with any margin above 45, any total above 90 and any 200-yard rusher calibrate per-game tail fits and guard against overconfident extrapolation.
nfl.season_extreme_era_base_rate.measurement: For 1978-2025 seasons compute max margin, max total and max single-game rushing yards; scale for games per season (16 to 17) and league scoring per game relative to the season mean; fit GEV per statistic with a scoring-environment covariate; report P(season max > rung) for the 2026 environment with bootstrap intervals. Report per-rung empirical frequency (seasons with exceedance / seasons) beside the GEV estimate; for the 225 rung use count of 225+ games per season, not a record-break model.

nfl.week_running_state_by_window.label: Within-week realised scores by kickoff window and market close time
nfl.week_running_state_by_window.mechanism: For the weekly argmax contracts, the highest game total and highest team score already realised after the Thursday, international, early Sunday and late Sunday windows condition what the remaining games must exceed, and the market close time relative to each window decides how much of that is already known.
nfl.week_running_state_by_window.rationale: Unlike season thresholds, a weekly argmax is partly settled before the last kickoff: after the early window a 55-point game or a 45-point team score sets a running bar that the late games and Monday night rarely beat, so the named game's or team's probability collapses or rises discretely as windows finish. Ignoring the running maximum treats a live market as if it were pre-week.
nfl.week_running_state_by_window.measurement: At each timestamp t in the week: running max game total M_g(t) and running max team score M_t(t) over completed games (final scores, OT included), the list of games not yet started with kickoff times, and for each remaining game P(total > M_g(t)) and P(team score >= M_t(t)) from the integer score PMFs (nfl.team_score_pmf_own_mean), with ties at the bar counted as dead heats. The named game or team's probability is the conditional argmax probability given the running bar. As-of the last completed final score; capture the market close timestamp so that positions are only evaluated before it. Units points and games.

nfl.combo_shared_weather_leg_coupling.label: Shared-weather common shock coupling same-game combo legs (total, kicker, passing, rushing)
nfl.combo_shared_weather_leg_coupling.mechanism: One kickoff-hour weather state (sustained wind, gusts, heavy precipitation, extreme cold) at an open-air venue shifts several legs of the same combo in fixed directions at once: it lowers the game total and team totals, lowers kicker points and long-FG legs, lowers QB passing-yard and receiver-yard legs, and raises rushing attempts and the leading back's carry legs.
nfl.combo_shared_weather_leg_coupling.rationale: Legs are priced from marginals that each absorb the weather forecast separately; multiplying them treats a 20 mph wind as an independent shock per leg, which understates the joint probability of same-direction combos (under + QB-yards under + kicker under) and overstates mixed-direction combos (over + QB-yards over). The effect is thresholded (near zero below about 10 mph sustained, steep above 15) and vanishes for domes and closed retractable roofs, so it is a regime variable, not a constant correlation.
nfl.combo_shared_weather_leg_coupling.measurement: For each open-air game 2010-2025 take the forecast weather state W (sustained wind mph, gust mph, precipitation flag, temp F) from nfl.weather_pit at the leg quote vintage (observed game-time weather from nflverse schedules for the historical fit, flagged as observed); roof in (dome, closed) sets W = calm. Bin W into calm (<10 mph, no precipitation), moderate (10-15 mph or light rain), severe (>=15 mph sustained or gusts >=25 or snow/heavy rain). For each leg pair type (game total x QB passing yards; game total x kicker points/long FG; QB passing yards x top receiver yards; game total x lead-rusher carries/yards; kicker points x team total) compute the residual of each leg statistic against its own-model expectation without the weather term (nfl.model_team_points_mean, qb/receiver/rusher projections), then the residual correlation and the weather-bin shift of both residual means; shrink bin correlations toward the calm-bin value with weight n/(n+80) leg-pairs. Joint simulation: draw W from the forecast distribution (forecast-error SD by lead time from archive vs observed), shift each leg mean by nfl.weather_total_response and the leg-specific weather slopes, and draw legs with the bin correlation. Output joint P(all legs) per combo and the weather share of the dependence. As-of the latest forecast vintage before the quote.
free_sources: nflverse schedules (roof, observed wind and temp)
Open-Meteo forecast and historical forecast API

forecast vintages: wind, gust, precip, temp at fixed leads

nfl.sibling_leg_marginal_interface.label: Cross-archetype leg output contract: per-leg P(yes) plus a shared latent game-state sample
nfl.sibling_leg_marginal_interface.mechanism: Defines what each sibling archetype model must export so combos can be priced coherently: the leg's marginal P(yes) and, for the same simulation draws, the latent game state (home and away points, margin, total, plays, starting QB and key-player availability state, weather bin) and the leg statistic itself, so joints are read from shared draws instead of a copula on marginals.
nfl.sibling_leg_marginal_interface.rationale: A combo is only as good as its marginals, and separate models that each simulate their own game state produce incoherent joints (a QB-yards draw from one game script paired with a cover from another). A fixed interface (fields, draw count, as-of time, seed alignment) is the definition that makes the combo layer reproducible; without it the cross-archetype dependency is undefined.
nfl.sibling_leg_marginal_interface.measurement: Interface spec, version 1. Producers: game_moneyline_spread, game_total, team_total, qb_passing_yards, receiving_yards_and_receptions, rushing_yards, anytime_first_td_scorer, first_half_and_quarter_totals. Each producer, for game g and as-of timestamp t (latest injury-report and forecast vintage before the quote), returns (a) for each listed leg: P(yes) under that leg's own settlement rule (OT in/out, push, DNP=0 or void) and (b) a draw matrix of S=20,000 simulations sharing a common seed per game: draw_id, home_pts, away_pts, regulation_home_pts, regulation_away_pts, ot_flag, team plays, QB1_active, key-player active flags, weather bin, and the leg statistic (yards, receptions, TD order). The game-level model (nfl.model_team_points_mean, nfl.model_margin_lattice) generates the shared columns; player archetypes condition on them. Consistency checks: mean of indicator over draws equals the exported P(yes) within 0.002; team-total and game-total draws obey home+away=total. Combos compute P(all legs) as the share of draws where every leg settles YES. Market prices are never inputs.

nflverse schedules and pbp for historical validation of joint hit rates
raw_data: simulation draw matrices from each sibling model

nfl.fantasy_kicker_points_chain.label: Kicker fantasy points under Sleeper default scoring from drive stalls by distance
nfl.fantasy_kicker_points_chain.mechanism: A kicker's Sleeper points are +3 per FG made 0-39 yards, +4 for 40-49, +5 for 50-59, +6 for 60+, +1 per extra point made and -1 per FG or extra point missed, so the score is a weighted count of drive endings: touchdowns (extra-point tries), drives that stall inside range (FG attempts by distance) and the kicker's make curve.
nfl.fantasy_kicker_points_chain.rationale: Kicker scores have a small mean (about 7-9) and a lumpy discrete distribution, and strikes such as 9.2 sit where one long FG changes the outcome; the distance tiers make a stalled drive at the opponent's 35 worth more than one at the 10, and coach 4th-down aggressiveness converts would-be FGs into TD tries. Team TD expectation and FG opportunity move in opposite directions inside the red zone, which a single 'team points' proxy misses.
nfl.fantasy_kicker_points_chain.measurement: Per team-game simulation using the shared drive draws: number of drives from nfl.drives; per drive, ending state (TD, FG attempt, other) from own-model drive outcome rates by field position, with FG attempt distance = line of scrimmage + 17 yards from the drive's stall yard line distribution (nflverse pbp 2018-2025, shrunk to league with k=200 attempts by stall bin) and the coach's FG-versus-go decision from nfl.fourth_down_fg_decision_rate; make probability from nfl.kicker's distance curve (weather and altitude adjusted); extra-point make rate per kicker shrunk to league with k=150 tries; two-point try share by coach. Points = 3*FG(0-39)+4*FG(40-49)+5*FG(50-59)+6*FG(60+)+1*XP - 1*(FG missed + XP missed). Output the full pmf and P(points > strike) as of the latest injury report (kicker active flag; replacement kicker if out).

nfl.fantasy_dst_points_chain.label: Team D/ST fantasy points under Sleeper default scoring (events plus points-allowed tier)
nfl.fantasy_dst_points_chain.mechanism: A D/ST score is the sum of event points (+1 sack, +2 interception, +2 fumble recovery, +1 forced fumble, +2 safety, +2 blocked kick, +6 defensive or special-teams TD, +1 special-teams forced fumble or fumble recovery) and a step function of points allowed (0: +10, 1-6: +7, 7-13: +4, 14-20: +1, 21-27: 0, 28-34: -1, 35+: -4), so it is driven by the opponent offence's dropbacks, sack and giveaway rates and by the opponent's scoring distribution.
nfl.fantasy_dst_points_chain.rationale: D/ST markets (e.g. 'Seattle Seahawks D/ST: Over 8.8') are decided by rare high-value events and a steep points-allowed step; a shutout or a pick-six moves the score by 6-10 points, so the distribution is right-skewed with a negative floor. Sacks and turnovers rise when the opponent trails and must pass, linking D/ST points to the margin, and the points-allowed tier depends on whether Sleeper counts points allowed by the offence (return TDs) as well, which is not stated in the Kalshi text.
nfl.fantasy_dst_points_chain.measurement: Per team-game, using the shared game draws: opponent dropbacks from the opponent's pass rate by simulated script; sacks = dropbacks x own pressure-to-sack rate (nfl.defence_sack_count_decomposition) as negative binomial; interceptions = opponent pass attempts x opponent QB INT rate adjusted for pressure (nfl.int_rate), fumbles and recoveries from league per-play rates shrunk to team with k=400 plays; D/ST TDs from nfl.dst_td_hazard; safeties and blocked kicks at league rates (shrunk team effect, k=40 games). Points allowed = opponent simulated points from nfl.team_score_pmf_own_mean conditional on the draw, mapped to the Sleeper tier. Sum event points + tier points per draw; output pmf and P(points > strike). Fit dispersion on 2015-2025 team-games. As-of the latest injury report of both teams' QBs and key pass rushers.

nfl.combine_bench_press_pool_and_prior.label: Bench-press (225 lb reps) participant pool and per-prospect rep prior
nfl.combine_bench_press_pool_and_prior.mechanism: The most-reps event is a maximum over prospects who choose to bench, a pool dominated by defensive and offensive linemen with long-standing strength histories; arm length lowers reps, and top prospects and players with upper-body injuries often skip the lift.
nfl.combine_bench_press_pool_and_prior.rationale: The speed and jump pools used for the 40 and broad jump are almost disjoint from the bench pool, so the existing priors say nothing about this event; the favourite is set by a few interior linemen with very high strength priors, and opt-outs among them change the maximum more than anything else.
nfl.combine_bench_press_pool_and_prior.measurement: Per invitee: expected reps = regression on 2006-2025 Combine bench results of position group (iDL, EDGE, OL, LB, TE, RB, other), weight (lb), arm length (in), and reported pro-day or college strength numbers where available (flagged by source), with prospect-level SD from residuals; shrink toward position-weight mean with weight 2 reported lifts. Participation probability from nfl.combine_drill_participation_hazard refit for the bench drill (covariates: projected round, upper-body injury in prior 90 days, position). Simulate the field maximum over participating invitees (integer reps); calibrate the yearly maximum against the 2006-2025 history in nfl.combine_drill_extreme_history. Output P(max reps >= k) and P(named prospect has the most reps), dead-heat ties shown separately. As-of the day before bench testing.
free_sources: NFL.com Combine invite list and measurements (arm length)
raw_data: combine: season, player, pos, wt, bench (reps)
invite list measurements: arm length, weight

nfl.combine_vertical_jump_prior.label: Vertical-jump participant pool and per-prospect jump prior
nfl.combine_vertical_jump_prior.mechanism: The highest vertical is a maximum over jumpers whose ceiling depends on elastic power relative to mass; receivers, corners, safeties and some running backs and edge rushers populate the tail, and the event shares participants and opt-out behaviour with the broad jump.
nfl.combine_vertical_jump_prior.rationale: Vertical and broad jump are correlated (both lower-body power) but not interchangeable: the vertical favours lighter, elastic athletes, measurement uses the Vertec standing-reach protocol, and best-of-attempt noise is larger relative to the spread of the top of the field, so the broad-jump prior cannot be reused unchanged.
nfl.combine_vertical_jump_prior.measurement: Per invitee: expected vertical (inches) = regression on 2006-2025 Combine results of broad-jump prior from nfl.prospect_pre_combine_athletic_prior, weight, height, position, and college track jump marks where available (long jump, high jump; FAT/wind-legal flags), with residual SD per position; participation from nfl.combine_drill_participation_hazard refit for the vertical; joint simulation with the broad jump using the empirical residual correlation (estimated per position group, shrunk to pooled with weight n/(n+50)). Field maximum by simulation; output P(max >= x) for half-inch strikes and P(named prospect highest), ties reported. Calibrate yearly maxima to the 2006-2025 history. As-of the day before jumps.

nfl.player_single_game_stat_extreme_fami.label: Season-long any-player single-game extreme by stat (passing, receiving, receptions, TDs, sacks, tackles, INTs)
nfl.player_single_game_stat_extreme_fami.mechanism: Each non-rushing KXNFLGAMESPECIALS rung pays if any player in any regular-season game reaches it, so its probability is one minus the product over the season's player-games of the chance of staying below the rung, built from each stat's own opportunity-times-yield process: passing yards and passing TDs from dropbacks and efficiency in shootouts; receiving yards and receptions from target share in high-volume passing games; non-passing TDs from goal-line usage; sacks from pass-rush wins against a trailing offence; tackles from defensive snaps and opponent run volume; interceptions from a defender's targets against turnover-prone passers.
nfl.player_single_game_stat_extreme_fami.rationale: The live rung list goes far beyond rushing: 475/500/525 passing yards, 6 passing TDs, 250/275/300 receiving yards, 15/17/20 receptions, 4+ non-passing TDs, 4/5/6 sacks, 20+ tackles, 2/3 defensive interceptions, 2+ D/ST TDs and 100 rushing plus 100 receiving yards. Each sits in a different tail with different drivers, and several were already settled YES early in the season (2 and 3 interceptions, 15 and 17 receptions), so banked state matters as much as the per-game tail. Tackle counts depend on the official scorer's solo-plus-assist tally, which varies by stadium crew.
nfl.player_single_game_stat_extreme_fami.measurement: For each stat k in {pass yds, pass TD, rec yds, receptions, non-passing TD, sacks, tackles (solo+assisted), def INT, D/ST TD, rush>=100 and rec>=100 jointly}: per player-game, simulate the stat from the player's opportunity share (last 8 games, half-life 4, shrunk to depth-slot prior k=3 games) times team volume conditioned on own-model margin and total draws (nfl.model_team_points_mean, never betting lines), with stat-specific yield distributions fitted on 2010-2025 player-games (negative binomial for counts, discretised gamma mixture for yards; tackle counts with a home-scorer random effect shrunk k=16 games). P(rung reached in game) per player-game; season probability = 1 - prod over remaining player-games (1 - p) with a shared-rating-error adjustment, conditioned on the realised season maximum to date (settled rungs = 1). Calibrate each stat's intercept to the 2010-2025 count of games per season above the rung. As-of start of each week.

nfl.player_single_quarter_stat_extreme.label: Any-player single-quarter stat extreme (250 passing, 150 rushing, 150 receiving yards; overtime excluded)
nfl.player_single_quarter_stat_extreme.mechanism: Quarter rungs pay if any player records the stat within one regulation quarter; a 15-minute window concentrates the outcome on explosive plays and on quarters with many possessions (two-minute drills, trailing scripts), so the per-quarter distribution is far more tail-heavy relative to its mean than the full-game total.
nfl.player_single_quarter_stat_extreme.rationale: The KXNFLGAMESPECIALS rules state that quarter-specific markets count only stats in an individual quarter, not overtime, so full-game projections cannot be scaled by one quarter: second and fourth quarters carry end-of-half possessions, and a single 80-yard play is a large share of a 150-yard quarter.
nfl.player_single_quarter_stat_extreme.measurement: From nflverse pbp 2010-2025, aggregate each player's passing, rushing and receiving yards by game and quarter (qtr 1-4 only; qtr 5 excluded). Per player-quarter model: yards = sum over the player's plays in the quarter of per-play yards drawn from the player's play-yard distribution (shrunk to position, k=150 plays), with play count negative binomial by quarter index and simulated score state. Season probability = 1 - prod over remaining player-quarters (1 - p), conditioned on settled rungs. Calibrate to the empirical per-season count of player-quarters above each rung. As-of start of each week.
raw_data: pbp: game_id, qtr, passer_player_id, rusher_player_id, receiver_player_id, yards_gained, play_type, score_differential

nfl.market_free_score_state_blowout_mass.label: Market-free score-state and blowout-mass distribution from team ratings and drive-level rates
nfl.market_free_score_state_blowout_mass.mechanism: Distribution of the in-game score state (lead or deficit size by quarter and time spent in each state) and the blowout mass (probability of a 14+ point fourth-quarter lead, of a 21+ point margin at any time) produced by simulating drives from own team ratings, together with state-conditional pass rate, pace and starter-exit response curves estimated from play-by-play.
nfl.market_free_score_state_blowout_mass.rationale: Largest lead, lead changes and comebacks depend on how often and how long a game sits in a lopsided or close state and how teams behave there. The existing script and garbage-time inputs are measured from betting spread and total, so they cannot serve a market-free path model; this input rebuilds the same quantities from team strength and drive-level rates so the state distribution does not inherit the market's view.
nfl.market_free_score_state_blowout_mass.measurement: Step 1, state distribution: per game, take opponent-adjusted offence and defence points per drive for both sides from nfl.own_team_rating_market_free (ratings with preseason prior, as of kickoff), drives per team from nfl.drives, and simulate 20,000 score paths with the drive-result probabilities of nfl.drive_result_lattice and the point package of nfl.scoring_event_point_values; record margin and remaining time at each drive boundary. Output P(|margin| >= 14 at the start of the fourth quarter), P(|margin| >= 21 at any time), expected fraction of second-half snaps by margin bin {<=-17, -16..-9, -8..-1, 0, 1..8, 9..16, >=17}. Step 2, response curves: from nflverse play-by-play 2015-2025 estimate pass rate over expected, seconds per play, rush attempts per drive and starting-quarterback exit hazard by the same margin bins and quarter, shrunk to the league cell with k=200 plays per cell and a team and coach offset (half-life 3 seasons); use the actual game state at each play, never a spread or total. Step 3, feedback: feed Step 2 curves back into the simulation of Step 1 for the second half and iterate once. Calibration target: empirical frequency of 14+ point fourth-quarter leads and 21+ point margins in 2012-2025 games by bins of the own-model expected margin, not closing lines. The schedule table's spread and total columns must be dropped before use. As-of kickoff, mixing over the starting-quarterback scenarios of nfl.qb.

nfl.league_window_banked_count_and_expos.label: League-window banked count and remaining-game exposure (ties and 60+ yard makes)
nfl.league_window_banked_count_and_expos.mechanism: For a league-wide count over a window, the number of qualifying events already banked at an as-of time and the list of games still to be played in the window with the features that set each game's event probability.
nfl.league_window_banked_count_and_expos.rationale: The league tie and long-kick contracts are banked-plus-remaining sums. The player-season accrual inputs of the season-stat blueprint describe individual players, not league-wide events, so the banked count, games remaining, the as-of rule and the treatment of unplayed games need their own definition.
nfl.league_window_banked_count_and_expos.measurement: At as-of time T: banked_ties = number of regular-season games with final status completed before T whose official final score is level; banked_60 = number of made field goals with official kick length >= 60 yards in regular-season games before T (flag free-kick field goals separately because their treatment by the contract is unstated). Remaining exposure = list of regular-season games in the window not yet completed at T (week, teams, roof, altitude, kickoff, expected margin from nfl.own_team_rating_market_free, kicker identities), with a flag for postponed, relocated or suspended games and the week they move to. For a weekly contract the window is that week's games only. Unplayed or cancelled games are flagged STATUS_UNSTATED and the output carries the count with and without them. Output (banked, N_remaining, per-game feature rows) as of T; recompute after every completed game.

nfl.fg_attempt_hazard_by_distance_band_6.label: Field-goal attempt hazard by distance band at 60+ yards (60-64, 65-69, 70+)
nfl.fg_attempt_hazard_by_distance_band_6.mechanism: Per team-game hazard of a field-goal attempt of at least 60 yards, split into 60-64, 65-69 and 70+ bands by the situations in which such attempts are chosen (end of half, trailing by up to three, short clock, venue and wind), the head coach and the kicker's demonstrated range.
nfl.fg_attempt_hazard_by_distance_band_6.rationale: The contract counts made kicks of 60 yards or more and most expected makes are likely at the short end of the range, so an attempt hazard defined only for 65+ yards misses the main contributors; a band-specific hazard is the attempt side of attempts times make probability for the contract threshold.
nfl.fg_attempt_hazard_by_distance_band_6.measurement: From play-by-play over the last 4 seasons count attempts with official kick length in each band per team-game and qualifying situations (game_seconds_remaining in half <= 20, offence with yardline_100 between 43 and 62 so that the kick length, about yardline_100 + 17 yards, is 60 to 79 yards (a 60-yard kick is snapped from about the opponent 43), score differential in {-3..0} at half end, plus venue altitude and roof); estimate P(attempt in band | situation) by a hierarchical logit with head coach and kicker random effects (kicker max made kick, 60+ history, wind, rule era including the K-ball regime of nfl.kicking_ball_and_fg_rule_era), shrinking coach rates to the league with 15 qualifying situations of prior weight. Output expected attempts per band for each remaining team-game and the league total for the remaining schedule; make probability by band comes from nfl.long_fg_attempt_and_make_model and nfl.kicker_ceiling_range_tail. As-of kickoff with the active kicker.

nfl.team_window_game_exposure.label: Team game list and issuance state inside a multi-week event window
nfl.team_window_game_exposure.mechanism: The list of regular-season games a named team still plays between a market's issuance and the end of its stated window, with byes, kickoff times, the state of any game in progress at issuance and the probability distribution over each opponent's starting quarterback.
nfl.team_window_game_exposure.rationale: An at-least-once event over a window is a product over the games in it, so the number of games, which of them are home or road, which opponents they are and whether a game is already under way at issuance are first-order inputs. None of the player-level inputs defines the window; the contract text says only 'after issuance and before Week 8'.
nfl.team_window_game_exposure.measurement: From the official schedule as of the market's issuance timestamp T, for team t build the rung ladder of windows: for each end week W in {2,4,6,8,12,14,16} and 'anytime' (the whole regular season) the window of rung W is the set of regular-season games with week < W (these rungs were reported by a reviewer from Kalshi API metadata, not by the sampled rules text, and are unverified); compute N_g(W) for every rung (from 1 to about 17 games) so nested windows share the same game list. For each game record week, kickoff time, opponent, home or road, roof and bye weeks (a bye contributes no game). Game g is inside a window if kickoff_g > T; a game in progress at T is flagged IN_PROGRESS and carried with both readings (counted with remaining plays only versus excluded) because the sampled text does not say; the reviewer reports the nine sampled markets were all opened before Week 1 (unverified), in which case no game is in progress at issuance. Attach to each game the as-of distribution over the opponent's starting quarterback from nfl.qb and nfl.weekly_qb_depth_slot_model (widening with weeks ahead, up to 17 weeks for the longest rung). Recompute whenever the schedule changes (flex, postponement, relocation) and flag postponed games and their new week. Output the game table with features and the N_g(W) ladder.

nfl.window_hazard_survival_with_game_cor.label: Window survival product with cross-game dependence
nfl.window_hazard_survival_with_game_cor.mechanism: Turns per-game event hazards into the probability of at least one event over each nested window of a rung ladder as one minus the expected product of per-game zero-event probabilities, averaging over shared uncertainty (the team's defensive quality, scheme changes, quarterback injuries) that links the games.
nfl.window_hazard_survival_with_game_cor.rationale: Multiplying independent per-game probabilities overstates how fast the probability of at least one event approaches one when the games share a common unknown such as the defence's true rate; the shared factor fattens the no-event tail, which is exactly the part of the distribution that prices a Yes contract near the top.
nfl.window_hazard_survival_with_game_cor.measurement: Per game g for team t: expected event count lambda_g = D_g x p0 x m_def(t) x m_qb(q_g), where D_g = expected opposing dropbacks (opposing plays from nfl.pace and nfl.total_plays_state_model times the opposing dropback rate; nfl.proe is a pass-rate-over-expected input whose pass-attempt versus dropback definition is not verified, so the dropback rate must be re-measured as qb_dropback per play, sacks and scrambles included, and p0 is defined per qb_dropback to match), p0 = league interceptions per dropback, m_def(t) = the named team's defensive interception multiplier relative to the league (a ratio, not a rate): a base multiplier from nfl.opp_def_int_propensity (already adjusted for the quality of quarterbacks faced) times an availability-and-scheme adjustment A(t) as of T, where A(t) is estimated by regressing past team interception multipliers on the snap-weighted availability of cornerbacks and safeties from nfl.def_personnel (injury and absence vintages) and on the change in man/zone and single-high/two-high shell rates from nfl.coverage_scheme versus the base period (these inputs measure availability and scheme, not ball skills, so ball-skill differences enter only through the team's own past takeaways), and m_qb(q_g) = the opposing quarterback's multiplier relative to the league (a ratio) from nfl.int_rate, estimated net of the defences he has faced; the two multipliers are ratios so that no per-attempt rate is multiplied by another and the quarterback is not counted twice (if m_def were not quarterback-adjusted it must not be combined with m_qb). The team's takeaway rate uses the interception flag only (fumble recoveries excluded); nfl.turnovers is a regression benchmark, not the rate. Draw a shared log-multiplier u_t ~ Normal(0, tau^2) for the defence (tau to be fitted from between-season variation of team interception rates after shrinkage) and draw each game's opposing starter from its as-of distribution. Survival to the end of rung W: S(W) = E[ product over games with week < W of exp(-lambda_g exp(u_t)) ]; compute every rung from the same draws so S(W) is non-increasing in W and P(at least one by W) = 1 - S(W) is monotone across the nested rungs. Report with and without the shared factor. As-of issuance timestamp and recomputed after each game.

nfl.end_of_half_goal_line_snap_and_spike.label: End-of-half goal-line snap exposure and quarterback spike probability
nfl.end_of_half_goal_line_snap_and_spike.mechanism: Expected number of snaps on or inside the opponent's 1-yard line in the closing seconds of each half (when a spike can stop the clock) and the probability that such a snap is a quarterback spike rather than a run or pass call.
nfl.end_of_half_goal_line_snap_and_spike.rationale: A spike is a clock-management play, not a pass call chosen against a sneak, and play-by-play commonly logs it as an incomplete pass. If a spike counts for KXNFL1YDPASS it adds attempts that no coach pass-call model explains, and it must be separated from the pass-call rate before fitting coach effects.
nfl.end_of_half_goal_line_snap_and_spike.measurement: From nflverse play-by-play 2015-2025 (the data dictionary lists a qb_spike flag and play_type 'qb_spike'; field semantics to confirm) count, per team-game, snaps with yardline_100 <= 1 and game_seconds_remaining in the half <= 60, and estimate P(spike | such snap) by logistic regression on seconds remaining, timeouts remaining, score differential bucket from the own-model margin distribution (not betting lines), down, and a coach random effect (shrink to league with k=10 snaps). Expected spikes on or inside the 1 per team-game = (expected end-of-half snaps from the 1, from drive success and the drive-reaching-the-1 rate of nfl.redzone and nfl.field_pos) x P(spike). Output separately the expected non-spike pass calls and the spike count so that either reading of the contract can be priced. As-of kickoff.
