game_side.mechanism: Moneyline, spread, win-margin and half/period winner markets all price the distribution of final margin: team strength differences (QB-adjusted), home edge, rest and environment shift the mean, while the lattice of NFL scoring (key numbers 3 and 7) and overtime/tie rules shape probabilities at specific lines. The market line already contains most public information, so the model is mainly a calibration and lineup-timing exercise.
game_side.target: Probability that the team wins (moneyline), covers a spread, or the margin falls in a bucket, under the contract's regulation/overtime settlement.

inputs.why: Market-implied and Elo-style team strength is the prior that every other input must add to.
Starter QB status is the largest single swing in margin and resolves late; must be mixed by probability.
Opponent-adjusted offensive efficiency gives the structural mean margin independent of the line.
Defense efficiency completes the team-strength matchup; pass and rush splits matter for specific opponents.
Timestamped injury vintages show which stars are missing at market time.
Short weeks, byes and travel create small systematic margin shifts.
Home-field strength, roof and surface adjust the margin mean.
Wind/precipitation compress scoring and favor the run-heavy/defense-heavy side.
Key-number lattice converts rating differences to probabilities at half-point spreads.
Tie/OT mass differs between regulation-only and including-OT settlement.
Seeding stakes and starter rest change effort and lineup late in the season.
Sharp reference lines are the benchmark; inconsistent Kalshi prices reveal staleness.
Settlement wording (OT, ties, postponement) must match the modelled outcome.
Division games are scouted more heavily; a candidate residual adjustment to margin variance and cover rates.
Defensive injuries alter the defense rating and are knowable from the report vintage.

interactions.hypothesis: QB-status uncertainty interacts with spread size: a backup QB shifts the margin mean and widens the margin SD, so cover probability changes more than moneyline for large spreads.
Wind and cold interact with passing-reliant teams: bad weather lowers the efficiency of pass-first favorites more than run-first teams, narrowing expected margin.
Late-season seeding stakes interact with injury reports: a clinched team with questionable starters has much higher rest probability.

period.mechanism: Half and quarter markets inherit the full-game strength model but add period-specific structure: scripted opening drives, who receives the opening kickoff, two-minute drills before halftime, second-half adjustments and garbage-time. Scoring is smaller and lumpier per period so ties/pushes and key numbers have greater weight; late-game clock management mostly affects only the fourth quarter.
period.target: Points, margin, winner or total in a defined period (first half, quarter), settled per contract wording on ties and overtime.

inputs.why: Team-specific historical quarter/half scoring shares are the base for period totals and margins.
Scripted first drives drive Q1 scoring and the tied-after-Q1 outcome.
Possession order shifts first-quarter and second-half-start scoring.
Two-minute drills produce a disproportionate share of Q2 points.
Lead/trail scripting determines Q3-Q4 pace and how early garbage time begins.
Full-game team strength sets the period margin mean.
Implied team totals from the game total and spread are scaled to the period.
Coaching tendencies (tempo, 4th-down aggression, halftime adjustments) vary the period profile.
Key-number structure for short periods differs from full-game residuals.
Period markets can differ on ties and overtime inclusion.

interactions.hypothesis: Opening possession and opening-drive scripts interact: a team that defers but has a strong scripted offense gets the ball second in Q1 yet first in Q3, shifting scoring between quarters.
Two-minute efficiency interacts with timeout and pace habits to concentrate first-half scoring in the last 2 minutes of Q2.
Halftime lead interacts with script: second-half pace and run rate depend on whether a team is leading by more than a score.

game_total.mechanism: Totals are the product of possessions and points per possession for both teams. Drives depend on pace, run/pass mix and turnover rates; points per drive on opponent-adjusted efficiency, field position, red-zone finishing, kicker range and weather. Both teams' outputs are correlated through game script and environment, so the distribution of total has a fat right tail from blowouts and explosive plays; both-teams-score and team-total markets are slices of the same joint distribution.
game_total.target: Sum of the two teams' points (or each team's points, or whether each team scores at least N) under the contract's regulation/OT settlement.

inputs.why: Plays per game scale all scoring; pace is a stable team trait.
Expected possessions are the base unit of scoring; drive count differs from plays due to turnovers, punts and clock-killing.
Pass-heavy teams stop the clock and sustain pace; PROE sets passing volume and yards.
Offensive EPA per play, opponent-adjusted, anchors points per drive for each team.
Opponent defense efficiency suppresses points per drive and changes the pass/rush split of scoring.
Explosive-play rates raise scoring variance and the fat right tail of the total distribution.
Red-zone TD versus FG conversion changes points per scoring opportunity by up to 4 points per trip and regresses to league mean.
Wind and precipitation lower totals; effects nonlinear.
Kicker range and accuracy determine how many stalled drives convert to 3 points and the key-number structure of totals.
Starter versus backup QB shifts both team points and pace and is only resolved late; total must be a mixture.
Teams scoring above or below their drive-efficiency expectation regress; recent points should be discounted accordingly.
Empirical total residuals and key numbers calibrate rung probabilities.
OT adds points in tied games; inclusion depends on wording.
Sharp totals incorporate weather and lineup information; the Kalshi ladder should be compared to the de-vigged consensus.

interactions.hypothesis: Pace and efficiency are multiplicative: a high-pace offense against a high-pace defense compounds possessions, while two slow, run-heavy teams under-shoot even if efficiency is average.
Wind interacts with explosive passing and kicking: high wind removes deep-pass explosives and long FG, cutting points more for vertical offenses than for run-heavy teams.
Spread size interacts with total: lopsided expected games shift clock-killing run rate for the leader, reducing the favorite's late scoring.

game_event.mechanism: Game-event and stat markets (overtime, safety, both teams score, team stats, TD counts, period TDs) are tails or slices of the underlying drive and score process. They depend on base rates of rare events (overtime, safeties, defensive TDs), the correlation structure of scoring, and team style indicators (pass rush, red-zone play, turnovers) that shift event hazards.
game_event.target: Occurrence or count of a game-level event or team stat (overtime, safety, touchdowns, turnovers, sacks, etc.) under the contract definition.

inputs.why: Margin distribution mass near zero determines overtime probability and tie mass.
OT rules and rate underpin OT-related events.
Event counts scale with plays and drives.
Turnover and takeaway hazards drive event counts such as turnovers or defensive TDs.
Pass-rush strength drives sacks and safeties.
Weak pass blocking raises sack and safety hazard.
Red-zone finishing governs TD counts.
Rare-event base rates conditioned on style.
Penalty-heavy games alter drive counts.
Weather shifts pass rate and thus sacks, turnovers and scoring events.
Expected team scoring is the basis for count markets.
Event definitions (OT inclusion, which team, official scoring) must be matched.

interactions.hypothesis: Close pre-game spread interacts with total to determine overtime probability: tight, low-scoring games with kicker-dependent scoring have more mass on ties.
Pass-rush strength interacts with OL weakness and QB time-to-throw to raise sack, safety and turnover hazards.
Turnover luck interacts with scoring: takeaways produce short fields and drive TD counts, so realized turnover luck should be regressed before using it for event hazards.

first_event.mechanism: First-score and race-to-N markets resolve on the earliest scoring events: opening possession, scripted early plays, red-zone and kicker behaviour, turnovers giving short fields, and overall team scoring rates. The probability that a team scores first is roughly proportional to its share of early scoring hazard, shifted by who has the ball first; timing markets integrate the hazard over play time.
first_event.target: Which team scores first (or reaches N points first) and at what game time, under contract definition of scoring play.

inputs.why: Who receives first shifts first-score probability by several percentage points.
Opening-drive scripts give team-specific first-drive scoring rates.
Efficiency determines hazard of scoring on each possession.
Opposing defense efficiency suppresses hazard.
Faster tempo increases number of plays before a reference time.
Red-zone finish determines TD vs FG for first score type.
FG range and accuracy matter for first-score timing when drives stall.
Expected scoring split by team gives baseline hazards.
Early turnovers create short fields and quick scores.
What counts as scoring (TD, FG, safety) and how ties/no-score resolve.

interactions.hypothesis: Receiving first and scripted opening drive: a team with high opening-drive TD rate and the first possession is much more likely to score first than the average, and the opposite for slow starters.
Kicker range and weather change whether first-score hazard is TD or FG, shifting timing distribution for TD-specific markets.
Pace affects the number of plays available before a time threshold, so high tempo teams have higher early scoring hazard.

player_td.mechanism: Touchdown scorer markets (first, next, anytime) decompose into team TD expectation, player share of scoring opportunities (goal-line carries, red-zone targets, QB sneaks), timing of the first score, and opposing red-zone defense. Because scoring is rare per player and highly role-concentrated, opportunity usage beats realized TD history, and TD luck regresses.
player_td.target: Probability that a named player scores the first/next TD (or any TD) in the game under contract wording on which scores count.

inputs.why: Role-based scoring rate is the core of the player probability.
Red-zone and goal-line shares reveal opportunity concentration.
Team TD expectation sets total scoring pool.
First-drive usage sets first TD probability.
Possession order affects first scoring team.
Goal-line carry share determines rushing TD probability.
End-zone and red-zone targets determine receiving TD probability.
Injuries change shares of teammates.
Realized TD rate regresses; use opportunity not outcomes.
Opposing red-zone defense and position funneling modulate scoring.
Early exit lowers TD probability and shifts volume to others.
Whether defensive/special-teams TDs and 2-pt plays count.

interactions.hypothesis: Team total and personnel share interact: a goal-line back's TD probability rises with team rushing TD expectation but falls if the QB or WR is the preferred red-zone option, so shares must be conditional on formation.
Spread and script interact with goal-line role: trailing teams pass more near the goal line, shifting TD probability from RBs to WR/TE.
Injury to a teammate interacts with target competition to redistribute red-zone looks.

lineup_role.mechanism: Availability and role-event markets resolve on whether a player is active, starts, plays a threshold of snaps or has a specified role; the information chain is practice participation, official designation, coach statements, depth chart and inactive list, each arriving at known times. Probabilities come from calibrating these signals against historical outcomes by position and injury type.
lineup_role.target: Whether a player plays/starts/reaches a role threshold (active status, snap count, starter) as defined by the contract and source.

inputs.why: Timestamped practice status and designation are primary signals.
Inactive list is the definitive pre-game signal.
Starter ordering and role changes.
Beat reporting and coach statements often precede official reports.
Return-from-injury snap limits affect snap-threshold events.
Clinched or eliminated teams rest or limit starters in late-season games, raising the chance a player on the report is Out.
Recent snap share sets role baseline.
Coach history on resting players and use of designations.
Mid-game exit risk affects threshold events.
Market closing relative to report timing defines information set.
Definitions of active, started, played and source determine settlement.

interactions.hypothesis: Practice sequence and designation interact with position: a limited Friday practice with Questionable label implies different play probabilities for QB, RB and OL.
Seeding stakes interact with injury designation: a minor injury plus clinched seed greatly increases rest probability.
Market close time interacts with report timing: before inactives the market must hedge, after inactives it should converge to 0/1.

player_other.mechanism: Player stat markets (yards, receptions, TDs, passing, rushing) are volume times efficiency, where volume comes from team plays, pass/run mix (script) and role share, and efficiency from opponent-adjusted skill, scheme and environment. Ladders over multiple thresholds require a full distribution with variance from role, script, weather and injury exit, and neighbouring rungs are strongly correlated.
player_other.target: Probability that a player's stat (passing/rushing/receiving yards, receptions, completions, TDs) exceeds a threshold (or beats another player), under official stat settlement.

inputs.why: Team pass volume is the base for QB and receiver counting stats.
Plays per game scales opportunity.
Expected game script splits volume between passing and rushing.
Target share and depth determine receiving distributions.
Carry share determines rushing volume.
Quarterback efficiency drives passing and receiver output.
Opponent adjusted position defense.
Coverage shells shape which receivers get targets.
Pressure and time to throw modify passing efficiency.
Wind and rain reduce passing and shift to rushing.
Teammate injuries redistribute volume.
Distribution shape determines ladder probabilities.
Rung consistency and implied distribution.
DNP/void rules and stat source.
Thresholds within a yard or a reception of the line are exposed to post-game stat revisions and source differences.
Realized hit rates by rung calibrate the model and expose systematic over/under-pricing of specific thresholds.

interactions.hypothesis: Spread and pass rate over expected: trailing teams throw more, so for the underdog's QB and WRs volume rises while efficiency falls against softer coverage; favorites run more.
Pressure and time to throw: a quick-release QB behind a poor OL has a low sack and efficiency loss; a slow-release QB suffers more.
Wind and deep passing: high wind cuts air yards and deep completions, hitting deep-threat receivers and QB yardage more than underneath roles.

combo.mechanism: Combo and parlay markets multiply legs whose outcomes are correlated through game script, team strength and shared stat sources; a fair price requires the joint probability, not the product. Contract wording per leg (void/push handling, overtime) and fees affect value, and executable liquidity is thinner.
combo.target: Joint probability that all (or specified) legs resolve as required, under each leg's wording and the combo's own voiding rules.

inputs.why: Correlation structure between legs determines joint probability.
Team strength underlies winner/margin legs.
Team total consistency across legs.
Script links spreads, totals and player props.
Key-number lattice for margin legs.
Marginal distribution for player legs.
Combo price versus correlated product.
Per-leg void and push handling.
Fees scale with price and apply to the combo as a whole, so a thin correlation edge can be consumed by fee plus spread on the combined contract.
Combo books thinner; slippage large.

interactions.hypothesis: Winner and total legs interact via scoring script: a favorite winning correlates with the over only when its offense drives the margin, not when it wins through defense.
QB yardage and team total legs are positively correlated via pass volume, but negatively correlated with the favorite covering in garbage time.
Per-leg wording interacts with fees: voided legs change the effective payout and combo pricing, so compare executable price after fees to joint probability.

season_outcome.mechanism: Season-level outcome markets (win totals, division, conference, Super Bowl, playoffs, seeds, head-to-head) derive from team strength with uncertainty, schedule, injuries (especially QB) and tiebreaker/bracket rules; simulation produces a coherent set of probabilities in which markets are linked by constraints. Preseason priors rely on roster continuity and regression of past results, in-season updates shift via ratings and luck-adjusted records.
season_outcome.target: Probability of season-long team outcomes (win count, playoff/seed/division/conference/SB result, head-to-head season comparisons) under the contract definition.

inputs.why: Monte Carlo of the schedule with tiebreakers.
Time-varying team strength with uncertainty.
Preseason regression and offseason changes.
Forward-looking schedule difficulty.
Close-game luck regresses; avoids overreaction to records.
QB injury risk and replacement quality dominate season variance.
Season win and playoff odds depend on how many games key players (QB especially) miss, and the distribution of absences is skewed.
Seed and bye effects on title odds.
Constraints across linked markets.
Late-season incentives and rest.
Sportsbook futures prices as benchmark.
Ties, forfeits and cancelled-game handling.

interactions.hypothesis: QB availability interacts with schedule: a backup QB in games against strong divisional opponents changes the win-count distribution non-linearly and the tiebreaker path.
Close-game luck and Pythagorean records interact with the market win total: teams outperforming expected wins have inflated implied ratings and regress.
Bracket path interacts with seed: the one seed bye and home field boost title odds more than the rating difference alone implies.

season_stat.mechanism: Season-long statistical markets (leaders, totals, fantasy, team events, weekly leaders) are sums of per-game outputs integrated over games played, role changes and schedule, and for leader markets an order statistic over many correlated contenders. Early in the season priors dominate; as games accumulate realized totals plus remaining expectation drive probability.
season_stat.target: Season or weekly statistical outcome (player total over threshold, league leader, fantasy rank, team event count) under contract definition.

inputs.why: Realized accrual plus projected remainder.
Games-played risk from injuries.
Max-of-N modeling for leader markets.
Target volume per game is the base for receiving yards, receptions and TD leaders; it must be projected with role stability in mind.
Carry share and goal-line role project season rushing yards and TDs; committee changes mid-season are the main risk.
A regressed QB efficiency prior converts projected attempts to season passing yards and TDs, avoiding overreaction to early-season hot or cold stretches.
Bottom-up fantasy points translation.
Remaining opponents, adjusted by position-specific defense, change per-game expectation and are partly knowable from the schedule.
Season TD totals are the noisiest component; regressing TD luck lowers exceedance probabilities for players who are ahead of pace and raises them for those behind.
Injuries and roster changes to teammates reallocate volume mid-season, so the leader probability moves with the supporting cast.
Game-level variance for aggregation.
Definition of eligible games, ties, and stat source.

interactions.hypothesis: Games-played attrition interacts with per-game rate: leader probabilities for high-rate but injury-prone players are lower than a rate-only model suggests.
Remaining schedule interacts with role stability: soft remaining defenses lift receivers more if target share is stable.
TD regression interacts with realized accrual: players with TD luck to date should have their remaining-season TD rate regressed, lowering exceedance probabilities.

season_award.mechanism: Season awards depend on production relative to peers, team success, narrative momentum and voting mechanics (electorate, ballot timing, position bias). Statistical standing predicts the candidate set but the winner emerges from voter behavior; late-season performance and visible highlights shift media odds, and injury or team collapse can end a candidacy.
season_award.target: Which player wins an annual award (MVP, OPOY, DPOY, ROY, etc.) as announced by the official body.

inputs.why: Production features and historical voting model.
Team success strongly affects voting.
Electorate, ballot close and rules.
Narrative and injury news shift candidacy.
Candidate availability for remaining games.
Efficiency baseline for QB candidates.
TD hot streaks overstate candidacy.
Market price path indicates narrative momentum.
Award definition and eligibility.
Sportsbook award odds as benchmark.

interactions.hypothesis: Team record interacts with production: voters reward high production on winning teams, so a candidate's probability depends on joint standings and statistical rank.
Ballot timing interacts with injuries and late news: if ballots close before the playoffs, late-season injuries still count in the regular-season vote but later narratives do not.

off_field.mechanism: Off-field markets (draft, coaching changes, transactions, Super Bowl events, weekly events) are resolved by organizational decisions, reporting and official announcements rather than play outcomes. Edge comes from institutional calendars and constraints (cap, contracts, draft order), credible reporting, base rates and precise resolution wording.
off_field.target: Occurrence or outcome of an off-field event (draft pick, coach hire/fire, transaction, event prop) as announced by the official source.

inputs.why: Timestamped reporting and source credibility.
Cap and contract timelines make events forced or unlikely.
Draft markets resolve on pick order and selections, so consensus rankings, team needs and order after trades are the baseline.
Coach hazard from record versus expectation.
Base rates for novelty events.
Team results drive firing and draft position.
Official calendars for announcements.
Resolution source and wording.
Off-field markets close at announcements or deadlines; knowing when the market closes relative to the information event avoids look-ahead.
Price reaction to leaks and reports shows how quickly insider information is absorbed and when the market is stale.

interactions.hypothesis: Reporter credibility interacts with timing: leaks close to a deadline are more informative than early speculation, and consensus across independent insiders raises confidence.
Team performance interacts with ownership signals: coach firing hazard rises with losing versus expectation, but strongly depends on contract and cap.

qb_passing_yards.label: QB passing yards ladder
qb_passing_yards.target: Probability a quarterback's official regulation-and-overtime passing yards exceed each rung (e.g. 199.5 to 349.5), or exceed another QB (H2H).
qb_passing_yards.mechanism: Passing yards = dropbacks x (1 - sack rate) x attempt share x completion rate x yards per completion. Volume comes from expected plays (pace), neutral pass rate (PROE) and game script from the spread; efficiency from opponent-adjusted EPA per dropback, air yards and CPOE, and is modified by pressure faced (OL versus pass rush, time to throw), coverage shell and target distribution, receiver and OL availability, weather and roof. The distribution is right-skewed, with garbage-time and overtime volume in the tail and injury exit in the left tail.

inputs.why: Expected pass attempts: neutral pass rate over expected is the volume baseline independent of score.
Plays per game scale dropbacks; slow offenses cap yardage ceiling.
Spread-implied lead/trail states shift pass rate: underdogs gain attempts, favorites lose late volume.
Career-regressed QB EPA/CPOE gives per-attempt yield prior.
Team ANY/A, aDOT and YAC profile determine yards per attempt.
Opponent pass defense EPA/dropback and yards allowed adjusts efficiency.
Two-high/zone shells concede underneath yardage and limit deep shots; man/blitz heavy invites explosives.
Pressure rate and time to throw determine sacks and completion loss.
Opponent pass-rush win rate sets pressure and sack exposure.
OL continuity and injuries change protection quality.
WR/TE/RB availability changes target quality and YAC.
Depth profile sets completion rate versus yards per completion trade-off.
Wind and precipitation cut deep passing and pass rate.
Dome/roof, altitude and surface affect passing environment.
Trailing-team garbage-time volume inflates tail yardage.
End-of-half hurry-ups add yards in short spans.
Starter status and any QB injury limiting mobility or throw.
QB exit or blowout benching truncates attempts.
Play-caller tendencies and recent coordinator changes.
Distribution shape for rung probabilities.
Rung monotonicity; adjacent rungs are one bet.
Overtime inclusion, DNP void, stat source.
Missing EDGE rushers or starting corners/safeties change the pressure and coverage the QB faces, and are often underweighted relative to offensive injuries.
Passing-yard rungs can be within a yard of final after stat corrections; check source and lock time.
Empirical hit rates by rung and price bucket show whether the ladder is biased at round-number thresholds.
Volume and open interest weight how much the price reflects information versus stale quotes, and bound feasible size.
Executed trades show where liquidity actually transacted, informing realistic fills and whether price moves are informed flow.
Defines the left-tail mass for strong favourites and the refund trigger for KXNFLPASSYDSPROT that the generic exit-risk input cannot separate from injuries.
Converts the volume stage into attempts and explains why dropback forecasts overstate attempts for scramble-prone quarterbacks facing strong rushes.
Gives the receiving-corps leg of a passing-yards forecast a continuous quantity rather than the skill-availability flag.
Directly shapes the probability of high rungs and the correlation between a QB's yards and his top receiver's yards.
Supplies the margin-state distribution that drives dropback inflation and the benching line for quarterback yards without using sportsbook lines.
Supplies the completions distribution for KXNFLPASSCOMP and the joint completions-yards structure, which yardage efficiency alone does not give.

interactions.hypothesis: Pressure rate x time to throw: pressure harms a slow-release QB far more than a quick-release one, so expected efficiency loss from a strong pass rush must be scaled by individual time to throw and screen/quick-game usage.
Spread x pass rate: a double-digit underdog's QB gains attempts but meets defenses in prevent shells; yardage rises less than attempts, and the favorite's QB loses garbage-time volume.
Wind x deep passing: wind above ~15 mph removes air yards for high-aDOT offenses while quick-game QBs are less affected; the effect on the yardage mean is larger than on attempts.
Coverage shell x target distribution: against heavy two-high zone, TE/RB targets and short completions rise and deep yards fall, so a QB's yards depend on whether his receivers win underneath.
Receiver availability x pressure: loss of the top WR plus a pressured pocket lowers both separation and time, compounding efficiency loss.

For a heavy favourite the starter's dropbacks fall once the lead passes the coach's benching line: before that point the offence runs, after it the backup throws; for a mid-sized favourite the benching line is never reached and the starter finishes the game. The result is a discontinuity in expected attempts at a coach-specific margin, not a smooth decline in the expected margin.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit P(starter plays 4th quarter) by coach and own-rating expected-margin bucket; contrast starters' attempts in games with lead>=17 at the 3rd quarter versus lead<=10, by coach.

interactions.hypothesis: Pressure turns dropbacks into sacks and scrambles at a rate set by the passer's escape style; a mobile quarterback behind a poor line converts pressure into scrambles that lose attempts but not yardage-per-attempt, while a pocket passer converts the same pressure into sacks. The product of opponent pressure and leakage propensity is what removes attempts.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress attempts per dropback on opponent pressure rate x passer scramble propensity; check the interaction coefficient is positive for scramble-prone passers.

interactions.hypothesis: Two-high shells give up short completions and take away depth: a deep-target corps loses yards per attempt against heavy two-high, while a short-area corps with high yards-after-catch holds up. The sign of the coverage effect depends on the corps' depth profile, so it only appears as a conditional contrast.
interactions.how_to_test: Split per-attempt yield by opponent two-high rate terciles and by team aDOT terciles; look for a sign flip of the coverage coefficient between terciles.

interactions.hypothesis: Wind above roughly 15 mph removes deep completions and compresses the right tail much more than it reduces the mean; below that threshold the tail rate is unaffected. Cold and rain affect catch rate but not the tail in the same way.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate the long-completion rate by wind bin (0-8, 8-15, 15+ mph) for high versus low aDOT offences; test a break at ~15 mph.

interactions.hypothesis: A pass-heavy offence (high neutral PROE) already throws near its ceiling when level, so a trailing score state adds fewer extra dropbacks than for a run-balanced offence; the pass-rate response to a deficit is steeper for low-PROE teams, and the heavy-PROE team's attempts are bounded by plays, not by script.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit dropback share by lead bin separately for terciles of neutral PROE and test whether the deficit slope differs; compare out-of-sample rung calibration of an additive versus a PROE-by-deficit model.

interactions.hypothesis: A high-efficiency quarterback gains less yards per attempt over a replacement-level one when the defence generates heavy pressure, because pressure forces early throws and sacks that efficiency priors measured against average defences do not capture; the efficiency premium saturates in the high-pressure regime.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress yards per dropback on qb_efficiency x opponent pressure-rate tercile using opponent-adjusted data; a negative interaction coefficient confirms saturation.

interactions.hypothesis: In the head-to-head contract both quarterbacks share tempo and wind (positive covariance in passing yards) while the score path is zero-sum (the trailing side throws more), so the correlation between the two totals is positive in shootouts and negative in lopsided games; the H2H probability depends on the covariance, not on two independent means.
interactions.how_to_test: From historical games compute the correlation of the two starters' passing yards in bins of pregame own-rating margin and of wind; compare H2H win-rate calibration for an independent versus a covariance-aware simulation.

interactions.hypothesis: Completion rungs and yardage rungs respond oppositely to target depth: a short-passing plan raises completion probability (more completions per attempt) but lowers yards per completion, and trailing scripts raise attempts while pushing depth up, so the completions ladder and the yards ladder for the same QB can move in different directions when the game plan or script changes.
interactions.how_to_test: In 2018-2025 QB-games, regress completions and passing yards on attempts interacted with aDOT tercile and compare the residual correlation of the two across terciles.

nonlinearities.shape: hump-shaped: attempts rise as the expected deficit grows to about 10-14 points, then flatten or fall as prevent defence, clock-killing and benching take over
nonlinearities.why: Passing volume is not monotone in the expected margin; for 17+ point underdogs yards per attempt fall faster than attempts rise, so a linear expected-margin coefficient mis-prices both tails.

nonlinearities.shape: threshold near 15 mph sustained wind; low sensitivity below, steep above
nonlinearities.why: Deep-pass completion probability drops sharply once wind exceeds the throwing envelope, so the effect on yards is a regime switch and also hits the highest rungs hardest.

nonlinearities.shape: step/atom: a mass at very low yardage for any early exit, nearly independent of the pre-game mean
nonlinearities.why: A concussion or hand injury in the first half creates a discrete outcome far below every rung regardless of efficiency, which is why the left tail of the distribution is a mixture, not a thickened normal.

nonlinearities.shape: convex in the top rungs: small increases in explosive rate move P(300+) far more than P(225+)
nonlinearities.why: A 60-yard completion is worth 20-25 percent of the distance to a 300-yard rung, so the tail probability grows multiplicatively with the explosive rate rather than additively.

mechanism_review.summary: A quarterback's passing yards in one game is a compound sum: the number of completed passes times yards per completion, where completions are a thinned binomial of attempts, attempts are dropbacks minus sacks and scrambles (spikes are counted as incomplete attempts), and dropbacks are team plays times a script-dependent pass rate. Each layer has its own noise. Plays are set by both offenses' tempo and clock behaviour; pass rate swings with the score path (trailing offenses throw, leaders run); a pass's yield depends on the QB's accuracy, receiver separation, depth of target and the defence's pressure and shell; and a small number of explosive completions create a heavy right tail around any rung. Before the number of attempts is even defined, the quarterback must start, stay on the field and not be pulled in a blowout, which is a discrete scenario switch with a left-hand mass at low yardage and, for protected contracts, a refund. The same chain settles the attempt and completion ladders: attempts are the count after dropback leakage, completions the attempts thinned by a depth- and pressure-dependent completion probability.

stages.name: Starter status, snap ceiling and removal scenarios
stages.description: Whether this passer is the QB1 for the whole game, plays part of it or never plays sets the mass at zero-to-low yards and decides which contract variants refund. The inputs are the practice and game-day inactive vintages, how the coach handles a bench-in-blowout, and the base rate of in-game concussion or throwing-hand exits. It is a mixture: full game, truncated game after injury, truncated game after benching, backup start. Each scenario carries its own attempt ceiling and the contract variant (precise, protected, H2H, attempts, completions) pays differently in each.
stages.distribution: Discrete mixture with an atom at 0-40 yards for exits; benching depends on margin and minute, injury exit is near-memoryless (~3-6% per game for QBs, assumption).

stages.name: Team plays and neutral pass tendency
stages.description: Total offensive plays come from both teams' pace and how long each drive lasts (own tempo, opponent's clock drain, penalties, two-minute situations); the pass share of those plays is the team's neutral pass rate over expected, modified by play-caller regime. Early-season sample sizes are small, so the offensive coordinator and the quarterback change since last year matter more than raw last-season rate. This stage produces dropbacks before game state is applied.
stages.distribution: Plays per game roughly normal (sd ~7 plays), dropbacks ~45-70, mild positive skew from overtime; pass-rate regimes are coordinator-specific and persistent within a season.

stages.name: Score path, game script and dropback inflation
stages.description: The score path rewrites the stage above: trailing teams raise pass rate and play faster until the final minutes, leaders run the clock, large leads can end with the starter benched. Because passing yards are positively linked to deficit but only until prevent-defence and late-lead compression bite, the mapping from pre-game margin to expected dropbacks is hump-shaped, not linear. Overtime and two-minute drills add short high-density volume.
stages.distribution: Margin is roughly normal (sd ~13 points) around the own-rating expected margin (nfl.own_rating_game_state_prior); attempts respond concavely, with the heaviest right-tail mass from trailing-by-10-to-17 paths.

stages.name: Dropback outcome split: sack, scramble, throwaway, attempt
stages.description: Only attempts can produce passing yards, so the leakage of dropbacks to sacks (yardage lost on team net but not QB gross), scrambles and kneels shrinks the count before efficiency applies (spikes remain attempts but add zero yards). A pressured pocket either converts to a sack, a scramble or a rushed attempt depending on the passer's mobility and release time, and offensive-line health shifts the split. This is separate from, and not captured by, overall EPA per dropback.
stages.distribution: Binomial leakage per dropback (sack ~6-8% league average, scramble 2-5% by passer), jointly dependent on pressure rate; adds attempt-count variance of a few throws.

stages.name: Per-attempt yield: completion, depth and yards after catch
stages.description: Given an attempt, yardage is completion probability times yards per completion. The QB's accuracy and decision prior, the target depth distribution, the quality of the receiving corps (separation, yards after catch over expected) and the defensive shell decide the mean; opponent adjustment must be done on a per-unit basis. Receiver and defensive-back absences change both the mean and the skew.
stages.distribution: Yards per attempt ~6-8 with sd roughly 2 yards at the game level; completion count approximately binomial; yards per completion right-skewed.

stages.name: Explosive completions, weather and the heavy right tail
stages.description: Wind and rain remove deep shots, domes inflate them, and a single 50-70 yard play can add a fifth to a third of a typical rung distance. The long-completion rate is largely a team-and-receiver property and is more volatile than the mean yield, so tail probability for the highest rungs should be modelled separately rather than inferred from variance of yards per attempt.
stages.distribution: Heavy-tailed compound distribution; the top rung (300+) probability is dominated by the tail of both volume and one or two long plays.

stages.name: Settlement, stat provenance and rung coherence
stages.description: Rungs are nested events of one random variable, so their probabilities must be monotone and adjacent rungs are almost the same bet; official yardage can be corrected after the fact, and different variants refund in different ways. These contract mechanics decide how a model's single yardage distribution maps to prices per variant.
stages.distribution: Nested thresholds: P(Y>=k) is decreasing, increments are the discretized density of the yardage distribution.

stages.name: Attempt and completion count rungs
stages.description: KXNFLPASSATT and KXNFLPASSCOMP settle on counts, not yards. Attempts are dropbacks x (1 - nfl.qb_dropback_to_attempt_leakage) plus the QB's expected spikes added back (that input's measurement counts spikes as leakage, but spikes are official incomplete attempts), so their distribution is driven by team plays, the script-dependent pass rate and the QB's full-game participation, with no efficiency term. Completions are attempts thinned by a per-attempt completion probability that depends on target depth, pressure, receiver separation and the QB's accuracy over expected; short-passing offences convert attempts into completions at 68-72 percent and deep-shot offences at 58-62 percent, so the same attempt count gives different completion rungs. Completions and yards are positively but imperfectly correlated: a dink-and-dunk game can clear a completions rung while missing a yardage rung.
stages.distribution: Attempts: overdispersed count (negative binomial, sd about 7-8 on a mean of 34) with a left mass from early exits; completions: beta-binomial given attempts, integer-valued with nested rungs.

contract_review.settlement_definition: Six live per-game series, all with rules text. KXNFLPASSYDS, KXNFLPASSYDSPRECISE and KXNFLPASSYDSPROT settle YES when the named quarterback 'records N+ passing yards' in the named game (floor_strike = N-0.5); KXNFLPASSATT and KXNFLPASSCOMP use the same 'N+' construction on passing attempts and passing completions. Non-participation: PASSYDS, PASSATT and PASSCOMP settle at the pre-game fair price if the QB 'is active but does not appear in any live play'; PRECISE uses 'active but never takes a snap'; in all of them one play or snap, even nullified by penalty, locks settlement to the recorded statistic. PROT adds a refund at pre-kickoff fair price when the QB plays in the first half but in no play after it (overtime counts as after the half) unless the rung was already reached. KXNFLPASSYDSH2H settles YES if player A has strictly more passing yards than B, 50/50 on equal yards, and fair price if either does not enter or the game is cancelled or not started within 48 hours. No text states whether overtime statistics count, which statistics provider is the source of truth, or what happens to an inactive QB (u1, u5).
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Not stated in any of the six rules texts (only the 'Governing League' disclaimer); treat official NFL game-book/GSIS statistics as the assumed source and capture the Kalshi expiration value to check stat-correction drift. Sleeper is named only in the fantasy series.
variants_and_edge_cases: PASSYDS, PRECISE and PROT share the 'N+' yardage construction (floor_strike = N-0.5); only PROT carries the first-half-only refund. PASSYDS's non-participation trigger is 'does not appear in any live play' while PRECISE's is 'never takes a snap', a wording difference that matters only for a QB who appears in a live play without receiving the snap (e.g. lined up as a receiver or on a special-teams unit).

KXNFLPASSYDSH2H is the only variant whose YES event is a difference of two QBs' totals: 50/50 on equal yards, fair price if either QB does not enter or the game is not started within 48 hours of the original start.

Sampled passing-yards texts never say whether overtime yards count or which statistics provider is the source of truth; the existing draft's 'regulation-and-overtime' is an inference, recorded as CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS u1.

NFL official passing yards are gross yards (sack yardage is deducted only from team net passing), plays nullified by penalty are not credited, and a kneel-down is a rush, so dropbacks that end in sacks or scrambles add zero to this contract.

PROT refund versus PRECISE settlement: an early injury exit after a first-half snap refunds PROT (unless the rung is already hit) but is a normal loss on PRECISE, so the same injury hazard prices differently across the two ladders.
Inactive-QB treatment: every per-game ladder text covers only an 'active' QB who never plays; an inactive or scratched QB is not addressed and is carried as CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS u5.

KXNFLPASSATT and KXNFLPASSCOMP settle on attempt and completion counts: spikes count as attempts (and incompletions), two-point tries are not passing attempts in official statistics, and a pass nullified by penalty is not counted, so attempt rungs depend on clock-management habits that do not affect yardage.

qb_passing_tds_and_ints.label: QB passing TD and interception counts
qb_passing_tds_and_ints.target: Probability a QB throws at least N touchdown passes, or at least N interceptions (or both), in the game as officially scored.
qb_passing_tds_and_ints.mechanism: Passing TDs = red-zone and goal-line pass trips x conversion; team scoring expectation and the run/pass split near the goal line determine opportunities, and passing TD luck regresses strongly. Interceptions = attempts x INT rate, where INT rate mixes QB turnover-worthy throw rate, pressure, aggressiveness, throw depth and defender luck. Both are low-count Poisson-like events whose means depend on script, opponent pass rush/ball skills, weather and QB health.

interactions.hypothesis: Red-zone play-calling x team total: when a high team total comes from field goals and explosive plays rather than goal-line passing, QB TD counts are lower than the total suggests.
Pressure x turnover-worthy throws: pressure raises INT probability mostly for QBs with high aggressiveness, while a zone defense with ball skills converts more of the bad throws.
Trailing script x INT rate: increased attempts and deeper throws when trailing push INT counts up, interplaying with game spread and opponent pass rush.
TD luck x QB rushing: QBs with goal-line rushing use convert fewer passing TDs even with high red-zone volume.

Passing TDs equal the team's TD count times the pass fraction near the goal line; a team that scores mostly through field goals and long runs, or that runs the ball inside the 5, converts a high total into few passing TDs; the product of TD pool and pass share matters, not either one.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress QB TDs on the model team TD mean, goal-to-go pass rate and their product.

interactions.hypothesis: Pressure increases interception probability mainly for QBs with a high turnover-worthy throw rate and mostly when the coverage behind it is zone with ball-hawk safeties; the effect is conditional on both QB trait and defence structure.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate INT probability by pressure bucket within QB aggression terciles and coverage type.

interactions.hypothesis: A large lead in the fourth quarter shifts the state from attempts accumulating to the QB being pulled; the same favourite who runs more also loses its QB for the end of the game, capping TD counts and voiding protected contracts, so attempts are a mixture over two regimes.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare QB attempts and pull rates by pregame spread bucket and halftime lead.

interactions.hypothesis: Above a wind threshold of about 15 mph deep passing falls and goal-line plays tilt toward the run or sneak; passing TD expectation drops more for QBs who depend on deep targets and less for short-game QBs.
interactions.how_to_test: Split QB-games by wind bucket and compare TD per attempt relative to xPassTD.

interactions.hypothesis: If the red-zone TE or WR1 is out, TD per attempt in the red zone falls by more than the loss in yardage-based production because the backup lacks size or contested-catch ability; the effect is concentrated on short-yardage throws.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare red-zone TD per attempt with and without the top red-zone target, controlling for QB.

nonlinearities.shape: right-tail convexity: P(N>=k) in lambda
nonlinearities.why: The probability of 4+ TDs is convex in the mean TD count; small changes in expected attempts and pass share near 2 TDs expected multiply the tail probability by a large factor.

nonlinearities.shape: convex in pressure rate
nonlinearities.why: Interceptions rise slowly with pressure rate at low levels and then steeply when pressure exceeds roughly 35-40% of dropbacks, as throws become hurried and off-balance.

nonlinearities.shape: step with lead and clock
nonlinearities.why: QB pull probability is near zero until the lead reaches about 21 with under ten minutes left, then jumps to high levels, which truncates counts and triggers protected-contract voids.

nonlinearities.shape: regression curve with sample size
nonlinearities.why: The weight of a QB's realized TD rate versus expectation rises with attempts, with half the weight around a thousand attempts; short samples are mostly noise.

mechanism_review.summary: A quarterback's touchdown-pass count is a thinned counting process: attempts times the per-attempt TD probability, where attempts are set by the team's pass volume (game script, pace, pass rate over expected) and the QB's playing time, and the per-attempt TD probability is concentrated in a few attempts inside the 20 and especially the 5-yard line. Therefore the number of goal-to-go and red-zone dropbacks is the key opportunity variable, and the pass-versus-run split near the goal line (the QB's rushing and the goal-line back) determines how many of the team's TDs are passes. Interceptions are a separate thinned process: attempts times the per-attempt interception rate, which is a mixture of bad decisions (turnover-worthy throws), pressure-induced errors, deep targeting and defender skill and randomness (tipped balls, drops by receivers). Both counts are overdispersed relative to Poisson because attempts, script and offensive environment are shared across the game. The quarterback must also play: active-but-no-play voids, protected markets void at a halftime pull, and blowout benching truncates attempts. The career version adds games played, retirement hazard and aging.

stages.name: Participation, protection and blowout pull
stages.description: The count only accumulates while the QB is in the game. Starter status, in-game injury and the coach's willingness to pull a starter in a lopsided score (typically when a lead exceeds about three scores in the fourth quarter) truncate attempts and, for protected contracts, determine voiding. A backup who appears late has a very short window. The model must separate the voided states from the realized-count distribution. nfl.qb is used for starter status only; its catalog QB point value estimated from market line moves is not used.
stages.distribution: Discrete states (does not play / plays full game / pulled early); pull probability rises steeply with lead size in Q4

stages.name: Pass attempt volume from script and pace
stages.description: Attempts equal team dropbacks (plays times pass rate) minus sacks and scrambles. Pass rate depends on expected game state: trailing teams pass much more; the team's neutral pass tendency (PROE), pace, weather (wind) and the run-game quality all shape the distribution. Attempts per game by QB are overdispersed and correlated with the score differential.
stages.distribution: Negative-binomial-like count with mean 28-40; strongly script-dependent; right-skewed

stages.name: Per-attempt TD probability and goal-line allocation
stages.description: Per-attempt TD probability is the sum of long completions (low probability, any field position) and short-yardage red-zone throws. The team's goal-to-go pass rate, the quality of red-zone targets (TE/WR availability), defensive red-zone performance and the QB's own rushing at the goal line determine how many team TDs are passes. TD luck regresses hard: a QB's season TD rate over expectation is mostly noise. Red-zone catcher quality (nfl.red_zone_target_quality) lifts or lowers the per-attempt TD rate for the same QB.
stages.distribution: Binomial thinning of attempts; heavy dependence on red-zone dropback count (about 4 to 6 per game); strong regression to expectation

stages.name: Interception generation process
stages.description: Interceptions arise from throws into coverage: turnover-worthy throw rate (decision quality), pressure, depth of target, ball-hawk defenders and randomness (tipped passes, receivers' bobbles). A single bad game is largely luck; QB-level rate regresses to mean with a half-life of many attempts. Defence-level interception propensity is mostly random but has a skill component (zone coverage with ball-hawk safeties, pass rush forcing hurried throws).
stages.distribution: Low-rate counts: mean 0.6 to 1.0 per game; zero-heavy; overdispersion from game script

stages.name: Dispersion, ladders and cross-statistic dependence
stages.description: TDs and INTs are not independent of attempts or of each other: trailing scripts increase attempts and both TDs and INTs; strong pass-rush games raise INTs and lower TDs. Rung probabilities P(>=k) must be monotone, and overdispersion widens the upper tail beyond Poisson, which is what 4+ TD and 2+ INT rungs depend on.
stages.distribution: Mixed Poisson (gamma-mixed) counts with positive correlation between TD and INT counts via attempts; discrete monotone ladder

stages.name: Career accumulation toward a milestone
stages.description: KXNFLCAREERPASSTDS (title only) is a career milestone: the probability of crossing a career total depends on the remaining distance, expected games per future season (injury attrition, benching, retirement hazard by age), the per-game TD rate with age decline and offensive-system changes, so it is a sum over a random number of remaining seasons and games rather than a per-game question. The single-season accrual series is no longer filed here.
stages.distribution: Sum of per-game counts over a random number of games across seasons; retirement and injury truncate; age-dependent mean

stages.name: Settlement rules
stages.description: The label is determined by the official stat sheet, the fair-price void for no live play, the half-time protected rule (no postponement clause appears in the sampled TD/INT texts); passing TD credit excludes plays nullified by penalty, and stat corrections can change counts.
stages.distribution: Deterministic rules plus small stat-correction probability

contract_review.settlement_definition: Four live series; three have rules text (KXNFLPASSTDS, KXNFLPASSTDSPROT, KXNFLPASSINT), KXNFLCAREERPASSTDS is TITLE_ONLY. Single-game count markets resolve YES if the named QB records at least N passing touchdowns or N passing interceptions (floor_strike 3.5 = '4+' TDs, 2.5 = '3+' INTs, strike_type greater). If he is active but does not appear in any live play the market settles to the fair market price before game start; once he appears in one live play, even one nullified by penalty, it settles on the recorded statistic. KXNFLPASSTDSPROT additionally settles at the pre-kickoff fair price if the QB plays in the first half but in no play after it (including overtime), unless he already reached the count. No sampled text states whether overtime statistics count for the standard props, or the stat-correction window; source is the official game statistics. The career series' counting window and strike construction are not visible.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official NFL game statistics (passing touchdowns, interceptions, completions, attempts) as credited in the official scoring and statistical summary; Kalshi settles on the 'official final result' with the participation rule for the named player.
variants_and_edge_cases: Strike construction: floor_strike 3.5 ('4+') for TDs and 2.5 ('3+') for interceptions on integer counts; rungs are nested P(>=1) >= P(>=2) >= ... and a ladder must be monotone; no push.

Standard versus protected TD contracts differ for a QB pulled in a blowout or injured at halftime: standard markets stay live with a truncated count; protected markets void to a pre-kickoff fair price unless the count is already reached. No protected interception series is live.

Interceptions count as official interceptions thrown (pick-sixes included); a nullified play counts only for participation ('even if nullified by penalty'), while the counted statistic follows the official stat sheet.
Overtime statistics are not mentioned for the standard props; protected text mentions overtime only for the participation test.
KXNFLCAREERPASSTDS (title only) is a career milestone accrual over remaining seasons; the season passing-TD, completions and attempts series are no longer filed here and are not claimed.

rushing_yards.label: Player rushing yards and attempts
rushing_yards.target: Probability a player's rushing yards (or attempts) exceed a threshold, or exceed another player.
rushing_yards.mechanism: Rushing yards = rush attempts x yards per attempt. Attempts come from team rush volume (neutral run rate, script: favorites and leading teams run more, trailing teams less) times the player's carry share in the committee; yards per attempt from OL run blocking and yards before contact, RB creation (yards over expected), opponent front and box counts and a heavy explosive-run tail. Variance is high because a few long runs dominate.

Expected lead/trail state determines rush volume; leaders run out clock.
A low PROE team runs more in neutral situations.

Prevents the common error of letting spread-driven carries inflate expected yards at the neutral yards-per-carry rate in the favourite's own rung.
Converts opponent run defence from a single rank into a game-plan-specific yard expectation for each runner.

interactions.hypothesis: Spread x run rate: a heavy favorite leading late converts to many carries, but the carries go to whichever back is on the field (often the backup), so the starter's carry share is score-state-dependent.
Box count x run blocking: light boxes against a strong run-block unit give higher yards before contact; against stacked boxes, only high yards-over-expected backs keep efficiency.
Weather x run share: bad weather increases rush attempts but also decreases pass efficiency, and the net effect on RB yards depends on opponent run defense.
Committee splits x injury: when the lead back is limited, share to the backup rises non-linearly, while goal-line carries may go to a third back.

When a favourite leads in the second half the extra carries go to whichever runner is on the field, often the backup, and they gain fewer yards per carry because boxes are loaded; the lead back's expected yards therefore rise less than team carries, and the backup's rise more.
interactions.how_to_test: Split the lead back's carry share and yards per carry by lead state and quarter; compare to backups' in the same states.

interactions.hypothesis: Yards before contact multiply blocking quality by the defence's weakness in the gaps the offence uses most; a strong line against a stout front in its chosen direction yields little, while a mediocre line attacking a soft gap does well.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress yards before contact on blocking score x gap-weighted front weakness; check the product term beats separate additive rankings.

interactions.hypothesis: When the lead back is limited, carries move to the backup by more than the reduction in the lead's share and a third back often takes goal-line work, so the share vector shifts discontinuously at certain snap-count caps rather than smoothly.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate share vectors for games with lead back at 0, 1-50 and 51-100 percent of normal snaps and test for a break at the cap.

interactions.hypothesis: Designed quarterback runs and scrambles use up goal-line and short-yardage carries that would go to the back, and the effect is largest when the quarterback is a runner and the opponent pressures heavily.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare back carries per game with and without a running quarterback, split by opponent pressure rate.

interactions.hypothesis: Bad weather raises the run share, but whether yield per carry rises or falls with blocking style (zone/power versus perimeter runs) is a hypothesis only, not evidenced here; the net yardage effect is the sum of a volume gain and an unsigned yield change.
interactions.how_to_test: Interact weather indicators with run-scheme type in a yards model and see whether the net weather effect changes sign across schemes.

interactions.hypothesis: Yards in a game combine a number of carries with a heavy-tailed per-carry yield; the probability of a high rung depends on the covariance of carries and explosive rate (a heavy workload gives more draws from the tail), so volume and explosiveness compound rather than add.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate yards with carries and explosive draws independent versus joint and compare P(100+) calibration across runner types.

interactions.hypothesis: The probability that a lead back tops the game's rushing list rises steeply with his team's expected margin because late clock-killing carries go to the winner; for a committee back the same margin raises a teammate's chance instead, so the margin effect is conditional on carry-share concentration.
interactions.how_to_test: On 2016-2025 games, regress an indicator of leading the game in rushing on own-rating expected margin interacted with carry-share Herfindahl of the back's team.

nonlinearities.shape: convex in the leading side: carries accelerate once a lead exceeds about a touchdown late in the game and flatten once the clock is nearly exhausted
nonlinearities.why: Late-lead carries are mostly forced by the clock, so a spread of 3 and a spread of 10 differ in expected carries by more than the linear spread difference suggests.

nonlinearities.shape: piecewise: a jump from near full workload to a capped share at the first game back
nonlinearities.why: Teams use snap counts on returning backs, so carry shares are step-like in practice rather than continuous in injury severity.

nonlinearities.shape: heavy-tailed: P(100+) is roughly linear in explosive rate times carries, while P(60+) is nearly independent of it
nonlinearities.why: The highest rungs are reached only through long runs; below it the steady-yardage mass determines the probability, so the response of rung probabilities to the explosive rate increases with the rung.

nonlinearities.shape: hazard-mixture: a point mass at truncated carries proportional to time of exit
nonlinearities.why: A first-half exit leaves a runner under most rungs regardless of efficiency, causing a bimodal outcome distribution for backs.

mechanism_review.summary: A runner's rushing yards equal his carries times his yards per carry, and both have to be forecast through different chains. Carries are team rushing plays times the share this runner takes; team rushing plays come from total plays and run rate, which respond strongly to the score path (leaders run to burn clock, trailers abandon the run), and the share depends on his role in a committee by down, distance and the goal line, backup handoffs in blowouts, and his health and snap ramp. Yards per carry come from the blocking and the front he faces (box count, run gap), the runner's ability to create yards over what the blockers provide, and a heavy right tail from explosive runs that makes yardage rungs very discontinuous. For quarterbacks the same contract records scrambles and designed runs, which come from pressure and scheme instead. The settlement rules decide whether the position is refunded, lost or settled when a runner is injured or rested.

stages.name: Who carries the ball: lead back, committee and quarterback share
stages.description: The runner's share of team rushes is set by his designated role (early down, passing down, goal line, change of pace), by the quarterback's own designed runs, and by the competition for touches in the room. Committee rotations are partly predetermined and partly reactive to performance and fatigue. The prior is the last several games' carry share conditioned on game state, but a coaching change or an acquisition can reset it.
stages.distribution: Carry shares among backs are Dirichlet-like with strong negative correlation; a lead back's share is typically 55-80 percent of running back carries, with persistent regimes.

stages.name: Health, snap ramp and in-game exit
stages.description: Running backs carry the highest in-game injury rate among skill positions, and returning runners are held to snap counts; either removes carries quickly and non-linearly, and a loss of the lead back hands carries to the next on the depth chart rather than reducing the team's carries. The outcome is a mixture of full-workload, ramp, and early-exit scenarios.
stages.distribution: Mixture distribution with a large mass at truncated workloads (a back exits in perhaps 8-12% of games, assumption), producing a left tail not captured by the mean.

stages.name: Team rushing volume from plays and run rate
stages.description: Team rushes follow total plays (tempo and clock) times run rate; a low-PROE team has more neutral-situation runs, and a run-first coach keeps running under pressure. This stage determines the pool the share applies to, and is correlated with the quarterback and the line's health.
stages.distribution: Team rushes ~20-35 per game; moderately dispersed with weak positive skew from clock-killing finishes.

stages.name: Score path: leading offences run, trailing offences stop
stages.description: The pre-game margin distribution, realised as the game unfolds, determines late-game carry volume: favourites generate extra clock-killing carries (often to backups when starters rest), underdogs shift to the air by the third quarter. Garbage-time carries are low-efficiency and may be taken by a different back, so volume and yield change together.
stages.distribution: Margin ~ normal around the own-rating expected margin from nfl.own_rating_game_state_prior (sd ~13), never the spread; carries are convex in lead in the leader's fourth quarter and capped by the clock.

stages.name: Yards per carry: blocking, front and scheme match
stages.description: Yards before contact depend on the offensive line's run-block quality and the front and box count, while yards after contact depend on the runner. Zone-versus-gap scheme and the defensive front's per-gap weakness determine the run direction yield, and stacked boxes concede explosive plays when beaten. These interact, so an offence-defence pairing rather than separate rankings is needed.
stages.distribution: Yards per carry per game ~ 3.5-5.5 with a per-carry distribution heavily right-skewed (median 3, mean 4.4, long runs of 15+ are 5-8% of carries).

stages.name: Explosive-run tail and quarterback scramble yield
stages.description: One or two 20-plus runs decide whether a back clears a high rung, and these are property of the back, the blocking scheme and the opposing safeties. For a quarterback, scrambles on pressured plays and designed runs produce the yards, with yardage per scramble depending on coverage and the passer's speed.
stages.distribution: Compound of carries with a Pareto-like right tail; per-game rung probability for 100+ driven by 0-2 explosive runs.

stages.name: Contract rules: refunds, non-participation, ties
stages.description: Each variant maps availability and ties differently: the protected ladder refunds for first-half-only participation, H2H refunds when a player does not enter, the attempts and longest-rush series refund only an active player who never appears, and game-most gives No to a non-participant with 1/N on ties. A correct valuation applies a different participation probability to each payoff while sharing one carry and yardage forecast. The scalar series add two more payoff shapes on the same yardage distribution: the escalator is a cubic in yards floored to tens (value concentrated in the 120-200 yard tail) and the ladder is linear with a 400-yard cap (value equals the mean), and neither text refunds a non-playing back.
stages.distribution: Variant-specific payoff functions of the same yardage and participation random variables.

stages.name: Game rushing leader and carry-count rungs
stages.description: KXNFLMOSTRSHYDS compares the named runner with every ball carrier on both sides, so the opposing workhorse and a running quarterback are rivals; the projected winner's lead back usually holds the top because clock-killing carries come late. KXNFLRSHATT counts carries rather than yards, so it rests on carry share and team rush volume (stages s1-s4) with no yardage term, and KXNFLLONGRSH is a maximum over the runner's carries driven by the per-carry tail of nfl.rush_yardage_tail, which gives P(k+) per carry for k = 7 to 40 and so covers low strikes such as over 6.5 yards.
stages.distribution: Leader indicator from a joint simulation with a small 1/N tie mass; carry counts are overdispersed integers (variance about 1.5x the mean); longest rush is a maximum over carries of heavy-tailed per-carry draws.

contract_review.settlement_definition: Eight live per-game series, all with rules text. KXNFLRSHYDS and KXNFLRSHYDSPROT settle YES when the player 'records N+ rushing yards' (floor_strike N-0.5); an active player who appears in no live play settles at the pre-game fair price and one live play (even nullified) locks settlement to recorded yards; PROT refunds at pre-kickoff fair price when the player plays in the first half and in no play after it (overtime counts as after the half) unless the rung was already reached. KXNFLESCALATORRSHYDS pays floor(10000 x (y/200)^3)/10000 with y = official rushing yards floored to tens, capped at 200 and floored at 0; KXNFLLADDERRSHYDS pays $0.0025 per rushing yard capped at 400 yards; neither scalar text has a non-participation clause. KXNFLRSHATT ('9+ rushing attempts') and KXNFLLONGRSH ('longest rush of over 6.5 yards') use the live-play activation rule. KXNFLRSHYDSH2H: strictly more yards is YES, 50/50 on equal yards, fair price if either player does not enter. KXNFLMOSTRSHYDS is a max over every player in the game: No for a non-participant, 1/N on ties, fair price if not started within 48 hours. Overtime and the statistics source are not stated in any text (u1, u6).
contract_review.settlement_data_source: The sampled rules never name a provider; 'Governing League' official statistics are implied and the existing draft's mention of kneel-down counting is a statistical convention, not text in the rules.
variants_and_edge_cases: KXNFLRSHYDSPROT lists a quarterback (Drew Lock, 40+) and a back in the same series: quarterback rushing yards (scrambles and designed runs, sack yardage excluded) and running back yards need different mechanisms, but share one ticker family.

Rushing yards can be negative (kneel-downs count as rushing attempts for the QB or back who takes the knee), which matters near low rungs and for H2H differences, though negative totals are rare in a full game.

Scalar series: KXNFLESCALATORRSHYDS (cubic in yards floored to tens, cap 200, negatives pay 0) and KXNFLLADDERRSHYDS (linear $0.0025 per yard, cap 400) now have rules text; neither states a non-participation refund, so an inactive or non-playing back appears to pay the zero-yard value (u9).
Protected variant: overtime appears only in the definition of post-half participation; whether overtime yards count and how a player with no first-half play settles are unstated and carried as u6.

KXNFLMOSTRSHYDS resolves No for a non-participant and 1/N on ties, while the binary yards, attempts and longest-rush series refund an active non-playing player at fair price and the H2H refunds if either player does not enter (the scalar escalator and ladder texts state no refund); one injury report therefore moves the variants in different directions.
KXNFLRSHATT counts official rushing attempts: QB scrambles and kneel-downs are rushing attempts, so a mobile QB's count includes scrambles, while a back's count comes from designed carries only.

receiving_yards_and_receptions.label: Receiving yards and receptions
receiving_yards_and_receptions.target: Probability a player's receiving yards or receptions exceed a threshold (or exceed another player) in the game.
receiving_yards_and_receptions.mechanism: Receptions = team targets x player target share x catch rate; yards = receptions x yards per catch (air yards + YAC). Team targets follow pass attempts (pace, PROE, script); target share depends on route participation, role (slot/outside/inline), teammate competition and coverage; catch rate on aDOT, QB accuracy and pressure; yards on depth and YAC. Opponent coverage scheme and the CB matchup shift share and efficiency; injuries redistribute shares; weather shifts depth.

inputs.why: Target share, air-yards share, TPRR and aDOT.
Route participation separates role from usage.
Team pass-rate over expected sets the targets pool and is stable by coordinator regime, with larger weight than recent receiving numbers.
Trailing script boosts targets for volume receivers.
Teammate availability redistributes targets.
Man/zone and shell influence slot vs outside production.
Shadow coverage suppresses share for the covered WR.
Opponent-adjusted yield by alignment and position.
Receiver catch ability and YAC over expected.
Depth drives yards-per-catch and variance.
QB accuracy, which also alters completion probability.
Pressure shortens routes and reduces targets to deep receivers.
Personnel (11/12) changes who is on the field.
A receiver returning from injury or limited in practice often has a snap or route cap, cutting expected targets below baseline.
Wind and rain reduce deep targets.
Distribution of receptions vs yards.
Receptions and yards ladders share information; consistency check.
Contract treatment of a player who does not play (void versus loss) and the stat source determine whether the position is exposed to DNP risk.
Tracking-based separation, cushion and YAC over expected help split receiver skill from QB and scheme in per-target yardage.
Reception and yards ladders have different calibration by rung; empirical hit rates anchor tails.
Volume and open interest weight how much the price reflects information versus stale quotes, and bound feasible size.
Executed trades show where liquidity actually transacted, informing realistic fills and whether price moves are informed flow.
Directly addresses the largest error source for WR2/WR3/TE/RB reception and yards rungs when a starter is out and prices change within hours.
Required for KXNFLLONGREC and for tails of escalator yardage contracts, neither of which can be priced from mean and variance.
Moves a receiver's expected share at the target stage, independently of dvp efficiency, and is the reason RB/TE reception rungs often shift with opponent scheme.
Explains differences in reception overdispersion between teams with equal average shares and controls the second-option response when a primary receiver is out.
Gives the probability that the named catcher posts the most receiving yards in the game, the only quantity KXNFLMOSTRECYDS pays on.
