interactions.hypothesis: Coverage shell x target distribution: slot receivers gain share against man-heavy teams with a weak slot corner, while outside deep threats lose against two-high shells; the same defense helps different players differently.
Teammate injury x target competition: removing the WR1 raises WR2/TE targets but increases coverage attention; the net per-target efficiency typically falls.
aDOT x wind x QB arm: a deep-threat receiver with a low catch rate sees both volume and catch probability fall in wind; slot players with high catch rate are insulated.
Pressure x time to throw: heavy pressure reduces target to deep routes and increases dump-offs to RB/TE, changing reception counts more than yards.

Expected targets equal team pass attempts times route participation times targets per route run; an error in any term scales the entire expectation, and each is estimated with separate noise. A receiver with strong TPRR on a run-heavy team can have fewer targets than a lesser receiver on a pass-heavy team.
interactions.how_to_test: Decompose realised targets into attempts, route rate and TPRR, and compare the explained variance of the product model to a model using lagged target counts.

interactions.hypothesis: The target gain of a remaining receiver when a teammate is out depends on which role the missing player filled and on how concentrated the quarterback's reads are: a concentrated passer gives the next read a larger boost, a spread passer distributes gain across several receivers.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate share change by receiver role in games without the top target, split by quarterback concentration terciles.

interactions.hypothesis: A shadowing cornerback against the WR1 lowers his share and his yield, but the same defence's funnel toward the slot or tight end offsets for others; the net effect on a given receiver depends on alignment, so position-level opponent features flip sign across alignments.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare target share changes for slot, outside and TE under shadow versus zone defences using play-level alignment tags.

interactions.hypothesis: Receptions and yards per reception are negatively correlated at the player level, since deep targets are caught less often; the joint distribution matters for the cubic escalator and for yards rungs because a high-yardage game for a deep threat arrives with few catches, and for a slot receiver with many.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate correlation of per-game receptions and yards per reception by aDOT tercile; test whether product-of-marginals mis-prices the yards 80th percentile.

interactions.hypothesis: When trailing, pass volume rises and running backs and slot receivers get more routes while tight ends in 12 personnel lose them; the sign of the script effect on routes depends on the receiver's usual personnel role.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress route share on expected margin by position and personnel role and check heterogeneity by role.

interactions.hypothesis: The cubic escalator payoff (min(s,14)/14)^3 for receptions and (y/200)^3 for yards is convex only below its cap: for a receiver whose expected total sits well under 14 receptions or 200 yards extra variance raises fair value, but for a high-volume receiver near or above the cap the payoff goes flat and extra variance lowers value, so the sign of the variance effect flips with the mean relative to the cap.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate the escalator payoff for receivers across mean tiers with fixed mean and two dispersion levels; check the sign of the fair-value difference changes near 10-14 receptions and 150-200 yards.

nonlinearities.shape: piecewise: near-zero route share while inactive, ramped fraction (e.g. 40-70 percent of normal) in return games, normal after
nonlinearities.why: Returning players are on routes caps that do not scale smoothly with the injury designation, so the expected route share is a piecewise function with a jump at the first game back.

nonlinearities.shape: heavy upper tail: longest reception exceeding strike rises sublinearly in the number of catches
nonlinearities.why: The maximum of N heavy-tailed lengths grows with log N, so doubling expected receptions raises P(longest over 40) far less than doubling.

nonlinearities.shape: saturating: receptions rise concavely with targets at the high end because catch rate falls as target depth and contested rate rise
nonlinearities.why: Players with extreme target share are asked to take lower-quality targets, so extra targets convert at a lower rate than the average target.

nonlinearities.shape: threshold near 15 mph: little effect below, rapid drop in deep targets and yards above
nonlinearities.why: Wind removes deep targets and the yardage tail; receptions of short routes are insensitive, so the effect concentrates in high yards rungs of deep receivers.

nonlinearities.shape: winner-take-all: flat near zero below the field's typical top value, then steeply rising
nonlinearities.why: A catcher's chance of leading the game barely moves while his projection sits below the opposing top receiver's, then rises sharply once it overtakes it, so small mean changes near the crossover are worth far more than elsewhere.

mechanism_review.summary: A receiver's yards and receptions are the product of three counts that need separate modelling: how many routes he runs, how many targets he draws per route, and what each target yields. Routes follow snaps, offensive formation and the team's passing volume (which is itself a function of tempo, pass tendency and score path). Targets per route depend on his role (alignment, depth), competition from teammates, the quarterback's tendency to concentrate reads, and the defender and coverage he sees. Targets convert to catches at a rate depending on depth and quarterback accuracy, and catches to yards through air yards and yards after the catch, with a heavy right tail from one long play. Receptions are a small count with strong overdispersion; yards are a compound of receptions and per-catch distance. Contract shape then matters: binary rungs need tail probabilities, linear ladders need means, the cubic escalator needs the upper tail, and the longest-reception contract needs the maximum of the receiver's catch lengths.

stages.name: Availability, snap and route participation
stages.description: Whether the receiver is active and for what fraction of the offence's dropbacks he is running a route is the base of everything. Practice-status vintages, return-from-injury snap caps, the depth chart behind him, and in-game injury drive the route count. A returning player on a pitch count or a third receiver in 12-personnel behaves very differently from a full-time starter; route participation is not equal to snap share because blocking snaps and screens do not count.
stages.distribution: Route participation is bounded (0 to ~100% of dropbacks) with a mass near 0 for inactive, a ramp for returning players, and near-constant for ironclad starters.

stages.name: Team pass attempts available to be targeted
stages.description: The team's dropbacks and pass attempts form the pool: tempo, pass tendency over expectation and the score path define it, and the defence's tendency to force the opponent into passing or running changes the pool. Pool size is a stable function of coordinator regime plus a game-script component, and the receiver's expected share is applied to it, so the pool and the share multiply. The score-path distribution behind nfl.script is taken from the market-free nfl.own_rating_game_state_prior, never from the spread or total. The starting quarterback is the largest single shifter of this pool and of target concentration: a backup start changes attempts, depth of target and which receivers the passer reads, and for the protected variant the receiver's own in-game exit (nfl.in_game_exit_risk) truncates routes after the first half. The catalog measurement values the starter-minus-backup gap from market line moves; that component is a benchmark only and is replaced here by an own valuation (starter versus backup EPA per dropback from nfl.qb_efficiency, or nfl.qb_scenario_rating_drop for team ratings).
stages.distribution: Attempts ~28-45 per team-game with positive skew from trailing scripts; overdispersed Poisson-like count.

stages.name: Target share and who absorbs a teammate's vacated targets
stages.description: Given routes, targets per route run depends on alignment, separation skill, role (primary read versus decoy), the quarterback's progression habits and competing receivers. When a teammate is out, targets flow nonuniformly: to the slot, to the tight end or to the back depending on the role the missing player filled and the scheme. The with-without evidence for a specific team is thin, and the redistribution is the largest single source of error for second and third options.
stages.distribution: Target counts are overdispersed (negative binomial-like), team-share fractions are Dirichlet-like across receivers with strong negative correlation among teammates.

stages.name: Defensive allocation of targets and coverage
stages.description: The defence funnels targets by position and alignment (which units it tolerates being thrown at) and uses shell, man or zone coverage and possible shadowing of the top receiver. The effect on a single receiver is conditional on alignment (slot versus outside versus inline) rather than only on position, and a shadow assignment removes both share and efficiency for the covered player.
stages.distribution: Share and yield effects are modest (a few percentage points of share) but lumpy for shadow assignments; position-level aggregates mask alignment-level variation.

stages.name: Catch probability and yards per target
stages.description: Catch probability depends on target depth, receiver hands and separation, quarterback accuracy and pressure; yards per catch splits into air yards and yards after the catch (tackle breaking, scheme). Receptions and yards are linked negatively through depth: deep threats have fewer catches but more yards per catch, so a receptions rung and a yards rung on the same player respond differently to the same inputs.
stages.distribution: Receptions binomial in targets (variance ~ n p(1-p)); yards per reception log-normal-like with heavy right tail; negative correlation between catches and yards per catch across players.

stages.name: Single-play extremes and longest-reception structure
stages.description: The longest reception is a maximum of that player's catches, so it depends on the number of receptions and on the length distribution of each, with a right tail dominated by yards after the catch. For yards escalators, a single 60-yard play moves the value by ten buckets. This stage is separate from the mean because the extreme-length behaviour is a property of the player and offence, not of the average yield.
stages.distribution: Maximum of N heavy-tailed lengths: with N around 4-6 the longest is often 20-35 yards with a long right tail (>60 about 5-8% for a WR1, assumption).

stages.name: Contract payoff mapping and ladder coherence
stages.description: The same predictive distribution must be translated into four payoff shapes: threshold probability, cubic expectation, linear capped mean, and maximum-over-strike. Rungs of one variable are nested, receptions and yards ladders share information, and the void rules determine how availability news is priced.
stages.distribution: Payoffs: indicator, convex cubic with cap, linear with cap, maximum statistic.

stages.name: Game-most receiving yards and rush-plus-receive sums
stages.description: Two live series leave the single-receiver threshold frame. KXNFLMOSTRECYDS asks whether one catcher out-gains every other catcher in the same game: a slot receiver on a team facing a pass-funnel defence can be the favourite even with a lower mean than the opposing alpha, because one 50-yard catch reorders the top. KXNFLRRYDS sums a back's carries and receptions, so the lead back's carry share, his yards per carry and his receiving role all feed one total, with a trailing script trading carries for targets.
stages.distribution: Max over 8-14 catchers is right-skewed with a 1/N tie atom near zero; the rush-plus-receive sum is a convolution of two overdispersed counts with role-dependent correlation.

talent_strength.note: Receiver hands and separation plus quarterback accuracy; skill prior regression is unspecified.

opponent_matchup.note: Coverage shell, shadowing, position yield and target funnel share by alignment.

role_personnel.note: Share, route role and redistribution when teammates are out.

availability_news.note: Return-from-injury caps and participation; inactive timing relative to quote time is not specified in the catalog text. Quarterback status (nfl.qb) and the receiver's own in-game exit risk are now attached; a backup-QB start is treated as a regime that rescales every receiver's volume.

coaching_scheme.note: Personnel groupings and motion from the offence side, and defensive schemes; coordinator-regime effects on target distribution are only implied.

environment.note: Wind and rain cut deep targets; dome and surface not attached to this archetype.

pace_volume.note: Pass attempts pool = plays (nfl.pace) x pass rate (nfl.proe); both are attached in stage s2; nfl.pace is a catalog input newly attached here, not part of the original archetype list so it has no audit entry.

distribution_variance.note: Overdispersion of targets and catch lengths; the receiver-to-quarterback and receiver-to-receiver within-game correlations in nfl.corr are now attached in stage s6 and fed from the play-level dataset (used for the H2H and combined-yards variants).

officiating_rules.note: Crew tendencies affect receivers through pass-interference and holding calls that nullify plays; those effects are small and noisy relative to target share and are not credited as receiving yards.

contract_review.settlement_definition: Twelve live per-game series; all but KXNFLLONGESTREC have rules text. 'N+' rungs (KXNFLRECYDS, KXNFLRECYDSPROT, KXNFLREC, KXNFLRECPROT, KXNFLRRYDS) resolve YES when the player's official receiving yards, receptions or combined rushing-plus-receiving yards reach the integer rung; for KXNFLRECYDS, KXNFLREC and KXNFLRRYDS an active player who appears in no live play settles at the pre-game fair price and one live play (even nullified) locks settlement to recorded stats (the sampled PROT texts are truncated before any such clause); the PROT variants add the first-half-only refund (overtime counts as after the half). Escalators pay a cubic function of receptions (capped at 14) or of receiving yards bucketed to tens (capped at 200, negatives pay 0); ladders pay $0.05 per reception (cap 20) or $0.0025 per yard (cap 400). KXNFLRECYDSH2H pays 50/50 on equal yards and fair price if either player does not enter or the game is not started within 48 hours. KXNFLMOSTRECYDS is a max over every player in the game: No for a non-participant, 1/N on ties, fair price if not started within 48 hours. KXNFLLONGESTREC (longest reception) is title-only. Overtime inclusion and the statistics source are not stated in any receiving text (u1).
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official NFL statistics are implied by the 'Governing League' wording but the sampled rules do not name a provider or a correction rule; capture the Kalshi expiration value and compare with the game book.
variants_and_edge_cases: Four payoff shapes share one statistic: binary N+ (KXNFLRECYDS/REC and their PROT versions), convex cubic escalator (KXNFLESCALATORRECYDS: yards bucketed to tens, capped at 200, negative totals pay 0; KXNFLESCALATORREC: capped at 14), linear ladder (cap 400 yards, cap 20 receptions) and the title-only longest-reception series (KXNFLLONGESTREC).
Escalator yards use y = min(200, max(0, 10 x floor(s/10))): bucket rounding down to tens makes the payoff a step function of final yards, so yardage between 190 and 199 pays the same 0.8573.

Sampled texts do not state overtime handling or the official statistics source for receptions/yards; reception credited on a play nullified by penalty is not credited under standard NFL scoring, but the 'live play' appearance rule counts it for activation only.

KXNFLRECYDSH2H voids to fair price if either player does not enter the game and pays 50/50 on equal yards; KXNFLRECYDSPROT adds the first-half-only refund; KXNFLMOSTRECYDS instead resolves No for a non-participant and 1/N on ties, so one injury report moves these variants in opposite directions.

KXNFLRRYDS (rushing plus receiving yards) shares the 'N+' activation wording but its total includes carries, so for running backs the rushing chain (carry share, run efficiency) is part of this archetype.

KXNFLLONGESTREC is the only title-only series: its strike construction, activation rule and the value of a zero-catch game are not visible. The former rules-sampled KXNFLLONGREC was re-filed to the extreme-play-length archetype, so no longest-reception rules text is available inside this archetype. KXNFLREC and KXNFLRECPROT now have rules text matching the yardage rungs.
Scalar escalator and ladder texts carry no activation or refund clause (the binary rungs refund an active non-playing player), so an inactive receiver's scalar position has unstated treatment (u7).

anytime_first_td_scorer.label: Anytime, first and next TD scorer
anytime_first_td_scorer.target: Probability that a player scores a touchdown (first, next, or any) as defined by contract; no-score mass for first-TD markets.
anytime_first_td_scorer.mechanism: Player scoring probability = team expected touchdowns x player share of scoring opportunities, adjusted for opponent red-zone defense. For first-TD markets, multiply by the probability the player's team scores first and the player's share of that team's first TDs (first-drive script, who has the ball first). Red-zone and goal-line role dominates; realized TD luck regresses; in-game exit risk and role changes matter; team-level scoring (via total and spread) sets the pool.

For first-TD markets, the team with the first possession has higher first-score probability and its goal-line players gain proportionally.

Absences of teammates or rotational players change who receives goal-line touches, shifting scoring shares non-proportionally.

Opponent red-zone defense and position funneling.

interactions.hypothesis: Team TD pool x player share: shares are conditional on the game environment, so a goal-line back's share shrinks if the offense's expected TDs come from passing.
First-possession x opening script: a team that gets the ball first and scripts early runs for its goal-line back raises that back's first-TD odds.
Injury to a competitor x usage: when a teammate in the red-zone group is out, share shifts nonlinearly to the next in the same role.
Scoring pool x spread: a trailing team scores more through the air; a leading team scores on the ground late, altering first versus anytime probabilities.

When a primary goal-line back is out, the vacated carries go mainly to whichever back has the next heaviest inside-5 role, not to the next-highest snap player; the shift is non-proportional and can leave a pass-catching back's TD rate unchanged while a rotational power back doubles.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare TD probability change for each teammate when a goal-line player is inactive vs active, grouped by replacement role (power back vs receiving back vs QB), controlling for team xTD.

interactions.hypothesis: Team TDs are expected scoring trips times the TD fraction of those trips; a team with an aggressive 4th-and-goal policy and good red-zone offence converts the same total into more TDs, scaling every scorer's probability, while FG-prone teams do the reverse.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress team TD count on the model TD mean with interaction terms for go-for-it rate and red-zone TD rate; the interaction coefficient reveals the uplift.

interactions.hypothesis: For the team-own first-TD contract P(player) = P(team has >=1 TD) x P(player | team's first TD): the first factor is set by the team TD mean (rarely below 0.9), the second by scripted early plays and where the first scoring drive starts. A pass-heavy scripted opener moves the second factor toward the WR/TE group away from the goal-line back, and a high team TD mean saturates the first factor so the allocation factor dominates. Opening possession enters only the game-first contracts.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate P(player is team's first TD scorer) for teams split by model TD-mean tercile and by opener pass rate; confirm the first factor saturates by checking P(team >=1 TD) against lambda, then compare the allocation factor across scripted-opener types.

interactions.hypothesis: In wind or heavy precipitation, red-zone pass rate falls and short-yardage runs rise, so receivers' TD share falls and runners' and the QB's rise; the shift is a regime change above a wind threshold, not a linear drift.
interactions.how_to_test: Split goal-to-go plays by wind bucket (<10, 10-15, >15 mph) and compare pass/run TD shares by team.

interactions.hypothesis: A player's second TD is much likelier in games where his team's total is high and the team leads, so P(2+) is not a function of P(1+) alone; the shared game-state factor widens the right tail beyond Poisson.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare empirical P(2+|1+) for goal-line backs across model-TD-mean terciles against a Poisson baseline.

nonlinearities.shape: convex in distance to the goal line
nonlinearities.why: TD probability per carry rises from low single-digit percent at the 10 to roughly half or more at the 1; linear yardage-based role shares badly misprice players whose carries are inside versus outside the 5.

nonlinearities.shape: saturating: P(team >= 1 TD)=1-exp(-lambda_TD)
nonlinearities.why: Probability that the team scores any TD (the first factor of the team-own first-TD contract and anytime props) is concave in the TD mean, so raising lambda from 3 to 4 changes little while raising it from 1.5 to 2.5 changes a lot; the player's own lambda is team lambda times his share.

nonlinearities.shape: step at designation boundaries
nonlinearities.why: Player-level participation switches from near 1 to near 0 across Out/Doubtful/Questionable/Active, so P(void) is a step function of status rather than a smooth variable.

mechanism_review.summary: A player's first-TD or anytime-TD outcome is the product of five stochastic layers. (1) He must take a snap (and, for protected props, play after halftime) or the contract voids. (2) His team must score touchdowns rather than field goals: a Poisson-binomial count over roughly 10-12 drives, with TD vs FG decided by red-zone and 4th-and-goal policy. (3) Each TD is allocated to a scorer through a categorical draw over rushers, receivers, the QB and non-offensive units, where the weights depend on field position at the TD (a 1-yard plunge versus a 40-yard throw), the personnel package and the game script. (4) For first-TD markets the two teams race: the first TD goes to the team whose drive converts first, so opening possession, scripted opening drives and defensive/special-teams scores determine team order, and then that team's first-TD scorer distribution (different from its average TD scorer distribution) applies. (5) For 2+ TD contracts, within-player TD counts are overdispersed relative to Poisson because goal-line role and a high-scoring game state are shared across a player's TDs. The pool, allocation and ordering layers must be modelled separately; a single 'TD rate' conflates them.

stages.name: Participation gate and void states
stages.description: The contract only pays or loses if the player takes a snap; active-but-no-snap voids to a pregame fair price and a protected contract voids on a first-half-only appearance. So the modelled quantity is P(TD | plays), plus a separate P(void) that affects sizing but not the label. Drivers are the Friday designation, the 90-minute inactive list, depth-chart role (a gadget RB3 may be active and never see a snap), and in-game injury exit hazard by position and snap load. Early exits shorten the exposure window; late exits matter less once the TD is already recorded for protected markets.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli at status level (active/inactive), then a position-specific hazard of leaving the game; protected void adds a halftime step function; discrete and heavily mass-at-0/1 near kickoff

stages.name: Team TD pool and TD-versus-FG conversion
stages.description: The team's expected touchdown count is drives times P(TD per drive). The value that matters for scorer markets is touchdowns, not points: an implied total of 24 can be 3 TDs and a FG or 2 TDs and 3 FGs. Red-zone TD rate, 4th-and-goal go-for-it policy, kicker range and opponent red-zone defense decide the split. The team TD mean is derived from the model (drives times TD-per-drive, nfl.model_team_td_mean) and regressed because red-zone TD rate has low year-to-year stability; market-implied team totals are used only as a benchmark, never as an input.
stages.distribution: Count of 1 to 5 TDs per team per game; approx Poisson-binomial with mild overdispersion from game-state sharing; discrete, right-skewed

stages.name: TD source and scorer allocation within the team
stages.description: Each team TD is drawn from a categorical distribution over rushers (including QB sneaks and scrambles), receivers by route and target role, and unit-level scores (pick-six, return). The weights are not season TD shares: they are a function of the yard line at which the score occurs, which is a function of the drive type. Goal-line carries inside the 3 and end-zone targets behave very differently from open-field touches. Teammate absences shift weights non-proportionally because a replacement has a different goal-line role than the player he replaces. Realized TD counts regress heavily to opportunity-based expectation.
stages.distribution: Categorical with player-specific weights; TD per carry convex in distance to the goal line; high noise at player level because a player sees only 3-10 goal-line touches per season-quarter

stages.name: Ordinal TD allocation: team-first, game-first and k-th touchdown
stages.description: Three ordinal contracts differ. KXNFLTEAMFIRSTTD: P = P(team scores >=1 TD) x P(player scores the team's first TD | team scores); opponent and opening possession matter little and a 'No <team> Touchdown' strike absorbs the zero case. KXNFLFIRSTTD adds a competing-risk race for the game's first TD: opening possession, each side's per-drive TD probability on drives 1-3 (nfl.drive_outcome_by_index) and defensive/return TDs decide which team scores first, then that team's first-TD scorer distribution applies. KXNFLNEXTTD settles on the k-th TD of the game: P = P(game TD count >= k) x a scorer share for the k-th TD that drifts with script (a trailing team's passing share rises later), so it needs the joint game TD-count distribution from both teams' pools rather than a single team-first share.
stages.distribution: Competing-risk process over alternating drives with geometric-like per-drive first-TD hazard; for the k-th TD a count-threshold probability P(N_game>=k) times a categorical scorer share that shifts with score state

stages.name: Multiplicity and cross-TD dependence
stages.description: 2+ TD (protected) contracts and anytime markets need P(N>=k) for a player, not just P(N>=1). A player's TDs are positively dependent: a high team total and his goal-line role both scale every TD, and an early TD signals a favourable script. The count is therefore a mixed Poisson (overdispersed) with a team-level and a role-level shared factor, and team scoring is positively correlated with opponent scoring through pace. The lead-state weights used with nfl.script come from the market-free margin lattice (nfl.model_margin_lattice), not from a spread-implied margin distribution.
stages.distribution: Mixed Poisson / negative-binomial player counts; thick right tail for goal-line backs and WR1s in high-total games

stages.name: Settlement attribution, stat correction and void mechanics
stages.description: Contracts settle on the official scoring summary: who gets credit on fumble-recovery TDs, laterals, nullified plays and kick-return TDs, whether OT TDs count, and the fair-price rule for no-snap or protected exits. Stat corrections can flip a close attribution. The tradable edge also depends on the exact void rule because P(void) changes capital at risk.
stages.distribution: Deterministic rule application given the scoring summary; small probability of post-game stat correction and of ambiguous credit

talent_strength.note: Team offense strength enters via the TD pool; player talent enters mostly through xTD shares rather than season TD totals.

opponent_matchup.note: Opponent red-zone defence and opponent-adjusted defensive efficiency enter through the red-zone rate and the model TD mean; defence-vs-position (nfl.dvp) is audited WEAK and dropped from stages and coverage.

role_personnel.note: Goal-line and end-zone roles and personnel packages decide scorer shares.

availability_news.note: Snap eligibility, void states and teammate absences.

coaching_scheme.note: Scripted openers and 4th-and-goal aggressiveness change TD versus FG and who gets the ball.

environment.note: Wind and precipitation regime enters through nfl.weather_pit (forecast vintages) and drives the pass-to-run split in goal-to-go plays; PROE and D/ST hazard are the downstream rates.

game_context_script.note: Expected game state comes from the market-free team TD mean and the model-based script input; opening possession and first-TD attribution matter only for the game-first contracts and the race variant.

pace_volume.note: Drives set the number of TD chances.

efficiency_conversion.note: TD conversion per trip and per touch with regression.

distribution_variance.note: Overdispersion for 2+ TD props.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Resting starters in clinched games and late-season role changes shift goal-line roles, but no input here captures motivation-linked rest for TD scorers; the generic motivation id exists in the catalog but is not attached or tested for scorer shares.

officiating_rules.note: Officiating crews shift penalty counts only marginally for who scores; goal-line pass interference spot fouls can create scores but the effect is second-order next to role and pool.

settlement_contract.note: Void, protected and fair-price rules change what is modelled.

contract_review.settlement_definition: Live series (7, all with rules text): player count props KXNFLTD ('scores at least 1+ touchdowns', floor_strike 0.5 'greater'), KXNFLANYTD ('scores a touchdown'), KXNFL2TD ('scores two or more touchdowns'), KXNFLTDPROT (protected N+, e.g. floor 1.5 '2+'); ordinal scorer props KXNFLFIRSTTD (scores the first touchdown of the game), KXNFLTEAMFIRSTTD (scores the first touchdown for his team) and KXNFLNEXTTD (scores the k-th touchdown of the game, e.g. '4th TD'). YES when the named player is credited with the required touchdown(s) in the game. Active-but-no-snap players settle to the (last) fair market price before game start; once he takes one snap, even one nullified by penalty, the market settles on touchdowns scored. Ordinal markets carry a 'No Touchdown (Scorer)' strike that resolves YES, with all player strikes NO, if no (team / k-th) touchdown is scored. Protected contracts settle at the pre-kickoff fair price if the player plays in the first half but in no play after it (including overtime) unless he already reached the count. KXNFLTD/FIRSTTD state fake-punt/fake-FG TDs by the offence are not special-teams TDs. No sampled text states whether overtime touchdowns count for the count or ordinal props; source of truth is the official game result/scoring summary.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official NFL scoring summary/game book (scorer credit per play) as the Governing League's official result; stat-correction window not stated in sampled text.
variants_and_edge_cases: Families: (a) player N+ count props (KXNFLTD, ANYTD, 2TD, TDPROT); (b) ordinal scorer props: game-first (FIRSTTD), team-first (TEAMFIRSTTD) and k-th TD of the game (NEXTTD, listed per ordinal e.g. 'TD4'). Team TD counts (KXNFLTEAMTD) and D/ST TD (KXNFLDSTTD) were re-filed to game_events and are no longer claimed here.

KXNFLNEXTTD is the k-th touchdown of the game counted from kickoff; P(YES) = P(game TDs >= k) x P(player scores the k-th | it occurs). The sampled NEXTTD ticker and text date the Seattle-New England game Feb 6, 2026 while the ANYTD and 2TD samples date the same matchup Feb 8 (a date discrepancy, not explained); the market is closed, so listing time (pregame vs in-game after earlier TDs) is not visible.

Zero-snap void: non-protected props use 'fair market price before game start' (KXNFLTEAMFIRSTTD, KXNFLFIRSTTD, KXNFLTD) or 'last fair market price before game start' (KXNFLANYTD, 2TD, NEXTTD); the effective event is TD | at least one snap.
Protected contracts (KXNFLTDPROT) pay fair price on a first-half-only participant unless the count was already reached; strike floor 1.5 with 'greater', i.e. integer N+ with no push.

No sampled text addresses overtime touchdowns, defensive/return touchdowns by a named offensive player's team in team-first markets, laterals or stat corrections; these are recorded as CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS.

game_moneyline_spread.label: Game moneyline, spread and win-margin buckets
game_moneyline_spread.target: Probability a team wins (with or without overtime per wording), covers a spread rung, or wins by a margin bucket.
game_moneyline_spread.mechanism: Win and cover probability derive from the distribution of final margin: mean = rating difference (QB-adjusted) + home edge + rest/travel + environment, with key-number mass (3, 7, 10) and tie/overtime rules. The model works as a deviation from the market-implied line by lineup (QB, OL, key defenders) and weather, using shrinkage to market. Win-margin buckets need the whole lattice, not just a Gaussian SD.

interactions.hypothesis: QB status x line: a backup QB shifts the mean by a QB-specific value and increases margin variance; cover probability at integer lines near key numbers moves more than moneyline.
Turnover luck x record: a team whose record is inflated by fumble recoveries is overrated by raw ratings; adjusting to expected turnovers lowers its margin mean.
Rest/travel x venue: a West-coast team playing early east-coast kickoffs on short rest has a small deficit that scales with travel; effect is offset by roof/surface differences.
Tie mass x settlement wording: a regulation-only moneyline leaves tie mass while an OT-inclusive one does not; use the key-number mass at zero margin.
A backup QB lowers the mean margin and raises its variance and skews it; the cover probability at +3 and +10 changes differently from the moneyline since both location and scale move together.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit location-scale model with a backup-QB indicator and compare calibration at several rungs.

interactions.hypothesis: Pass-rush win rate multiplies with offensive-line pass-block weakness and the QB's sack-avoidance; the interaction, not the sum, drives sacks and drive failures; strong rush against a weak tackle with a slow QB creates outsized damage.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress drive-success on rush win rate x pass-block rate x time-to-throw.

interactions.hypothesis: High wind or heavy precipitation lowers totals and compresses margin variance, shifting cover probability for heavy favourites down and raising the underdog's cover probability; effect appears past a wind threshold around 15 mph.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare cover rates for favourites by wind bucket after controlling for rating difference.

interactions.hypothesis: A west-coast team travelling east for an early kickoff on short rest loses a fraction of a point, but the effect is offset in domes and for teams used to travel; it is conditional on kickoff time and venue.
interactions.how_to_test: Interact kickoff hour with time zones crossed in a margin residual regression.

interactions.hypothesis: Blowout probability rises convexly in the expected margin because turnovers snowball (short fields, garbage-time scoring); a team that is a 14-point favourite with a backup quarterback on the other side has a deep-rung probability several times higher than a linear extrapolation.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate P(margin>21) by expected-margin decile and compare to Gaussian prediction.

nonlinearities.shape: spikes at 3, 6, 7, 10, 14
nonlinearities.why: Probability of covering a half-point line jumps when the line moves across a key number; the body of the margin distribution is lumpy, so linear rating-to-probability maps misprice rungs next to 3 and 7.

nonlinearities.shape: S-shaped (normal CDF) rating-to-win probability
nonlinearities.why: Win probability is a normal-CDF-like function of the model expected margin with SD around 13 points; the slope at a pick'em is far larger than at -10, so equal margin-mean errors cost much more near zero.

nonlinearities.shape: step at the starter-replacement boundary
nonlinearities.why: The QB effect is discrete: starter vs replacement differ by a large block of points, so the mean margin is a mixture of two modes rather than a smooth variable.

mechanism_review.summary: The final margin M = (home points - away points) is the sum of a structural expectation and a heavy-tailed, lattice-valued noise term. The structural mean is team quality difference (offence and defence, QB-weighted, regressed from preseason priors and updated through the season) plus home-field edge plus situational shifts (rest, travel, weather, motivation), then adjusted at kickoff by the actual lineup: the QB, offensive line, pass rush and secondary starters. The noise is not Gaussian: scores come in discrete packages so the margin has spikes at 3, 6, 7, 10, 14; its variance depends on total scoring, pace, weather and QB volatility; and its tails are heavier than normal because of blowout snowballing (turnovers, garbage time) and rare events (defensive TDs). Moneyline probability is the mass above zero (with ties and overtime assigned by the wording); each spread rung is a tail probability of the same distribution, so a ladder is a monotone curve whose far rungs are determined by tail shape. The week's highest-scoring game is a maximum over the slate's game totals, and the Pro Bowl conference winner is a separate exhibition process with selected rosters, opt-outs and flag-football rules.

stages.name: Structural team-strength difference
stages.description: The expected margin starts with the strength of both teams: offence and defence efficiency adjusted for opponent, with recency weighting, preseason priors from returning production and an in-season updating rule. The effective rating of each team depends on who is playing, so ratings need a lineup layer. Rating noise itself is a source of uncertainty (state-space process noise) that widens the margin distribution.
stages.distribution: Gaussian-like estimate with uncertainty about 2 points in margin for each team's rating; mean difference sets the margin location

stages.name: Lineup and unit adjustments at kickoff
stages.description: Starting QB is the largest single change (a replacement-level QB is worth several points of margin and raises margin variance); offensive-line absences, pass-rush injuries and secondary absences change specific matchups (pass rush against protection, coverage against route concepts). These arrive as timestamped reports (Wednesday to inactive list), so the pregame margin is a mixture over lineup states until about 90 minutes before kickoff.
stages.distribution: Discrete mixture over QB and unit states; position-weighted points adjustments; inactive list collapses mixture

stages.name: Environment and situational shifts
stages.description: Home-field edge varies by team and by travel and rest; a short week or cross-country early kickoff shifts the mean by a point or less; weather lowers scoring (and thus margin variance) and favours the run; stakes and rest decisions late in the season change effort and starter participation.
stages.distribution: Small mean shifts (tenths to one point) and variance changes; regime effects in extreme weather and in week 17-18 rest

stages.name: Margin distribution: lattice, variance and tails
stages.description: Given the mean, the margin distribution has a lattice with spikes at 3 and 7, a standard deviation of roughly 13 points that varies with the total and with the lineup state, and heavier tails than a normal. Heteroskedasticity matters: a 38-point total game has a narrower margin distribution than a 52-point one. Probabilities of covering integer lines and of exact-margin buckets are read off this lattice; deep rungs (20-35 points) depend on the tail model. Atoms and tails are centred on the market-free model means (nfl.model_team_points_mean), not on line residuals.
stages.distribution: Discrete non-Gaussian with key-number atoms; variance heteroskedastic; tail heavier than normal

stages.name: Overtime, ties and settlement mapping
stages.description: The moneyline settles a tie at $0.50 per team, so its fair value is P(win incl. OT) + 0.5 x P(tie after OT); win-margin includes overtime and puts the tie in the 'exactly 0' bucket; a spread rung resolves NO on a tie and its text is silent on overtime. Overtime collapses margins to small values (3, 6, 7 or 0 under sudden death; with both teams possessing, 1 or 2 are also possible, and the format in force is unverified), so the OT model moves the regulation zero-margin atom (about 6% of games) to small margins and leaves about 0.4% as ties.
stages.distribution: Mass transfer from zero margin to +/-1..7 after OT; deterministic mapping by wording with half-payout on moneyline ties

stages.name: Ladder coherence and aggregate order statistics
stages.description: Spread ladders are cumulative tails of one distribution, so rung probabilities must decline monotonically and deep rungs are priced as tail, not as extrapolation of the body. KXNFLWEEKHIGH (title only) is the maximum of 13-16 game totals in a week, which needs each game's total distribution, their shared-weather dependence and the slate composition (byes, international and Monday games).
stages.distribution: Monotone ladder of tail probabilities; maximum-of-N over the weekly slate's game totals with heterogeneous means

stages.name: Pro Bowl flag-football exhibition
stages.description: KXNFLPROBOWL (and title-only KXNFLPROBOWLWIN) pay on the conference that wins the Pro Bowl flag football game. The process shares nothing with regular-season margins: rosters are fan/player/coach-voted selections thinned by injury opt-outs and Super Bowl participants, the game is non-contact 7-on-7 flag football with short fields, so QB passing accuracy and receiver/defensive back speed dominate, and effort is low and variable. With few games in this format, the outcome is close to a coin flip shifted by the realized roster quality, especially which quarterbacks actually play.
stages.distribution: Single Bernoulli near 0.5 with modest shifts from roster quality; very small history in the flag format, so heavy shrinkage to 0.5

contract_review.settlement_definition: Six live series; four have rules text (KXNFLGAME, KXNFLSPREAD, KXNFLWINMARGIN, KXNFLPROBOWL), two are TITLE_ONLY (KXNFLPROBOWLWIN, KXNFLWEEKHIGH). KXNFLGAME (moneyline) resolves YES for the team that wins; 'If the game ends in a tie, the market will resolve to $0.50 for each team', and postponed games not started within 48 hours settle at a fair price. KXNFLSPREAD is 'wins by more than X.5 points' (half-point strikes, no push; overtime not mentioned). KXNFLWINMARGIN settles on the point differential 'in the full game (including overtime)' with exact-margin strikes ('exactly 0' = tie after OT). KXNFLPROBOWL resolves YES if the named conference (NFC/AFC) wins the Pro Bowl flag football game. KXNFLWEEKHIGH (week's highest-scoring game) and KXNFLPROBOWLWIN have no sampled text; their tie-splitting and settlement are not verified. Source: the official final result.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official final scores of the league (official final result); for the Pro Bowl, the official Pro Bowl Games result published by the NFL.
variants_and_edge_cases: Tie handling differs: KXNFLGAME pays $0.50 to each team on a tie; KXNFLWINMARGIN has an 'exactly 0' strike (full game incl. OT); KXNFLSPREAD 'wins by more than X.5' simply resolves NO for a tie; spread text does not mention overtime.
Only the 35.5 rung of KXNFLSPREAD was sampled; ladders presumably also list competitive rungs (not verified), and a 35.5-point rung is priced entirely by the far tail of the margin distribution.

KXNFLWEEKHIGH (title only) is a maximum over the week's slate of game totals; dead-heat handling is not visible. The season blowout series and the former week-game-high ticker are no longer filed here.

KXNFLPROBOWL/PROBOWLWIN are all-star exhibitions in a flag-football (Pro Bowl Games) format with conference rosters; whether skills-event points carry into the 'flag football game' result is not stated.
Postponement: KXNFLGAME states the 48-hour fair-price rule; SPREAD and WINMARGIN sampled texts do not.

game_total.label: Game total points and both-teams-score
game_total.target: Probability that total points exceed a rung (with or without OT per wording) or that both teams score at least N points.
game_total.mechanism: Total = home points + away points = sum over possessions of points per possession. Model plays per game from the pace of both offenses and defenses (and clock use from run rate), drives from turnover and punt rates, and points per drive from opponent-adjusted EPA, explosiveness, red-zone conversion, field position and kicker; then apply weather and venue adjustments, and mix over uncertainty in lineups. Totals have fat tails (blowouts, defensive TDs) and key-number mass (e.g., 41, 44, 47), and both-teams-score requires each team to exceed its threshold with correlated outcomes.

inputs.why: Offense and opponent pace combine to set plays.
Expected possessions are the base unit of scoring; drive count differs from plays due to turnovers, punts and clock-killing.
Pass rate drives clock usage and yards.
Offensive EPA per play, opponent-adjusted, anchors points per drive for each team.
Opponent defense efficiency suppresses points per drive and changes the pass/rush split of scoring.
Success rate captures consistency: sustained-drive teams run more plays per drive and burn clock, differing from explosive-dependent teams.
Explosive-play rates raise scoring variance and the fat right tail of the total distribution.
Red-zone TD versus FG conversion changes points per scoring opportunity by up to 4 points per trip and regresses to league mean.
Turnover rates change the number of drives and field position, so expected turnovers (not lucky realized ones) enter the total.
Starting field position from special teams and turnovers sets scoring probability per drive.
Kicker range and accuracy determine how many stalled drives convert to 3 points and the key-number structure of totals.
Starter versus backup QB shifts both team points and pace and is only resolved late; total must be a mixture.
OL availability changes efficiency.
Wind, precipitation, temperature.
Roofs and surfaces change the weather exposure and passing environment, systematically shifting totals.
Penalty-prone teams lose drive efficiency and extend game clock; adds a small, persistent adjustment.
Crew-level flag rates (holding, DPI) alter drive extensions and game length with a small but knowable effect.
Teams scoring above or below their drive-efficiency expectation regress; recent points should be discounted accordingly.
Total residual and key numbers.
Home/away scoring correlation for BTTS.
Sharp totals incorporate weather and lineup information; the Kalshi ladder should be compared to the de-vigged consensus.
Total ladder implied distribution.
Divisional familiarity may lower scoring relative to efficiency-based projections and is knowable from the schedule.
Volume and open interest weight how much the price reflects information versus stale quotes, and bound feasible size.
Executed trades show where liquidity actually transacted, informing realistic fills and whether price moves are informed flow.
Pressure shortens drives and lowers totals.
Soft shells concede completions and add scoring.
Run defence controls clock and drive length.
Turns two team paces into the number of snaps that the total actually counts.
Deep rungs are tail events; the existing key-number input does not define tails.
The existing weather input lists data fields but not the response function or the forecast-versus-actual issue.
Contract text for full-game totals is silent on OT; this quantifies the effect of either reading.
Market-free expected total (sum of both team means) and its drivers; the source of the 'expected total' that tail and joint-distribution inputs condition on.

interactions.hypothesis: Both teams' pace: a fast offense against a slow-clock opponent regresses to a mutual pace not an average; the opponent's run rate controls clock burn.
Wind x kicker x explosive passing: wind removes deep explosives and long FGs, so points per drive drops for vertical offenses; the effect is nonlinear above a threshold.
Spread x total: large spreads reduce the favorite's late pace and raise garbage-time scoring for the underdog; total quality depends on both.
Sequencing luck x red-zone conversion: a team with unsustainably high red-zone TD rate should be projected with regression, lowering expected points.

A fast-paced team facing an opponent who runs the ball and burns clock gets fewer plays than its own pace implies; the product of the two teams' tempo preferences, not their average, determines total plays, and the effect is amplified when the leader runs more.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress total plays on the product and difference of team paces.

interactions.hypothesis: Wind has little effect below about 12 mph then removes deep passing and long field goals sharply; the total falls by several points over a narrow range of wind speed, and the loss is larger for vertical offences and for teams reliant on 50-yard kickers.
interactions.how_to_test: Piecewise-linear regression of total residual on wind with knots at 10, 15, 20 mph.

interactions.hypothesis: A backup QB changes efficiency and tempo together (more runs, fewer plays, shorter drives) and the total drops more than the efficiency change alone, but only when the opponent is a good defence; with a poor defence a backup can still score.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate total residual by QB status interacted with opponent defence tercile.

interactions.hypothesis: Home and away scores correlate positively in shootouts and negatively through clock control; the variance of the sum and the tails depend on the regime, so a single correlation understates the upper tail in shootout conditions and overstates in blowouts.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate corr(home,away) by expected-margin and expected-total bucket.

interactions.hypothesis: A team with a red-zone TD rate far above the league mean and unchanged EPA is projected to regress; the correction is larger for teams whose red-zone sample is small, and affects the total by roughly a point per team.
interactions.how_to_test: Out-of-sample test of regression with shrinkage constant against realized points.

interactions.hypothesis: Tail dependence of the two scores is strongest when both expected team totals are high and the expected margin is small (a projected shootout) and turns negative-to-neutral when one side is a large favourite, because a big leader runs the clock and the trailing side's late points come against soft coverage but too few possessions to reach 35.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate P(both>=35)/(P(home>=35)P(away>=35)) by bins of expected total and |expected margin| on 2002-2025 games and test whether the ratio varies with |margin| at fixed total.

nonlinearities.shape: piecewise linear with a knee near 15 mph wind
nonlinearities.why: Total points are nearly flat in wind below the knee and fall steeply above it; a linear weather coefficient underestimates storms and overstates mild wind.

nonlinearities.shape: right-skewed heavy upper tail
nonlinearities.why: The total distribution is right-skewed: games over 65 are much more frequent than a normal with SD 10 implies, and TOTALPRECISE-type rungs near 98.5 are far-tail events.

nonlinearities.shape: spikes at key totals (37, 41, 44, 47) on top of a right-skewed tail
nonlinearities.why: Probability of exceeding a half-point strike jumps when the strike crosses a key total, because 3- and 7-point packages concentrate mass on particular integer sums; smooth totals models misprice rungs adjacent to those integers.

nonlinearities.shape: saturating (clock-limited)
nonlinearities.why: Play counts are bounded by the 60-minute clock: increasing neutral pace beyond a point yields smaller increments in plays because stoppages and timeouts dominate.

mechanism_review.summary: The total is the sum of points from about 22 to 26 possessions. Think of it as plays times points per play, split into how many snaps the game contains and how many points each snap yields. The number of snaps is set by clock consumption: each play burns 5-7 seconds if inbounds and a few if incomplete, passing rates and incompletions stop the clock, timeouts and penalties shape late-half tempo, so the total plays are determined by both offences' pace and run rates and by the lead (a leader runs the clock). Points per snap depend on efficiency and field position, with TD/FG conversion near the goal line and turnovers that both end drives and shorten fields. Environment multiplies efficiency: wind, cold and precipitation reduce passing and kicking beyond thresholds, domes and altitude shift it the other way. The two teams' scores are positively correlated through shared pace and weather but negatively through clock-killing leaders. The result is a lattice-valued, right-skewed distribution with a mean near 44 points and heavy tails: some games score under 25 and some over 70, and ladders reaching 98.5 are priced almost entirely by the tail. Settlement wording (overtime included or not) shifts the distribution by the 6-7 percent mass of games that go to overtime.

stages.name: Number of plays and possessions from clock consumption
stages.description: The number of plays is determined by clock time: seconds per play depends on run/pass mix, incompletion rate, no-huddle use, timeouts and penalties; both teams' paces combine toward a mutual tempo, and the leading team slows the game. Possessions follow from plays per drive (drive length depends on efficiency) and from scoring/turnover frequency. This stage fixes the opportunity count for points. Coach and coordinator tempo and 4th-down policy (nfl.coaching) shift seconds per play, no-huddle use and the TD-versus-FG outcome of stalled drives, so they enter as a secondary plays-and-drive-ending input. The catalog nfl.two_minute_tempo measurement takes lead/trail states from the spread; here those states come from the market-free nfl.model_margin_lattice.
stages.distribution: Count of plays about 125 +/- 10; possessions 22-26; both right-skewed in shootouts; tempo mutual rather than additive

stages.name: Points per possession from efficiency and field position
stages.description: Points per drive depend on offensive EPA and success against the specific defence, starting field position (kickoff rule, punting, turnovers), red-zone TD versus FG conversion, explosive plays and kicker range. Finishing luck regresses to the drive-efficiency expectation, so recent scoring above expectation should not be extrapolated. Efficiency is correlated across the two teams only through shared environment.
stages.distribution: Points per drive about 2 with SD near 2.2 per drive; drive-level distribution (0, 3, 6/7/8) is discrete and zero-heavy

stages.name: Environment: weather, venue and roof
stages.description: Wind above about 15 mph cuts deep passing and long field-goal range, temperatures under freezing reduce passing and kicking efficiency, precipitation raises fumbles; domes and warm weather raise passing efficiency. Responses are thresholded, and forecast error is the real unknown pregame, so the weather effect is an expectation over forecast vintages rather than a point.
stages.distribution: Piecewise response with thresholds; forecast uncertainty adds a discrete mixture (calm vs windy)

stages.name: Lineup state and unit matchups
stages.description: QB status is a mixture that shifts both teams' points and pace; offensive line and pass-rush availability change sack rates, drive failures and pressure-driven turnovers; coverage injuries change completion efficiency. The total is therefore a mixture over lineup states until inactives. Short-week and post-bye rest (nfl.rest_travel) and late-season clinched or eliminated starter rest (nfl.motivation_seeding) change effective lineups and tempo.
stages.distribution: Discrete mixture over QB/line states; each component with its own mean and variance

stages.name: Joint distribution of the two scores and tails
stages.description: Home and away points are positively correlated through pace and environment and negatively through clock control by a leader and garbage time, so the variance of the total is not the sum of the variances. The distribution has key-number spikes (37, 41, 44, 47), a heavy right tail (turnover-fuelled blowouts, defensive TDs) and a lower tail (defensive slogs, wind). Deep rungs like 24.5 and 98.5 are tail events.
stages.distribution: Lattice-valued, right-skewed, SD near 10 points, with tail multipliers; key-number atoms

stages.name: Overtime inclusion and ladder coherence
stages.description: If overtime counts, a regulation tie (about 5-7% of games) adds roughly 3 to 10 points to the total; if it does not, the total is truncated. P(OT) is the regulation zero-margin mass of the market-free margin lattice and the OT points distribution comes from the rule-era overtime model. The ladder across rungs is one monotone survival curve of that mixture. The wording determines which of two distributions applies, so it must be resolved from the rules rather than inferred.
stages.distribution: Mixture of regulation and OT-extended distributions; monotone ladder constraint

stages.name: Both teams reaching a high threshold
stages.description: KXNFLBOTH pays only if each team scores at least N points (35 sampled), overtime included. That is the joint upper tail of two team scores: P(X_home>=35, X_away>=35). Each marginal is perhaps 10-15% for an average offence, and the joint is driven by shootout dependence (fast pace, weak defences, a trailing team forced to keep scoring), offset by the clock-killing of a comfortable leader. A blowout total of 70 can resolve NO, so this rung needs each team's own points distribution and their copula in the upper tail, not the total's survival curve. Overtime adds a few points to both only in tied games, mainly raising 35-35 style outcomes. The joint tail is read from nfl.paired_score_covariance_own, the shared joint home/away score pmf (a Student-t copula per expected-total and wind bin, so upper-tail dependence is estimated rather than assumed zero) over the marginals of nfl.team_score_pmf_own_mean; the same joint feeds team totals and slate extremes. Its tail calibration at N = 28-42 against empirical joint frequencies remains to be tested (u5).
stages.distribution: Joint survival of two positively tail-dependent lattice counts; a small probability (low single digits percent for typical games) highly sensitive to upper-tail dependence

contract_review.settlement_definition: Three live series, all with rules text. KXNFLTOTAL and KXNFLTOTALPRECISE resolve YES if the two teams 'collectively score more than' a half-point strike (24.5 and 98.5 sampled), so no push; neither sampled text says whether overtime points count or states a postponement rule. KXNFLBOTH resolves YES if each team records at least N points (sampled N=35, strike_type greater_or_equal), with 'Points scored in overtime count'; postponed games starting within 48 hours stay open, otherwise fair price. The first-half total was moved to first_half_and_quarter_totals. Source: official final result.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official final scores of the league; Kalshi uses the 'official final result' of the game.
variants_and_edge_cases: Overtime: KXNFLBOTH explicitly counts overtime points; KXNFLTOTAL and TOTALPRECISE texts are silent, so whether a regulation tie's OT points count for totals is unverified.
Rungs span an extraordinary range (24.5 to 98.5 for one game) versus a central total near 44; far rungs are priced by the tail shape of a lattice-valued distribution.

KXNFLBOTH uses 'at least N' (greater_or_equal 35), so 35 counts; a 35-35 game satisfies it, and its probability depends on the dependence between team scores, not on the total alone (a 56-14 game has total 70 but resolves NO).
Half-point total strikes eliminate pushes, but key numbers (37, 41, 44, 47, 51) make the probability over x.5 a step function of the integer score distribution.
The first-half total now sits in first_half_and_quarter_totals and is not claimed here.

team_total.label: Team total points
team_total.target: Probability one team's points exceed a rung in the game, per wording on overtime.
team_total.mechanism: Team points = team possessions x points per possession, bounded by the game total and spread split (mu = (T +/- s)/2). The relevant inputs are the team's own offense efficiency against the opponent's defense, pace and clock control (possessions), red-zone and kicker finishing, QB/OL/skill availability and weather; distribution is right-skewed with discrete clusters at multiples of 3 and 7. Team-total rungs must be consistent with game total and spread quotes.

Possessions allocated to team.
Team-specific red-zone TD conversion sets points per trip; shrunk to league average.
Own kicker accuracy and range add FG points when drives stall, and affect clusters at multiples of 3.
The team's starting QB status is the dominant driver of its own total and resolves late.
Own OL health shifts sack/pressure rates and run efficiency, affecting points per drive.
Absence of receivers and backs reduces the team's scoring ceiling.

Consistency with game total and spread.
Volume and open interest weight how much the price reflects information versus stale quotes, and bound feasible size.
Executed trades show where liquidity actually transacted, informing realistic fills and whether price moves are informed flow.
The opposing coverage shell sets this offence's passing efficiency.
Run defence caps the ground game.
Pressure against this offensive line cuts scoring.

Provides the integer pmf (OT-inclusive and regulation-only) from which every KXNFLTEAMTOTAL rung is read, without importing market lines.
Joint home/away score pmf from which the single-team pmf conditional on the game state (pace, weather, script) is read for KXNFLTEAMTOTAL.

interactions.hypothesis: Spread-implied split x blowout script: a heavy favorite's team total has a right tail from long drives but a left tail from clock-killing late; the underdog gains garbage points.
Opponent pass-defense x team pass rate: a pass-heavy offense is hurt more by a strong pass defense; run-heavy offense by run defense.
QB injury x OL: a backup QB behind a weak OL reduces points more than QB value alone.

A pass-heavy offence is hurt more by a strong pass defence and a run-heavy one by a strong run defence, and the script chooses which side the offence leans on, so the opponent effect on points depends on the offence's style mixture and the expected score state.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress team points on offence pass-share x opposing pass-defence EPA and offence run-share x opposing run-defence EPA, separately by expected score state; the separate coefficients differ in sign pattern from a single defensive EPA.

interactions.hypothesis: In wind or cold the effective kicking range shrinks by 5-10 yards, and a coach who would kick from 48 yards goes for it, which changes the expected points of stalled drives from 2.4 to a 0 or 7 gamble; the decision flips at a threshold distance that depends on weather.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate go-for-it probability and make rate by yard-line bin split by wind; test threshold shifts.

interactions.hypothesis: Total points are a convolution over a random number of drives, and the number of drives is correlated with drive outcomes (long touchdown drives remove possessions, quick scores add them), so independent treatment of drive count and outcomes understates the dispersion.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare simulated team total variance with realised variance, using independent and joint draws of drives and outcomes.

interactions.hypothesis: A backup quarterback behind a weak line and a thin receiver room compounds: pressure rises, completion probability falls and yards after catch fall, so the points loss is greater than the sum of single-position losses.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare scoring in games with combined absences versus single absences, controlling for opponent.

interactions.hypothesis: The probability mass at key totals (3, 6, 7, 9, 10, 13, 14) depends on the touchdown versus field-goal split, so rung probabilities move discontinuously as the red-zone touchdown rate or the kicker accuracy changes the mixture even if the mean points are constant.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit the score pmf with a mixture model and test the change in P(total >= 17) with fixed mean but varying TD/FG mixture.

interactions.hypothesis: Non-offensive scores arrive more often when the opponent is trailing and passing (more interceptions) so the team's total gets a lift in precisely the game states where its offence is conservative; the contribution is conditional on opponent script.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate return-score frequency by opponent score state and pass rate.

nonlinearities.shape: lumpy: rung probability changes in steps around the key numbers 3, 7, 10, 14, 17, 21, 24
nonlinearities.why: The own-mean score pmf has mass concentrated on sums of 3 and 7, so a shift in the model's own expected points moves P(over 13.5) and P(over 16.5) by different amounts rather than smoothly; this shape is fitted around own means, not closing lines.

nonlinearities.shape: steep decay of make probability beyond about 50 yards, and decision threshold at about 50-55 yards for go-for-it
nonlinearities.why: Field-goal accuracy decays nonlinearly with distance, and coaches switch policies at a similar distance, so points per drive near the 35-yard line is a nonlinear function of range.

nonlinearities.shape: threshold effects near 15 mph wind and near freezing temperature on kicking and deep passing
nonlinearities.why: Wind affects long field goals and deep passes sharply above a threshold, so team points fall in a step-like pattern in wind speed.

nonlinearities.shape: concave for the leader: points per late drive fall as the lead grows because of clock-killing runs, convex for the trailer
nonlinearities.why: A large lead reduces the leader's late scoring chance even as expected margin increases, so team total for a favourite is not monotone in the own-rating expected margin.

mechanism_review.summary: A team's final score is the sum of points from a discrete sequence of possessions plus rare non-offensive scores. The number of possessions is set by both offences' tempo and style, the result of each possession is a discrete lottery over touchdown, field goal, no score and turnover with the points of 7 (or 6 or 8), 3, 0 and a chance of opponent return score, and the probabilities depend on starting field position, own offence against the opponent's defence, personnel and weather. Coach decision rules (go for it versus kick, one versus two points) change the points attached to a stalled drive. The score path then rewrites late possessions: leaders run clock, trailers throw and score faster. Because the discrete clusters at 3 and 7 are dense, the response of rung probability to the mean is lumpy and the correct object is the whole score distribution, not a mean plus normal noise.

stages.name: Possessions available to this offence
stages.description: The count of own possessions comes from combined pace, rushing share and clock use of both teams, penalties, turnovers (which add possessions) and the half-end structure; it is typically 10-13 drives per team, and the opponent's ball-control style removes possessions from this offence. A slow, run-heavy opponent cuts this team's chances in a way that own pace alone misses. Roles to avoid double counting: nfl.pace gives plays per minute, nfl.drives gives the possession count, nfl.opponent_ball_control_denial is the opponent term inside that possession estimate (not an extra independent driver) and nfl.drive_result_lattice conditions on the resulting count.
stages.distribution: Drives per team per game roughly 9-14 (sd ~1.5); correlated with the opponent's drive count and with game script.

stages.name: Drive start position and field-position inputs
stages.description: Where drives start (after kickoffs, punts, turnovers, returns) determines the expected points per drive, as does the quality of special teams. Turnovers by the opponent give short fields and high scoring chances, so the distribution of start positions reflects both defence and special-teams play.
stages.distribution: Starting yard line ~ distribution centred at the 27-30 yard line with a right tail of short fields after takeaways.

stages.name: Drive outcome lottery: touchdown, field goal, no score
stages.description: Each drive ends in a touchdown with probability that depends on the team's offence, the matchup with defence (pass rush, coverage, run front) and red-zone efficiency, in a field goal when drives stall inside kicker range, or in no points. The points per drive distribution is discrete and the team's total is a convolution across drives.
stages.distribution: Drive points take values 0, 3, ~7 with probabilities ~ 0.65, 0.12-0.15, 0.20-0.25 (league average assumption); sum over ~11 drives gives a discrete distribution with clusters.

stages.name: Kicker and fourth-down decision rules
stages.description: On stalled drives the coach decides to kick or go for it, and the kicker's accuracy by distance and weather decides the three points; changes in 4th-down aggressiveness convert a 3-point outcome into a 0 or 7 gamble. The extra point and two-point decisions add a variance term of about 0.5-1 point per touchdown.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli outcomes with decision-dependent probabilities; FG make probability falls from ~95% at 30 yd to ~65% at 55 yd.

stages.name: Personnel availability and offensive-line health
stages.description: The starting quarterback, line and skill players determine the offence's rate; a backup quarterback behind a weak line can reduce the team's expected score (the 4-7 point size is an unsourced assumption to be estimated from starter-versus-backup games, see u5). These status changes arrive late and are partially known at kickoff, and can happen in-game.
stages.distribution: Mixture over personnel scenarios with a heavy shift for the quarterback scenario; in-game injuries produce a smaller shift.

stages.name: Weather, score path and non-offensive scoring
stages.description: Wind and cold reduce passing and field goals, and a blowout compresses the leader's late scoring while the trailer's passing yields more. In addition, the team's defence and special teams can score directly (pick-six, return touchdowns, safeties), adding points independent of its offence, and the opponent's equivalent scores add to the opponent's total but also end the team's drives.
stages.distribution: Defensive/special-teams touchdowns occur in ~10-12% of team games (assumption); weather effects scale with wind above ~15 mph.

stages.name: Discrete score distribution and ladder mapping
stages.description: The team total's rungs are nested events of the same discrete variable; key numbers 3, 7, 10, 14, 17 and so on make the cumulative distribution step-like. The model has to produce the integer probability mass function and read every rung from it, with overtime included or excluded once the rule is known. The pmf is built around the model's own mean points per team (no sportsbook line); the opponent's score enters only through the script coupling (a team that falls behind passes more and scores faster), captured by the paired-score covariance.
stages.distribution: Discrete multi-modal distribution; the rung probability from a smooth normal approximation is biased by 2-4 points near key numbers.

distribution_variance.note: Discrete score pmf with key numbers around the own mean, plus the paired-score correlation used for script coupling; the market-derived team_total_split and the line-centred score_resid are removed.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Short rest, travel and late-season clinch rest of starters influence a team's scoring, but no schedule or motivation input is attached to this archetype.

officiating_rules.note: Penalties extend or end drives and shape scoring slightly, but a crew effect on one team's points is second-order and can be captured inside the offensive and defensive efficiency inputs.

contract_review.settlement_definition: KXNFLTEAMTOTAL is the only live series: it settles YES when the named team scores over the strike (floor_strike, half-point rungs such as 'over 7.5') in the named game 'originally scheduled for' the listed date, so the settled quantity is one team's final points and a score equal to the next integer above the strike is YES. The rules text names no source of truth and is silent on whether overtime points count and on what happens if the game is postponed, suspended or cancelled; those are carried as CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS (u1). The former joint 'both teams score N' series (KXNFLBOTH) was re-filed to game_total and no longer belongs to this archetype.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Not stated in the sampled text; official game result by the league scoreboard is implied. Two-point conversions and extra points count as points in the final score by standard scoring.
variants_and_edge_cases: Only an over-strike ladder exists (floor_strike 7.5 in the sample); every rung is a nested event of the same team score, and low rungs near 7.5 are driven by the chance of a near-shutout rather than offence quality.

Points include non-offensive scores (interception and fumble returns, kick returns, safeties credited to the scoring team), so a team's offence is not the only source; the contract is about the scoreboard, not offensive points.

Overtime handling is not stated in the KXNFLTEAMTOTAL text; unconditionally overtime adds roughly 0.1-0.2 points to each team's expected total (about 6 percent of games reach overtime, about 2-3 extra points per team in those games), so the pmf is kept in two versions, with and without overtime, until the rule is confirmed.

'Originally scheduled for' anchors the contract to a specific game, but the text gives no postponement or cancellation rule (no 48-hour window or fair-price clause appears), so a rescheduled game's treatment is unknown.

Team scores cluster at 3 and 7 multiples, so rungs on the half-point such as 17.5, 20.5 and 23.5 correspond to different integer score masses and the same-sized gap in mean moves the probability by different amounts.

first_half_and_quarter_totals.label: First-half, second-half and quarter totals, spreads and winners
first_half_and_quarter_totals.target: Probability for period winner/halftime-fulltime result/ quarter or half total/spread rungs under tie and overtime rules.
first_half_and_quarter_totals.mechanism: Period scoring = possessions in the period x points per possession, with different structure: Q1 uses scripted drives and opening possession, Q2 contains the two-minute drill, Q3 the half-opening drive and adjustments, Q4 clock-management and garbage time. Use the game total/spread as anchor and allocate by team-specific period shares, adjust for opening possession, coach tendencies, and lead state; period markets have lower scoring, so zero and tie masses matter.
