interactions.hypothesis: Opening possession x opening-drive script x first-quarter total: the first possession advantage matters more for slow-pace teams with strong scripted drives.
Two-minute efficiency x halftime ordering: the team receiving second-half kickoff plays the end of Q2 and the start of Q3 consecutively, raising scoring chances with timeouts.
Lead x script in Q4: the leader's run rate and kneel-downs cut Q4 totals more than average pace suggests.

If a team receives the opening kickoff and runs a long scripted drive, Q1 can contain only one drive for the other team, so P(both score in Q1) falls while P(over 7.5) depends on whether the first drive ends in a TD; the effect is conditional on drive length.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare Q1 BTTS and over 7.5 rates by receiving team and its first-drive length distribution.

interactions.hypothesis: The team that deferred receives at halftime and can score at the end of Q2 and then again at the start of Q3, producing back-to-back scoring chances; the benefit is larger for coaches who use timeouts aggressively and for strong two-minute offences.
interactions.how_to_test: Test 2Q + 3Q scoring for the deferring team versus others controlling for team quality.

interactions.hypothesis: Q4 totals are bimodal: close games produce hurry-up and late FG attempts (more scoring), while two-score leads shorten the game and lower scoring; the pregame total is a mixture whose weights come from the model's distribution of halftime and late-game margins.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate Q4 scoring by model expected-margin bucket and halftime-lead bucket; test bimodality and whether the mixture weights from the model lattice calibrate.

interactions.hypothesis: A single FG changes a quarter from 0 to 3 and crosses neither 7.5 nor tie; but two FGs or one TD pass 7.5 only with additional scoring, so O/U 7.5 probability depends on a joint of kicker range and red-zone TD rate that is threshold-like.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare P(over 7.5) for team-quarters with equal expected points but different TD/FG mix.

interactions.hypothesis: A backup QB cuts efficiency and tends to shorten drives, reducing both points per drive and drives; the two effects multiply in quarter scoring, with a larger proportional effect in Q1 where scripts are heavier.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare Q1 totals for games with a backup QB vs starter with pace controls.

interactions.hypothesis: P(scoreless quarter) is not linear in the expected game total: below roughly 38 combined expected points a 0-0 Q1 or Q3 becomes likely, while above about 50 it nearly vanishes; the argmax share also concentrates on Q2 as totals rise because two-minute drives add points mainly in high-efficiency games.
interactions.how_to_test: Bin 2012-2025 games by model expected total and plot empirical P(min quarter = 0) and Q2/Q4 argmax shares; test for a kink versus a logistic-linear fit.

nonlinearities.shape: atoms at 0 and at equal scores
nonlinearities.why: Quarter scores are not near-continuous; zero for each team and equal score pairs hold large probability, so smooth normal approximations misprice tie and BTTS strikes.

nonlinearities.shape: regime step above a lead threshold
nonlinearities.why: Once the lead exceeds about 17 in the 4th quarter, scoring behaviour changes discontinuously because starters leave and teams run the clock.

nonlinearities.shape: step at the effective range boundary
nonlinearities.why: FG probability drops sharply beyond the kicker's range (50-plus yards), so stalled drives past midfield convert to 3 points only in a narrow band that varies by kicker.

mechanism_review.summary: Scoring in a period equals a small number of scoring events, each worth 3, 6, 7, 8 or 2 points, which happen when a possession finishes inside that window. The chain is (1) how many possessions start and finish in the period for each team: determined by the kickoff, the coin-toss deferral choice (which sets who starts Q1 and Q3), tempo, and clock burning; Q2 and Q4 also contain end-of-period tempo regimes; (2) the points per possession in that period, which differs by period because early drives are scripted, late-half drives are hurry-up with timeouts, and the fourth quarter is dominated by game state; (3) the discreteness of a quarter, in which 0, 3, 7, 10 and 14 absorb most of the mass and the two-team joint determines 0-0 and ties; (4) second-half periods being conditional on the halftime margin and on adjustments; and (5) contract specifics: regulation only, OT only in the 2nd half, ties settled by a Tie strike. A game-level total divided by four is a bad model because the distribution of drives and scoring is not uniform across quarters and quarter totals are lumpy.

stages.name: Possession allocation per period
stages.description: How many drives each team gets that begin in a given quarter depends on kickoff order, the second-half kickoff to the team that deferred, scoring that gives the ball back, and clock use. Q1 usually has 2 to 3 drives in total and Q2 3 to 4; a long first drive can consume most of Q1. At the end of a half, a team can run out the clock or force a final possession, so possession counts in Q2 and Q4 are state-dependent. Drive starts and ends should be tracked to the clock.
stages.distribution: Small count (1-5 drives per team per quarter), discrete; Q1 has especially few starts, producing a high zero-score mass

stages.name: Points per possession by period and script
stages.description: Efficiency in a quarter is not the game average: the first 15 scripted plays are rehearsed and tilt towards the offence's best plays, two-minute situations raise passing efficiency, the third quarter follows halftime adjustments, and the fourth quarter has prevent defences and clock-killing. Team strength (EPA) must therefore be carried into period-specific scoring rates with opponent adjustment and strong shrinkage since one team has ~3 drives per quarter.
stages.distribution: Per-drive Bernoulli-like outcomes (TD, FG, none) with period-specific rates; heavy small-sample noise at the team-quarter level

stages.name: Score lattice and tie mass
stages.description: A quarter's team score is mostly 0, 3, 6, 7, 10, 13, 14: a lattice with a spike at 0 for each team and a spike at equal scores for the two teams. Tie and 0-0 probabilities, BTTS and over/under 7.5 therefore depend on joint zero mass and increments. Over 7.5 requires at least a TD plus a point from either side or FG+FG+..., making it a lumpy event; this also generates strong key-number effects around 7 and 3. The whole-game anchor for the period allocation is the market-free team points mean (nfl.model_team_points_mean), so weather, availability and matchup channels enter the period expectation directly instead of through the market.
stages.distribution: Compound discrete distribution with atoms; P(0-0) is material in Q1 and Q3; ties are 10-20% in a quarter depending on scoring level

stages.name: Second-half state dependence
stages.description: Q3 and Q4 depend on the halftime lead: leading teams run more and shorten the game, trailing teams pass and press, and a large lead drives garbage time with backups. Q3 specifically also reflects the opening drive after halftime for the team that deferred. Because the margin is a latent variable only resolved after Q2, pregame quarter-3/4 totals are mixtures over halftime states. For the second-half contracts that count overtime (KXNFL2H, KXNFL2HTOTAL, KXNFL2HSPREAD) a tied regulation adds an overtime points term to the half total and can break a 2H tie, which is modelled as an explicit lattice term from nfl.ot_model. KXNFL2HWINNER is the exception: it settles on regulation only, so its Tie strike keeps the regulation tie mass that OT removes from KXNFL2H. The halftime/full-time contracts (KXNFL1HFT, KXNFLPREPACK1HFT) are the joint of the halftime state and the full-game winner, read directly off this halftime-conditional mixture.
stages.distribution: Mixture over halftime margin states; Q4 scoring is bimodal (competitive vs garbage time)

stages.name: Cross-period dependence and BTTS-every-quarter joint
stages.description: The probability both teams score in every one of four quarters is the joint of eight team-quarter events that are slightly positively associated through the common pace and quality of the offences and negatively through clock burn by a long drive. The product of marginals is not the correct joint.
stages.distribution: Joint over 8 dependent Bernoulli events; probability small, dominated by the weakest-scoring team-quarter

stages.name: Availability, rules and settlement
stages.description: A backup QB or missing key skill player changes early scripting and pace; period contracts count only points scored in the named period (the boundary attribution rule is not stated in the sampled text) with OT inclusion varying by market; ties settle on a Tie strike; postponement rules apply.
stages.distribution: Mostly deterministic given lineup states; QB status is a high-impact discrete mixture

stages.name: Quarter order statistics: highest-scoring and scoreless quarter
stages.description: KXNFLHIGHSCOREQ asks which of the four regulation quarter totals is largest, splitting the payout 1/N on ties; KXNFLNOSCOREQ asks whether the smallest quarter total is zero. Both are functionals of the joint distribution of four lumpy quarter totals, not of any single period. The second and fourth quarters carry structural advantages (two-minute drives before each half end, trailing-team urgency in Q4) so they win the argmax most often; Q1 and Q3 have fewer drives and a large 0-0 atom, so a scoreless quarter is usually Q1 or Q3 and is much more likely in low-total, bad-weather games. Ties at the top (e.g. 7-7 quarters) are common because totals sit on a 3/7 lattice, so the 1/N dead-heat mass must be modelled explicitly.
stages.distribution: Argmax and minimum over four dependent discrete lattice variables; top-quarter ties occur in a material share of games; P(any 0-point quarter) rises steeply as the expected game total falls

contract_review.settlement_definition: 34 live series, all with rules text. Each market counts only points scored inside its named period: Q1-Q3 and the 1st half are regulation by construction; Q4 markets say '(excluding overtime)'; KXNFL2H, 2HTOTAL and 2HSPREAD say '(including overtime)', whereas KXNFL2HWINNER settles on 'the second half of regulation time' (overtime excluded). Totals are 'more than X.5' combined points, team totals 'over X.5' for one team, spreads 'wins by more than X.5' in the period; period-winner series (KXNFL1Q..4Q, 1H, 2H and the *WINNER series) are three-way with a Tie strike that resolves YES when the period score is level. BTTS series need points by both teams in the quarter (all scoring plays count); KXNFLEQBTTS needs both in every regulation quarter. KXNFLNOSCOREQ is YES if the teams combine for 0 points in any regulation quarter; KXNFLHIGHSCOREQ pays the highest-scoring regulation quarter, split 1/N among N tied quarters, OT ignored. KXNFL1HFT and KXNFLPREPACK1HFT are conjunctions of the halftime result and the full-game result (1HFT: 'including overtime'). Postponement: BTTS/1HFT series stay open if the game starts within 48 hours, else fair price; the *WINNER series stay open until the rescheduled game finishes 'within two weeks'.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official league scoring by period (game book/play-by-play quarter attribution); Kalshi references the official final result. Boundary attribution of untimed-down scores is not stated (u7).
variants_and_edge_cases: Overtime inclusion differs: Q1-Q3 and 1H regulation by construction; Q4 series '(excluding overtime)'; KXNFL2H/2HTOTAL/2HSPREAD '(including overtime)'; KXNFL2HWINNER 'second half of regulation time' (excludes OT); KXNFL1HFT full-game leg includes overtime; HIGHSCOREQ, NOSCOREQ and EQBTTS consider regulation quarters only.

Strike construction: totals/spreads/team totals are half-point (7.5, 11.5, 17.5) so no push; period-winner markets are three-way with a Tie strike; KXNFLHIGHSCOREQ pays 1/N on an N-way tie for the top quarter (a dead-heat rule, not a void).

Postponement differs by series: BTTS and 1HFT series resolve to a fair price if the game does not start within 48 hours; the *WINNER series stay open until a rescheduled game finishes within two weeks; quarter total/spread/winner (KXNFL1Q style), half total/spread/winner/team-total (KXNFL1H, 1HTOTAL, 1HSPREAD, 1HTEAMTOTAL, KXNFL2H, 2HTOTAL, 2HSPREAD), NOSCOREQ, HIGHSCOREQ and PREPACK1HFT texts are silent on postponement.
KXNFL1HTOTAL (moved here from game_total) shares the regulation-only first-half window with 1H spread, winner and team-total series. KXNFLDRAFTQB is no longer filed here.
Deep tail rungs (17.5 points in one quarter) exist, priced by tail shape of the period margin lattice.
KXNFLPREPACK1HFT does not state whether its full-game 'wins the game' leg includes overtime or how a full-game tie is handled.

player_availability.label: Player availability, starter and snap-role events
player_availability.target: Whether a named player is active, starts, or meets a role threshold (snaps, designation) per contract source.
player_availability.mechanism: Availability probability = P(plays | injury type, practice sequence, designation, position, team behavior) updated through the week: Wednesday/Thursday estimated practice, Friday status, coach comments, then the Sunday inactive list. The decision-maker is the team (and for some contracts the league), so base rates come from calibrated histories by designation and practice pattern, adjusted for seeding stakes, return timelines and team transparency. Market close time decides which signals are available.

Definitive pre-game signal; timing around 90 min.
Starter ordering changes indicate role changes that affect starter and snap-threshold markets.
Coach press conferences and beat reports often resolve availability before the official designation.
Playing but limited/snap-count.
Clinched teams rest starters, especially in the final week, and coach history of resting players predicts it.
Recent snap share defines the baseline for starter and snap-threshold events and shows trends in role.
Coach habits with designations and rest.
Mid-game exit for snap thresholds.
QB availability has special weight: teams often announce QB decisions earlier than other positions.
Market close vs report timing.
Definitions (active, played, started) and source.
Active/started definitions and source determine labels; reconcile settled outcomes against inactive lists.
Short weeks and byes change practice participation and the odds a questionable player plays.
A recovery clock is the mechanism of return markets; the existing list records status snapshots without a time-to-return model.
Existing inputs hold the raw data but no calibration of participation by sequence and team.
Handles the absences with no injury, which injury inputs cannot predict.
The key mechanism for first-start contracts, absent from the existing list.
Settlement requires a snap rather than active status.
Settlement artefact separate from football events.
Hard rules truncate the distribution of return dates and are missing from the existing list.
Covers WEEKCOMPETE for retired or unsigned players, NEXTTEAM and RETURN, which the injury-report chain cannot model.
Defines the measurable QB gap the benching hazard needs, including for rookies with no NFL sample.
Prices KXNFLWEEKQBSTART and KXNFLDEPTHPOSITIONCLEQB2, which settle on chart slots rather than on play.
KXNFLEVERYWEEKCOMPETE resolves on a snap in every team game of the season.

interactions.hypothesis: Practice sequence x designation x position: DNP-limited-full patterns have different play rates for skill players and linemen; calibrate by position.
Clinched stakes x minor injury: coaches rest at higher rates in meaningless games; Questionable becomes Out more often.
Close time x inactive list: before the list the price should be a probability mixture; afterwards, near 0 or 1, and mispricing shows up in stale quotes.

The same practice pattern (limited, limited, full) predicts play at different rates for different positions and teams: for offensive linemen and QBs the full Friday practice often means active, while for running backs a limited Friday after a lower-body injury means a smaller snap load but still a play; the mapping is conditional on position and team transparency.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate P(play) by pattern within position group and team tercile and compare with pooled estimate.

interactions.hypothesis: Return probability is zero until the IR minimum has passed, then follows the injury-specific clock, and a coach's statement about 'week to week' shifts the clock; the curve is piecewise, with a hard step at four games for players on IR.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare empirical return week to IR minimum and injury type for players placed on IR.

interactions.hypothesis: QB benching hazard is low during the season and rises in the week after a bye or a bad loss; the chart for that week is the first moment the change is visible, so the contract window determines whether the hazard spike falls inside it.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate hazard by weeks since bye and by prior game result; map to windows 7-10.

interactions.hypothesis: A Questionable veteran on a team that has clinched is much more likely to be held out than the same player on a team fighting for a seed; stakes change the mapping from designation to play, mainly in the last two weeks.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare play rates for Questionable players by clinch status and week.

interactions.hypothesis: For a market that closes before the inactive list, probability is a mixture over states; after the list the outcome is nearly known, so time-to-close determines how much information the pregame model can use and where stale quotes appear.
interactions.how_to_test: Measure forecast accuracy by hours-to-kickoff at close.

interactions.hypothesis: The QB2 slot probability depends on the QB1 outcome: when the incumbent is healthy and performing, the backup order is stable and QB2 markets are near-deterministic; once a QB1 change becomes likely, the current QB2 is likely to be promoted out of the QB2 slot, so P(QB2) falls as P(QB1 change) rises for the current backup and rises for the third-stringer.
interactions.how_to_test: On 2016-2025 chart snapshots, regress next-week QB2 identity on current QB2 and an indicator of a QB1 change, and compare slot transition matrices with and without a QB1 change.

nonlinearities.shape: step function by designation
nonlinearities.why: Participation probability steps from about zero (Out) through low (Doubtful) and roughly even (Questionable) to near one (no designation), so treating designation as ordinal-linear misstates the middle category.

nonlinearities.shape: convex in performance shortfall and spike after bye
nonlinearities.why: Benching probability is low until performance falls below a threshold, then rises quickly; and the week after the bye has a spike, so a linear performance coefficient misses the clustering.

nonlinearities.shape: right-skewed survival with hard step at the IR minimum
nonlinearities.why: Return time has a long tail of setbacks and a hard floor for IR placements; the probability of playing by week k is not linear in elapsed time.

nonlinearities.shape: exponential decay in weekly hazard
nonlinearities.why: Season streak survival is approximately exp(-17h): moving the weekly miss hazard from 1% to 4% drops survival from about 84% to about 50%, so small errors in weekly hazard become large errors in price.

mechanism_review.summary: Availability outcomes come from a sequence of decisions by medical staff, coaches and front offices acting on physical state and incentives. For a one-snap participation market: P(plays) = P(medically able on game day) x P(team chooses to activate him) x P(he takes at least one snap given active). Medical ability follows an injury-specific recovery clock (a hamstring strain, a high ankle sprain and an ACL tear have very different return-time distributions) revealed through the practice sequence (did not participate, limited, full) and the Friday designation; the team's choice reflects stakes, rest policy for veterans, roster depth and sometimes a coach's reluctance to disclose; and the snap condition fails for emergency depth players and gadget roles. For first-start markets the process is a hazard over weeks that the current starter is replaced (benching for performance, injury, a bye-week reset, a contract or draft-capital decision) and the depth chart lists the new name; the chart is a team publication with its own timing. Weekly starter and QB2 markets read the same depth-chart process as a categorical over the team's quarterbacks each week, and the every-week participation market compounds a weekly injury and rest hazard over a whole season. Close time determines which of these signals have been revealed.

stages.name: Physical state and injury recovery clock
stages.description: The underlying cause is the injury (or absence of one): body part, grade, whether surgery occurred, and elapsed days since onset. Each injury type has a recovery-time distribution that is right-skewed with a long tail of setbacks, and return-to-play rules (IR minimum of four games, designated-to-return windows) put hard constraints on the clock. The player's own history of reinjury adds to the hazard.
stages.distribution: Right-skewed recovery time (Weibull/lognormal) by injury type; long tail of setbacks; discrete hard constraints from IR rules

stages.name: Practice sequence to official designation
stages.description: Between Wednesday and Friday, teams report each player's practice participation (did not participate, limited, full) and then a game designation (Out, Doubtful, Questionable). The mapping from the sequence to actual participation is calibratable and differs by position and by team transparency: a limited-limited-full pattern for a skill player implies something different from the same pattern for a lineman, and a Friday 'Questionable' resolves very differently across teams.
stages.distribution: Ordinal sequence mapped to Bernoulli participation; step probabilities at designations (Out ~ 0, Doubtful low, Questionable around half, no designation near one)

stages.name: Team decision, rest policy and healthy scratches
stages.description: Even a healthy player can be inactive: veterans rested in meaningless late games, rookies and depth players left off the 46-man game-day list, players disciplined by coaches or held back after returning. The decision depends on coach, roster composition, the stakes (clinched seeds) and the opponent.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli at the team's discretion; base rates by role and coach; higher for veterans in weeks 17-18 and for backups

stages.name: Depth-chart ordering and QB-change hazard
stages.description: For first-start contracts the question is whether and when the depth chart lists the player first. A QB gets promoted when the incumbent is injured, benched (performance relative to expectation, team record, a bye week as a natural reset point) or when development timelines force a change. The hazard per week depends on incumbent performance, the challenger's draft capital and contract, and the coach's patience; the contract's window turns this into a probability over about 3-4 charts. The incumbent-versus-challenger gap is measured by nfl.qb_challenger_prior, which uses a draft-slot prior when the challenger has few dropbacks.
stages.distribution: Discrete-time hazard per published chart; event probability 1 - product of (1 - h_week); rare but front-loaded after bye weeks

stages.name: Snap appearance given active
stages.description: A player who is active may not see a snap: an emergency third QB, a gadget wide receiver, a backup lineman, or a rotational back in a blowout. Whether special-teams snaps count is a contract detail. The conditional probability of at least one snap depends on role, game script and injury attrition among starters.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli with role-specific base rates; near one for starters and near zero for emergency depth

stages.name: Information vintage and market close
stages.description: The state of information available at market close is what matters: probability before Wednesday reflects only the injury and base rates; after Friday designations it reflects the practice sequence; after the 90-minute inactive list it is nearly decided. Contracts that close earlier carry a mixture over scenarios; those closing at kickoff are almost certain.
stages.distribution: Probability mass moves from a prior mixture to near 0/1 as vintages accrue; discrete jumps at report times

stages.name: Roster-status transitions for non-roster players
stages.description: For a retired, unsigned, suspended or long-term injured player the chain is not injury then designation then inactive list but a status transition: a decision to un-retire or sign, a contract before the roster deadline, a physical and activation (or IR/PUP activation), and then a snap. The sampled KXNFLWEEKCOMPETE subject is outside any current roster, and KXNFLRETURN requires a regular-season appearance for a named team before a given week, so probabilities come from comeback reference classes, activation-window rules and insider-reported interest rather than practice participation.
stages.distribution: Rare-event discrete-time hazards with long periods of near-zero probability and jumps at reported interest; binary outcomes after a multi-step funnel

stages.name: Weekly depth-chart slot designation: starter and QB2
stages.description: KXNFLWEEKQBSTART is a categorical over the team's quarterbacks for one week's published chart, and KXNFLDEPTHPOSITIONCLEQB2 asks who is listed second. The QB2 slot depends on the QB1 outcome: if the incumbent is injured or benched, the former QB2 moves up and a third QB (or a signing) becomes QB2, so P(player is QB2) = P(he is not promoted to QB1) x P(he outranks the remaining backups). Preseason competition, draft capital, coach statements and whether the team lists co-starters ('OR') decide the order; injured-but-listed players still count, so the chart publication policy matters more than health.
stages.distribution: Categorical over 2-4 quarterbacks per team-week; strong persistence week to week with jumps after injuries, bye weeks and benchings

stages.name: Season-long every-week participation streak
stages.description: KXNFLEVERYWEEKCOMPETE needs a snap in each of roughly 17 team games. The probability is a product of weekly survival terms: each week the player can miss through new injury (position- and age-specific weekly hazard, higher for players with a recent injury history), lingering injury (recovery clock), rest decisions late in the season and benching or healthy scratch. Because one miss ends the streak, small weekly hazards compound: a 3% weekly miss rate gives about 60% survival over 17 games. Trades do not break it, and games before he joins a roster do not count.
stages.distribution: Product of weekly Bernoulli survival terms with heterogeneous, positively autocorrelated hazards (injury begets missed games); strongly convex in the weekly hazard

talent_strength.note: For first-start contracts the incumbent-versus-challenger EPA gap with a draft-capital prior for unproven QBs is defined in nfl.qb_challenger_prior; its calibration for rookies remains open in u3.

opponent_matchup.note: Opponent identity has little role in whether a named player is active or listed first on a depth chart; in-game snap exposure can vary, but that effect is second-order and handled by the snap-given-active input.

coaching_scheme.note: Coach transparency, rest habits and QB patience.

environment.note: Weather and venue have no meaningful effect on whether a player is active or listed first; heat illness or conditions rarely drive inactive decisions, so no environment input is needed here.

game_context_script.note: Blowouts determine whether deep backups see a snap.

pace_volume.note: The contracts count a single snap or a chart listing, not volume; plays per game affect only the chance that an active backup appears, which is covered by the snap-given-active input.

efficiency_conversion.note: The practice-sequence-to-play mapping is the 'conversion rate' of the process.

distribution_variance.note: Right-skewed recovery times and weekly hazards.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Stakes, short weeks and rest policy.

officiating_rules.note: IR, PUP, NFI and suspension rules impose hard availability constraints.

settlement_contract.note: Snap, chart-listing and signing definitions with close time.

contract_review.settlement_definition: Eight live series; seven have rules text, KXNFLWEEKSTART is TITLE_ONLY. Participation: KXNFLWEEKCOMPETE resolves YES if the named player takes at least one snap, even if nullified by penalty, in the stated regular-season week; KXNFLEVERYWEEKCOMPETE needs at least one snap in every regular-season game played by the team whose active roster he is on, byes excluded and games before he joins a team not counting; KXNFLRETURN needs him to enter a regular-season game for the named team after a date and before a week (preseason excluded). Depth chart: KXNFLFIRSTSTART (listed as starting QB 'for the first time this season') and KXNFLDEBUT ('for the first time', i.e. a career first start) resolve YES on his team's official depth chart within an inclusive week range (byes skipped; fallback to official team communications); KXNFLWEEKQBSTART resolves for the QB listed as the team's starter in the stated week; KXNFLDEPTHPOSITIONCLEQB2 resolves YES if the player is officially designated QB2 for the week (injured-but-listed counts; practice-squad/inactive players do not qualify unless promoted; elimination before a postseason week resolves NO; bye weeks use the last chart before the bye). Source: official depth charts/team communications for designations; official participation records for snaps.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official depth charts published by the team and official team communications (injury reports, press releases) for designations; official game participation records/play-by-play for snaps.
variants_and_edge_cases: Five availability definitions: one snap in a week (WEEKCOMPETE), a snap in every team game of the season (EVERYWEEKCOMPETE), first regular-season appearance for a named team in a window (RETURN), depth-chart starter (FIRSTSTART, DEBUT, WEEKQBSTART, WEEKSTART title only) and depth-chart QB2 (DEPTHPOSITION).

Depth-chart contracts settle on the published listing: a listed starter who is then inactive still resolves YES, an injured but listed QB2 resolves YES, and a surprise starter after a late injury may not appear on a chart published earlier in the week.

KXNFLDEBUT's sampled market uses first-start wording without 'this season' (a career first start, week range 7-10 for a rookie QB), whereas KXNFLFIRSTSTART is the first start of the current season; neither is a first-appearance definition despite the DEBUT title.

EVERYWEEKCOMPETE: byes excluded and games before joining a roster do not count; whether a week in which the player is on a reserve list (IR, suspension) breaks the streak follows from 'each game ... played by a team on whose active roster' he is a member, which suggests games while off the active roster do not count against him (not explicit).
QB2 postseason weeks resolve NO if the team is already eliminated; bye weeks use the last chart before the bye.
KXNFLNEXTTEAM was re-filed to off_field_events and is no longer claimed here.

QB2 text says an injured player still listed at the position resolves YES but also that inactive players do not qualify unless promoted to the active roster; precedence for an injured, listed but game-day-inactive QB2 is not stated.

season_win_totals_and_futures.label: Season win totals, playoffs, division, conference and Super Bowl futures
season_win_totals_and_futures.target: Probability of season-long team outcomes: win count thresholds or exact wins, playoffs, division, seed, conference title, Super Bowl, head-to-head season comparisons.
season_win_totals_and_futures.mechanism: Simulate the remaining season from time-varying team strength with uncertainty, QB and key-player availability, home/rest effects and the full tiebreaker rules; produce correlated probabilities for wins, playoffs, seeds, division, conference and championship. Preseason rating priors blend last-year ratings with roster continuity regression and market win totals; in-season updates use adjusted efficiency and luck regression. Cross-market coherence (sum-to-one, implications) constrains the family set and exposes stale quotes.

inputs.why: The simulation turns team ratings and schedules into correlated win, seed and title probabilities with proper tiebreakers.
Time-varying rating with uncertainty.
Preseason ratings need regression based on how much of last year's production returns, especially at QB and lines.
Forward-looking opponent strength changes expected wins; stale last-year records mislead.
Records overstated by close-game luck should be regressed before using them for future win expectations.
Takeaway luck inflates records and ratings; using expected turnovers gives a truer strength estimate.
QB injury and quality dominate team win variance, and replacement QB scenarios matter for season simulations.
Distribution of key-player absences (QB, EDGE, OL) widens win distributions and lowers the title odds of top-heavy teams.
Current injuries and expected return dates adjust near-term ratings and in-season futures.
Title and conference markets depend on seed, bye and bracket path, not only team rating.
Late-season rest and incentives.
Bye placement and rest differences in the schedule shift expected wins marginally across teams.
Linked futures must satisfy sum-to-one and implication constraints; violations flag stale or mispriced contracts.
Sportsbook futures prices provide the benchmark probabilities after de-vig, although they are vig-heavy.
Price drift around injuries and results shows how quickly futures incorporate new information.
Ties, cancelled/forfeited games.
Volume and open interest weight how much the price reflects information versus stale quotes, and bound feasible size.
Executed trades show where liquidity actually transacted, informing realistic fills and whether price moves are informed flow.
Win totals and division markets are tails of a 17-game schedule simulation with injury and rating uncertainty.
Controls tail mass of wins and playoff probabilities in the season simulation, which the current catalog states as 'with uncertainty' without a defined quantity.
Directly converts quarterback availability into a team win distribution, which the current catalog treats as a flag.
Explains why division and seed contracts are not functions of expected wins alone and identifies when a single rival game decides the contract.
Title and round-qualification futures depend on playoff-time strength, not on the average over games with a different lineup.
The sampled KXNFLDRAFT1ST rules state that the team making the selection resolves YES, and none of the other inputs model the loser race or pick ownership.
Defines the latent strength that all win-total, exact-win, seed, division and title simulations consume, without sportsbook ratings or spreads.
Provides the probability distribution over the season of a team's next playoff appearance for KXNFLENDSTREAK.

interactions.hypothesis: QB risk x schedule: probability the QB misses games and which opponents those games are against changes the win distribution non-linearly.
Close-game luck x rating: teams outperforming Pythagorean expectation carry inflated ratings and regress in the second half; the simulation should use luck-adjusted ratings.
Seed x bracket path: bye and home field make title odds convex in seeding probability.
Market coherence x liquidity: where linked futures violate sum-to-one, the least liquid contract is likely stale.

A single team-level strength draw and a quarterback-absence scenario both apply to all of a team's remaining games, so they jointly widen the win-total distribution beyond the binomial; the shared draw dominates early in the season while the absence scenario adds a discrete left shift, and the two together create the fat tails at the 4-win and 13-win lines.
interactions.how_to_test: Backtest win-total and exact-win calibration at the 10th and 90th percentiles of the simulated distribution for (a) independent games, (b) shared strength draw only, (c) shared draw plus QB scenario mixture.

interactions.hypothesis: The cost of a quarterback's missed games depends on who the games are against: a miss in a division rival game costs more in a tied race and in a weak week of the schedule costs little, so the timing of absence interacts with schedule.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate the same absence in different weeks and measure the change in playoff probability.

interactions.hypothesis: Division outcomes are zero-sum: a rival's win is a loss for another contender, so probabilities of division titles across four teams are negatively correlated and sum to one; late-season motivation changes the leverage once a team is clinched or eliminated.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare division-winner probabilities from a joint simulation with independent probabilities and measure the sum-to-one error.

interactions.hypothesis: Title probability is convex in seed because only the top seed receives a bye and home field, and convex in full-strength rating because a team must win three or four games in a row; a small rating edge compounds across rounds.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate title probability by seed and rating bucket using historical playoffs.

interactions.hypothesis: Teams with a record better than their point differential carry an inflated results-based rating that regresses; the regression is strongest early in the season and for teams whose own rating has a large posterior sd, so pythag luck should shrink the own rating by an amount conditional on that sd.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress second-half win rate on first-half record and point differential, interacted with games played.

interactions.hypothesis: Once a team is eliminated from the playoffs it may lose more often (tanking incentives, starters rested), and a clinched top seed rests starters in Weeks 17-18; both switch the per-game win hazard late in the season, which ends long win streaks of clinched teams and delays the first win of a winless eliminated team, so sequence contracts cannot assume a constant rating across the season.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare win rates relative to rating-implied probability for eliminated and clinched teams in Weeks 15-18 versus Weeks 1-14 over 2012-2025, and the frequency of streaks ending in Weeks 17-18.

nonlinearities.shape: S-shaped: playoff probability rises steeply from about 8 to 11 expected wins and flattens outside
nonlinearities.why: The qualification threshold lies in the middle of the win distribution, so a change of one expected win moves playoff probability by 15-20 points near 9 wins and by a few points at 5 or 13 wins.

nonlinearities.shape: step: the top seed receives a bye and the other six seeds do not
nonlinearities.why: A step function in seed distinguishes the number-one seed from the rest, so the title probability rises discontinuously and a team's expected wins only partly determines it.

nonlinearities.shape: mixture: a discrete loss of several rating points with probability equal to the chance of the miss
nonlinearities.why: The quarterback's absence shifts team rating by a lump, so the rating is a mixture rather than a normal, and the win distribution has a heavier left tail for teams with weak backups.

nonlinearities.shape: variance of the win total grows with the square of games played times the rating variance (rating sd about 4 points before the season, shrinking as results arrive)
nonlinearities.why: The shared error contributes quadratically to the variance of wins, so it dominates binomial variance by season end for a given rating uncertainty.

mechanism_review.summary: Season outcomes are produced by a hierarchical process. Each team has a latent strength with real uncertainty at the start of the season (the prior is a blend of last-year performance, roster continuity and quarterback change, regressed hard toward the league mean) that is learned slowly from games, and that shared uncertainty acts on every game the team plays, making win totals more dispersed than independent games would give. Each game's win probability is a function of rating difference, home field, rest, and the availability of the quarterback and a handful of other key players, which are random across the season and correlated within a team. Win totals aggregate 17 such games, ties are possible, and standings follow from all teams' results through the league's tiebreakers, where division games are zero-sum and who plays whom decides leverage. Seeds give a bye only to the top seed, and playoff single elimination turns seed and full-strength roster into title odds. Cross-market consistency then follows from the same simulated worlds.

stages.name: Latent team strength with persistent uncertainty
stages.description: Each team's latent strength enters every game and is updated by results; early in the season most of the uncertainty is the shared prior error, which does not average out across 17 games. The prior combines previous efficiency (regressed), roster continuity, quarterback change and coaching change, and the posterior is revised by opponent-adjusted performance with luck-related components removed.
stages.distribution: Normal prior on the own rating with sd about 4.0 points of margin before Week 1 (nfl.own_team_rating_market_free, assumption to recalibrate) shrinking to about 2.5 points after 17 games; the shared error induces correlation between a team's game results.

stages.name: Key-player availability, especially the quarterback
stages.description: The quarterback accounts for a larger share of team strength than any other player, and his missed games change the whole team's rating for those games; other key players (edge, tackle, cornerback) matter less. Injuries are a random process across the season with clustering, and the drop to the backup depends on who the backup is.
stages.distribution: Mixture across scenarios: QB1 plays all games (about 70% of teams), misses 1-4 games, or misses a large block; rating shift of several points between QB1 and backup, team-specific.

stages.name: Game-level win probability and schedule
stages.description: For each remaining game win probability is a logistic function of the rating difference plus home field and rest/travel, and the schedule composition determines both the expected wins and the leverage. Ties can occur, contributing half-win in standings and a not-lost result in some contracts.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli with probability in roughly 0.1-0.9; ties ~0.2-0.3% per game; outcomes conditionally independent given ratings and availability.

stages.name: Win-total aggregation and exact-win distribution
stages.description: The number of wins is the sum of game outcomes, with variance larger than the binomial because of shared rating uncertainty and correlated availability. Exact-win and threshold contracts need the full probability mass function, and a 9.5 line is much more sensitive to the tails than to the mean. The simulation is conditioned on games already played (banked wins, ties and tiebreak state as of the current week) and on current injury and quarterback status, not re-run from Week 1. KXNFLWINSWEEK reads the same simulated games truncated at games scheduled in weeks 1-12, KXNFLH2HWINS the joint win totals of two teams (50/50 on equal wins), and KXNFLDIVMOSTWINS/DIVLEASTWINS/DIVISIONWINS the sums over a division's four teams.
stages.distribution: Overdispersed Poisson-binomial with sd approximately 2.0-2.4 wins; exact-win probabilities peak around 15-20 percent at the mean.

stages.name: Standings, tiebreakers and zero-sum leverage
stages.description: Division and seed contracts are determined jointly: division games produce a winner and a loser, so a team's chance depends on rivals' results, and ties at the same record are resolved by the league's tiebreak ladder (head-to-head, division record, common opponents, strength of victory and others). Games between direct competitors are more informative than other games. The same standings draws settle the exact division order (KXNFLDIVISIONORDER), worst-to-first (a 2025-26 fourth-place team finishing first) and the division-wins aggregates.
stages.distribution: Joint distribution across all 32 teams' win totals with negative correlation among division rivals; tiebreak resolution is a deterministic function of full results.

stages.name: Seed, bye and bracket path to title
stages.description: Only the top seed receives a bye, and seed determines home field and opponent strength; the title contract is the product of three or four game win probabilities in a reseeded bracket where roster health at playoff time matters and regular-season rest games distort the rating. Playoff win probabilities use a full-strength rating rather than season-average. Round-reached contracts (KXNFLSTAGEOFELIM, KXNFLROUNDQUAL) and the conference-championship pairing (KXNFLMATCHUP) are read from the same bracket draws.
stages.distribution: Product of 3-4 correlated game probabilities; convex in seed because of the bye; title odds heavy-tailed across the top teams.

stages.name: Sequence and extreme futures: undefeated, win streaks, any-team-17 and first-win races
stages.description: Several contracts depend on the order of results rather than the total: the last undefeated team (week of first loss, ties do not count as losses, same-week losses tie), the last team to win (week of first win), undefeated in division, any team reaching N consecutive regular-season wins, and any team reaching 17 wins. Each is a first-passage or maximum over 32 correlated team paths, so it must be read from the same simulated season paths, keeping weekly order, byes and tie results, rather than from win-total marginals. Late-season rest of clinched teams and tanking of eliminated teams change the hazard of ending runs.
stages.distribution: Passage times on the weekly grid (discrete, with ties at the same week) and maxima over 32 teams; heavy dependence on the one or two strongest teams' rating draws.

stages.name: Multi-season horizon: season of the next playoff appearance
stages.description: KXNFLENDSTREAK prices which future season ends a team's playoff drought, so it extends the current-season simulation with a year-to-year model of team strength: roughly one third reversion toward average each offseason, a random component from roster churn, a jump when a new starting quarterback arrives, and a playoff probability per season from the fourteen-team format. The current season's playoff probability is the first term; later seasons carry most of the uncertainty.
stages.distribution: Discrete first-passage distribution over seasons, geometric-like after the first year with a rate set by the reverted rating and QB-change jumps.

talent_strength.note: Own market-free rating (nfl.own_team_rating_market_free) with uncertainty and playoff-time full-strength rating; the catalog nfl.ratings input mixes market-implied history, is audited BENCHMARK_ONLY and is removed from stages and coverage.

opponent_matchup.note: Opponent strength and the matchups among direct rivals.

role_personnel.note: Quarterback and replacement quality dominate role effects at the team level.

availability_news.note: Injury vintages and scenario tree for the quarterback.

coaching_scheme.note: Head-coach and coordinator changes are part of the preseason prior but have no specified quantity; the effect of a new play-caller on team win expectation is not defined in the catalog.

environment.note: Venue and weather matter in single games but their season-level effect on win totals is small and symmetric across teams, except through home-field and dome versus outdoor schedules already in the rating and rest inputs.

game_context_script.note: Seed and bracket path define playoff game contexts; in-game script is not relevant at season level.

pace_volume.note: Season-level wins are not driven by a count of opportunities such as plays or possessions as a modelling stage; pace enters only through the rating's efficiency measures.

efficiency_conversion.note: Close-game and takeaway luck removal from ratings.

distribution_variance.note: Overdispersed win totals and joint division outcomes.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest, byes and seeding incentives.

officiating_rules.note: Officials do not alter season outcomes beyond what is already captured in the team's results; the tiebreaker rules are the relevant rule set and are included under standings.

settlement_contract.note: All 98 series have rules text: per-team WINS-*/EXACTWINS* say ties do not count as wins, sequence contracts define bye, same-week and tie conventions, standings contracts cite the league tiebreak methodology; open: tie line absent from KXNFLWINS/WINS-ANY (u1), #1-seed bye under ROUNDQUAL (u6), no cancelled-game clause (u7).

contract_review.settlement_definition: Ninety-eight live series, all with rules text, settling on the 2026-27 regular season or postseason. Win totals: KXNFLWINS ('wins at least 9 games'), per-team KXNFLWINS-* ('more than N wins') and KXNFLEXACTWINS* ('exactly N wins'), with the per-team texts stating 'Ties do not count as wins' (the sampled per-team markets are for 2025-26); KXNFLWINS-ANY asks whether any team wins 17; KXNFLWINSWEEK counts games scheduled in weeks 1-12 only; KXNFLH2HWINS is 50/50 on equal wins. Division aggregates: DIVISIONWINS (at least N total wins), DIVMOSTWINS and DIVLEASTWINS ($1/N rounded down among tied divisions). Standings: division winners (KXNFLAFCEAST etc.), exact order (KXNFLDIVISIONORDER) and worst-to-first under the league's official tiebreak methodology; seeds at the end of the regular season (KXNFL1SEED, KXNFLSEED, KXNFLSEEDOU '#N seed or better'). Postseason: PLAYOFF, PLAYOFFC (both teams), ROUNDQUAL (qualifies for the divisional round), STAGEOFELIM (round of elimination, with failure to qualify as its own outcome), PLAYOFFHOST (scheduled to host a playoff game, championship excluded), MATCHUP (conference-championship pairing), AFCCHAMP/NFCCHAMP and SBOUTCOME. Sequence contracts: KXNFLWINSTREAK (any team with at least N consecutive regular-season wins), KXNFLLASTTOLOSE (week of first loss; a tie is not a loss; same-week losses tie), KXNFLLASTTOWIN (week of first win), KXNFLDIVUNDEFEATED (a tie is not a loss). KXNFLENDSTREAK prices the season of a team's next playoff appearance and resolves No if the franchise ceases or relocates first. Whether the bye-holding #1 seed 'qualifies for the divisional round' is not stated (u6).
contract_review.settlement_data_source: The rules refer to the league's regular-season standings, the 'Governing League' official tie-breaking methodology (division order, worst-to-first) and announced playoff schedules; no explicit data vendor is stated.
variants_and_edge_cases: Per-team KXNFLWINS-* ('more than N wins') and KXNFLEXACTWINS* ('exactly N wins') state 'Ties do not count as wins'; the main KXNFLWINS series ('at least N games') and KXNFLWINS-ANY do not repeat the tie line. The sampled per-team markets reference the 2025-26 season, so 2026-27 listings are assumed to keep the wording. Ties occur at roughly 0.25 percent per game (about 9 in 3,700 games since 2012, to be recomputed from nflverse schedules).

KXNFLSBOUTCOME (exact winner and runner-up) and KXNFLPLAYOFFC (both teams make playoffs) are joint events: for same-conference or same-division pairs the events are negatively correlated through zero-sum games, for different conferences close to independent.

Regular-season contracts (seed, win totals, division) are fixed at the end of Week 18 under the league's tiebreaker rules, while KXNFLROUNDQUAL and the pairing market depend on the playoff bracket and reseeding; KXNFLENDSTREAK spans several future seasons.

KXNFLROUNDQUAL: with seven playoff teams per conference the #1 seed skips the wild-card round, so whether it 'qualifies for the divisional round' changes P(contract) by about P(1 seed); the sampled rule has only the primary sentence (u6).

KXNFLENDSTREAK asks in which season a team next makes the playoffs (2030-31 in the sample), a multi-season first-passage problem with roster and coaching turnover, and resolves No if the franchise relocates or ceases first.

KXNFLDIVMOSTWINS pays 1/N among tied divisions, KXNFLH2HWINS 50/50 on equal wins, and KXNFLLASTTOWIN ties teams whose first wins fall in the same week, so the simulation must keep exact tie states rather than rounding.
KXNFLLASTTOLOSE measures the week of first loss: ties do not end the run, same-week losses are ties, and a team on a bye is still undefeated that week; KXNFLLASTTOWIN mirrors this for first wins.
KXNFLSTAGEOFELIM includes a 'Regular Season' outcome for failing to qualify, so its outcomes partition the season; KXNFLPLAYOFFHOST excludes the championship game and counts scheduled hosting.

KXNFLWINS-ANY (any team to 17 wins) and KXNFLWINSTREAK (any team to N straight) are maxima over all 32 teams, driven by the strongest teams' rating uncertainty and remaining schedules rather than one team's mean.

season_awards.label: Season awards (MVP, OPOY, DPOY, ROY and similar)
season_awards.target: Which candidate is named winner of an annual award by the official body.
season_awards.mechanism: Winner probability = P(candidate survives injuries and team results) x P(voters choose him | stats, team success, narrative). Production features (EPA, yards, TDs vs peers), team record and positional bias determine the candidate set; the narrative path through the season and ballot timing determines the vote; injuries and team collapse eliminate candidates. Betting and prediction-market odds are benchmarks only and are not inputs to this chain.

inputs.why: Voters reward team success, so award probability depends on team win and seed distributions.
Electorate composition, ballot close date and tie rules determine which information can still affect the result.
For quarterback-dominated awards, efficiency and volume to date are the production leg of voting.
TD hot streaks inflate narratives; regression suggests production may be overstated.
Accrual and remaining schedule.
Remaining opponent difficulty.
Eligibility (e.g. rookie status), definition of the award and which body announces determine the candidate set.
Captures threshold effects in voting that a smooth production-to-vote function misses, especially for OPOY, DPOY and rookie awards driven by round-number totals.
Needed to make winner probabilities sum to one and to price second-tier candidates on a team that has a front runner.
Defines the viable candidate set and base rates for KXNFLDROTY, KXNFLOROTY, KXNFLROTM and Rookie All-Team, the awards sampled in the rules text.
The October rookie-of-the-month sample contract is decided inside a short window; opportunities vary by bye and the model must use the real game count.
Gives KXNFLCOTY (and the Comeback/COTY style awards) a quantity that responds to over-performance, which the existing production-based inputs lack.
Provides a voter-behaviour signal without importing prices, helping to distinguish the front runner from candidates with equal production.
Gives DPOY/DROY/OPOY/OROY a production measure that is comparable across positions, instead of the weak award-stats and QB-only fields.
Turns banked production into a projected final production rank, the quantity voters ultimately compare, at the date the contract trades.
Sets the probability that a named candidate is in the announced class, which is the only event KXNFLHALLOFFAME and KXNFLHOFINDUCTEES settle on.
Gives KXNFLEXECOTY a candidate model; none of the player-award inputs describes front-office credit.
Provides the only candidate model for KXNFLWPMOTY, whose outcome is unrelated to production inputs.
KXNFLPROOTY and the All-Pro offensive-line slots depend on protection evidence that no production input supplies.

Ranked-ballot aggregator parametrised by voters, places and points vector per award and season (MVP top-5 10-5-3-2-1 and a top 5 for all eight AP awards in 2025 are seen in search-result copies only; earlier non-MVP schemes, the 2022 start and the tie rule are unverified) that turns candidate features into winner probabilities in stage s6.

Supplies each candidate's production rank among peers as one ballot feature for nfl.vote_outcome_model; it is not the winner rule, because the AP winner is the highest total of ranked-ballot points, not the maximum of production.
Narrative momentum, injuries and highlight events shift voters' perception and candidate availability before the ballot closes; betting odds are not used.
Games-played availability risk for remaining games decides whether a candidate survives to ballot close; staged in the availability stage and in a threshold non-linearity.

interactions.hypothesis: MVP voters effectively require a top-two seed for quarterbacks: below that line a leading efficiency edge earns little, above it the same edge translates into most of the first-place votes. The effect of production is therefore conditional on the seed distribution.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare winners' seeds historically and fit vote share as a function of production separately for seeded and unseeded candidates.

interactions.hypothesis: A record or milestone chase concentrates the narrative when the candidate is on pace with games to spare; missed games reduce both the total and the probability of reaching the threshold, so the milestone effect is conditional on staying healthy through the remaining weeks.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate P(milestone) with and without injury risk; compare vote-share residuals for candidates who reached versus narrowly missed thresholds.

interactions.hypothesis: Candidates with correlated support (same team, same position) have negatively correlated chances of winning, so the joint distribution of winners is not a product of marginals; a rival's collapse benefits his teammate more than the field.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit a joint vote model on historical ballots and compare the log-likelihood to independent softmax; test beta > 0.

interactions.hypothesis: Touchdown luck is rewarded by voters only when it is visible: the vote-share boost from touchdown counts above expectation is multiplied by primetime and highlight exposure, so for a low-exposure candidate a lucky touchdown total adds little, while for a high-exposure candidate it adds vote share even though regression predicts it will fade.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress past vote share on td_luck x exposure index (primetime snaps share, straw-poll rank) and test the product term against td_luck and exposure alone.

interactions.hypothesis: For a monthly rookie award the chance to be selected is roughly proportional to the number of games in the window times expected production per game, so a high draft slot with a bye in the window can lose to a lower slot with five games.
interactions.how_to_test: Model window outcomes with games in window as an exposure term and test the coefficient against 1.

interactions.hypothesis: Executive and Coach of the Year voters credit the same turnaround to different people: when a new head coach arrives with few roster additions, writers credit the coach; when the roster turned over through trades and free agency under an incumbent coach, they credit the executive, so the two awards' candidate probabilities for one team are partly substitutes conditional on the cause of the win surprise.
interactions.how_to_test: Across 2000-2025 team-seasons with win surprise above +3, compare the rate of COTY versus Executive of the Year wins by new-coach flag and acquisition-share tercile.

interactions.hypothesis: An injury changes a candidate's vote probability by an amount that depends on whether it occurs before or after ballots close and on how many games remain, so the ballot model must be fed the injury and the ballot-close date together, not the injury alone.
interactions.how_to_test: Split news events by weeks before ballot close and measure change in vote share and in the model's own ballot-based probabilities.

nonlinearities.shape: step-like: vote share jumps at the first seed or division title and is flat elsewhere
nonlinearities.why: Voter behaviour treats a number-one seed as a qualification, so the expected vote is a step in seed rather than linear in wins.

nonlinearities.shape: piecewise: nearly no penalty for 1-2 missed games, steep penalty beyond about 3 missed games
nonlinearities.why: A candidate who misses three or more games is often dropped from the ballot, so award probability is not linear in games played.

nonlinearities.shape: cliff near round-number thresholds and records; flat elsewhere
nonlinearities.why: Voters remember totals like 2,000 yards or the single-season sack record, so probability changes sharply across the threshold.

nonlinearities.shape: square-root scaling of variance with games in the window, with a mean proportional to games
nonlinearities.why: A 5-game window has a different winner distribution than a 3-game window; ignoring the count mis-estimates the favourite's probability by changing both mean and sd.

mechanism_review.summary: An award is decided by a bounded electorate that ranks candidates from what it saw, not from true value. The chain starts with who is eligible (rookie status, offence versus defence) and who plays enough to be considered. Production is then measured relative to the peers the voters implicitly compare against, mostly through the counting stats and milestones they remember (yards, touchdowns, sacks, interceptions) rather than efficiency. Team success acts as a multiplier, strongly for the MVP and the Coach of the Year. The narrative path (hot streak, late-season surge, primetime exposure, injury timing relative to ballots) moves a candidate within the list, and among close candidates the split of votes across teammates and similar profiles decides the points total. Finally the contract adds mechanics: ballot close, ties paying 1/N, and monthly windows with only a handful of games. Predictions must therefore be of voter behaviour on a candidate set, not of player quality. Three honours sit outside the production chain (Executive of the Year, Walter Payton Man of the Year, Protector of the Year) and need their own candidate models, and the conference/division specials are sums of candidate probabilities grouped by the winner's team.

stages.name: Eligibility and candidate pool
stages.description: Eligibility defines the pool: rookies for the Rookie awards, offence or defence for the position-split awards, the month window for monthly awards, and any quarterback bias in the MVP. Pool size is small (3 to 8 live candidates for a typical award at the end of the season) and non-uniform: recent history shows that most MVPs are quarterbacks on top seeds, while non-quarterbacks win Offensive Player of the Year.
stages.distribution: Candidate set is a short list; probability mass concentrated on 2-4 names with a long tail of those who need a late surge.

stages.name: Realised production relative to peers
stages.description: Voters see counting statistics and milestones: passing and rushing yards, touchdowns, sacks, interceptions, receptions, with a lean to visible plays. Production per game and cumulative both count, so injuries trade rate for volume. Production must be compared with the pool of candidates at the same position and across positions for the cross-position awards. Defensive candidates (DPOY, DROY) are scored on a sack, pressure, interception, tackle-for-loss composite and offensive skill candidates on EPA, all ranked within the eligible pool by nfl.position_peer_production_index, with banked totals extended by nfl.rest_of_season_stat_projection.
stages.distribution: Production totals approximately normal across the season with heavy tails for TDs; ranking relative to peers is what matters, and seasonal rank changes slowly late in the year.

stages.name: Team success multiplier
stages.description: Team record, seed and division title are strong predictors of award votes, especially for the MVP and Coach of the Year: the same stat line earns a vote share depending on the team's seed. The standings simulation gives the distribution of final record and seed, which is a function of the remaining schedule and injuries across the roster.
stages.distribution: Seed distribution is discrete; vote share is a step-like function of seed (top-seed premium) rather than linear in wins.

stages.name: Availability and games-played risk
stages.description: Injury and rest before the ballot date eliminate or discount candidates; an injury after ballots close has no effect. Because games missed have a visible penalty in voting, the probability of playing the remaining games matters in a non-linear way: missing a few games costs far less than missing a month.
stages.distribution: Games-played distribution with a mass at full availability and a left tail; voters apply a penalty that jumps at roughly 3+ missed games (assumption, to be estimated).

stages.name: Narrative, exposure and milestone effects
stages.description: Voters respond to milestones (1,000 yards, 2,000 yards, sack or touchdown records), to national-television performances and to recent games. The distinction between realised and expected production (touchdown luck) matters because voters do not regress, so the luck inflated stat line wins votes even if its true value is lower; the model should predict what voters see.
stages.distribution: Narrative effects are discrete and path dependent: a milestone or record chase produces a jump in the vote probability rather than a gradual change.

stages.name: Vote aggregation: ranked-points ballots (50-voter panel seen in search copies for the 2025 awards only) and vote splitting
stages.description: The AP awards are decided by ranked-points ballots from a media panel, not by first-place plurality, and the ballot is modelled as parameters per award and season (voters V, places K, points vector w) with explicit evidence status, as listed in nfl.vote_outcome_model: the MVP ballot with five places scored 10-5-3-2-1 and V=50 for 2025, and a top 5 scored 10-5-3-2-1 for all eight AP awards in the 2025 season, are seen in search-result copies of AP wire text, with the AP primary pages not fetched. A 2022 start of the ranked MVP ballot, a top-3 5-3-1 scheme for the non-MVP awards (reported in search copies of an AP statement, unverified, change season unknown), pre-2022 single-vote seasons, the voter count outside 2025 and the tie rule are unverified. The winner is the candidate with the most points, so second- to fifth-place support can beat a first-place-vote lead (reported in search copies as the 2025 MVP tally: Stafford 366 points with 24 firsts beat Maye 361 with 23; the season attribution of one cited page date is unconfirmed). Win probability is the chance a candidate's simulated point total exceeds every rival's under a ranked-ballot model; teammates and same-position rivals split first places but can both collect lower-place points, so the split penalty acts mainly on the first-place share. The aggregation itself is nfl.vote_outcome_model: a rank-ordered ballot model simulating V ballots per draw with that award-season's points vector; nfl.leader_order_statistic only supplies each candidate's production rank among peers as a ballot feature (it is not a max-of-production winner rule), and the split penalty adjusts first-place placements.
stages.distribution: Each voter's ballot ranks K candidates (K=5 seen in search copies for the MVP and, in 2025, every other AP award; other seasons' K unverified); the point total is a weighted sum of placement counts with heavy concentration on two or three finalists; ties in points are rare but possible, and the tie rule was not found

stages.name: Award-specific drivers: coaches, comebacks and monthly windows
stages.description: Coach of the Year follows the surprise in team wins relative to a pre-season expectation, Comeback Player depends on the severity of the prior-year setback, and monthly awards are decided on four or five games with the bye week removing games from some teams. These contracts need their own sub-model on top of the common chain.
stages.distribution: Window sums over 3-5 games have much higher variance than season totals; coach surprise is approximately normal in wins but selects the top few overachievers.

stages.name: Slot selections: All-Pro teams, finalists, Hall of Fame class and Top 100 rank
stages.description: Several honours are capacity-limited selections rather than a single plurality winner. All-Pro and All-Rookie fill one or two places per position from media ballots, finalists are the top three to five vote-getters, the Hall of Fame class is chosen by a committee from about fifteen modern-era finalists under a class cap, and the Top 100 is a rank produced by players' votes on the previous season. Probability comes from where a candidate sits in the queue for a slot, not from beating one favourite.
stages.distribution: Selection indicators with strong year-to-year persistence for Hall of Fame finalists and Top 100 ranks; capacity limits induce negative dependence among same-position candidates.

stages.name: Non-production honours: executive, Man of the Year and offensive-line protector
stages.description: KXNFLEXECOTY is a PFWA writers' vote on a general manager or front-office head, driven by the team's win improvement over its pre-season expectation and by how visibly the executive's moves (trades, free agents, draft class, coaching hire) explain it. KXNFLWPMOTY is chosen by a selection panel from 32 team nominees on community and charitable work plus on-field standing, so nominee status, tenure and media visibility of the charitable programme matter, not statistics. KXNFLPROOTY rewards an offensive lineman's protection, so pass-block pressure and sack allowance, games started and team sack rate, plus reputation, decide it. Each is a small-panel vote with sparse history, so priors dominate.
stages.distribution: Categorical over a small candidate set (often a clear favourite plus 3-6 contenders); very few historical winners, so posterior probabilities are wide and heavily prior-driven.

stages.name: Conference and division specials: grouping winners by team
stages.description: KXNFLMVPSPECIALS, KXNFLOPOYSPECIALS and KXNFLDPOYSPECIALS do not name a player: they pay if the winner's team at announcement is in a given division or conference. Their value is the sum of each candidate's win probability over candidates on teams in that group, so they inherit every candidate model above, plus correlation within groups (two NFC West quarterbacks split the same voters) and the small chance a candidate changes team by trade before the award. Co-winners pay the group in full when both are in it and 1/N across distinct groups otherwise.
stages.distribution: Sum of correlated candidate probabilities; group probabilities are concentrated (one or two groups carry most mass for MVP) with a fractional-payout atom for split co-winners.

talent_strength.note: Player production (cross-position index including a defensive composite), QB efficiency and team strength; the WEAK nfl.award_stats input is detached from this archetype and not used.

opponent_matchup.note: A season award is decided from a whole-season body of work, not from a specific opponent; opponent strength enters only through remaining schedule and through who the candidate faced in highlighted games, already in the schedule input.

role_personnel.note: Rookie role and position determine the candidate pool; cross-position comparison uses the position-peer production index (the WEAK fantasy-points translation is detached).

availability_news.note: Games-played attrition and news before the ballot; ballot close timing is in award_voting_mechanics.

coaching_scheme.note: Coach of the Year relies on team over-performance; scheme is relevant to players only through production.

environment.note: Weather, venue and altitude affect single games, not an annual vote; their effect is absorbed in the production and record that voters see.

game_context_script.note: Accrual and remaining opportunity for milestone chases.

pace_volume.note: Remaining games and the number of games in the monthly window.

efficiency_conversion.note: Production versus expected; voters see raw totals but regression shows which leaders are fragile.

distribution_variance.note: Ranked-points ballot aggregation (nfl.vote_outcome_model) with a vote-split penalty for similar candidates; the leader statistic is only a production-rank feature of the ballot model, not a plurality or max-of-production winner rule.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Remaining schedule and primetime exposure; clinch-driven rest reduces counting stats late (not modelled).

officiating_rules.note: Officials do not influence a voting outcome; any penalty effect on production is already inside the stat line.

settlement_contract.note: Awarding body per series, 1/N for monthly co-winners and split specials, finalist no-announcement rule, Tie/Co-Winners outcome; annual-tie rule and ballot close remain unresolved.
