contract_review.settlement_definition: Twenty-seven live series, 21 with rules text (title-only: KXNFLOROY, KXNFLDROY, KXNFLOPOY, KXNFLDPOY, KXNFLCOACH, KXNFLHOFINDUCTEES). Single-winner awards resolve YES if the named candidate 'wins' the award from the named body: AP for KXNFLMVP ('AP Regular Season MVP'), OPOTY, DPOTY, OROTY, DROTY, COTY and CPOTY; Pro Football Writers of America for KXNFLEXECOTY; KXNFLWPMOTY (Walter Payton Man of the Year) and KXNFLPROOTY (Protector of the Year) name no body. COTY and EXECOTY list 'Tie/Co-Winners' as its own outcome. Monthly awards (KXNFLROTM, KXNFLPOTM) pay $1/N rounded down to the cent among N co-winners. Slot selections: KXNFLALLPRO (All-Pro First-Team, per side) and KXNFLALLROOK (PFWA All-Rookie, offence, defence and special teams) resolve on the selection 'as reported by one of the Source Agencies'; KXNFLAWARDFIN resolves on the named finalists and resolves No for every candidate if finalists are not announced before the winner; KXNFLHALLOFFAME resolves No once the 2027 class is announced without the candidate; KXNFLT100 (exact rank) and KXNFLT100TOP (top N) settle on the player-voted NFL Top 100 list. Specials (KXNFLMVPSPECIALS by division, KXNFLOPOYSPECIALS and KXNFLDPOYSPECIALS by conference) settle on the winner's team at the time of the announcement, 1/N across distinct groups for split co-winners. No series has an injury void; ballot close dates and the annual-award tie method are not stated.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: AP (single-winner player awards, coach), Pro Football Writers of America (Executive of the Year, All-Rookie), the Governing League for the player-voted Top 100 list; the monthly-award texts (KXNFLROTM, KXNFLPOTM) name no awarding body and unnamed 'Source Agencies' (All-Pro, finalists, Hall of Fame). Walter Payton Man of the Year and Protector of the Year texts name no body. Ballot close dates, re-announcement handling and annual-award tie methods are not stated.
variants_and_edge_cases: KXNFLOROY / KXNFLDROY / KXNFLOPOY / KXNFLDPOY / KXNFLCOACH (NFL-titled) are title-only, while their AP-titled twins (OROTY, DROTY, OPOTY, DPOTY, COTY) have rules naming the AP; whether the NFL-titled series settle on the same AP award is unverified.
Monthly awards (KXNFLROTM, KXNFLPOTM) cover roughly four or five games (the texts name only the month, see u5), so an injury or bye inside the window matters far more than for a season award.

KXNFLMVP rules text names the AP Regular Season MVP but not the ballot format, tie handling or ballot close date; a top-5 10-5-3-2-1 ballot is seen in search-result copies for 2023 and 2025 (primary page not fetched), the 2022 start year and the tie rule are unverified, and the ballot enters the model as parameters.

Coach of the Year and Comeback Player rules name the AP award only; both reward change relative to the prior season, a different driver from production, and COTY lists 'Tie/Co-Winners' as a separate outcome, so a named coach's treatment under a shared award is not stated.
Monthly window definition (calendar month versus week block) and MVP ballot format are not stated in sampled text and are carried as unresolved u5 and u7.

Multi-slot selections differ from single-winner awards: All-Pro and All-Rookie name one or two players per position, award finalists name three to five, a Hall of Fame class has a capped number of modern-era inductees, and the Top 100 contract is a rank cutoff, so a candidate competes for a slot rather than for first place.
KXNFLHALLOFFAME settles at the class announcement before the Super Bowl, months after the eligible career ended; season production plays no role, while finalist history and the class cap do.
Conference and division specials (OPOY/DPOY by conference, MVP by division) settle on the winner's team at announcement; co-winners in one group pay that group in full, split groups pay 1/N.
KXNFLAWARDFIN resolves every candidate No if finalists are not announced before the winner; KXNFLT100 settles on an exact rank (#3), a much narrower event than KXNFLT100TOP's top-N cutoff.

Non-production honours: KXNFLWPMOTY (community service, chosen from one nominee per team) and KXNFLEXECOTY (front-office executive) are decided on criteria unrelated to on-field statistics; KXNFLPROOTY (Protector of the Year) names no awarding body or criteria in its text.

Ballot format by award, modelled as parameters (voters V, places K, points vector w) with evidence status; sources are search-result copies of AP wire text only, no AP page was fetched (evidence_zblk/NFL_u7_ap_ballot.json): MVP 2025 V=50, K=5, w=10-5-3-2-1 (seen in search copies); MVP 2023 K=5, w=10-5-3-2-1 (seen in search copies); other seven AP awards 2025 K=5, w=10-5-3-2-1 (seen in search copies; Coach of the Year result reported as Vrabel 302/19 vs Coen 239/16); 2022 MVP top-5 with top-3 5-3-1 for the other awards: reported in search copies of an AP statement, unverified, and the season of the change to five places is unknown; pre-2022 single vote, voter count outside 2025 and tie rule: not found. PFWA (Executive of the Year), Hall of Fame selection, All-Pro, Walter Payton Man of the Year and the player-voted Top 100 use their own processes, not this ballot.

Blueprint-inherited context inputs (m.external_lines, m.quote_history, nfl.award_stats) are benchmark-only or weak and are not used by any stage of this record; they were detached from the archetype list by patch.

game_events.label: Game events and stats (overtime, safety, both teams score, TD counts, team stats)
game_events.target: Occurrence or count of game events: overtime, safety, defensive/special-teams TD, total TDs, period TDs, team stat thresholds.
game_events.mechanism: Event probability = base rate conditioned on drive and score process: overtime is the mass of tied-after-regulation outcomes (key-number mass at zero margin); safeties and defensive TDs depend on pass-rush/OL matchups and turnover hazards; TD counts follow team scoring expectations and red-zone style; team stat counts scale with plays and style. Many are rare events needing pooled priors and careful wording.

Counts such as total TDs, sacks and penalties scale with the number of plays.

Event definitions and OT inclusion.

Behaviour at the end of regulation moves the zero-margin atom, which sets both tie and OT markets.
Needed because the tie market equals OT probability times this hazard; the existing ot_model lacks an explicit definition.
Provides the opportunity count for the rare event rather than relying on team-level safety counts that are mostly zero.

interactions.hypothesis: Tight spread x low total: overtime probability is highest when the expected margin is near zero and scoring is kicker-driven with many 3-point increments.
Pass rush x OL x QB: sacks and safeties concentrate in games where an elite rush meets a weak OL and slow QB.
Turnover process x luck: defensive TD base rates depend on turnovers; regress fumble recoveries and use INT process data.
Officials x pace: crews with more flags lengthen games, shifting counts and TD totals slightly.

Regulation tie probability needs the pregame margin to be small and total low, because with fewer scoring drives the probability mass at exactly zero rises; the effect is concentrated at model expected margins under 3 and totals under the mean.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate P(regulation tie) by model mean-margin and model-total bucket against a smooth normal model and against the lattice.

interactions.hypothesis: When tied in the last two minutes a coach with ball may run the clock to force overtime, which makes a regulation tie probability above what a lattice model gives; this behaviour differs by coach and applies only in a narrow state.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare empirical regulation tie rates against lattice prediction by coach policy tercile.

interactions.hypothesis: Safety probability equals exposed plays times per-play sack/penalty rate; an offence that starts many drives deep faces a pass rush that wins often, so exposure and rush win rate multiply rather than add.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress safeties on exposure x opposing pressure rate product.

interactions.hypothesis: The game TD count is the sum of two team counts that share pace and shootout states: when both offences are efficient each extra possession for one side is also one for the other, so P(total >= 8) is well above the product of independent team tails; overtime adds a further TD chance only in tied games, which are more likely when both means are similar.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare empirical P(game TDs >= k) for k = 6, 7, 8 with an independent-Poisson sum built from the two model team TD means, binned by combined model mean; estimate the residual between-team correlation.

interactions.hypothesis: Wind above a threshold of roughly 15 mph or very cold temperatures cut overtime FG reliability and stall drives, raising the chance that overtime ends level; below the threshold the effect is negligible, so the response is a regime switch applied to P(level | OT), not a continuous effect on regulation ties.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare OT outcomes in weather regimes using playoffs and regular season OT games.

interactions.hypothesis: A defensive touchdown needs a takeaway and a return to the end zone; the takeaway count scales with the opponent QB's turnover-worthy play rate and with pressure, and the return conversion with field position and defender speed, so the D/ST TD probability rises with the product of pressure and giveaway propensity, not their sum.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit per team-game pick-six and fumble-return TD counts against opponent turnover-worthy play rate, pressure rate and their product on 2016-2025 pbp; compare deviance.

nonlinearities.shape: convex upper tail in the combined TD mean
nonlinearities.why: For a high rung such as 8+ total TDs, the probability rises convexly with the sum of the two team TD means (and faster still with positive between-team dependence), so a one-TD error in the combined mean moves deep rungs by a large relative amount.

nonlinearities.shape: low-rate Poisson: P = 1 - exp(-lambda)
nonlinearities.why: With rates of a few percent per game the probability is near linear in lambda, but team differences in lambda arise from exposure counts, not from observed rare outcomes.

nonlinearities.shape: product of two small probabilities
nonlinearities.why: Tie = P(OT) x P(level | OT): each factor is small and uncertain; relative errors multiply, so the tie market is the most sensitive to rule changes. Note the P(level | OT) factor is a rule-era input; the OT margin lattice is wider than 0, 3, 6 when both teams possess (a TD plus extra point can leave a 1 or 2 point margin).

mechanism_review.summary: These markets are rare or count events built from the same drive process, each with its own generator. A tie requires the game to be level after regulation and then level after overtime: P(tie) = P(regulation tie) x P(overtime ends level). Regulation ties come from the margin lattice (mass at zero, boosted by the 3/7 increments and end-of-game management), while the overtime ending depends on the OT rule set, each team's scoring rate and 4th-down policy in a 10-minute period. A safety is a count of rare special events: an offence is tackled or commits a foul in its own end zone, a punt or kick leaves the end zone, a snap or fumble goes out of bounds; the rate scales with plays run near its own goal line, pass rush versus protection, and punting from deep. A game touchdown count is the sum of the two teams' TD counts, each drives times TD-per-drive plus a small defensive and return TD rate, positively dependent through pace and shootout states, with overtime TDs included. Overtime occurrence is the regulation-tie atom itself. A defensive or special-teams touchdown is a rare hazard driven by takeaways, return opportunities and returner/coverage quality, and a single team's TD count ladder is that team's drives times TD-per-drive plus its own non-offensive TD rate.

stages.name: Regulation tie mass at zero margin
stages.description: P(tied after four quarters) depends on the final-margin distribution evaluated at zero, which has more mass than a smooth normal density implies because scores come in 3s and 7s and late-game kneeling or FG-for-tie decisions sit at zero. Tight spreads and low totals concentrate probability at small margins; coaches who are tied late may play for overtime. The margin atom comes from the model-centred lattice (nfl.model_margin_lattice) built on the market-free team means, never from line residuals. KXNFLOT is priced directly off this atom (P(level after regulation)), so g1 alone settles the overtime market.
stages.distribution: Discrete mass on the integer margin lattice; P(zero) a few percent of games with sensitivity to totals and lines

stages.name: Overtime resolution and the level-after-overtime event
stages.description: Since the 2025 season the regular-season overtime follows the playoff possession rule: each team gets a possession (an opening-drive touchdown no longer ends the game), then sudden death, inside a single 10-minute period after which the game is a tie. The team receiving first can still win without the other team touching the ball if its opening drive uses the whole 10 minutes and scores, and a second team trailing late in the period may run out of clock. A touchdown that wins the game outright ends it with no try (Super Bowl LVIII ended 25-22 on a walk-off touchdown), so the final OT margin is set as follows: after nothing or a FG by the first team, a second-team TD wins by 6 or 3 and a second-team FG wins by 3 or ties; after a first-team TD plus try (6, 7 or 8), a second-team FG loses by 3, 4 or 5, and a second-team TD that only ties or trails is followed by a try, leaving margins of 1 or 2 or a tie that continues into sudden death; unanswered first-team TDs end 6-8; sudden-death scores end 3 (FG), 6 (TD, no try) or 2 (safety). The game ends level only when the period expires with equal scores. P(level | OT) therefore depends on clock use and two-point decisions of both coaches, team TD/FG rates per drive, kickers and weather, and differs materially from the 2017-2024 first-TD-wins regime.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli given overtime with rule-era dependence; final OT margin on the lattice {1,...,8} with mass concentrated at 3 and 6-8; level outcome a few percent of OT games

stages.name: Safety hazard from end-zone exposure
stages.description: Safeties occur when the offence runs plays inside its own 5-yard line (sacks, intentional grounding, holding, tackles for loss on runs, fumbles through the end zone) or on special teams (blocked or errant punts and kicks). The rate is the number of exposed plays times a per-play safety probability that depends on pass rush win rate, offensive line, QB sack avoidance and defensive front. Rate per game is low (a few percent) so team-level estimation is noisy and requires pooling.
stages.distribution: Rare-event Poisson with rate from end-zone exposure; zero-inflated at the team level

stages.name: Game and team touchdown counts from the TD pools
stages.description: KXNFLTOTALTD/KXNFLGAMETD count every touchdown by either team (offensive, defensive, return; overtime explicitly for TOTALTD) and KXNFLTEAMTD counts one team's touchdowns. Each team's count is expected drives times TD-per-drive (red-zone conversion and 4th-and-goal policy decide TD versus FG) plus a low-rate non-offensive TD hazard. The two teams' counts are positively dependent: a fast, efficient game gives both offences more possessions and a trailing team keeps throwing. Game rungs such as 8+/9+ and team rungs such as 4+ sit in the right tail, so overdispersion and between-team dependence matter more than the means.
stages.distribution: Team count: overdispersed integer with mean about 2-3 TDs; game count: sum of two positively correlated counts, right-skewed; 8+/9+ game and 4+ team rungs are upper-tail events

stages.name: Defensive and special-teams touchdown hazard
stages.description: KXNFLDSTTD pays if either team scores a defensive or special-teams touchdown (interception or fumble return, punt or kick return, blocked kick return), overtime included. The game rate is roughly one such TD every five to six games. It is the sum of two team hazards, each the opponent's giveaway rate times return-TD conversion plus kick/punt return opportunities times returner threat and opposing coverage quality. Turnover-prone QBs, high pressure rates, wet weather and a trailing opponent forced to throw raise it; the kickoff rule regime (touchback rate) controls return volume.
stages.distribution: Rare-event Poisson per team-game with a small rate; game-level P(>=1) roughly 0.15-0.2, heavily driven by realized turnovers, which are mostly noise

stages.name: Participation, void and rule application
stages.description: All live series here are team or game events, so there is no named-player void; the rule that matters is the 48-hour postponement clause (fair-price settlement) and which window counts: safeties, D/ST TDs and KXNFLTOTALTD include overtime, the tie market is the post-overtime result, the overtime market is the regulation result, and GAMETD/TEAMTD are silent on overtime. The source is the official scoring summary; a stat correction can relabel a TD's type (offence vs return), which matters for KXNFLDSTTD.
stages.distribution: Deterministic rule application with a small probability of correction; participation is a discrete mixture

contract_review.settlement_definition: Seven live series, all with rules text. KXNFLTIE resolves YES if neither team wins and the game ends in a tie (NO if either team wins). KXNFLOT resolves YES if the game 'goes to overtime', i.e. is level after regulation. KXNFLSFTY resolves YES if either team records a safety, overtime safeties counting. KXNFLDSTTD resolves YES if either team records at least one defensive or special-teams touchdown, overtime counting. KXNFLTOTALTD and KXNFLGAMETD resolve YES if both teams together record at least N touchdowns (8+, 9+; floor 7.5/8.5), TOTALTD stating overtime TDs count while GAMETD's sampled text is silent on overtime. KXNFLTEAMTD resolves YES if one named team records N+ touchdowns (e.g. 'Green Bay: 4+', floor 3.5); its text does not mention overtime or TD type. Games postponed but started within 48 hours stay open, otherwise fair price (stated in every sampled text except KXNFLGAMETD, which has no postponement clause). Source: official final result / scoring summary.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official NFL scoring summaries (touchdowns by type, safeties, overtime, final result); Kalshi refers to the 'official final result'.
variants_and_edge_cases: Window differences: KXNFLOT is the regulation-tie event; KXNFLTIE additionally needs overtime to end level (nested, far smaller); safeties, D/ST TDs and KXNFLTOTALTD explicitly include overtime; KXNFLGAMETD and KXNFLTEAMTD texts do not mention overtime.

KXNFLTOTALTD and KXNFLGAMETD are both combined-TD ladders (8+ and 9+ sampled); only TOTALTD states that overtime TDs count, so they are not interchangeable until GAMETD OT treatment is confirmed; KXNFLTEAMTD is a single-team ladder (4+ sampled). Strikes are integer N+ via half-point floors, so no push.
KXNFLDSTTD counts either team's defensive or special-teams TD; whether a fake-punt/fake-FG TD counts as special teams is not stated here (the player TD series say such TDs are offensive).
Team-level events only: no named-player void; the 48-hour postponement clause is the only void path.
The weekly-tie series (KXNFLWEEKTIE) and the longest-rush series are no longer filed here and are not claimed.

Overtime rule era (verified from 2025 league-meeting reports): regular-season OT gives both teams a possession since 2025, stays 10 minutes, and can still end in a tie; the first team can win on a drive that consumes the full period. Seasons 2017-2024 used the 10-minute first-possession-TD-wins format, so P(level | OT) must be fitted by rule era.

interactions.hypothesis: Opening possession x scripted first drive: the benefit of getting the ball first is amplified for teams with high scripted opening-drive TD rates.
Pace x time bucket: first-TD time distribution shifts earlier for faster tempo teams and later for run-heavy slow teams.
Kicker x weather x red zone: in bad weather, first score is more likely a FG, delaying first TD and reducing race-to-7 probability.

P(team scores the game's first TD) is the receiver's first-drive TD probability plus the survival product of both teams failing on earlier drives; receiving first and a high scripted TD rate add on drive one but their effect then compounds only through the survival product over later drives, so the gain from receiving first shrinks as the per-drive TD rate falls.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute first-TD rate for receivers versus deferrers within bins of team early-drive TD rate and compare with the survival-product prediction from per-drive rates.

interactions.hypothesis: Time to first TD is a convolution of right-skewed drive durations over a random number of drives (a duration-and-hazard composition rather than an interaction of input levels); a fast offence with a high per-drive TD rate moves the median earlier and fattens the early bucket more than proportionally, while a clock-killing team shifts mass past the first quarter.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit the renewal convolution from per-drive TD rates and duration distributions and compare predicted with observed bucket frequencies by team pace tercile.

interactions.hypothesis: In race-to-N points, the TD/FG split of early scoring drives decides whether N=7 is reached by one TD or two FGs plus; the probability is piecewise in the sequence rather than smooth in expected points.
interactions.how_to_test: Enumerate sequences to N and compare model and empirical race outcomes by team TD fraction.

interactions.hypothesis: Above a wind threshold FG range shrinks and passing efficiency falls so first score becomes a TD or nothing for strong run teams and slower overall; regimes switch around 15-20 mph.
interactions.how_to_test: Group early-drive outcomes by wind regime and kicker range.

interactions.hypothesis: A first-drive turnover gives the opponent a short field and raises its first-score probability above any offence-based rate; the conditional hazard after a turnover is much higher than the unconditional.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare opponent's first-drive TD rate after a first-drive turnover vs after a punt.

nonlinearities.shape: right-skewed (lognormal) duration
nonlinearities.why: Drive durations have a long right tail from sustained marches, so time to first TD has fat tail and bucket probabilities are not symmetric around the mean.

nonlinearities.shape: logistic mapping from efficiency to P(TD per drive)
nonlinearities.why: TD per drive increases with EPA in an S-shape; extremes (very high or low EPA) saturate, so a linear EPA coefficient overstates the first-drive edge for elite offences.

nonlinearities.shape: compounding with scoring rate
nonlinearities.why: The value of the first possession rises convexly with per-drive TD probability, because the benefit equals the chance the opponent has no chance to respond; small in low-scoring games, larger in high-scoring ones.

mechanism_review.summary: The first score is a first-passage problem on a drive-level race. Teams alternate possessions after the kickoff; each possession ends in one of a few outcomes (touchdown, field goal, punt, turnover, turnover on downs, safety, end of half) with probabilities that depend on the team's offence, the opposing defence, starting field position and, for the first one or two drives, the coach's scripted plays. The first team to produce a TD (or reach N points) wins; the clock time of that event is the sum of the durations of the drives before it, so the time distribution depends on drive durations, which are right-skewed, and on how many drives pass before the first score. Non-offensive scores (pick-six, return TD, safety) arrive on a different, rarer hazard. Race-to-N markets add a lattice problem: points come in packages of 3, 6, 7, 8 and 2 and the first team to cross N depends on the order of TDs and FGs, not just the number of scoring drives. Because the first possession goes to one team, small advantages in first-drive TD probability compound into a first-score edge.

stages.name: Possession order and early-drive scheduling
stages.description: After the opening kickoff the receiving team has the first possession; the toss winner's choice (receive/defer) and kickoff rules decide this. Possessions then alternate subject to scores and turnovers. The probability that a team has the ball for the first, third and fifth drives determines how many early chances it has before the opponent can respond; the order gives a modest but systematic edge to the receiving team that compounds when drive-level TD probabilities are high.
stages.distribution: Binary draw (receive/defer) then alternating renewal process; cumulative drive counts by game clock differ by up to one drive between teams

stages.name: Per-drive outcome with scripted early drives
stages.description: Each drive's outcome is multinomial. Early drives differ from average because the coach scripts the first 10-15 plays; the first drive's TD rate and the shape of the call mix are not predictable from season EPA alone. Opposing defence quality, red-zone TD conversion and kicker range decide TD versus FG. Starting field position after the kickoff (touchbacks, returns) also shifts this probability.
stages.distribution: Multinomial per drive: TD, FG, no score, turnover, safety; a first-drive TD rate near one in five to one in four for typical teams with heavy variation across offences

stages.name: Drive duration and the time-of-first-TD clock
stages.description: The time of the first TD equals the sum of elapsed time over earlier non-scoring drives plus the scoring drive's own duration. A TD drive consumes about 4 to 6 minutes on average with wide dispersion; short fields and explosive plays end quickly. Pace, run rate and fourth-down policy determine the duration of failed drives. Time buckets (for example, 0-10 minutes, 10-20) therefore have mass shaped by a convolution of right-skewed durations, with discrete jumps at quarter ends. KXNFLFIRSTTDTIME also lists an overtime bucket, so the no-TD-in-regulation mass (roughly 1% of games or fewer; frequency not verified here) must be split by the overtime model into an OT-first-TD bucket and the no-TD case.
stages.distribution: Sum of right-skewed (lognormal-like) durations over a geometric number of drives; heavy right tail in time to first TD

stages.name: Non-offensive scores and turnovers
stages.description: Defensive and special-teams touchdowns, safeties and short fields after turnovers produce scores without an offensive drive completing. They have a low rate per game (roughly 15-20% of games contain a defensive or special-teams TD, a recollection-level estimate consistent with game_events g5, not verified here) but they pre-empt the offensive race and add mass to very early times; a turnover on the first drive creates a short field for the opponent. The mass of 'no TD in regulation' is split by nfl.ot_model: under the sampled KXNFLFIRSTTDTEAM text a first TD scored only in overtime still resolves the team strike Yes, and 'No team scores a TD' needs a TD-less overtime too, with the overtime possession rules of the season in force.
stages.distribution: Rare-event Poisson with low rate; turns first-score mass towards the early minutes and toward the defence

stages.name: Race-to-N points lattice
stages.description: KXNFLRACE pays the first team to score N points in the full game including overtime, or 'Neither team'. The winner depends on the sequence of scoring packages: TD (6-8 points), FG (3), safety (2), so P(team A first to N) is a path probability on a lattice driven by the TD/FG split, extra-point success and two-point tendency. At the sampled rung N=35 the dominant term is whether either team reaches 35 at all (the right tail of each team's points, roughly a 10-20% event for one team), so the race needs each team's full points distribution plus the order of crossing when both get there; low rungs are order-dominated. Package probabilities come from the model drive-outcome input, not from market lines.
stages.distribution: Compound renewal-reward process on a 2/3/6/7/8 lattice; for high N a first-passage probability dominated by the team-points tail, with a large Neither atom

stages.name: Contextual modifiers, availability and settlement
stages.description: Weather affects early FG versus TD decisions; QB or skill-player availability changes first-drive scripts; the rule text decides what counts as a score and the no-score case. Because the markets are early-game, only pregame information is relevant and lineup uncertainty at kickoff is a key mixture. nfl.qb is used for starter status only; its catalog QB point value estimated from market line moves is not used.
stages.distribution: Context shifts to drive probabilities; settlement is deterministic from the scoring summary

contract_review.settlement_definition: Three live series, all with rules text. KXNFLFIRSTTDTEAM resolves YES for the team that scores the game's first touchdown of any kind ('All touchdowns count ... including offensive, defensive, and special teams'); a first TD in overtime still counts, and 'No team scores a TD' resolves YES if no TD is scored in the full game including overtime. KXNFLFIRSTTDTIME is a time-bucket contract on when the first TD occurs; the sampled strike is 'record the first touchdown in the overtime period', so overtime is a bucket; the regulation bucket boundaries and the clock convention are not in the sampled text. KXNFLRACE resolves YES for the team that is first to score N points (sampled N=35) in the full game including overtime, with a 'Neither team' strike if neither reaches N. Postponed games starting within 48 hours stay open; otherwise fair price (FIRSTTDTEAM, RACE). Source: official final result/scoring summary.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official play-by-play scoring summary with game clock (official final result) for all three series; the time-bucket clock convention is not stated.
variants_and_edge_cases: First touchdown versus first score: a field goal is not a touchdown, so the first-TD hazard continues after FGs, whereas race-to-N advances on every score.

Race-to-N (KXNFLRACE) counts overtime and pays 'Neither team' when no team reaches N; at high rungs such as 35 the race outcome is dominated by P(either team reaches 35), i.e. by the team-points tail, and only secondarily by order. Low rungs (if listed) are order-dominated.
KXNFLFIRSTTDTIME has an overtime bucket; whether regulation buckets use game clock (e.g. by quarter or minutes elapsed) and how 'no TD at all' is settled are not in the sampled text.
A first touchdown in overtime still settles to that team in KXNFLFIRSTTDTEAM; the no-TD mass is its own strike.
Kickoff-return and defensive touchdowns can end the first-TD race before any offensive drive completes and count under 'All touchdowns count'.

season_player_stats_and_leaders.label: Season player stats, leaders, weekly leaders and fantasy
season_player_stats_and_leaders.target: Probability a player or team reaches a season (or weekly) statistical threshold, leads the league, or outranks another in a stat.
season_player_stats_and_leaders.mechanism: Season stat = sum of per-game outputs over games played; project per-game rate from role, team volume and efficiency with regression, multiply by games-played distribution, add realized to date, and simulate. Leader markets are order statistics over correlated contenders, weekly leaders have much higher randomness. Rule wording determines eligible games (regular season only) and stat source.

inputs.why: Realized totals plus projected remainder is the structure of any in-season probability.
Missed games are the principal tail risk for season-long counting stats and leaders.
Leader contracts resolve as a maximum over many correlated players, needing simulation of the whole field.
Target volume projects receiving yards, receptions and receiving TDs.
Carry share and goal-line usage project rushing yards and TDs.
QB efficiency prior converts projected attempts into yards and TDs.
Fantasy contracts are linear combinations of components whose covariances matter for rank outcomes.
TD totals regress strongly; used to adjust projection of both realized and expected TDs.
Remaining defenses by position adjust the projected per-game rate.
Teammate changes and injuries during the season shift usage and leader probability.
Per-game variance aggregates across games and sets the spread of season totals.
Team volume tendencies project season-long attempts and thus counting stats.
Contract defines eligible games (regular season only), the stat source and tiebreak rules for leaders.
Adds the largest unmodelled variance source for season totals: a 25 percent share change on 8 remaining games moves a season total by far more than game-level noise.
Provides the correct dispersion for threshold and leader probabilities and is why season-stat rungs are wider than normal-approximation estimates.
Cuts the expected games and snaps of the leading contenders in the exact weeks when many leader contracts are decided, which season-to-date pace ignores.
Needed so leader probabilities sum correctly across the field and so a teammate's injury changes the leader odds of another candidate.
Weekly leader contracts are a different statistical object from season leaders and cannot be priced from the season-to-date pace input.
Prices KXNFLCAREERPASSYDS, KXNFLCAREERRECYDS, KXNFLCAREERRSHYDS and KXNFLCAREERRSHTDS, whose strikes are all-time records plus one and whose horizon is the rest of a career.
Needed for the rookie sack record and the interceptions leader series, which are defensive season accruals.

Gives KXNFLTSPEC team-statistic lines (net passing yards per the rules text) a season-total forecast and adds late-season rest to the team-points extremes of KXNFLTEAMPTS/KXNFLTEAMDPTS without duplicating the existing team points model.

interactions.hypothesis: Games-played attrition x per-game rate: high-rate injury-prone players have lower leader probability than rate-only models suggest.
TD regression x accrued total: regress TD rate on remaining games.
Remaining schedule x role: soft remaining defenses lift receivers only when target share is stable.

The season total is the product of a discrete games-played count and a persistent per-game rate, so a high-rate player with a high attrition hazard has a bimodal distribution; moments of the total from independent components understate the left tail and overstate the median.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate the total from games and rate jointly versus from independent normal approximations and compare calibration at the 10th and 90th percentiles.

interactions.hypothesis: Targets and carries move together after an event: when a teammate is lost, one player's share rises and another's falls, and a coordinator change shifts the pass-run balance for everyone, so the rate is a mixture whose weights are updated by news.
interactions.how_to_test: Detect regime shifts around events and compare usage share before and after, by position.

interactions.hypothesis: The expected snaps of starters fall at the point a team clinches a seed (usually Week 16-18) and the effect is concentrated in the last two weeks; before that point pace extrapolation is valid and after it drops.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare Weeks 17-18 snap shares of starters on clinched versus unclinched teams.

interactions.hypothesis: Leader probability for a player depends on the variance of his lead over each rival: positive covariance between two contenders on one offence (quarterback and a receiver sharing team passing volume) shrinks the variance of their gap so the better one is more reliably ahead, while negative covariance within a backfield (competing for the same carries) widens the gap variance and makes order flips more likely. The sign is positive for same-team passing pairs and negative for same-position teammates.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit leader probabilities from a covariance-matrix simulation versus an independent simulation, and compare Brier score and calibration on historical position leaders, separately for same-team positive-sign and same-position negative-sign pairs.

interactions.hypothesis: Banked touchdown excess fades toward the role-based rate only to the extent it came from luck (long scores, fumble-recovery touchdowns); excess that rests on a stable red-zone share persists, and a role-regime change redefines the role-based rate itself, so the shrinkage of banked touchdowns toward expectation depends on how stable the underlying role is.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress remaining touchdowns on banked touchdowns, role-based expectation and an indicator of red-zone share stability or a regime-change event; test the banked x stability term and the null that banked excess has no effect.

interactions.hypothesis: The weekly leader's probability depends on the tail of a player's single-game distribution rather than on its mean, so two players with equal means can differ several-fold in leader probability; this effect is a function of the tail index.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare weekly-leader frequency among players by tail-heaviness (95th percentile over mean) controlling for mean.

interactions.hypothesis: For a career record chase a lost season matters only if it pushes the expected crossing past the likely retirement age; a player 400 yards short is barely affected by missing three games, while one needing two more full seasons at 35 loses most of his chance from a single long injury.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate attainment with and without a one-season absence across gap and age bins and compare with historical record chases (players within two seasons of a career record since 1990).

interactions.hypothesis: A team leading the league in points scored that clinches early rests starters in Weeks 17-18, cutting its last two games' scoring by several points each, so the most-points market leader is penalised precisely when its season is strong; for fewest-points-allowed the same rest weakens the defence and raises points allowed, so clinching moves both team-extreme markets against the clinched team.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare Weeks 17-18 points for and against of clinched versus unclinched top-seed teams in 2012-2025 relative to their season-to-date rates.

nonlinearities.shape: bounded and left-skewed: total increases linearly with games but the probability of a rung drops steeply when the required games approach the games remaining
nonlinearities.why: A threshold requiring almost every remaining game at an above-average rate becomes very sensitive to a single missed game, so the rung probability is nonlinear near the feasible limit.

nonlinearities.shape: sigmoid in the standardized gap (lead divided by remaining-sum standard deviation), saturating near 0 and 1
nonlinearities.why: A lead of one standard deviation yields only about 84 percent, while a two-sd lead yields 98 percent, so leader odds change quickly in the middle range and slowly in the tails.

nonlinearities.shape: shrinkage toward the role-based mean: realised touchdown excess decays with remaining games
nonlinearities.why: Banked touchdown luck does not carry into remaining games, so the extrapolated total regresses by a factor that depends on how many games remain.

nonlinearities.shape: heavy right tail: extreme-value shape parameter above zero for yards and fantasy points
nonlinearities.why: The weekly leader has a distribution with a long tail, so very high weekly leader values are more likely than normal-extreme extrapolation implies.

mechanism_review.summary: A season statistic is the sum over games played of a per-game output, and the contract is decided by three quantities that are separate in kind: how many games the player appears in (a discrete attrition process), what per-game rate he runs at once on the field (a role and efficiency process that is autocorrelated within the season and can switch regimes after an injury, trade or coaching change), and the realised total already banked. For threshold contracts the probability is the chance that banked plus remaining output crosses the rung, which depends on remaining games and the variance of the sum, larger than independent-game variance because of the persistent role state. For leader contracts the question is a maximum over many correlated contenders, where covariance among teammates and shared schedules matters and the open field of unlisted players holds real mass. Late-season rest of clinched teams and weather add a seasonal truncation to the final weeks. Team-level series (most/least points scored and allowed, team specials) follow the same banked-plus-remaining logic at team grain, with the extreme taken over the league's teams.

stages.name: Banked total and games remaining
stages.description: Season-to-date output is known, so the forecast begins from the realised accrual and counts the games each team still plays, with byes and the Week 18 finale deciding how many chances remain. The remaining chances are discrete and unevenly spread across contenders: one player with four games left behind another with five changes the leader odds by a visible margin.
stages.distribution: Deterministic given the schedule; remaining games are 0 to 17, and early in the season most of the variance is in the not-yet-played games.

stages.name: Availability: games played and attrition
stages.description: Each remaining game has an appearance probability set by injury status, age and position, suspension risk and (late) rest by clinched teams. Attrition is a hazard process with absences clustering across weeks (a hamstring injury costs several games), so the games-played count has a heavy left tail and strong dependence on the current report.
stages.distribution: Discrete count; near-binomial but with clustered absences, so variance exceeds binomial; mass at 0 additional games for players on injured reserve.

stages.name: Role and usage regime across the remaining season
stages.description: The per-game rate depends on a role state (target share, carry share, snap share) which persists but can change when a teammate is hurt, a depth chart is reshuffled, an offensive coordinator is replaced or a player is traded. Regimes are detected late and priced late, so the regime-change hazard widens the distribution beyond what current usage implies.
stages.distribution: Mixture of regimes: stable role with persistent shares plus a small probability of a shift of 20-40 percent in share (assumption), producing season-level variance beyond sum of independent games.

stages.name: Team volume and efficiency conversion
stages.description: Passing and rushing opportunity come from the team's plays and pass rate, and yield from the quarterback and line; touchdown totals regress heavily and so the per-game expected touchdown rate must be separated from the realised one. A quarterback change can reset volume and efficiency for every skill player on the team.
stages.distribution: Per-game output is a compound count with overdispersion; touchdown counts are low-count Poisson-like with strong regression to role-based expectation.

stages.name: Distribution of the remaining sum with persistent state
stages.description: Remaining output is the sum of games with a within-season autocorrelation: good weeks cluster with a stable role and bad weeks with changed role, so the standard deviation of the sum is larger than sqrt(n) times single-game standard deviation. The distribution over games played and rate is a compound mixture rather than a normal.
stages.distribution: Compound with positive intra-season correlation (roughly 0.1-0.3 at the game-rate level, assumption); right-skewed for touchdowns and receptions.

stages.name: Leader order statistic and contender covariance
stages.description: For a leader contract the event is that one player's total exceeds every rival's: the probability depends on the gap, the remaining games and the dispersion of each contender, and on covariance (teammates share volume negatively for rushing, positively for team-level volume), and is not a product of marginals. The field of less-visible contenders carries mass for position-wide leaders.
stages.distribution: Maximum of N correlated heavy-tailed totals; the probability of leading is a steep function of gap divided by remaining-sum standard deviation.

stages.name: Weekly leaders and settlement rules
stages.description: Weekly leader contracts are single-game maxima over the full player pool, so the tail of the per-game distribution and the ties convention (1/N) matter and are completely different from cumulative leader contracts; regular-season-only wording and statistic source decide eligibility.
stages.distribution: Single-game maximum of ~hundreds of players; heavy right tail; dead-heat splitting of ties.

stages.name: Career record chases and defensive season accruals
stages.description: The career series are set one unit above the all-time records, so they ask whether a player in his late twenties or thirties keeps playing long enough at a high enough rate: the gap, an age decline curve and a retirement or release hazard decide them, and a retirement announcement ends the contract. The rookie and all-player season sack records (14.5 and 22.5, both must be broken) and the interceptions leader are defensive accruals: pass-rush snaps, pressure rate and a heavily regressed conversion to sacks, or coverage targets and an interception rate.
stages.distribution: Career attainment is a survival-weighted mixture over 0-6 more seasons with a heavy left tail from retirement; individual sack and interception season totals are overdispersed Poisson counts with strong regression of conversion rates.

stages.name: Team season totals and league-wide team extremes
stages.description: KXNFLTEAMPTS and KXNFLTEAMDPTS ask which team scores or allows the most or fewest points over the regular season, and KXNFLTSPEC includes team statistics such as net passing yards. Each team's final total is banked points plus the sum over remaining games of its points for or against, which depends on its offence and defence ratings separately, the remaining opponents, pace and the clinched-team rest of starters in Weeks 17-18. The extreme is an order statistic over the league's teams with shared rating uncertainty, and dead heats pay 1/N. Net team passing yards subtract sack yardage, so pass protection enters the team total but not the player passing totals.
stages.distribution: Sum of remaining-game team scores (approximately normal with sd about 35-45 points over 8 games) plus banked total; the extreme over teams is a max/min order statistic with mass concentrated on two or three teams by mid-season.

contract_review.settlement_definition: Twenty-two live series, 19 with rules text (title-only: KXNFLLEADERPINT, KXNFLCAREERRSHTDS, KXNFLSEASONRUSHYDS). Season rungs (KXNFLSEASONPASSYDS, SEASONPASSTDS, SEASONRSHYDS, SEASONRSHTD, SEASONRECYDS, SEASONREC, SEASONRECTD) resolve YES if the player 'records N+' of the statistic 'during the 2026-27 Pro Football regular season'; missed games have no refund. KXNFLTSPEC (team specials) uses regular-season stats only, counts a traded player's combined totals across teams, and defines team passing yards as net of sack yardage. Career rungs (KXNFLCAREERPASSYDS 89,215+, CAREERRECYDS 22,896+, CAREERRSHYDS 18,356+) count career regular-season totals reached before the player or a Source Agency announces his retirement. Record series resolve YES only if the record is broken, not tied: KXNFLSZNRECORD (rookie sacks, 14.5), KXNFLSACKRECORD (season sacks, more than 22.5) and KXNFLRECYDSRECORD (season receiving yards, more than 1,964); the sampled record markets are for the 2025-26 season. Weekly-most series (KXNFLWEEKMOSTPASSYDS/RECYDS/RSHYDS) are maxima over all players in the week: No for a non-participant, 1/N on ties. Team extremes (KXNFLTEAMPTS most/least points scored, KXNFLTEAMDPTS fewest/most points allowed) are over all teams for the whole regular season with dead-heat 1/N on ties. No text states overtime treatment or the statistics source.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: The sampled texts name the 'Source Agencies' for retirement announcements and the 'Governing League' implicitly for statistics; no provider or correction rule is named. Capture the Kalshi expiration value and compare with official season totals.
variants_and_edge_cases: Season rungs are one-sided and unrefunded: a player who misses the season fails the rung, unlike per-game ladders with a void rule, so games-played risk is a loss and not a refund.
Weekly-most series resolve over every player in the week and give No to a non-participant with 1/N on ties; the contender set is an open field, not a list of names.

Career rungs end at a retirement announcement and the sampled strikes equal the all-time record plus one (Brady 89,214 passing, Rice 22,895 receiving, Emmitt Smith 18,355 rushing), so the horizon is several seasons and the contract expiry date, not visible in the sample, may end it earlier (u1).

KXNFLSZNRECORD (rookie sacks, 'broken, not tied', 14.5) and KXNFLSACKRECORD (season sacks, more than 22.5) are defensive accruals and KXNFLLEADERPINT (title-only) is presumably an interceptions leader; they need individual defender inputs, unlike the offence-yardage series.
The 2026-27 schedule has 18 weeks with 17 games per team, so remaining games differ by team through byes, and Week 17-18 rest of clinched starters truncates the final total.
KXNFLSEASONRSHYDS (rules sampled) and KXNFLSEASONRUSHYDS (title-only) share the title 'Rushing Yards' and may be one series spelled twice (u7).

Team extremes (KXNFLTEAMPTS, KXNFLTEAMDPTS) pay 1/N dead heats over tied teams and cover the entire regular season; KXNFLTSPEC's team stat definitions are truncated in the sample after 'Team Passing Yards: Recorded as net yards', so other team stat definitions are unseen (u8).
KXNFLTSPEC player markets count combined statistics across teams after a trade, while the record and weekly series do not mention trades.

off_field_events.label: Draft, coach, transaction and Super Bowl novelty events
off_field_events.target: Occurrence or outcome of off-field events per official announcement or defined source.
off_field_events.mechanism: Off-field events resolve by organizational decisions and official announcements: supplemental-draft and draft-capital context follows team need and declared prospects; coach changes follow performance vs expectation, ownership signals and contract timing; transactions follow cap and contract calendars and insider reports; novelty events follow historical base rates and pre-announced details. The main edge is information timing and resolution wording rather than football modeling.

inputs.why: Timestamped reports and their credibility are the main information source for transaction and coach events.
Cap space, guarantee dates and contract deadlines constrain transaction timing and make some events near-forced.
Firing hazard follows record versus expectation, ownership statements and contract status.
Base rates and pre-announced details for novelty events replace football modeling.
Close and expiry times determine which news can still affect the resolution.
Resolution source and wording (official announcement vs report) define settlement.
Coach firings, trades and announcements are priced from historical frequency by calendar window.
The key quantity for any 'before date' contract; the existing base-rate input does not define the calendar structure.
Directly estimates how much a report should move probability and when; the existing input is only a generic news feed.
Specific mechanism for roster contracts that no existing input defines.
Defines the hazard model beyond a qualitative hot-seat signal.
KXNFLTRADE settles on an officially processed trade before a date.

interactions.hypothesis: Performance x contract: firing hazard depends on record vs expectation and contract/ownership cost.

A report from a top-tier insider with 'agreed to terms' wording converts to an official signing with high probability within days, while a speculative report by a lesser source barely moves the hazard; the update depends on reporter tier, wording and time before market close.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare event frequencies after reports binned by reporter tier and wording class.

interactions.hypothesis: A losing team with an owner who has a history of quick firings and a coach with an expiring contract has a firing hazard that multiplies these factors, especially after the season ends; no single factor is sufficient in isolation.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit the discrete-time hazard with interactions of win% shortfall, contract years and owner history.

interactions.hypothesis: A player with large contracted money is nearly sure to make the 53 unless on IR; a fringe player with no guarantee has probability set by roster slots at his position; the IR designation at cut-down switches the outcome to NO regardless of talent.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate inclusion by guarantee tercile with and without injury exclusion flag.

interactions.hypothesis: The coach-out hazard is near zero between weeks, climbs slowly in the season after bad losses and jumps after the final game; a date-based contract's probability depends mainly on whether the horizon spans the post-season window.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare empirical hazard by calendar week against a constant-hazard model.

interactions.hypothesis: A player's trade hazard rises sharply only when his team falls out of contention in the weeks right before the trade deadline; a contender's veteran or a team still in the race has near-zero deadline hazard, so contention status gates the calendar spike.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit weekly trade hazards with an interaction between playoff probability (from standings simulation) and weeks-to-deadline on 2010-2025 player-weeks and compare with an additive model.

interactions.hypothesis: Delay risk is essentially zero under a fixed roof and becomes material only at open-air venues once the forecast thunderstorm probability in the kickoff window passes a threshold, because the league's lightning rule suspends play for any strike within the stadium radius.
interactions.how_to_test: Plot delay frequency against forecast thunderstorm probability split by roof type on 2010-2025 games and test for a kink versus a linear logistic fit.

nonlinearities.shape: spikes at calendar dates
nonlinearities.why: The hazard is piecewise: Black Monday, cut-down day, trade deadline, free agency and flex-announcement dates carry most of the mass, so a smooth time-to-event model misallocates probability across weeks.

nonlinearities.shape: logistic in draft round with hard exclusion
nonlinearities.why: Inclusion probability falls steeply from first-round picks to undrafted free agents, and an IR placement acts as a hard zero rather than a smooth penalty.

nonlinearities.shape: winner-take-most competing risk
nonlinearities.why: A coach's probability of being next out is a steeply convex function of his hazard relative to the hottest other seats: doubling a mid-ranked coach's hazard barely moves his first-out probability while the top seat holds most of the mass.

mechanism_review.summary: Off-field outcomes are generated by organisations, schedulers and the weather, not by plays. (1) Who decides: owners and general managers (coach exits and hires, signings, trades, cuts, contract offers), players and agents (retirement, free-agent destination, supplemental-draft declaration), the league office and broadcasters (schedule windows, flex, international venues), or physical conditions (lightning and severe weather). (2) What constrains them: contract terms and guarantee dates, the salary cap, roster limits and designation rules, the calendar (Black Monday, the trade deadline, cut-down day, free agency, schedule release, flex windows) and the standings. (3) How information leaks: insiders report intentions before official acts, with reporter-specific reliability and lag, while the contract requires the official act. (4) Selection among alternatives: a destination among 32 teams, which coach goes first among 32, or which games a network flexes. Probabilities come from calendar-structured hazards, competing-risk orderings, categorical choice models and reference-class base rates, with edge mostly in timing and in resolution wording.

stages.name: Event owner and decision process
stages.description: Each contract has a decision-maker: head-coach exits and hires are owner/GM decisions after performance and contract considerations; roster inclusion is a GM and coach decision under a 53-man limit; signings, extensions and trades are bilateral negotiations under the cap; retirement and supplemental-draft declaration are player decisions; primetime counts are league/broadcaster scheduling decisions. Identifying the decision-maker determines which information matters and what base rates apply, so the contract types cannot be pooled into one model.
stages.distribution: Mixture of categorical event types with distinct generators; very small samples per type (a handful of coach firings per year)

stages.name: Calendar structure and hazard timing
stages.description: Events concentrate in windows: coach firings in-season after bad losses and especially the week after the regular season; roster cuts on a fixed date; retirements after the season and before free agency; trade deadlines in early November (date taken from the original draft and not verified here; the league calendar varies by season); free agency opening in March and schedule release in May. A time-to-event model must therefore have a time-varying hazard that spikes at known dates and is near zero elsewhere, and a deadline in the contract (before Mar 1, 2027) integrates the hazard over those spikes.
stages.distribution: Piecewise-constant hazard with spikes at calendar dates; probability within a window is 1 - exp(-integral of hazard)

stages.name: Information flow from insiders to official act
stages.description: Credible insiders report agreements, intentions and injuries before the official act; the conversion probability depends on reporter tier, wording ('agreed to terms' vs 'expected to') and time to the announcement. The contract requires the official act, so the model must predict both occurrence and the lag against close time. Rumour mass without credible attribution has little value.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli conversion given a report; lag distribution is right-skewed (hours to weeks); high reporter heterogeneity

stages.name: Player movement: trade hazard, next-team choice and contract value
stages.description: KXNFLTRADE is a hazard of an officially processed trade before a date, concentrated before the early-November trade deadline (date from the original draft, unverified) and in the March-to-draft window; it rises with the team's record falling out of contention, the player's contract (cheap control is tradeable, dead cap blocks moves) and reported availability. KXNFLNEXTTEAM is a categorical choice over the current team (extension, franchise tag, simply remaining under contract), 31 other teams and 'Retires / No Team', driven by contract status, cap space by team, positional need and reported interest. KXNFLCONTRACTSIZE (title only) is a value distribution anchored on positional market comps scaled by cap growth.
stages.distribution: Trade: piecewise hazard with deadline spike, most players near zero; next team: categorical with a large mass on the current team; contract size: right-skewed value distribution around positional comps

stages.name: Roster-battle process for the 53-man list
stages.description: A player's chance of making the initial 53 is a function of draft capital, contracted money (dead-cap cost of cutting), preseason performance, depth at the position, special-teams value and injury status. The contract excludes IR/PUP/suspended players, so an injured star may resolve NO, and the 53-man list is a constrained selection (a fixed number of slots by position group).
stages.distribution: Binary with strongly informative covariates; most starters near one; borderline players in the 30-70% range; the IR exclusion creates a discrete state

stages.name: Settlement wording and novelty events
stages.description: Official announcement versus report, effective-date clauses for retirement, rescission-proof trade settlement, practice-squad exclusion and NO-on-postponement for game location decide the label. KXNFLCOMPETE (a celebrity must take a snap, preseason included) is a signing-then-activation chain with a tiny base rate; KXNFLHKANE is the same chain without the snap; KXNFLGAMELOCATION is venue-retention risk for an international game (security, weather, stadium readiness). These have no football-performance driver and rest on reference-class priors. Reference classes are now defined per series in nfl.offfield_base_rate: KXNFLHKANE and KXNFLCOMPETE use a cross-sport-athlete class (non-football athletes publicly linked to an NFL tryout or signing, outcome official signing or a recorded snap within the window), KXNFLGAMELOCATION uses the history of announced international regular-season games and whether each was played in the announced city. The ownership-stake (KXNFLOWNERSTAKE) and stadium-completion (KXNFLSTADIUM) series were re-filed by the final series assignment to OUT_OF_SCOPE (franchise_ownership_business, team_facilities) and are explicitly excluded from this archetype.
stages.distribution: Deterministic rule application; novelty events are Poisson or Bernoulli with reference-class base rates

stages.name: Draft family: supplemental-draft declaration and draft-capital context
stages.description: The draft-order mechanism for 'k-th quarterback drafted' contracts now belongs to the separate draft archetype that owns KXNFLDRAFTQB. What remains here is KXNFLSUPDRAFTPICK: whether a player declares for the supplemental draft, a rare eligibility-driven decision (lost college eligibility, academic or disciplinary status) settled on the league's announcement. The draft board and QB class model are kept as context for draft-related specials and for 53-man and first-start contracts that depend on draft capital, not as the primary source for a selection-order market.
stages.distribution: Rare binary declaration event with a very low base rate in recent seasons; announcement-dated

stages.name: Coaching carousel: next coach out and candidate hires
stages.description: KXNFLNEXTCOACHOUT asks which permanent head coach leaves first after issuance and before Feb 15, 2027: a competing-risk race in which coach i wins with probability integral of h_i(t) times the joint survival of all other coaches, so a coach with a modest hazard can still be unlikely to be first if a hotter seat exists elsewhere. Interim coaches are excluded. KXNFLHIRECOACH asks whether a named candidate is hired as a coach before a date: vacancies opened by exits, the candidate's interest in returning, his reputation and connections to owners/GMs with openings, and the breadth of 'a coach' (head coach versus coordinator or other leagues).
stages.distribution: Competing risks across 32 coaches with calendar spikes (in-season firings after losses, Black Monday); hire: product of vacancy count and candidate selection share, a small probability for most named candidates

stages.name: Schedule windows and weather delays for scheduled games
stages.description: KXNFLPRIMETIME counts a team's games in SNF, MNF, TNF windows plus Thanksgiving and Christmas, excluding the Wednesday opener; after schedule release the base count is fixed and only flex scheduling moves it, driven by team records and appeal in flex-eligible weeks. KXNFLDELAY asks whether a game has any official weather delay (pre-start or in-game): this is mostly lightning within the stadium radius (a 30-minute suspension per strike, as stated in the original draft; the league lightning rule is not verified here) at open-air venues, so roof type, month, kickoff hour and regional thunderstorm climatology dominate, and a fixed dome has near-zero risk.
stages.distribution: Primetime: base count plus a small number of Bernoulli flex events; delay: rare Bernoulli (near zero indoors, a few percent for early-season afternoon games in thunderstorm-prone regions)

contract_review.settlement_definition: Fourteen live series of non-game events, 13 with rules text (KXNFLCONTRACTSIZE is TITLE_ONLY). Each settles on an official act, list or occurrence: head-coach departure before a date, firing/resignation/announced exit (KXNFLCOACHOUT) and which coach is next out among all head coaches before Feb 15, 2027, interims excluded (KXNFLNEXTCOACHOUT); a named person hired as a coach in men's pro football before a date (KXNFLHIRECOACH); listing on the initial post-cutdown 53-man active roster, reserve/practice-squad lists excluded and later cuts not reversing YES (KXNFL53MAN); official team-announced or league-registered signing, media reports insufficient (KXNFLHKANE); retirement announcements effective before the next regular season (KXNFLRETIRE); a non-NFL athlete recording at least one snap, preseason included (KXNFLCOMPETE); supplemental-draft declaration confirmed before July 15 (KXNFLSUPDRAFTPICK); a trade officially processed and approved before a date, YES even if later rescinded (KXNFLTRADE); a player's next team before a date, with 'Retires / No Team' and stay-with-current-team outcomes (KXNFLNEXTTEAM); a team playing N+ primetime games (SNF, MNF, TNF plus Thanksgiving and Christmas, Wednesday opener excluded) (KXNFLPRIMETIME); any official weather delay of a game, including pre-start delays and in-game stoppages (KXNFLDELAY); and an international game beginning in the named city before a date, NO on cancellation or postponement past it (KXNFLGAMELOCATION).
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official league and team announcements, the league transaction wire (trades, signings, roster lists), the published NFL schedule and flex announcements, official game delay records, and venue of kickoff.
variants_and_edge_cases: Resolution source differs: official team/league announcement (signing, retirement, 53-man, coach exit, hire, trade processing), the published schedule and broadcast windows (primetime), an official weather delay, or venue of kickoff (game location). 'Announced vs reported' is explicit for signings.

Strike construction: per-candidate binaries (coach out, hire, trade), categorical outcome sets with residual strikes (next team incl. current team and 'Retires / No Team'; next coach out across all coaches), and count thresholds (5+ primetime games).

KXNFLTRADE resolves YES on official processing even if the trade is later rescinded or the player fails a physical; KXNFLGAMELOCATION resolves NO (not fair price) on cancellation or postponement past the date.

Coach and retirement series have an 'announces' clause, which front-loads resolution relative to the actual departure; KXNFLNEXTCOACHOUT excludes interim coaches and counts only departures after issuance.

KXNFLHIRECOACH counts any coaching hire 'in men's pro football' (wording could include coordinator roles or other leagues); KXNFLCONTRACTSIZE is TITLE_ONLY, so the value definition (total, APY, guarantees) is unknown.
Award specials, the Top 100 list, the on-air role series and draft-order markets are no longer filed here and are not claimed.

Blueprint-inherited context inputs (m.external_lines, nfl.award_voting_mechanics, m.quote_history) are benchmark-only or irrelevant here and are not used by any stage; nfl.award_voting_mechanics, nfl.broadcast_role_assignment and m.quote_history are detached by patch.

combos_and_parlays.label: Multi-leg combo and parlay markets
combos_and_parlays.target: Joint probability that all legs resolve as required.
combos_and_parlays.mechanism: Joint probability = integral over a shared game process: team win, margin and total are driven by the same latent script, and player legs share pass volume and scoring. Naive products miss positive/negative correlation (QB yards and team total positive; favorite cover and underdog receiver negative). Leg wording (push/void/OT) and fees reduce edge, and combo order books are thin.

inputs.why: Leg correlation matrix converts marginals into a joint probability.
Team strength for outcome legs.
Consistency across total and spread legs.
The shared latent game script drives positive and negative dependence between team and player legs.
The margin lattice at key numbers matters for legs that involve spreads and exact margins.
Marginal player distributions.
Quoted combo price versus the correlated joint probability is the core mispricing check.
Per-leg void, push and overtime handling decide whether a combo pays or voids.
Fees are larger in absolute terms on thin combo markets and must be deducted from edge.
Combo books are thin and spreads wide; executable price may erase modeled edge.
Provides the specific conditional dependence structure that a constant matrix misses and is what separates combo pricing from multiplying marginals.
Directly handles same-team multi-leg combos that are the dominant retail leg set.
Late news makes combos stale unevenly; the mixture decomposition is needed to price the correlated move.
Combo wording is unknown here and materially changes the joint event.
Supplies the market-free side, total and team-total marginals and their coherent joint mean that same-game combo legs inherit.
Key-number atoms and push probabilities for spread and total legs built around model means rather than line residuals.
Gives the regime-specific dependence that separates combo pricing from multiplying marginals, without importing the market spread as a regime selector.
KXNFLNBA settles on two championships in different sports; this input is the only route by which the non-NFL leg enters the record.
Multi-game moneyline parlays (PREPACK2ML/3ML) are a product of legs only if this residual dependence is negligible.

Closes the missing shared-weather dependence of same-game combos: names the coupled leg pairs (total, kicker, QB/receiver yards, rusher) and makes the joint draw conditional on one weather state instead of independent per-leg adjustments.

Turns the undefined dependency on sibling marginals into an explicit export contract, so combo joints come from shared latent draws with coherent margin, total and availability rather than a product or copula of separately calibrated legs.
