interactions.hypothesis: Favorite win x over: correlation depends on whether the favorite wins by scoring (positive) or by defense (negative).
QB yards x team total x spread: passing volume is positively correlated with the total and negatively with the favorite covering.
Leg wording x fees: voided legs change payout; compare executable price after fees.

The favourite's own QB passing yards and the favourite covering are positively linked in competitive shootouts, where passing builds the lead, but turn negative in blowouts where the leading team runs the clock; the underdog's QB yards are positively linked with the underdog scoring and negative with the favourite covering once the underdog trails. The sign depends on the margin regime and on whose QB is on the leg, so one fitted coefficient is wrong in both.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate the pair correlation (favourite QB yards, favourite cover) and (underdog QB yards, favourite cover) separately for modelled |margin| bins and total terciles and test the sign change.

interactions.hypothesis: Two receivers' yardage overs on the same team require a passing total that few games reach; the accounting identity makes the pair's joint probability much lower than the product conditional on the same team total, and zero for first-TD pairs.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare model joint for teammate pairs with and without the sum constraint on historical player-games.

interactions.hypothesis: A QB scratch moves the favourite-win leg, team total and passing legs in the same direction but by different amounts; the combo's joint is a mixture over QB states whose weights are only known at inactive-list time.
interactions.how_to_test: Backtest mixture-versus-product predictions on games with late QB changes.

interactions.hypothesis: At integer lines on 3 and 7, a push leg changes the combo's payoff; the joint probability has a discontinuity at the key numbers and the effect depends on whether the push is dropped or loses.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute joint probability under both push rules for combos with lines on 3, 7 and 10; compare to settled outcomes.

interactions.hypothesis: A favourite-covers-and-over combo requires the favourite to score roughly 27 or more, so the joint depends on the model margin and total means and on the lead-state script together rather than on each marginal alone; correlated margin and total residuals on the score lattice make the joint above the product when the favourite's offence drives both and below it when the favourite wins by defence and clock control.
interactions.how_to_test: On historical games compute the empirical joint of cover and over in bins of model margin mean and model total mean and compare with the product of marginals and with a lattice simulation using key-number mass.

interactions.hypothesis: For multi-game moneyline parlays the error of the product approximation grows with the number of legs and with leg favouritism: a small positive residual correlation matters more when all legs are heavy favourites (joint near the product of large p) than for long-shot legs.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare realized parlay hit rates against product-of-legs predictions binned by number of legs and minimum leg probability on 2012-2025 same-week game sets.

interactions.hypothesis: Below about 10 mph the weather term barely moves any leg, so same-game legs are close to their script-only dependence; above about 15 mph sustained (or gusts near 25) total, kicker and passing legs all drop together, so the joint of an under/kicker-under/QB-under combo jumps above the product while an over/QB-over combo falls below it. Roofed games stay in the calm regime.
interactions.how_to_test: On 2010-2025 open-air games compute empirical joint hit rates of synthetic under+kicker-under and under+QB-yards-under pairs by wind bin and compare to the product of bin-specific marginals; repeat for dome games as the placebo.

nonlinearities.shape: sign-changing across margin regimes
nonlinearities.why: Correlation between the favourite covering and the QB's yards is positive in close games and negative in blowouts; averaging gives near zero and misses both.

nonlinearities.shape: spikes at key numbers 3, 7, 10, 14
nonlinearities.why: Margin distribution has lumps at 3 and 7, so spread legs near these numbers have jump changes in cover and push probability that a continuous model does not produce.

nonlinearities.shape: convex in mean pairwise correlation at fixed marginals; bounded above by the smallest marginal
nonlinearities.why: For an all-legs-must-win combo the joint probability at fixed leg marginals rises convexly with the pairwise correlation and can never exceed the smallest marginal, so a misestimated correlation matters far more for long combos of positively linked legs than for mixed-sign legs.

mechanism_review.summary: A combo's probability is the probability of an intersection of leg events, so the objects to model are the dependence structure and the joint support, not the marginals. In football all same-game legs are functions of one latent process: the drive sequence. A single drive outcome (a 12-play field-goal drive versus a 2-play deep touchdown) simultaneously moves team points, quarter scoring, the QB's yards and TDs, the rusher's attempts, and the clock that decides how many more drives occur. Hard accounting identities link the legs: individual yards cannot exceed the team total, individual TDs sum to team TDs, a team's points must be 3a+6b+... in discrete steps, and the winner's margin and the game total are tied through team scores. Between games there is near independence, apart from shared weather, referee crew or league-wide shocks. So the pricing task is: (i) good legs, (ii) a joint simulator or copula calibrated to these identities and to regime-dependent dependence (script, QB status, weather), (iii) exact leg wording so that void/push/OT states are handled, and (iv) execution cost and thin liquidity once a price exists.

stages.name: Leg marginals from the underlying archetype models
stages.description: Each leg inherits a marginal probability from the model of its own archetype: spread and moneyline from the margin distribution, total from drive-by-drive scoring, QB yards from attempts and efficiency, TD scorer from the allocation model. If the marginals are wrongly calibrated, the joint is wrong whatever the copula; the combo error is approximately the sum of leg errors because probabilities multiply. Marginals must also be coherent with each other (for example, a team total leg and a game total leg imply an opponent total). The marginals are an explicit dependency on the model outputs of the sibling archetypes (moneyline/spread, total, QB, scorer); this record does not rebuild them and uses market-free team means, never ratings implied by lines. The dependency is now an explicit interface (nfl.sibling_leg_marginal_interface): each sibling archetype exports its leg P(yes) and shared simulation draws of home/away points, margin, total, plays, availability and weather bin, so legs are read from the same draws.
stages.distribution: Each leg is Bernoulli with its own probability; the joint support is a subset of {0,1}^k with k = 2 to 6 legs; errors in marginals compound multiplicatively across legs

stages.name: Shared latent game state
stages.description: Same-game legs depend on the same latent variables: expected margin, expected total, pace, QB and key-player availability, weather and the lead state across time. A trailing script raises the QB's attempts and yards and lowers the favourite's rushing, so favourite-cover and the trailing team's QB yards are negatively related (and the leading team's QB yards positively only while the game is competitive) even though 'good team' and 'high total' are positively related. These dependencies are regime-dependent: the sign of the correlation between a rusher's yardage and the favourite covering flips between competitive and blowout games.
stages.distribution: Continuous latent factors (margin ~ N-ish with key-number lattice, total, pace) driving conditional Bernoulli legs; dependence is conditional and non-constant across regimes

stages.name: Accounting identities and hard constraints
stages.description: Football box-score numbers obey sums: the TDs of all players on a team sum to the team's offensive TDs, individual receiving yards are bounded by the team's passing yards, and team points are non-negative combinations of 7, 3, 2, 6 and 8. These constraints create dependence that Gaussian correlations miss: two teammates both scoring first-TD legs is impossible, and two skill players both going over their yardage lines requires a large passing team total.
stages.distribution: Deterministic constraints on a discrete lattice; produces exactly zero joint probability for incompatible leg sets and large non-Gaussian dependence in the tails

stages.name: Leg wording: push, void, overtime and fair-price states
stages.description: The joint event is determined by each leg's own settlement text. Legs ending in a push on integer lines, voided on postponement, excluding overtime, or settling at a fair price on a no-snap player each remove or alter the event. A combo containing a regulation-only leg and a full-game leg has a joint outcome that diverges whenever the game is tied after 60 minutes. Combo contract text decides if a voided leg is dropped or whether the combo is cancelled. KXNFLCOMBO adds a participation condition ('as a participant in both halves') to each player leg, so an in-game exit by any of the named players can decide the combo regardless of the stat.
stages.distribution: Rule-based, deterministic given leg and combo wording; tiny probability of tie/postponement but concentrated on key numbers

stages.name: Execution cost, fees and book thinness
stages.description: Once a model joint probability exists, realized edge is the model joint minus the executable price, fees (often a larger share of a long-shot combo price) and the cost of hedging legs that do not exist as markets. Combo books are thin and stale, so the price can reflect a market-maker's correlation assumption rather than information. This stage is execution economics, not game information; it is context for trade evaluation and does not count as an input interaction.
stages.distribution: Price is a dealer quote; edge is small relative to spread; deterministic fee schedule applies to the whole combo payoff

stages.name: Cross-league futures conjunction
stages.description: KXNFLNBA pays only if a named NFL team wins the Super Bowl and a named NBA team wins the NBA Finals of the same 2026-27 cycle. The NFL leg is a season-long playoff path (seeding, bye, single-elimination games) produced by a standings and playoff simulation; the NBA leg is a best-of-seven playoff path from that sport's own model. The two are effectively independent, so the price is near the product of the legs, but the NFL leg resolves in February and early elimination of either team resolves NO, so the combo's value path is front-loaded by the NFL season.
stages.distribution: Product of two small, independent Bernoulli probabilities (each typically under 0.2); absorbing early-NO state on the first elimination

stages.name: Cross-game moneyline parlays on one slate or round
stages.description: KXNFLPREPACK2ML/3ML pay if each named team wins its own game, e.g. three divisional-round games on Jan 17-18. Each leg's win probability comes from that game's market-free margin lattice including overtime (regular-season ties possible). Legs are different games, so the dependence is weak and comes only from shared model error (a common rating-system bias applied to all games), shared weather systems or officiating directives, and in playoffs from nothing structural. The joint is therefore close to the product of leg probabilities, and the main error source is miscalibration of each leg compounding multiplicatively; overestimating dependence would misprice favourites-parlays.
stages.distribution: Product of 2-3 Bernoulli legs with p roughly 0.2-0.85 each; small positive residual correlation via shared model error; tie mass per regular-season leg about 0.4%

stages.name: Shared weather state as a common shock across same-game legs
stages.description: At open-air venues a single kickoff weather state moves several legs together: sustained wind above roughly 15 mph or heavy precipitation lowers the game and team totals, cuts kicker points and long-field-goal legs, lowers QB passing-yard and receiver-yard legs and pushes play-calling toward the run, raising the lead back's carries. Same-direction combos (under, QB under, kicker under) therefore have joint probability above the product of marginals and mixed combos below it. Domes and closed roofs remove the shock entirely, and forecast uncertainty at quote time means the joint must integrate over the weather distribution, not plug in a point forecast.
stages.distribution: Regime mixture over calm, moderate and severe weather bins; within a bin legs share mean shifts and a residual correlation; zero effect for roofed games

talent_strength.note: Team strength enters through the market-free team points mean that feeds side and total leg marginals; market-implied ratings are benchmarks only. For the cross-league futures combo, NFL team strength enters through the season simulation.

opponent_matchup.note: Matchup effects live inside each leg's own archetype model and enter the combo only through its marginals; the combo layer adds no separate opponent-matchup variable.

role_personnel.note: Role shares matter through the identity that player outputs sum to team outputs.

availability_news.note: A QB or WR1 scratch moves several legs at once, so availability is a shared factor.

coaching_scheme.note: Coaching tendencies act through team marginals and script, which are already represented by the script lattice; no combo-specific coaching variable exists.

environment.note: Shared weather enters the joint draw as a regime variable (calm/moderate/severe) coupling total, kicker, QB/receiver yards and rusher legs; elasticities by leg pair remain to be estimated.

game_context_script.note: Lead-state script is the main source of cross-leg dependence.

pace_volume.note: Plays and drives are shared across volume legs; covered via the correlation matrix.

efficiency_conversion.note: Marginal stat shapes for each leg; conversion luck is in each leg's own model.

distribution_variance.note: Joint distribution on the score lattice with constraints for same-game packs; residual cross-game dependence for multi-game moneyline parlays.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest, stakes and motivation affect legs only through each leg's own marginal; they create no separate dependency channel between legs at the combo layer.

officiating_rules.note: Crew tendencies are small and affect legs in each model individually; no combo-level effect has been identified beyond the shared game environment.

settlement_contract.note: Per-leg void, push and overtime wording plus combo fee mechanics.

contract_review.settlement_definition: Six live series, all with rules text. Same-game pre-packs KXNFLPREPACK and KXNFLPREPACKSGP (e.g. 'New York G wins against New England, ... collectively score under 46.5 points') and the championship player-prop parlay KXNFLCOMBO resolve YES only if every leg occurs ('All outcomes encompassed in a market must occur'; 'All Components must resolve to yes'); KXNFLCOMBO player legs are worded 'records at least N+ ... as a participant in both halves'. Cross-game moneyline parlays KXNFLPREPACK2ML/3ML resolve YES if each named team wins its listed game (2 or 3 games, possibly on different days). KXNFLNBA is a cross-league futures conjunction (named NFL team wins the 2026-27 NFL title AND named NBA team wins the 2026-27 NBA title) resolving NO on the first elimination. Settlement source is each leg's official result. No sampled combo text states how a voided/postponed leg, a push on an integer line, a tie, or overtime is handled, nor what happens to a 'both halves' player leg when the player misses a half.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Per-leg official game results and box scores (NFL game book) for packs and parlays; NFL and NBA official championship results for KXNFLNBA. Leg-void, tie and push handling is not stated in the sampled text.
variants_and_edge_cases: Four variants: (a) same-game packs (PREPACK winner+total, PREPACKSGP), (b) cross-game moneyline parlays (PREPACK2ML, PREPACK3ML) over 2-3 games on possibly different dates, (c) single-game player-prop parlays (KXNFLCOMBO, Super Bowl, 5+ player legs with 'participant in both halves' wording), (d) cross-league futures (KXNFLNBA).
Moneyline legs ('wins against') in regular-season parlays can end in a tie after overtime; no sampled text says whether a tied leg is a loss or a void.

KXNFLCOMBO player legs require the player to be 'a participant in both halves'; the truncated text does not say whether failing that condition makes the leg NO or voids the combo, which matters for injury-exit risk across 5+ players.
Half-point totals (46.5, 41.5) cannot push, but integer lines in other packs could; push handling inside packs is not stated.
KXNFLPREPACKSGP titles are template-mangled ('Over 56.5 points scored wins against ...'), so leg identity must be read from market metadata, not the title.
Cross-league futures combos resolve at different dates (Super Bowl in February, NBA Finals in June) with early NO on elimination; same-game dependence inputs do not apply to them.

team_and_event_counting_specials.label: NFL team and event counting specials
team_and_event_counting_specials.target: A team's or both teams' additive count in a game (field goals, sacks, total yards, successful 2-point and 4th-down conversions) relative to a threshold.
team_and_event_counting_specials.mechanism: Per-game counts are opportunities times a per-opportunity rate: field goals follow drives that stall inside the kicker's range, sacks follow opposing dropbacks times a pressure-to-sack conversion, yards follow plays times yield per play, and two-point and fourth-down conversions follow each coach's decision to try times a success rate, all reshaped by score path, weather and overtime. Counts are overdispersed and discrete, so thresholds are tail masses of a mixture over score states; both-team counts add a script-driven negative dependence between teams. The multi-week next-interception series moved to its own archetype.

inputs.why: Red-zone conversion decides field goal versus touchdown.
Game script lattice sets pass volume and lead sizes.
Wind and cold depress passing and kicking.
Turns means into tail probabilities for the 'N+' strikes used in the per-game count series.
Splits the team sack count into three separately estimable factors and brings the opposing quarterback into a defensive count.
Coach aggression on fourth downs and two-point tries and tempo drive field-goal attempts and the conversion counts.
Go-for-it versus kick policy and two-point policy by state set attempts for field goals and for the 2-point and 4th-down conversion counts.
Go-for-it policy on 4th-and-goal decides two-point attempts and goal-line fourth-down tries counted by KXNFL4DCONV and KXNFL2PTCONV.
Overtime probability adds possessions to counts if overtime counts and adds a small tail mass to dispersion; tie-count use sits in the league tie archetype.
Offensive success rate links to yards per play for the team-yards series and to short-yardage conversion; no first-down series is live.
Safety frequency is a rare-event tail input to the dispersion stage; generic and demoted to context.
Pressure drives sack counts for the team and game sack series.
Starting quarterback status and sack avoidance change dropbacks and sacks for team sacks and game sacks.
In-game quarterback exit risk changes the opposing sack pool and the team's yards; staged in the sack stage.
Practice and designation vintages feed the starting-quarterback availability probability used by the sack stage.
Plays per game bound every count; the opponent's pace and ball control matter as much as own pace.
Expected drives set the opportunities for field goals and stalled drives.
Kicker range and accuracy by distance, altitude and wind decide field-goal counts for KXNFLFG.

interactions.hypothesis: Wind compresses effective kicking range, shifting field-goal attempts to go-for-it decisions.

Trailing teams throw more and take more hits late, so opposing defences with a lead produce more sacks per dropback, while a leading offence that runs reduces the opposing sack pool; the sign of the script effect on the sack count depends on which team leads.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate sacks per opponent dropback by the defence's score state and quarter.

interactions.hypothesis: Field goals per game equal drives times the chance of stalling in range, which is the complement of the red-zone touchdown rate; a strong red-zone offence produces fewer field goals even with many drives, so drives and red-zone efficiency move the count in opposite directions.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress field goals per game on drives and red-zone touchdown rate and test the interaction coefficient.

interactions.hypothesis: Trailing teams run more plays at a faster tempo and pass more, which raises opposing sack opportunities and total yards together, while a leading team runs the clock and shortens the game; the direction depends on which team leads, so plays and drives respond to the score state and not only to team tempo.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress plays, dropbacks and yards per team-game on time spent trailing and own tempo, with team effects, 2015-2025.

interactions.hypothesis: Go-for-it and two-point decisions are expected to rise when a team trails late (down 8, 14 or more in the fourth quarter), so the conversion counts would depend on whether the game produces a late deficit and on the coach's aggressiveness; this is a hypothesis to test, with no evidence offered here, and the sampled both-team series are all one game.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress team-game 4th-down and 2-point attempts on time spent trailing by 9+ in the second half, with a coach random effect.

interactions.hypothesis: Count dispersion depends on the score path because blowouts may produce extreme sack counts while close games produce long drives; mixing across score states creates fat tails in the marginal count distribution, so the threshold probability need not be that of a single negative binomial (a hypothesis to test).
interactions.how_to_test: Compare the mixture of state-specific negative binomials with a single negative binomial on tail frequencies of sacks and field goals.

nonlinearities.shape: right-skewed count tail: tail probability rises faster than a Poisson model for a given mean
nonlinearities.why: Over-dispersion increases the mass for 6+ sacks and 4+ field goals, so strikes in the upper tail are underpriced by Poisson assumptions.

nonlinearities.shape: steep logistic decay of make probability with distance, with a kicker-specific range threshold
nonlinearities.why: A few extra yards cut the field-goal make probability by several percentage points beyond 45 yards, so the field-goal count is a nonlinear function of the distance distribution of stalled drives, with wind and cold shifting the threshold.

nonlinearities.shape: threshold in win probability and score deficit: attempt rates jump when trailing late
nonlinearities.why: Go-for-it and two-point attempt rates are near the neutral baseline until the deficit and clock make kicking pointless and then rise steeply, so the conversion counts have a regime change in the simulated score path rather than a smooth response.

nonlinearities.shape: convex: sack probability per dropback rises faster than linearly with pressure rate at the extremes
nonlinearities.why: Teams at the high end of pressure rate convert pressure to sacks at similar rates but against quarterbacks with poor sack avoidance the conversion rises sharply, which fattens the upper tail that a 6+ team sack strike depends on.

mechanism_review.summary: Per-game counts (field goals, sacks, yards, successful two-point and fourth-down conversions, for one team or both teams combined) are opportunities times a per-opportunity rate: field goals come from drives that stall inside the kicker's range, sacks from opposing dropbacks times a pressure-to-sack conversion, yards from plays times yards per play, and conversions from each coach's decision to try times a success rate, all reshaped by score path, weather and overtime. The counts are overdispersed and discrete, so thresholds are tail masses of a mixture over score states, and both-team counts add a script-driven negative dependence between the two teams. Per-team and both-team counts share this chain and are kept in one archetype by decision; the multi-week next-interception series, the score-path functionals, rare play calls and league-wide rare-event counts have their own archetypes.

stages.name: Opportunity counts for the team in the game
stages.description: Counts are built on opportunities: plays and dropbacks for a team, drives and stalled drives, and for both-team counts the sum over two offences. The offence's tempo and the opponent's ball control determine how many occur, and overtime adds possessions if it counts. For the sack contracts the relevant pool is the opponent's dropbacks outside two-point tries.
stages.distribution: Plays, drives and dropbacks per team-game: approximately normal with small skew; the earlier ranges (plays 120-135 combined, drives 22-26, dropbacks 35-45 per team) are unsourced placeholders to compute from play-by-play

stages.name: Field goals: stalled drives inside range and kicker conversion
stages.description: A team's field goals (KXNFLFG, 4+ is a strike of 3.5) need a drive that stalls inside the kicker's range, a decision to kick rather than go for it, and a make. The rate of stalls inside range is the complement of red-zone touchdown efficiency, kicker accuracy falls with distance, wind and cold, and coach aggression on fourth down removes attempts. The count is small with a mean near 1.6 per team and a thin upper tail, so a 4+ threshold is a tail event of drive volume times stall rate times make probability.
stages.distribution: Count of field goals per team is a small overdispersed count (0-5 range seen in the draft; the mean of about 1.6 is an unsourced placeholder to compute); make probability falls with distance and wind

stages.name: Sacks: dropbacks times pressure conversion
stages.description: A defence's sacks (KXNFLTEAMSACK, KXNFLGAMESACK) come from the opponent's dropbacks times the rate at which pressure turns into sacks, with the quarterback's sack avoidance and the offence's protection as modifiers. Counts are low with heavy dispersion. Quarterback status (nfl.qb) enters as a probability that the starter plays and an in-game exit hazard; KXNFLGAMESACK sums two defences' sacks, which are linked negatively through script (the trailing team drops back more and absorbs more sacks while the leader runs) and positively through shared pace and weather.
stages.distribution: Sacks per team-game overdispersed with a small mean; the mean (about 2.3 in the earlier draft) is an unsourced placeholder to compute from play-by-play

stages.name: Total yardage: plays times yield per play
stages.description: Total yards (KXNFLTEAMYDS, 450+ is a strike of 449.5) follow plays and success rate with a per-play yield distribution that has explosive-play tails; drive-level variance makes the totals overdispersed. Weather shifts both rates modestly (penalty rates are not modelled), and the script changes which play types dominate. The volume side comes from team plays (nfl.pace), drives (nfl.drives) and the script that tilts run/pass mix (nfl.script), multiplied by per-play yield; the 450+ strike is expected to sit well above the mean (an unsourced placeholder, to compute from play-by-play), so it depends on the explosive-play tail.
stages.distribution: Total yards per team right-skewed by explosive plays; the mean of about 330 and sd of about 80 in the earlier draft are unsourced placeholders to compute from play-by-play

stages.name: Conversion counts: two-point tries and fourth-down tries
stages.description: KXNFL2PTCONV and KXNFL4DCONV count successful conversions by both teams, so each is attempts times success. Attempts come from each coach's two-point and go-for-it policy by field position, distance and score state: trailing teams late are expected to go for two and for it more often (a hypothesis, not established here), and a close game may rarely invite either, so the count may depend on the simulated path as well as on coach habit. Success comes from short-yardage offence against the opposing defence, with red-zone and goal-to-go efficiency for two-point tries from the 2-yard line. Stakes are suspected to raise attempts but are unmeasured.
stages.distribution: Two-point successes per game mostly 0-2 (the strike of 2 is a rare double); fourth-down successes per game 0-6 (strike 5 is a tail), small overdispersed counts with strong score-path dependence (ranges are unsourced placeholders to compute)

stages.name: Count dispersion and rare in-game events
stages.description: Counts are overdispersed relative to Poisson because opportunities and rates are correlated within a game and across stats; blowouts produce extreme sack counts while close games produce long drives. Rare events (safeties, overtime) add small masses at the tails and, if overtime counts, extra possessions. The model needs a dispersion parameter per stat and score state rather than a single Poisson assumption, and for both-team counts a negative correlation between teams through script and a positive one through shared pace and weather.
stages.distribution: Negative binomial with a dispersion parameter that differs by stat; safety and overtime frequencies are unsourced placeholders to compute from play-by-play

talent_strength.note: Offensive success rate and kicker quality set the baseline rates for yards, field goals and conversions; defensive strength enters through the sack inputs (nfl.pass_rush and the sack decomposition); no interception input is attached.

opponent_matchup.note: Opposing pass rush and protection decide sack counts for a given team.

role_personnel.note: Kicker identity and starting quarterback are the personnel factors for field goals and sacks.

availability_news.note: Quarterback status and in-game exit risk shift dropbacks and sack hazards; practice-report vintages are not archived publicly (u3).

coaching_scheme.note: Go-for-it, two-point and fourth-and-goal policy decide attempts for the field-goal and conversion counts.

environment.note: Wind and cold depress passing and kicking and so field goals, sacks and yards.

game_context_script.note: Score state (nfl.script, measured on the own-model margin distribution after the round-3 patch) shifts dropbacks, rushes and aggression; overtime adds possessions if it counts.

pace_volume.note: Plays, drives and dropbacks are the opportunity base for every count.

efficiency_conversion.note: Red-zone conversion, offensive success rate and kicker accuracy are the per-opportunity rates for field goals, yards and conversions.

distribution_variance.note: Negative-binomial dispersion by stat and score state converts means into tail probabilities for 'N+' strikes.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Playoff and must-win stakes plausibly raise fourth-down and two-point attempts (the both-team samples are all for one game, Seattle vs New England on Feb 8, 2026) but no input measures a stakes effect; this is an unverified hypothesis.

officiating_rules.note: Penalty rates and crew tendencies are second-order for the counts in this archetype and have no direct link to a live series, so nfl.penalties and nfl.officials_crew are detached by patch round 3 and not staged.

settlement_contract.note: Strike construction, the 2-point-try sack exclusion, the 48-hour postponement rule and the regular-season window come from the sampled rules text; overtime treatment is unstated.

contract_review.settlement_definition: Six live series, all with sampled rules text, in two shapes of additive in-game count, kept in one archetype by decision: per-team and both-team counts share the opportunities-times-rate chain. One-team counts for a named game: field goals (KXNFLFG 'Minnesota 4+', floor_strike 3.5), sacks (KXNFLTEAMSACK 6+, 'Any sacks recorded during a 2-point conversion attempt do not count') and total yards of offense (KXNFLTEAMYDS 450+); each states that if the game is postponed but begins within 48 hours of its originally scheduled start the market stays open and resolves on 'the official final result', and if it does not start within 48 hours it resolves to a fair price. Both-team counts for the Feb 8, 2026 Seattle vs New England game: combined sacks (KXNFLGAMESACK, at least 9), successful 2-point conversions (KXNFL2PTCONV, at least 2) and successful 4th down conversions (KXNFL4DCONV, at least 5), whose sampled secondary text is empty so postponement, overtime and source are unstated. No sampled text says whether overtime events count or names a data source; official league statistics are implied. The multi-week next-interception series (KXNFLNEXTINT) moved to unreg:team_window_event_hazards.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Not named in the sampled rules texts (the one-team series say 'official final result'). Kalshi series metadata is reported by reviewers (not in contract_rules_sample.json, not verified by me) to name settlement sources (the league, ESPN; Fox Sports for KXNFLNONQBPASS).
variants_and_edge_cases: One-team series (KXNFLFG, KXNFLTEAMSACK, KXNFLTEAMYDS) carry the 48-hour postponement rule ('remain open and resolve based on the official final result'; fair price if not started within 48 hours); the three both-team series have no such sentence, although the primary text of the both-team series names the game 'originally scheduled' for a date, so postponement handling is unstated for them.

KXNFLTEAMSACK excludes sacks recorded during a 2-point conversion attempt; KXNFLGAMESACK (both teams) does not repeat the exclusion, so the treatment of conversion-try sacks in the combined count is unstated.

KXNFL2PTCONV and KXNFL4DCONV count successful conversions by both teams; the texts do not say whether a conversion on a play with an accepted penalty, a kick-based point after, or a fourth-down conversion by penalty (automatic first down) counts, which affects the realised counts.

No sampled text for any of the six series states whether overtime sacks, field goals, yards or conversions count; all samples named 'during the' or 'in the' game, so overtime is presumably included but unestablished (u5).

fantasy_points_markets.label: NFL fantasy-point markets (player totals, weekly leaders, head-to-head, ladders)
fantasy_points_markets.target: A player's full-PPR fantasy points in a game or period, or rank among players or head-to-head.
fantasy_points_markets.mechanism: Fantasy points are a weighted sum of the receptions, yards and touchdowns that the player prop archetypes already model, so they inherit volume (snaps, routes, targets, carries), efficiency and touchdown variance, with scoring weights that make touchdowns and receptions disproportionately important. Ranked and head-to-head markets are order statistics over correlated players, so game script and shared team volume create positive and negative correlations that a sum of marginals ignores.

inputs.why: Component model translating role and efficiency into PPR points.
Target share drives receptions and yards.
Carry share and goal-line role drive rushing points.
Snap share bounds opportunity.
Route participation separates real receiving roles.
Red-zone usage drives touchdown points.
Touchdown rates by role (regress toward the role mean).
Pass rate over expected sets volume.
Plays per game bound every volume count: fewer plays mean fewer targets, carries and scoring chances.
Game script shifts pass and rush volume (rebuilt from own forecast).
Availability and teammate absences redistribute opportunity.
Boom-bust variance shapes ladders and top-N.
Top-N and leader markets are order statistics.
Season totals need games-played risk.
Needed for H2H, top-N and ladder probabilities where correlation changes the answer, and for the shootout effect across a whole game.
Provides the touchdown component of a PPR forecast with a play-level calculation that red-zone share and anytime-TD rates only approximate.
Defines the target of every contract in the archetype and reduces risk from position classification and corrections, which have no equivalent in the other inputs.
Directly gives the probabilities for KXNFLFFPLAYERHIGH and KXNFLFFHIGHSCORE, which are not threshold events on the mean.
Provides a defined field model for the weekly leader contracts whose rules say all eligible players in the group are ranked.
Supplies KXNFLFANTASYMOST, the only single-game field maximum in this archetype and the only one on ESPN scoring.

KXNFLFFPTS lists kicker over/under markets (e.g. Will Reichard over 9.2); their settlement is a distance-tiered count of FG and XP events, which needs its own chain rather than skill-position scoring.
KXNFLFFPTS lists D/ST over markets for most teams each week; their score combines opponent-driven event counts and a points-allowed step that no skill-position stage composes.

interactions.hypothesis: Target share in the red zone multiplies into touchdown points beyond either alone.
Leading teams run; rushing points concentrate in favourites' lead backs.
A teammate's absence raises snap and target share most for the next player on the depth chart.

Touchdown points equal red-zone opportunities times conversion, and the number of red-zone trips depends on the score path and the team's total; a goal-line back on a high-scoring favourite gets multiplied opportunities, while the same share on a low-scoring team yields little.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress touchdowns on red-zone carries x team expected points and compare to additive models.

interactions.hypothesis: A quarterback and his top receiver share a touchdown pass, so their fantasy scores are positively correlated and the quarterback's total variance includes the receiver's; for H2H of a quarterback versus a receiver on the same team this correlation lowers the variance of the difference.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate correlation of QB and WR1 fantasy points by team and compare variance of the difference with the independent case.

interactions.hypothesis: When a starter is inactive his snaps and carries are taken by the next player on the depth chart, with a larger share to the one with a similar role, so one teammate's absence changes another's expected points non-uniformly by role.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare backups' snaps and fantasy points in games without the starter, split by role similarity.

interactions.hypothesis: In a high-total game several receivers have high scores, so the weekly leader is more likely to come from a shootout, and probabilities across players in the same game are positively correlated; independent field assumptions understate how often one game supplies the leader.
interactions.how_to_test: Check historical share of weekly WR leaders coming from games in the top quartile of totals.

interactions.hypothesis: The chance of a 34-point or 49-point game grows rapidly with touchdown count (three touchdowns plus yardage), so the high rungs are driven by the product of goal-line opportunity and big-play rate rather than by mean points.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute P(34+) conditional on touchdown count and on long-play count; compare to a normal approximation.

interactions.hypothesis: Fantasy value per target is catch probability times (1 reception point + 0.1 per yard) plus touchdown value, so the slope of points on target share depends on the receiver's depth: a short-area high-aDOT-low target profile gains mostly reception points at high catch rate, while deep targets are caught less often but carry more yards, so scoring is not linear in target share across depth profiles.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit points per target by aDOT bin and catch-rate bin, and test whether the slope of total points on targets differs across aDOT terciles.

interactions.hypothesis: D/ST points have a step in points allowed (+10, +7, +4, +1, 0, -1, -4) and event counts that rise when the opponent trails and throws; a defence facing a weak offence gains twice, through the higher tier and more sacks and interceptions in a passing script, so the response to the opponent's expected points is piecewise and convex at the low end.
interactions.how_to_test: On 2015-2025 team-games regress D/ST Sleeper points on opponent own-model expected points with tier dummies and compare the slope of event points across opponent-expectation bins.

interactions.hypothesis: A kicker's FG count depends on drives that stall inside range, so a more efficient red-zone offence or a more aggressive 4th-down coach converts FG tries into touchdowns: kicker points rise with team scoring only until red-zone conversion is high, then extra points replace field goals and the score flattens.
interactions.how_to_test: Bin team-games by own-model expected points and red-zone TD rate and compare kicker Sleeper points; test whether 4th-down aggressiveness terciles shift FG attempts at fixed expected points.

nonlinearities.shape: discrete six-point jumps: score distribution multi-modal at multiples of 6 plus a yardage base
nonlinearities.why: One extra touchdown moves a score by six points, so the cumulative distribution has steps; threshold probabilities move non-smoothly with the touchdown rate.

nonlinearities.shape: piecewise: zero if inactive, partial ramp for returning players, near constant for starters
nonlinearities.why: Fantasy output follows snaps closely, and snaps are step-like in injury status, which gives a bimodal distribution around the zero atom.

nonlinearities.shape: heavy right tail with probability of 34+ falling by a factor of 3-4 for each additional 10 points
nonlinearities.why: High fantasy scores come from rare multi-touchdown games, so probabilities for the highest rungs fall much faster than a normal tail with the same variance would predict.

nonlinearities.shape: expected maximum grows with log of pool size and heavy-tailed marginals
nonlinearities.why: The weekly position leader sits far out in the distribution of the pool, so small changes in a player's tail change his leader probability by more than his mean does.

mechanism_review.summary: A full-PPR fantasy score is a linear combination of a player's counting stats, and all of the weight is on four components: receptions (one point each), yardage (a tenth of a point per rushing or receiving yard, 0.04 per passing yard), touchdowns (six, with four for a passing touchdown) and negatives (interceptions, lost fumbles). The player must first be on the field; availability and snap share set an atom at zero and a ramp. Opportunity (targets, carries, dropbacks) comes from team volume and role; yield comes from efficiency and matchup; touchdowns come from goal-line and red-zone opportunity with a very large luck component and discrete six-point jumps. Components covary within a player (receptions with yards) and across teammates (a quarterback's touchdown pass is a receiver's touchdown), so total variance is far higher than the sum of marginals suggests. Ranking and leader contracts are order statistics over a whole pool with correlated members, and 'any game' contracts are maxima over a season; the settlement defers to Sleeper's own numbers and group definitions. One series (game-most fantasy points) is scored on ESPN's PPR settings and asks for the top scorer among all players of a single game.

stages.name: Participation: active status, snaps and the zero atom
stages.description: The player must be active and on the field; inactive or non-playing players are scored zero by contract. Snap share and role caps (a returning player, a rotational receiver) determine whether he gets opportunities. This stage produces an atom at zero (5-15 percent of player-weeks for those with injury designations) and a ramp.
stages.distribution: Zero-inflated: atom at 0 for inactive, ramp for limited players, near-constant for healthy starters.

stages.name: Opportunity volume: targets, carries, dropbacks
stages.description: Team plays and pass rate generate the pool of dropbacks and rushes, and the player's role determines his share; script moves volume toward passing or running by state. Opportunities are strongly overdispersed and are the most predictable part of fantasy points. Quarterbacks enter the pools of KXNFLFFH2HSEASON, position leaders and weekly leaders: their points come from dropbacks (nfl.proe, nfl.pace, nfl.script), starter status (nfl.qb) and rushing yards and touchdowns (nfl.qb_rushing), scored at 0.04 per passing yard, 4 per passing touchdown and the full rushing value. The catalog measurement values the starter-minus-backup gap from market line moves; that component is a benchmark only and is replaced here by an own valuation (starter versus backup EPA per dropback from nfl.qb_efficiency, or nfl.qb_scenario_rating_drop for team ratings).
stages.distribution: Counts with negative-binomial dispersion; team volume ~ plays 60-70, pass rate 55-60 percent.

stages.name: Yardage and reception yield
stages.description: Receptions earn one point irrespective of yards, so PPR rewards high-volume short-area roles, while yards add a tenth of a point per yard. The yield per opportunity depends on depth, efficiency and matchup, and the PPR reception point makes catch counts, not yards, the stable core of the score for slot receivers and backs. For quarterbacks the yield term is nfl.qb_efficiency (passing yards and touchdown rate per dropback); for skill players it is per-target and per-carry yield, each adjusted for the opponent's pass and run defence.
stages.distribution: Receptions binomial in targets; yards compound; receptions and yards are positively correlated within a player-game.

stages.name: Touchdown scoring: goal-line opportunity and luck
stages.description: Touchdowns are six points each, so one touchdown can equal 60 yards, and they come from goal-line and red-zone usage with a Poisson-like process whose variance dominates fantasy score variance. The expected rate is determined by play-level opportunity location; realised touchdowns are partly luck and regress.
stages.distribution: Poisson-like with mean 0.3-0.8 per game for starters; each touchdown a six-point jump (passing: four points for the quarterback, six for the receiver).

stages.name: Negative events and kicker special case
stages.description: Interceptions, lost fumbles and kicker misses subtract points; quarterbacks carry most of the downside, and kickers' scores are driven by the number of field-goal and extra-point opportunities, which depend on team drives and red-zone stalls. Kicker and D/ST weights are listed in the full KXNFLFFPTS rules text (read from the live Kalshi market on 2026-11-08; the stored sample is truncated before them) and are composed in stage s11. Kicker points follow field-goal and extra-point opportunities set by drive count (nfl.drives), red-zone stall rate (nfl.redzone) and the kicker's distance-specific accuracy (nfl.kicker); interceptions and lost fumbles use nfl.int_rate and nfl.fumble_luck. The ladder and per-game ticker KXNFLFFPTS includes kickers, whereas the Weeks 15-17 leader market excludes kickers, defence/special teams and IDP.
stages.distribution: Low-count events with small penalties; kicker points are discrete sums of 3-5 point field goals and 1 point extra points.

stages.name: Aggregation: component covariance and team stacks
stages.description: The score is the sum of components that move together: a touchdown pass is four points for the quarterback and six for the receiver, shootouts raise every player in the game, and teammates compete for the same carries and targets. This covariance determines the variance of the total, the joint distribution for H2H comparisons and top-N ranks.
stages.distribution: Variance of the score is the sum over components and covariances; positive within a pass-catching stack, negative among backs in the same room.

stages.name: Order statistics: season highs, weekly leaders and position ranks
stages.description: A season-high market is the maximum of the player's remaining single-game scores; a weekly leader is the maximum over the whole position pool; a season leader is a cumulative maximum. Each needs the right tail of the per-game distribution and the field beyond the listed players.
stages.distribution: Heavy right tail; maximum of N draws grows with log N; weekly leader of 100+ WRs has expected maximum around 30 points (assumption).

stages.name: Settlement: Sleeper scoring, group definitions and timing
stages.description: Contracts settle on Sleeper's published points at expiration; group membership (WR versus RB, rookie status) is determined by Sleeper, and corrections after expiration are ignored. Differences between Sleeper's settings and other fantasy platforms change the score. KXNFLFANTASYMOST is the exception: it settles on ESPN's PPR scoring, whose default settings differ from Sleeper's in kicker and bonus details, so the same stat line can score differently.
stages.distribution: Deterministic mapping from official stats to Sleeper points; settlement risk comes from classification and correction timing.

stages.name: Season accrual for season-total, season H2H and season-leader fantasy contracts
stages.description: KXNFLFFSEASONTOTAL, KXNFLFFH2HSEASON, KXNFLFFLEADER and KXNFLFFLEADERTOP settle on regular-season full-PPR sums, so banked Sleeper points to date are fixed and only the remaining games are random: their number per player (byes, injury absences, late rest of clinched starters), the role regime that can change after a teammate's injury or a trade, and the per-game point distribution from stages s1-s6. The Weeks 15-17 leader is a three-game sum inside that horizon.
stages.distribution: Banked total plus a sum over a random number of remaining games with persistent role state; heavy left tail from lost games and a long right tail for touchdown-heavy players.

stages.name: Game-most fantasy points across both rosters (ESPN scoring)
stages.description: KXNFLFANTASYMOST pays the player with the most ESPN-PPR fantasy points in one game. The candidate set is every player on both teams, so the probability is a single-game maximum over roughly 10-14 relevant scorers with strong positive dependence inside each offence (a passing touchdown scores for the quarterback and the receiver) and negative dependence between teams through script. Quarterbacks win most often because passing yards, four-point passing touchdowns and rushing add up, but a receiver or back with two touchdowns can overtake; a mobile quarterback's rushing floor raises his share. Scores must be computed under ESPN's default PPR settings rather than Sleeper's.
stages.distribution: Single-game order statistic over correlated player scores; win probabilities concentrated on the two quarterbacks (often 50-70 percent combined) with a long tail of skill players, plus a small 1/N tie atom.

stages.name: Kicker and team D/ST fantasy scores (Sleeper default tables)
stages.description: KXNFLFFPTS lists kicker markets (Will Reichard over 9.2) and team D/ST markets (for example Seattle Seahawks D/ST over 8.8) alongside skill players. Kicker points are a distance-tiered count of field goals (3/4/5/6 points by 0-39, 40-49, 50-59, 60+ yards) plus extra points, minus one per miss, so they come from drive stalls inside range, the coach's kick-or-go choice and the kicker's make curve, and fall when the offence converts red-zone trips into touchdowns. D/ST points are sacks, takeaways, safeties, blocks and return touchdowns plus a points-allowed step from +10 at a shutout to -4 at 35 or more, so they depend on the opponent offence, its quarterback and the score script that forces it to pass.
stages.distribution: Kicker: discrete, lumpy pmf on small integers with mean near 8 and an atom at zero if inactive; D/ST: right-skewed sum of rare events plus a step function, support roughly -4 to 30

talent_strength.note: Component model with efficiency; player skill priors by component are not defined in this archetype's inputs.

opponent_matchup.note: Opponent pass and run defence, position yield and coverage shell enter the per-target and per-carry yield (stage s3); how much opponent defence adds beyond role and script is unmeasured (u3).

role_personnel.note: Opportunity shares by role and zone. Quarterback starter status and rushing role are attached for the QB-inclusive pools (season H2H, position and weekly leaders).

availability_news.note: Active status and games played; the zero atom is explicit in the contract.

coaching_scheme.note: Play-caller tendencies enter through pass rate and tempo in the volume inputs; no separate coaching input is needed beyond those, and the contracts do not depend on in-game coaching decisions directly.

environment.note: Single-game tickers (KXNFLFFPTS, KXNFLFFPTSLADDER, weekly leader markets, any-game highs) are single games sensitive to wind, cold and roof, which cut passing and kicking and raise run share; weather and venue are attached in stage s3 with a weather dataset. Season-total and ranking tickers average these out.

game_context_script.note: Game state shifts volume between passing and rushing; the shootout correlation is handled through the covariance input.

pace_volume.note: Team plays and pass rate.

efficiency_conversion.note: Yield and touchdown conversion by opportunity.

distribution_variance.note: Components covary and the tail matters for highs and ranks.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Seeding stakes and starter rest (nfl.motivation_seeding) and rest and short-week effects (nfl.rest_travel) are attached for the Weeks 15-17 and any-game tickers; the field grid handles byes. The season ladders themselves are mapped out in series_mapping_issues.

officiating_rules.note: Penalties cancel individual plays and can shave a few points, but crews do not generate a stable per-player effect distinct from role and efficiency in a fantasy score.

contract_review.settlement_definition: Eleven of the twelve live series settle on Sleeper's full-PPR fantasy points (KXNFLFFPTS: 'Sleeper's default full-PPR scoring', 'no additional rounding', corrections after expiration not considered; the KXNFLFFPTSLADDER text says 'standard Points Per Reception (PPR)', a wording variant to confirm). Per-game tickers (KXNFLFFPTS) refer to the 'Full game (including overtime)' and a player who does not play or has no Sleeper value scores 0; the weekly leader and top-5 texts include overtime and rank all players in the group with membership fixed by Sleeper at expiration, non-players scoring 0; KXNFLFFH2HSEASON treats a non-player as 0 and pays 50 percent on a tie; any-game highs (KXNFLFFPLAYERHIGH, KXNFLFFHIGHSCORE) use any single regular-season game; top-N ranks pay 1/N at the cutoff tie; KXNFLFFPLAYOFFLEADER sums Weeks 15-17 and excludes defence/special teams, kickers and IDP. The exception is KXNFLFANTASYMOST (most fantasy points in one game, sampled for the Feb 8, 2026 Seattle vs New England game), which uses 'ESPN's FFL Points Per Reception (PPR) scoring', counts only points scored during that game and pays 1/N among tied players; its primary sentence says 'during the full game' but no sentence defines overtime or treats non-participants. Which of these sentences apply to which series is as sampled, not generalised across all twelve. The final series assignment keeps all twelve series here, including the season total, season H2H, position leader, top-N, weekly leader and Weeks 15-17 leader, so season accrual (stage s9) is part of this record.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Sleeper's published fantasy points (default full-PPR) at expiration, with Sleeper determining player group membership, for eleven series; ESPN's FFL PPR scoring for KXNFLFANTASYMOST. Official game stats feed both platforms; Sleeper corrections after expiration are ignored, while ESPN correction timing is not stated.
variants_and_edge_cases: Per-game over thresholds with non-integer strikes (9.2 for a kicker, 34 and 49 'at least' for any-game highs) mix player types: the full KXNFLFFPTS text (read from the live market, the stored sample is truncated) lists the Sleeper kicker table (FG 0-39 +3, 40-49 +4, 50-59 +5, 60+ +6, XP +1, misses -1) and a D/ST table with points-allowed tiers from +10 to -4.

Season-high contracts (KXNFLFFPLAYERHIGH, KXNFLFFHIGHSCORE for rookies) are the maximum of up to 17 single-game scores, and rookie pools combine many players, so they depend on the upper tail of each game's distribution and on availability.

Weekly and positional leader markets (KXNFLFFWEEKLEAD, KXNFLFFWEEKTOP, KXNFLFFLEADER, KXNFLFFLEADERTOP, KXNFLFFPLAYOFFLEADER) rank all players in the group using Sleeper's group membership at expiration; the Weeks 15-17 market sums three games and excludes defence, kickers and IDP.
Season ladders and totals use regular-season games only; the per-game ladder is capped at $1.00 for 100 points, which is rarely binding, and rounding half-up is explicit.

Sleeper's fantasy values are published for the 'full game (including overtime)' and corrections after expiry are ignored, so a late stat correction does not change the settlement even if the league changes the official stat.

The Weeks 15-17 leader market excludes kickers, defence/special teams and IDP, whereas the per-game KXNFLFFPTS ticker includes kickers (sample: Will Reichard above 9.2); overtime and post-expiration-correction sentences appear only in some series' sampled text, not all eleven.

KXNFLFANTASYMOST is the only series on ESPN PPR scoring and the only single-game order statistic: the winner is the top scorer among all players of both teams in one game (typically a quarterback, given 4-point passing touchdowns plus rushing), and its text says 'full game' without an explicit overtime or non-participant clause.

extreme_play_length.label: Longest/shortest play, touchdown and field-goal extremes
contract_types: Player longest reception in a game (over strike)
extreme_play_length.target: Probability that the maximum (or minimum) play length of a type over a window (regular season, one game, or one player's receptions in one game) exceeds, falls below or lands in a yardage band.
extreme_play_length.mechanism: Extremes of play length are order statistics of a count of eligible plays. Season contracts thin a large count of opportunities (own-1 snaps or, under a return-inclusive reading, long turnover returns for a 99-yard play; end-of-half 65+ yard attempts for a 70+ field goal) through a tail conversion, with the running maximum to date as an absorbing state. Single-game TD-length buckets are the max or min over a random number of touchdowns (zero TDs resolves NO) whose length depends on route (goal-line run, explosive pass, return). The player longest-reception contract is the max over a random number of catches, with a fair-price settlement when the player is active but takes no live snap.

inputs.why: Baseline attempt and make model for 50+ and 60+ yard kicks by kicker, venue and weather; the starting point for the 70+ field goal factor.
The 70+ field goal contract needs a leg-ceiling estimate beyond observed makes; this is the make-probability factor of the expected count of 70+ makes.
The attempt-count factor for the 70+ field goal contract: with no attempts at 68+ yards the longest-FG market cannot move, so this isolates the decision stage from leg strength.
Exposure count for the offensive route to a 99+ yard scrimmage play; it bounds YES only under the offence-only reading, since turnover returns on scrimmage downs may also count.
Turns the exposure count into a probability of the one outcome the 99+ yard contract settles on; the tail extrapolation is the main uncertainty.
Provides the statistical backbone for both threshold contracts and the sanity check on the exposure-times-conversion decomposition.
Needed to price KXNFLLONGESTTD and KXNFLSHORTESTTD readings under return-inclusive and scrimmage-only definitions.
Accuracy by distance and career long make; kickoff depth is only usable as a leg proxy within one kickoff-rule era because 2024+ kickoffs are strategic.
Team and opponent rate of 40+ yard completions indicates how often deep shots from backed-up positions connect.
Per-carry explosive tail by rusher bounds how often a handoff from the own 1 can run the full field.
Yards-after-catch and air-yard split for receivers shows who can turn a short catch into a 99-yard score.
Duplicates the own-1 snap exposure for the 99-yard play; kept only as a coarser cross-check of backed-up snap counts.
Altitude and roof change effective kick distance (Denver adds range; domes remove wind), shifting 70+ make odds.
Wind speed and direction at kickoff vintages decide whether a 66-70 yard attempt is reachable.
Go-for-it versus kick policy by coach shapes how many long attempts are taken before the half-ending situation.
Holding and other flags nullify long plays under the rules text, converting a would-be 99-yard TD into no event.
Running maximum to date and games left are an absorbing state: one qualifying event settles the season contracts, so this is a primary as-of input.
Kicker and quarterback availability changes the count of eligible long attempts over the remaining games.
Source agencies, regular-season scope and nullified-play exclusion define what counts for each strike.
Official settled value and timestamp for the max kick and max play, used to verify the record.
Official stat corrections to kick distance or yardage can flip a threshold market at the margin.
Under the return-inclusive reading of 'play from scrimmage', 99+ yard interception, fumble and missed or blocked FG returns are a second, more frequent route to YES.
Rule changes (2025 kicking-ball preparation, fair-catch free kick, kickoff regime) shift the 60+ and 70+ yard attempt and make rates, so tail fits need an era term.
Preseason and warm-up long makes are out of settlement scope but are the only direct evidence that a kicker can reach 70 yards.
Max and min of the touchdown lengths in one game settle KXNFLLONGESTTD and KXNFLSHORTESTTD buckets, including the zero-TD NO mass.
KXNFLLONGREC settles on a player's single longest catch in a game, the max over a random number of receptions.
Era flag for kickoff and touchback rules; needed to decide whether kickoff depth measures leg power and to pool return-TD lengths.
Market-free expected touchdowns per team sets how many TD lengths enter the single-game max/min and the zero-TD probability.
Red-zone and goal-to-go TD conversion sets the share of short touchdowns that drive the shortest-TD bucket.
Goal-line package (sneak, short run, play action) determines whether short TDs are 1-2 yards or 3-10 yards.
Defensive and special-teams TDs are long (return) or zero-yard (recovery in the end zone) and fatten both tails of single-game TD length.
Target count forecast is the volume over which the longest reception is a maximum.
Depth of target sets how far a typical catch travels before YAC; deep-target share drives the upper tail.
Catch rate converts targets to receptions, and YAC over expected sets how often a short catch becomes long.
Active-but-no-live-play settles KXNFLLONGREC at the pre-game fair price, so its probability changes the effective payoff mixture.
Game-day inactive list fixes whether the named receiver is active; the inactive case is not stated in the sampled text.
Shadow corner and coverage shell against the named receiver shift his reception-length distribution in that game.

interactions.hypothesis: Expected 70+ makes equal attempts times make probability, so a strong-legged kicker on a coach who never attempts contributes almost nothing.

Altitude plus a strong tailwind adds several effective yards, converting a 66-yard ceiling kicker into a 70-yard threat only in that combined outdoor regime; domes remove wind but give no altitude help.
The 99-yard play probability is the product of the rare exposure count and a tiny conversion, so a rate uncertainty compounds multiplicatively.
More touchdowns raise P(max >= 51) and push the minimum toward 1-2 yards, so the TD count shifts both buckets in opposite directions.

Expected number of 70+ makes is attempts at that range times make probability, so either factor near zero keeps the sum near zero; a strong-legged kicker on a coach who prefers a Hail Mary adds almost nothing, and a coach willing to try with a kicker below range adds only misses.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute expected 70+ makes per team as the product of the two factors and compare with a model that sums them; check that the product model ranks past 64+ yard attempts better.

interactions.hypothesis: Altitude (thinner air) plus a strong following wind adds several effective yards; a kicker with a 66-yard ceiling reaches 70 only when both help, which happens only outdoors in a few venues and weeks. Domes remove wind entirely, so indoor kicks get neither the tailwind gain nor the altitude gain except in a high-altitude dome.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate make probability at 62+ yards with a venue-by-wind interaction term and test the slope above 15 mph tailwind versus roof or sea-level venues.

interactions.hypothesis: The 99-yard play is Poisson thinning: exposure count times conversion; uncertainty in the count and the tail compounds, and snaps cluster by team and week, so the joint distribution is wider than independent factors imply.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate remaining games with a negative binomial exposure and a Beta conversion, and compare predictive intervals with a product-of-point-estimates calculation on historical seasons.

interactions.hypothesis: Long plays from deep starts carry a high chance of a holding flag or a rarer illegal block, which the rules exclude; the nullification share is conditional on play length and the offence's penalty profile, so it lowers the conversion more for teams that hold often.
interactions.how_to_test: From historical 50+ yard gains, estimate the nullification rate by length bucket and team penalty rate, then test whether it rises with yards gained.

interactions.hypothesis: Once games are played without an event, remaining exposure shrinks, so the probability of YES decays toward zero in the last weeks, while any past event resolves it; the response of P(YES) to games left is exponential not linear.
interactions.how_to_test: Backtest the hazard decay on prior seasons conditioned on no event before week N, comparing a constant-rate model with the thinned count.

interactions.hypothesis: The TD count moves the longest-TD and shortest-TD buckets in opposite directions at once: a high-scoring game raises P(max >= 51) and lowers the minimum toward 1-2 yards, while a one-TD game sets max = min. Buckets across the two series are therefore correlated through N.
interactions.how_to_test: On 2015+ games, compare observed P(max >= 51) and P(min in 6-10) by realised TD count with the order-statistic model, and test the correlation of the two bucket outcomes.

interactions.hypothesis: The probability that the longest catch beats the strike is 1 - F^K, which rises steeply from zero to three catches and flattens after; an extra target matters a lot for a low-volume tight end and little for a high-volume WR1.
interactions.how_to_test: Bin player-games by receptions and plot the observed rate of longest reception above 16.5 yards; fit 1 - F^K against a linear-in-targets model.

interactions.hypothesis: Under the offence-only reading the 99-yard probability is driven by own-1 snaps alone; under the return-inclusive reading long turnover returns dominate. The contract interpretation switches which exposure matters, so the price of the series depends on u5.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute season P(YES) under each reading from 1999-2025 history and report both; check past Kalshi settlements or rule clarifications for any return-yard event.

nonlinearities.shape: Steep logistic collapse of make probability beyond about 63-65 yards
nonlinearities.why: Make probability falls from near 40 percent at 60 yards to a small tail past 66, so a few yards of kicker or wind help changes the 70+ probability by multiples, not by an additive amount.

nonlinearities.shape: Threshold with saturation in tailwind speed; zero effect in domes
nonlinearities.why: Wind adds distance only after it exceeds roughly 10-15 mph and its effect is capped by the kick trajectory; roof games get zero tailwind benefit, so the response is piecewise, not linear.

nonlinearities.shape: Saturating exponent: P(at least one) = 1 - exp(-rate x games)
nonlinearities.why: The contract settles on at least one event, so the probability saturates as the expected count grows and is nearly linear only when the count is small.

nonlinearities.shape: Point mass at zero TDs plus order-statistic tails that sharpen with N
nonlinearities.why: P(max >= 51) grows roughly like 1 - (1 - p)^N and P(min in 6-10) falls as N grows, with all buckets NO at N = 0, so bucket probabilities are not linear in expected points.

nonlinearities.shape: Concave saturation in receptions K: 1 - F(s)^K
nonlinearities.why: Each extra catch adds less to P(longest > strike); with zero catches the probability is exactly zero, so the response to target volume is steep at low volume and flat at high volume.

mechanism_review.summary: Three windows share one idea: the outcome is an order statistic over a random count of plays. Season contracts: a 99-yard scrimmage play comes from snaps at the offence's own 1 (punts downed at the 1, goal-line stands, penalties) converted by a full-field breakaway, or, if Kalshi counts turnover returns on scrimmage downs, from 99-109 yard interception, fumble or missed-FG returns; a 70+ yard field goal comes from end-of-half or end-of-game spots where a coach prefers a kick to a Hail Mary, converted by a kicker whose ceiling (record 68 in the 2025 regular season) plus altitude or tailwind reaches 70, in a post-2025 rule era with higher long-kick rates. Running maximum and games left are an absorbing state. Single-game TD buckets are the max or min over the game's touchdowns, with a zero-TD NO mass and route mix (goal-line runs, explosive passes, returns). The player longest-reception contract is the max over a random number of catches, mixed with a fair-price settlement for active-no-play.

stages.name: Opportunity creation: snaps and situations eligible for an extreme
stages.description: The league produces eligible snaps for a 99-yard offensive play through field position (punts downed inside the 2, goal-line stands that turn the ball over at the 1, penalties walking an offence back) and, under a return-inclusive reading, through opponent red-zone and goal-line snaps that can end in a pick or fumble returned the length of the field. For kicks, eligible situations are 0-6 second end-of-half and end-of-game moments within about 68-75 yards of the goal line. Counts are small, clustered in a few team-games and not created by player skill.
stages.distribution: Overdispersed counts, negative binomial per team-game; heavy clustering in a few games

stages.name: Decision: attempt a long kick or call a deep shot
stages.description: Given an eligible situation the coach chooses a long field goal, Hail Mary, kneel or punt; from the own 1 he chooses safe runs or play-action shots. Coach tendency, the kicker's demonstrated range, timeouts and low-leverage record-chasing (end of first half with the score not at stake, indoors) determine the long-kick attempt; QB deep-ball rate and scheme decide whether a deep shot is called from the 1.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli per situation with strong coach heterogeneity; near zero for most coaches

stages.name: Execution tail: breakaway or kick that reaches the threshold
stages.description: A 99-yard play needs an unblocked deep route, a missed deep safety or an untouched run from a compressed field. A 70+ yard make needs ball speed and carry beyond the 68-yard regular-season record, helped by altitude, roof or tailwind, and by the post-2025 kicking-ball preparation rule era. The make curve is a steep logistic tail with very few regular-season points, so preseason long makes and era terms are needed and parameter uncertainty dominates the point estimate.
stages.distribution: Extreme-value tail with parameter uncertainty; orders of magnitude below bulk rates

stages.name: Nullification and aggregation over the remaining schedule
stages.description: A qualifying play or kick survives only if not erased by penalty (offensive holding on a long TD, a kick negated by a roughing flag then re-kicked) and then enters the league-wide maximum. Aggregation takes the running maximum to date, the count of remaining games and rest-of-season availability of kicker and QB, giving a Poisson-thinning probability of at least one qualifying event.
stages.distribution: Poisson-type with rate times remaining games; saturating in games left

stages.name: Settlement and record verification
stages.description: Settlement uses official recorded stats and the exact distance convention for kicks; the longest/shortest-TD buckets still depend on how return and 0-yard recovery TDs are recorded (u1) and the 99-yard play on return inclusion (u5). Stat corrections and source lag can alter the recorded length, and the market resolves from the record at season end.
stages.distribution: Deterministic given the record; residual risk from corrections and ambiguity

stages.name: Single-game touchdown count and length mix (longest/shortest TD buckets)
stages.description: For KXNFLLONGESTTD and KXNFLSHORTESTTD the game produces N touchdowns (both teams, overtime included per official play-by-play), N drawn from each side's drives times TD-per-drive. Each TD length depends on route: goal-line runs and sneaks (1-2 yards), red-zone passes (3-20), explosive scrimmage plays (20-99) and return or recovery TDs (0 to 109). The longest-TD bucket is the max and the shortest-TD bucket the min of these lengths; zero TDs resolves all buckets NO, and more TDs push the max up and the min down at the same time.
stages.distribution: Order statistics of a Poisson-mixture count of TD lengths; point mass at N=0; integer yards with heavy mass at 1-2 and a long right tail

stages.name: Player single-game longest reception (KXNFLLONGREC)
stages.description: The named receiver first must be active and take a live snap (active-no-play settles at the pre-game fair price; inactive handling is unstated). Given he plays, his targets in the game, catch probability per target and the yards of each catch (air yards plus YAC, against the coverage he draws) produce K receptions; the contract settles on the largest. Zero catches is a NO on an over strike, so low-volume tight ends carry a large zero mass, and one busted coverage decides the outcome regardless of total yards.
stages.distribution: Max of K i.i.d.-ish reception lengths with K overdispersed (negative binomial targets times catch rate); zero-catch mass; right-skewed length per catch
