contract_review.settlement_definition: Five live series, all with sampled rules. KXNFLLONGESTFG (floor 70, greater_or_equal): YES if the longest made field goal of the 2026-27 regular season is 70+ yards. KXNFLLONGESTPLAY (floor 99): YES if any play from scrimmage in the 2026-27 regular season is at least 99 yards on officially recorded Source Agency stats, penalty-nullified plays excluded; whether turnover returns on scrimmage downs count is not stated. KXNFLLONGESTTD and KXNFLSHORTESTTD are per-game bucket markets (sample: Seattle vs New England, 8 Feb 2026; buckets such as 51+ and 6-10 yards, inclusive bounds) on official play-by-play TD distances; if no touchdown is scored all buckets resolve NO. KXNFLLONGREC (sample strike over 16.5, Buffalo vs Minnesota, 9 Nov 2026): YES if the named player's longest reception in the game exceeds the strike; active but no live play settles at the pre-game fair market price; one live play, even nullified, makes it settle on the recorded longest reception.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Officially recorded stats of the Source Agencies (league play-by-play and gamebook); Kalshi names the league as Governing League. Post-game stat corrections are not described in the sampled rules.
variants_and_edge_cases: KXNFLLONGESTPLAY is titled 'NFL Longest Touchdown' while the rules say any play from scrimmage of 99+ yards; under the offence-only reading it needs a snap from the own 1, under a return-inclusive reading 99-109 yard interception, fumble or missed-FG returns also qualify (u5).
KXNFLLONGESTFG counts only made kicks; the distance convention and whether a fair-catch free kick (scored as a field goal) is included are not stated (u2).

KXNFLLONGESTTD and KXNFLSHORTESTTD are single-game bucket ladders with inclusive bounds; a zero-TD game resolves every bucket NO, and zero-yard TDs (fumble recovered in the end zone) can set the minimum. The sample is a Super Bowl; regular-season listings are assumed to share the wording.
KXNFLLONGREC is a per-game player prop with an over-strike (16.5 in the sample); active-but-no-live-play settles at the pre-game fair price, while the inactive case is not described (u6).
Season contracts are regular season only and partly decided at any as-of date by the running maximum to date; one qualifying event ends the market.

nfl_draft_selection.label: NFL Draft and Supplemental Draft selection markets
contract_types: Draft pick slot (1st overall, exact selection, team making a pick)
Team draft by position or round (incl. position of team's first pick)
Draft comparison and matchup (prospect vs prospect, school with most picks)
School draftee count over the whole draft
nfl_draft_selection.target: Probability a named prospect is selected at a slot, range or positional order, or a team makes/uses a given pick, per the official Draft results.
nfl_draft_selection.mechanism: Draft outcomes come from a deterministic order process (season results, tiebreakers, compensatory awards and trades decide who holds each of about 257 slots over seven rounds) combined with team decisions among prospects: each team picks from a board shaped by consensus value, positional need, quarterback regime and decision-maker habits, subject to the prospect being eligible, declaring and passing medicals. Trades break the order; positional order statistics, school counts and team-round outcomes are correlated across prospects, so a joint all-rounds simulation is required.

inputs.why: Consensus rankings, draft order and team needs are the baseline of every draft selection contract.
Race for the worst record and strength-of-schedule tiebreak decides who holds the first pick and the order of the top slots.
QB-class order, team need and trade-up model feed quarterback-order contracts.
Maps results to round-one slots (KXNFLDRAFTSELECT's 32nd pick, KXNFLDRAFT1ST's 1st pick); later-round order comes from the full-order input.
Resolves the team-level contract rule that a traded pick resolves to the team that actually selects, and drives pick-slot markets for named prospects.
Converts a ranking into the probabilities that top-5, exact-slot, over/under and Nth-at-position contracts actually settle on.
Drives which position a pick holder drafts: the main team-side term in position-drafted, team-draft-by-position and QB-order contracts.
Every named-prospect contract carries the pre-condition that the player is in the pool; the hurdle is largest in the months before the declaration deadline.
The position and trade behavior of the picking team is the part that a consensus ranking cannot supply.
Settlement of the QB-order and position-drafted series depends on which source's label counts for hybrid players.
Needed for KXNFLSDRAFTTOP, a separate mechanism from the April draft that no consensus board models.
Season simulation distribution supplies the uncertainty in final standings that sets slots and the 31st and 32nd picks.
Tiebreaker resolution (strength of schedule, then division and conference tiebreaks) among tied records, which the order rules need and the win-count simulation does not provide.
Timestamped reporting about team intentions, prospect visits and medical updates moves the pick distribution.
Cap room and contract guarantees decide whether a team can afford a rookie slot or a veteran QB.
Roster turnover and returning production indicate positional holes and need.
A coaching or GM change resets draft philosophy and quarterback need.
Draft-capital prior for unproven quarterbacks measures how a team views an incumbent against a rookie.
Draft-week and draft-night insider reports are the main late information for exact-slot and team markets that stay open into the draft; their hit rate by outlet sets the weight.
Calendar of the combine, declaration deadline and draft night structures when information arrives.
Reference-class frequency for rare procedural events (a Supplemental Draft being held, a draft postponed), used only where no draft-specific history exists.
Wording on traded picks, positions and which draft counts defines settlement for each series.
Markets close at the draft; knowing the timing avoids look-ahead and sets valid information cutoffs.
Official draft results and position labels used to verify settlement.
Seven-round order with compensatory picks fixes the last pick (KXNFLLASTPICKPOS), round-3 boundaries (KXNFLDRAFTTEAMPOS, KXNFLDRAFTCOMPARE) and pick 64 (KXNFLDRAFTOU).
League eligibility clock, NCAA eligibility rulings and NIL-era return incentives gate whether named prospects are in the pool at all.
Per-school pool of draft-eligible prospects with projected rounds drives KXNFLDRAFTCAT counts and the KXNFLDRAFTCOMPARE school argmax.

interactions.hypothesis: A team with a high quarterback need but a later pick trades up, so need raises the quarterback's slot only if the holder will move.
The gap between the top two quarterbacks and the class depth set the order and the quarterback premium over consensus.
The slot distribution is the season simulation passed through the order rules, so the 32nd pick is a Super Bowl winner distribution, not a record ranking.
A school's count of picks is a sum of correlated per-prospect draft events; slot dispersion around round boundaries decides counts in rounds 1-3.

A quarterback-needy team that holds a later pick trades up only when the gap to the top quarterback is large and it holds enough assets, so need raises a quarterback's expected slot only through the trade graph; with a top-3 pick and no quarterback the effect is direct.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare realized quarterback slots in drafts split by need of the top-5 holders and by presence of a trade-up; test the need effect with and without a trade indicator.

interactions.hypothesis: Quarterbacks are drafted earlier than consensus rank and the order among them is correlated: if the first quarterback goes first overall the remaining quarterbacks' slots shift together, so the 3rd-quarterback contract is an order statistic of dependent slots.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate the class with and without a position premium and rank-order correlation and compare with realized orders of quarterbacks in 2010-2026 drafts.

interactions.hypothesis: The 32nd pick is the Super Bowl winner and the 1st pick the worst record, so the slot distribution is the extremes of a simulated season: tails dominate and teams that look similar by rating have very different probabilities of the end slots.
interactions.how_to_test: Run the season simulation through the rules engine and compare predicted end-slot distributions with historical pre-playoff projections.

interactions.hypothesis: Prospects projected in round one declare almost surely, so declaration risk is a threshold in projected round; below the threshold return-to-school and medical flags dominate and the slot distribution is a mixture with a mass at undrafted.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit P(declare) against consensus rank at the declaration deadline and test for a step near the first-round boundary.

interactions.hypothesis: Team need only converts to a pick when the decision-maker's habit permits it: a GM who rarely reaches ignores need for the best player, while a reach-prone GM acts on need, so the two multiply rather than add.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress the position drafted on need by GM reach propensity and test the interaction coefficient.

interactions.hypothesis: A school's count of picks in rounds 1-3 sums dependent per-player events: a deep positional class at one school competes for the same team needs, and boundary prospects near pick 100 swing the argmax, so counts are overdispersed and ties at the top are frequent.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare simulated rounds 1-3 school counts and tie rates against 2010-2026 drafts with and without a shared school-class shock.

interactions.hypothesis: Declaration choice only matters once the eligibility clock is satisfied and no extra NCAA season is granted; in the NIL era a top underclass QB with remaining eligibility may return, so the declare probability is conditional on eligibility state and position.
interactions.how_to_test: Split post-2021 early-entry decisions by eligibility state and position and compare declare rates with the pre-2021 base rate.

nonlinearities.shape: Dispersion widens roughly linearly with consensus rank and is right-skewed for positions with a premium
nonlinearities.why: The standard deviation of realized pick around consensus is small for the top prospects and large later, so probabilities for top-5 and exact-slot events fall sharply with the rank, unlike over/under events near the middle.

nonlinearities.shape: Logistic step: quarterback selection probability jumps once need exceeds a no-franchise-QB threshold
nonlinearities.why: A holder with a franchise QB almost never takes one in round one while a holder without one near the top does with high probability, so the response is a step, not a linear need effect.

nonlinearities.shape: Trade probability rises convexly with the consensus gap between the first and second prospects at a slot
nonlinearities.why: When one prospect is clearly above the rest, buyers pay to move; when prospects are equal, the pick holder keeps the slot, so trade risk is convex in the gap.

nonlinearities.shape: Threshold count with tie-prone argmax
nonlinearities.why: P(count >= N) collapses once N exceeds the number of realistic draftees, and the rounds 1-3 argmax pays 1/N on ties, so the payoff is a step function of small integer counts.

mechanism_review.summary: A draft selection outcome is generated by a chain: eligibility rules and declaration decisions fix the pool; season results, tiebreakers and compensatory awards fix the seven-round order; trades reassign who holds slots; and each pick-holder chooses from a board mixing consensus value, positional need, quarterback regime and decision-maker habits. Ordinal contracts (3rd quarterback, top five, before pick 64), school counts and team-round outcomes are functions of correlated choices, so one team's decision at pick 2 changes every later probability. Consensus rank gives the centre of each prospect's slot distribution, but position premiums, trades and thin late-round boards give skewed, heavy-tailed errors, so the unit of analysis is a joint simulation of all rounds.

stages.name: Eligibility and gating: who is in the pool
stages.description: A prospect must be league-eligible (three seasons removed from high school), still have or have exhausted NCAA eligibility as courts and waivers decide, choose to declare rather than return under NIL and revenue-sharing pay, and clear medical and character checks. In November declaration is months away and these gates dominate named-prospect contracts for underclass quarterbacks; for the Supplemental Draft eligibility is a league ruling on a petition, and the draft itself may not be held.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli per prospect with a strong prior by projected round; late shocks from injury

stages.name: Order formation: standings and tiebreakers to slots
stages.description: Final standings and playoff results are mapped to round-one slots (worst record first with strength-of-schedule tiebreak, playoff teams by round exited, Super Bowl loser 31 and winner 32) and repeated each round, with compensatory picks (announced in March) appended to rounds 3-7. The order is unknown in November, so each slot is a distribution from a season simulation, and forfeitures or compensatory awards shift overall numbering and the identity of the final pick.
stages.distribution: Discrete slot distribution with fat tails for playoff teams; exact once the season ends

stages.name: Team choice: boards, need, quarterback regime and decision-maker habits
stages.description: Each pick-holder selects from its board. Consensus value sets the initial ordering, positional need and the quarterback regime tilt choices (a holder with no franchise QB near the top of the class faces strong pressure), and GM and coach habits determine reach tendency, trade-down frequency and how positions like EDGE are valued.
stages.distribution: Categorical choice among a few candidates with team-specific heterogeneity

stages.name: Trades and reshuffling before and on draft night
stages.description: Teams trade up for a quarterback or a rare talent and trade down for assets; each trade changes the team that makes a given pick and the demand curve for later slots. Trade-up hazard depends on the consensus gap between the prospect and the next, the buyer's pick stock and need, and the seller's willingness, and it is partly reported by insiders ahead of time.
stages.distribution: Rare but high-impact jumps; conditional on gap and need

stages.name: Realization, labelling and settlement
stages.description: Selections are announced on draft night and settle from the official record: slot, team, and the position label given by the league. Hybrid labels (edge versus linebacker) and Nth-at-position rules depend on that label; markets close at the draft, so information vintage must stop before the first selection.
stages.distribution: Deterministic after the draft; label disagreement risk at position boundaries

stages.name: School aggregates: draftee counts and the rounds 1-3 school argmax
stages.description: KXNFLDRAFTCAT counts one school's players over all seven rounds and KXNFLDRAFTCOMPARE asks which school has the most picks in rounds 1-3, with ties paid 1/N. A school's count is a sum of correlated per-prospect events: whether each senior and underclassman declares, whether he is drafted at all, and whether his slot falls before the round-3 boundary. Elite programs place 8-14 players, so the count is concentrated near a threshold and ties at the top are common.
stages.distribution: Poisson-binomial sum of dependent Bernoullis per school; discrete with frequent ties at the argmax; truncated by declarations

stages.name: Deep-round slots and team positional choices across rounds
stages.description: KXNFLLASTPICKPOS settles on the position of the final overall selection (a compensatory round-7 slot), KXNFLDRAFTTEAMPOS on whether a team takes a quarterback in rounds 1-3, and KXNFLTEAM1POS on the position of a team's first selection, which depends on whether it still owns its round-one pick. Late-round choices follow team need, special-teams value and positional scarcity rather than consensus boards, which thin out beyond about 150 prospects.
stages.distribution: Categorical position outcome with flat late-round priors; team-round events are Bernoulli conditional on pick inventory

talent_strength.note: Prospect quality as consensus value and team results that fix the order.

opponent_matchup.note: There is no opponent; the competition is the other pick holders in order, whose decisions are covered through team need, ownership and slot-dispersion inputs rather than a matchup variable.

role_personnel.note: Starter quality and depth by position and quarterback regime determine needs.

availability_news.note: Eligibility clock, NCAA eligibility rulings, NIL-era declaration choice, medicals and timestamped reports.

coaching_scheme.note: GM and coach habits and regime changes shape position valuation and trading.

environment.note: No venue, weather or surface exists in a selection meeting; draft-night location and crowd have no mechanism that moves who is selected.

game_context_script.note: The draft-night sequence (trades, clock, run on a position) plays the role of game flow.

pace_volume.note: Number of selections per round including compensatory picks and forfeits is the volume the counts and last-pick markets run over.

efficiency_conversion.note: Rate at which insider reports and consensus rank convert to the realized pick.

distribution_variance.note: Heavy-tailed slot errors, order-statistic dependence among prospects and tie-prone school counts.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Tanking incentives, late-season stakes and the calendar of deadlines.

officiating_rules.note: Draft-order and compensatory rules, the league eligibility rule and Supplemental Draft procedures play the rules role.

settlement_contract.note: Traded-pick rule, league position label and series with no rules.

contract_review.settlement_definition: Twenty-five live series, twenty-three with sampled rules (all but KXNFLDRAFTEAMPOS and KXNFLFIRSTPICK). Named-prospect slot series: KXNFLDRAFT1/KXNFLDRAFTPICK (selected 1st overall), KXNFLDRAFTTOP (drafted top 5), KXNFLDRAFTOU (drafted in the first 64 picks), KXNFLDRAFTMATCHUP (drafted first of two named players). Nth-at-position series (QB, RB, WR, TE, OL, DT, Edge, LB, DB) use the Governing League's position when sources differ. Team series: KXNFLDRAFT1ST and KXNFLDRAFTSELECT settle on the team that ultimately makes the 1st/32nd selection after trades; KXNFLDRAFTTEAM on the selecting team (undrafted = NO); KXNFLDRAFTTEAMPOS (QB in rounds 1-3) and KXNFLTEAM1POS (position of the team's first pick). Aggregates: KXNFLDRAFTCAT (at least N players of a school in the whole draft) and KXNFLDRAFTCOMPARE (school with most picks in rounds 1-3, ties paid 1/N) on the league's college classification; KXNFLLASTPICKPOS on the position of the last player selected. KXNFLSDRAFTTOP: named player selected at any point in the Supplemental Draft. KXNFLDRAFTEAMPOS and KXNFLFIRSTPICK have no listing.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official league draft results and position labels; Kalshi cites the Governing League and Source Agencies. Draft-night announcements are the primary record.
variants_and_edge_cases: KXNFLDRAFTEAMPOS and KXNFLFIRSTPICK have no listing or rules; by title they appear to duplicate KXNFLDRAFTTEAMPOS and KXNFLDRAFT1, but settlement wording is unverified.

Undrafted = NO is written only for KXNFLDRAFTTEAM; for exact-slot, top-5, over/under, matchup and Nth-at-position series the NO case for a non-declaring or undrafted player is inferred, and the matchup case where neither player is drafted is unstated (u7).
Position series use the league position at selection (DB = cornerback or safety; OL = tackle, guard or center; Edge separate from DT and LB), so hybrid labels shift the ordinal count.
KXNFLLASTPICKPOS and KXNFLDRAFTCAT depend on round 7 and compensatory picks; KXNFLDRAFTOU and KXNFLDRAFTCOMPARE on the round-2/round-3 boundaries, not only on round one.
The same prospect appears in a finalized 2026 first-pick market and in 2027 QB-order and top-5 markets, so pool membership can cross a draft year through eligibility decisions.
Draft postponement or cancellation, and a Supplemental Draft not being held, are not addressed in any sampled text (u8).

super_bowl_mvp.label: Super Bowl MVP and its position/defense/non-QB variants
super_bowl_mvp.target: Probability a player (or position group) is named Super Bowl MVP, given the game outcome and in-game performance.
super_bowl_mvp.mechanism: The award is a one-game vote that mostly goes to a member of the winning team, so P(player) is the product of the chance his team reaches and wins the final and the chance that, given a win, panel and fans credit him for the highlight lines the box score contains. Quarterbacks have a premium, but a non-QB or defender wins when the game script favours the run, defence or a scoring play; so the inputs are team-level path and matchup, game-level credit allocation and the voting mechanics, not a season stat total.

inputs.why: Sets the team-level probability that the winning side contains a given player, the first factor of every Super Bowl MVP variant.
Gives the second factor for each variant (overall, defensive, non-QB, position) once the winning team is fixed.
The effective primary prior for the position and non-QB contracts, which have about 60 historical outcomes and no season-stat process; the game-level model refines it.
Drives the defensive-player Super Bowl MVP variant, which is the only one of the four contracts decided mainly by defence.
Distribution of conference champions and finalists from the season simulation sets who reaches the game.
Seed, bye and path difficulty change the chance each team reaches the final.
Full-strength rating applies in the final because injured starters return or are lost across the two weeks.
Market-free opponent-adjusted rating feeds the matchup win probability.
Starting QB status is decisive: a backup or injured QB moves MVP mass from QB to other positions.
Vintaged injury reports before the game update candidate availability and team win probability.
Regressed QB efficiency gives the prior that the QB posts the highlight line.
Vote-share model maps in-game lines to selection probability; adapted to the panel.
Panel composition, timing and tie rules determine how credit becomes a winner.
Look-alike teammates split credit and lower each one's selection chance.
Single-game ceiling tails give the chance of outlier stat lines in the game that decide the vote.
Benchmark only: its team-total-based TD expectation is market-derived; the market-free TD mean is nfl.model_team_td_mean.
Game-script lattice indicates pass-heavy or run-heavy games and defensive control, shifting credit by unit.
Defensive and special-teams TD hazard sets the chance a defender or returner wins.
Pass-rush matchup quality raises the sack opportunity for edge defenders.
Neutral venue roof and surface affect passing versus running, a small shift in who posts the line.
Playoff overtime rule adds snaps and tail stat lines, boosting QB credit in extra-time games.
Narrative and injury reports in the two-week window affect candidacy and roles.
Award definition and the depth-chart position rule; text exists for KXNFLSBMVP and KXNFLSBMVPPOS only, not for the DEF and non-QB series.
Official MVP announcement and position classification verify settlement.
If markets trade during the game, the running box-score leader at ballot time (fan voting closes in the fourth quarter) is the dominant input.
KXNFLSBMVPPOS strikes settle on the depth-chart position(s) listed for the winner at game time, and one player can satisfy several strikes.
Close time relative to kickoff and the announcement decides whether the contract is pre-game or in-game, and sets valid information cutoffs.
League depth chart vintage at the time of the game supplies the position labels the position contract settles on.
Market-free expected touchdowns per finalist set how many scoring lines (passing, rushing, receiving TDs) the winner's candidates can post.

interactions.hypothesis: P(player MVP) is the product of his team's win probability and his conditional credit share, so a star on a likely loser can be below a role player on the favourite.
Defender MVP mass rises in low-scoring, turnover-driven wins where a pick-six or multi-sack game becomes the standout line.
A compromised or backup QB moves the position prior from quarterback to RB, WR and defence, so the base-rate shift is conditional on QB status.
In-game, credit is driven by the running leader on the likely winning side at ballot time; late swings matter only if they happen before ballots close.

P(player MVP) is the product of his team's win probability and his conditional credit share, so a star on the underdog can have lower probability than a supporting player on the favourite; credit shares are renormalised within the winner only.
interactions.how_to_test: Decompose historical winners into team-win and within-team credit parts and test that the product reproduces observed MVP frequencies by team win probability bucket.

interactions.hypothesis: In low-scoring, turnover-heavy wins a pick-six or multi-sack game becomes the standout line and defender MVP mass jumps; in shootouts it nearly vanishes, so the effect is a regime switch on the script.
interactions.how_to_test: Split past finals by total points and takeaway margin and compare the share of defensive MVPs across regimes.

interactions.hypothesis: If the starting QB is injured, backup or the offence is run-first, the QB premium shrinks and mass moves to RB, WR and defence, so the position base rate is conditional on QB status.
interactions.how_to_test: Condition the position prior on QB availability and the winner's pass rate in the final and compare shares across subsets.

interactions.hypothesis: A second strong line from a teammate dilutes the credit of the first; the combined probability of the pair rises less than the sum, so the response of one player's MVP chance to his own line is concave when a teammate also posts a big game.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit the conditional logit with and without a teammate-competition term and test the sign and size of the penalty.

interactions.hypothesis: Finalist odds are nonlinear in seed: the top seed gets the bye and a single-elimination path, so the probability of reaching the final is higher than the rating alone implies and mass concentrates on few teams.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare simulated finalist frequencies with and without seed and bye effects against past playoff histories.

interactions.hypothesis: Before kickoff credit is a projection; after the fan vote closes in the fourth quarter it is nearly fixed by the running leader on the team ahead, so plays after the ballot cut move the outcome much less than earlier plays of equal size.
interactions.how_to_test: On recent finals, compare the MVP with the running production leader at the start of the fourth quarter versus at the final whistle.

nonlinearities.shape: Convex above a threshold stat line (for example 3 or more TDs or 300+ passing yards)
nonlinearities.why: Voters respond to standout lines, so selection probability for a player rises sharply once his line crosses a visible threshold and is almost flat below it.

nonlinearities.shape: Softmax saturation: leading candidate share compresses as a second candidate rises
nonlinearities.why: Vote share across candidates is bounded and normalised; as one player's line grows the leader's share saturates, and split credit means the response is not linear in any one line.

nonlinearities.shape: Logistic in rating margin with SD about 13 points
nonlinearities.why: Win probability is logistic in the margin, so a rating edge moves the team layer less near even matchups and the MVP chance is only modestly sensitive to rating differences.

nonlinearities.shape: Many-to-many indicator map: position probabilities can sum above one
nonlinearities.why: A player listed at two positions pays both strikes, so a position's probability is a sum over listed candidates and jumps when one dual-listed star is the favourite.

mechanism_review.summary: A Super Bowl MVP outcome factors into three layers. First, team layer: which two teams reach the game (conference path and seeding) and who wins at a neutral site after two weeks, using full-strength lineups. Second, game layer: given a win, the in-game script and box score decide which player posts a standout line (a passing line with multiple touchdowns, a large rushing or receiving game, several sacks, a defensive or return touchdown), which depends on who is available and the matchup. Third, voting layer: a media panel and a fan vote convert highlights into a name, with a quarterback premium, split credit among teammates and decisions made late in the game. Position and non-QB variants are aggregations of the same chain over player sets.

stages.name: Team path: which teams reach the Super Bowl
stages.description: Each conference champion emerges from a bracket after seeding, byes and matchups; the weeks before the final shift each team's chance to reach it. The set of finalists is uncertain in November and is a draw from a season simulation with playoff structure, not a ranking.
stages.distribution: Discrete finalist-pair distribution from simulation; heavy mass on top seeds

stages.name: Final: neutral-site winner at full strength
stages.description: The finalists play at a neutral site after a two-week gap, with no home advantage, a playoff overtime rule and lineups that change with injury returns and losses. The winner's identity is a close-to-coin-flip draw modified by the margin SD, so the favourite's win rate is modest even with a rating edge.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli with win probability typically 35-65 percent; margin SD near 13 points

stages.name: Game script: who dominates the winner's game
stages.description: Conditional on the winner, the game shape (high scoring through the air, controlled run game, defensive turnovers, special-teams score) determines which unit posts the visible line; pace, pass rate and late-lead behavior matter, and overtime adds snaps.
stages.distribution: Mixture over script regimes with correlated player lines

stages.name: Player lines and credit allocation among the winner's players
stages.description: Given a script, the winner's players post lines: passing yards and TDs for a quarterback, yards and scores for receivers and backs, sacks and takeaways for defenders. Credit is shared when two teammates post strong lines, so top-line outliers drive the winner and teammate splits lower each player's probability.
stages.distribution: Heavy-tailed single-game lines; credit is a softmax over correlated candidates

stages.name: Voting and announcement
stages.description: A media panel and a fan vote name the MVP; fan voting closes during the fourth quarter, so ballots reflect the game state then, not the final whistle. Quarterbacks are favoured, narratives matter, and co-MVP or losing-team winners are rare. The position contract then maps the winner to strikes via the league depth chart at game time, with several strikes possible for one player.
stages.distribution: Categorical outcome with QB premium and rare exceptions; position markets are aggregations

stages.name: In-game state at ballot time (if markets trade live)
stages.description: If the contracts trade after kickoff, the information set is the live score, win probability and running player lines. Credit concentrates on the leading performer of the team ahead when ballots close in the fourth quarter; late plays after the fan-vote close move the panel only partly. Pre-game inputs then act only as priors for the remaining quarters.
stages.distribution: Time-varying categorical over candidates; collapses toward one player as the game state hardens; jump risk from late scores

contract_review.settlement_definition: Four series; two have sampled rules. KXNFLSBMVP: YES if the named player (sample: a Seattle linebacker) wins the 2025-26 Pro Football Championship Game MVP. KXNFLSBMVPPOS: YES if the MVP holds the named position group (sample WR/TE); multiple strikes may resolve YES, with eligibility from the position(s) on the league depth chart at the time of the game. Neither text states the source agency, co-MVP handling, a losing-team winner, the close time relative to the game, or postponement. KXNFLSBMVPDEF (defensive player) and KXNFLSBMVPQB (titled 'Non QB Championship MVP') have no listing or rules, so their YES direction and classification rules are unverified.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Not stated in the two sampled texts (KXNFLSBMVP, KXNFLSBMVPPOS); the MVP announced by the league is the presumed source of truth, and KXNFLSBMVPPOS names the league depth chart at game time as the position source.
variants_and_edge_cases: KXNFLSBMVPDEF and KXNFLSBMVPQB have no listing: defensive classification of returners or kickers and the non-QB YES direction are unverified (u1, u5).
KXNFLSBMVPPOS uses the league depth chart at game time and allows several strikes to resolve YES for one player (e.g. a WR also listed as a returner).
Co-MVP handling, a losing-team MVP and postponement are not stated in either sampled text.
Close time is not stated; if markets trade until the announcement, ballot timing (fan vote closes in the fourth quarter) makes the in-game state the main input (u6).
KXNFLSBMVPQB's ticker suffix suggests a QB contract while the title says non-QB; YES could be the complement of the assumed outcome.

combine_testing_results.label: NFL Scouting Combine athletic testing results
contract_types: Pro Football Draft Combine: Longest Broad Jump
Pro Football Draft Combine: Player with Fastest 40 Time
Pro Football Draft Combine: Highest Vertical Jump
Pro Football Draft Combine: Most Bench Press Reps
combine_testing_results.target: Probability that the best Combine measurement in a drill (40-yard dash, broad jump) clears a threshold or belongs to a named prospect, per official Combine results.
combine_testing_results.mechanism: Combine drill extremes are the maximum (broad jump) or minimum (40-yard dash) over the prospects who are invited AND choose to perform the drill in Indianapolis. The outcome is generated in three layers: the invite pool and its position mix fix how many genuine speed and explosiveness candidates exist, at any position; each prospect's opt-in decision (injury, agent strategy, deferral to pro day) thins that pool, often removing the favourite; each participant's best-of-attempts result is his trained athletic ceiling plus attempt noise measured by the Combine's timing protocol. A threshold beyond the all-time record or an argmax among near-equal sprinters is therefore a tail and participation problem, not a draft-board problem.

inputs.why: Position-agnostic count of invitees with a fast prior sets how many draws reach the tail of the fastest 40 and longest broad jump; secondary because it aggregates the per-prospect prior.
A named prospect only wins the 40 market if he runs at the Combine; opt-outs of fast prospects reshape the argmax.
College track times, verified sprint data and size give each participant's expected 40 time and jump before he tests.
Best of typically two 40 attempts and multiple jumps raises each participant's result above his mean by a variance-dependent amount.
Yearly best 40 and broad jump over a provisional electronic-timing window, and the record, anchor the order-statistic tail for the 148-inch strike.
Electronic timing, start trigger, indoor track and unofficial-to-official revision define the recorded number that settles.
Reports that a prospect will not run, is injured, or will only test at his pro day update the participation hazard.
Projected top picks skip drills more often; board rank is a covariate for opt-out, not a predictor of speed.
Strike of 148 inches, Combine-only scope and the missing tie clause for the fastest 40 come from the contract text.
Broadcast unofficial 40 times are later revised to official times, which can reorder the top two sprinters.
Recorded official Combine result and its timestamp are needed to audit each settled market.
Drills run by position group on fixed days, so the market state jumps when the fastest groups test before close.
KXNFLCOMBINE-BENCH26 (Most Bench Press Reps) exists in the series; its pool and prior are lineman-driven and not covered by the speed/jump inputs.
KXNFLCOMBINE-VERT26 (Highest Vertical Jump) exists in the series and needs its own prior and its correlation with the broad-jump field already modelled.

interactions.hypothesis: The fastest-40 probability of every other runner rises sharply when the prospect with the best prior declines to run, so opt-out news is worth more for elite priors.
The expected yearly best grows roughly with the log of the number of speed-position participants, so a thin receiver and corner class lowers the extreme.
Best-of-attempts helps a high-variance prospect whose mean trails the leader and hurts a favourite, so variance changes argmax share with a sign set by distance to the leader.

The fastest-40 probability of a named runner depends on which other elite priors actually run; if the top prior opts out, the remaining contenders gain argmax share in proportion to their closeness to the new top, so the value of an opt-out report is larger the more dominant the absent prior was.
interactions.how_to_test: In 2010-2025 classes, compare realized fastest-40 share of the second-best prior in years where the top prior skipped versus ran.

interactions.hypothesis: The expected yearly best improves roughly with the log of the number of speed-position participants: adding ten more corners shifts the best 40 by much less in a deep class than in a thin one, so the record-break probability is concave in pool size.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress yearly best 40 and broad jump on log participant count in speed positions with a season trend; test curvature versus a linear count term.

interactions.hypothesis: Under best-of-attempts the chance of the extreme mark depends on variance relative to the leader. For a runner whose mean is behind the target or the current leader, higher attempt variance raises his argmax or threshold chance; for the favourite, higher variance lowers it. The 148-inch tail effect is therefore signed by distance from the target, not uniformly convex.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare realized extremes against simulated ones using mean-only versus mean-plus-variance priors, splitting prospects into ahead-of and behind-the-leader by prior; check that the variance effect flips sign across that split.

interactions.hypothesis: Revision of unofficial to official 40 times only matters when the two fastest official times are within the revision sd (about 0.01-0.02 s); outside that band revisions cannot change the argmax, so the settlement risk switches on only for close races.
interactions.how_to_test: From tracker snapshots, count classes where the leader changed between first-displayed and official times as a function of the gap between first and second.

interactions.hypothesis: Vertical and broad jump outcomes are positively correlated within a prospect and opt-outs are usually joint (a prospect who skips jumps skips both), so the vertical and broad-jump maxima are dependent: one elite jumper opting out lowers both, and pricing the two events independently misstates their joint.
interactions.how_to_test: On 2006-2025 classes correlate yearly vertical and broad maxima and the identity of the leaders; test per-prospect joint skip rates for the two jumps.

nonlinearities.shape: steeply decaying record-exceedance tail
nonlinearities.why: Probability of the yearly best broad jump reaching 148 inches falls faster than exponentially beyond the 147-inch record if the tail is bounded (negative GEV shape), so the estimate is dominated by the fitted shape parameter.

nonlinearities.shape: step change in argmax share
nonlinearities.why: When a single dominant prior moves from likely to run to will not run, each remaining contender's fastest-40 probability jumps discretely rather than smoothly, because the argmax is over a small set of near-equal runners.

nonlinearities.shape: convex in expected-time gap
nonlinearities.why: A runner's fastest-40 probability rises sharply as his expected time moves within a few hundredths of the best prior and is near zero beyond about 0.08 s, a logistic-like shape in the gap.

mechanism_review.summary: The settling number is an order statistic over a self-selected field. About 320 prospects are invited; the league chooses the pool, so the count of wide receivers, corners, running backs and safeties determines how many plausible 4.2-second sprinters and 11-foot-plus jumpers exist. Each prospect then decides whether to perform each drill: injured players, projected top picks and players whose camps prefer a familiar pro-day surface opt out, which removes field members non-randomly and often removes the favourite. Each participant's result is his trained ceiling (from track background, college speed data and body mass) plus attempt-to-attempt noise, and the best of his attempts is recorded by the electronic timing system and later confirmed as official. The broad-jump strike sits above the all-time Combine record, so it is a record-break tail event; the fastest-40 contract is an argmax among a handful of near-equal sprinters where hundredths, ties and unofficial-versus-official revisions decide. Draft value, team needs and game statistics play no role in generating the measurement.

stages.name: Invite pool and positional composition
stages.description: The league's invite list (about 320-330 prospects, released in late winter) fixes the candidate field. Fastest 40 times come mostly from receivers, corners, safeties and running backs, while 11-foot jumps also come from edge rushers, linebackers and tight ends, so the pool is judged by pre-Combine prior rather than listed position: the number and quality of fast-prior invitees, and of small-school burners who were or were not invited, determine the size of the speed tail before anyone tests.
stages.distribution: Fixed count per class with year-to-year variation in speed-position share of roughly plus or minus 15 percent

stages.name: Drill opt-in decision by each invitee
stages.description: An invitee may skip the 40 or jumps because of injury, because his agent judges the risk of a slow time outweighs the upside, or because he prefers his pro day. Opt-out is concentrated among projected first-round picks and injured players and is announced through reports in the days before testing, so the realised field is a non-random thinning of the invite pool that can remove the best prior.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli per prospect-drill with strong dependence on draft rank and injury; correlated within agencies

stages.name: Individual testing performance
stages.description: For each participant the recorded result is the best of his attempts, drawn around a personal ceiling set by sprint mechanics, track history and mass. Pre-Combine signals (college track 60 m or 100 m times, verified sprint data, prior hand times) predict the ceiling with error, and attempt noise plus a best-of-k rule shifts results toward the favourable tail for high-variance athletes.
stages.distribution: Approximately normal around the ceiling; sd of roughly 0.04-0.05 s per 40 attempt and 2-3 inches per jump are unsourced working estimates pending the random-effects fit; min of k draws

stages.name: Field extreme and argmax formation
stages.description: The broad-jump contract takes the maximum over all jumpers and asks whether it reaches 148 inches, one inch beyond the record; the 40 contract asks whether a named runner holds the minimum. All four drills depend on the extreme-value tail of the class, so the yearly-best history and its era trend calibrate the tail, and the argmax share of a favourite is bounded by the number of runners within a few hundredths of him.
stages.distribution: Extreme-value (Gumbel/Weibull-type) yearly best; record exceedance probability small and highly sensitive to tail shape

stages.name: Measurement, official revision and settlement
stages.description: The electronic timing protocol and indoor venue produce the recorded value; broadcast times shown as unofficial are later replaced by official times that can differ by a few hundredths. The contract text names no source, no revision window and no tie rule, so settlement mechanics are partly unknown and the recorded official number must be captured with timestamps.
stages.distribution: Deterministic given the official record; revision risk of a few hundredths that matters only when the top two are within 0.02 s

stages.name: Vertical-jump and bench-press events of the same series
stages.description: The Kalshi event list for KXNFLCOMBINE in 2026 has four events: highest vertical jump, longest broad jump, most bench-press reps and fastest 40. The vertical draws on the same elastic-power athletes as the broad jump, so it reuses their participation decisions with a correlated but distinct per-prospect prior. The bench press is a separate pool of interior linemen and edge players lifting 225 lb for reps, where heavier players with short arms do best and the main uncertainty is which strong prospects opt out. Both are field maxima settled on the official recorded result.
stages.distribution: Vertical: continuous half-inch maximum over roughly 150-250 jumpers, Gumbel-like tail; bench: integer maximum over roughly 150-200 lifters, upper tail driven by a few linemen, dead-heat ties possible

talent_strength.note: Prospect speed and lower-body power ceiling from pre-Combine evidence is the talent variable.

opponent_matchup.note: There is no opponent: each prospect tests alone against the clock or tape; competition with the rest of the field is captured by the order-statistic tail and pool composition, not by a matchup.

role_personnel.note: Which positions and how many speed-position prospects are in the pool.

availability_news.note: Injury and opt-out reporting decides who actually runs and jumps.

coaching_scheme.note: Pre-draft training programmes (specialised speed camps) can improve 40 times by several hundredths between the college season and the Combine; no measured input captures which facility a prospect trained at or its effect.

environment.note: Indoor stadium track surface and timing setup are the environment; weather is irrelevant indoors.

game_context_script.note: No game is played: there is no score, clock or game flow, and drill order by position group does not change the measured values in any known way.

pace_volume.note: Number of participating prospects and attempts per prospect is the opportunity count.

efficiency_conversion.note: Conversion of trained ceiling into the recorded best attempt.

distribution_variance.note: Extreme-value tail of the yearly best and attempt variance.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Draft-stock incentives drive the decision to test or defer to pro day.

officiating_rules.note: Timing method, attempt rules and unofficial-to-official revisions.

settlement_contract.note: 148-inch inclusive strike, Combine-only scope, missing tie and source clauses for the sampled broad-jump and 40 markets; the vertical and bench events of the same series (verified on the Kalshi events API) have no retrievable rules text, so their tie and revision handling is unknown.

contract_review.settlement_definition: KXNFLCOMBINE-BROAD26-148 (floor_strike 148, greater_or_equal) resolves YES if any participant records a broad jump of at least 148 inches at the 2026 Combine; a pro-day jump does not count by the wording. KXNFLCOMBINE40-PLAYER26-ZTHO resolves YES if the named prospect records the fastest 40-yard dash at the 2026 Combine. Neither sampled text names the source of truth, whether unofficial or official times are used, or how a tie for fastest 40 is paid.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Not named in the sampled rules; presumably the official NFL Scouting Combine results published by the league (NFL.com Combine results), which is unverified.
variants_and_edge_cases: The 148-inch strike is one inch beyond the long-standing Combine broad-jump record of 147 inches (Byron Jones, 2015), so YES requires a new record; the probability is set by tail extrapolation, not by typical yearly bests.
The fastest-40 text has no dead-heat clause; official 40 times are reported to hundredths and a tie at the top is plausible, so payout under a tie is unknown.
Scope is the Combine only: a prospect who skips the Combine 40 and runs faster at his pro day cannot be YES, and his absence raises others' chances.
The text does not say whether broadcast unofficial times or later official times settle; these can differ by a few hundredths and reorder close sprinters.
rules_secondary is empty for both sampled markets, so no settlement source, revision window or void rule for a cancelled drill is visible.

Series scope verified on the Kalshi events API (2026-11-08): KXNFLCOMBINE-VERT26, -BROAD26, -BENCH26 and -4026 exist with settlement sources ESPN and NFL Network; only the broad-jump market text is sampled and the vertical and bench market rules could not be retrieved (markets no longer returned), so their tie and revision handling is unknown.

slate_extremes.label: Slate-wide single-game extremes (season/week max or argmax across games)
contract_types: season max game point differential over rung
season max game total over rung
any player single-game stat over rung in season (rushing, passing, receiving, receptions, TDs, sacks, tackles, interceptions, D/ST TDs, 100/100)
any player single-quarter yardage over rung (overtime excluded)
slate_extremes.target: Probability that the maximum (or argmax) of a per-game quantity (game margin, game total, team points, player single-game rushing yards; other player stats unsampled) across a week's or season's slate of games exceeds a threshold or falls on a named game/team.
slate_extremes.mechanism: Each contract reads the extreme of one per-game quantity over a set of games: the season's largest final margin, largest total including overtime, any player's rushing yards in one game, or which game or team scores most in one week. The extreme is produced by the few games with the most lopsided talent pairings, quarterback absences, calm conditions for totals (dome or mild weather) and, for margins, any weather since bad conditions can widen mismatches and runaway scripts (turnover cascades, defensive touchdowns, a leader that keeps scoring). Probability is one minus the product of per-game non-exceedance over remaining games for season thresholds, with shared team-rating error adding dependence; for weekly argmax it is a simulation over the slate's integer score distributions with dead-heat splitting.

inputs.why: Season thresholds settle YES once any game clears the rung, so the realised maximum to date and remaining games define the live state.
Per-game probability that the final margin exceeds 51.5 points is a deep tail of the margin distribution conditioned on mismatch.
Per-game probability that combined points exceed 109.5 is a far upper tail of the game-total distribution.
Weekly argmax of game totals across the slate, with shared weather correlation and payout splitting.
Separate offence and defence scoring rates give each team's point distribution for the weekly highest-scoring team.
The 225+ rushing-yard contract needs per player-game exceedance probability combining carry volume and long-run tail.
A 52-point margin needs the leading team to keep scoring after the game is decided; coach and backup-QB behaviour set that.
Number of games and teams on the weekly slate (byes, Week 18 full slate) sets the baseline argmax share.
Integer scores tie at the weekly maximum often enough that the 1/N dead-heat payout changes expected value.
Historical season maxima of margin, total and single-game rushing yards by era anchor the tail and the rung choice.
Market-free team ratings give the pairing mismatches that generate blowouts and the expected scoring for shootouts.
A team's rating error is shared across its remaining games, which correlates per-game tail events for season maxima.
Backup or rookie quarterbacks on bad teams create the deepest mismatches that produce 50-point margins.
Very high totals need both teams to score; the joint upper tail of the two scores, not the sum of marginals, sets P(total > 109.5).
Wind, cold and rain suppress totals outdoors, so the weekly highest-scoring game leans toward domes and calm venues.
Defensive and return touchdowns add points without offence and accelerate runaway margins.
Benchmark only: team rush attempts are conditioned on the closing spread; carry volume uses nfl.carries with a market-free margin.
Per-carry explosive probability of the rusher decides whether volume turns into 225 yards.
Leading teams feed the back late, so blowout scripts add carries for the 225-yard contract.
Weak run defences allowing explosive runs are where single-game rushing records happen.
Starters are pulled at large margins, capping both further margin growth and a starter's single-game yardage.
Late-season resting of starters creates mismatches and lowers the scoring of resting teams in the weekly argmax.
The current kickoff regime shifts field position and scoring rates, so era base rates must be adjusted for it.
Regular-season scope, over-rung strikes, overtime inclusion and dead-heat 1/N splitting are read from the contract text.
Official rushing-yard corrections after a game can move a 223-227 yard performance across the 225 rung.
Weekly argmax markets are partly settled by earlier kickoff windows, so the running in-week maximum and close time condition the remaining games.
Integer team-score key-number PMF drives the weekly team and game argmax and the tie mass at the top; rates alone do not give it.
Weekly market close time relative to the last window (timing only, no price) sets how much of the week is already realised.
P(tie after regulation) from the market-free margin distribution and OT points under the current rule add the overtime mass that KXNFLHIGHSCORE explicitly counts.
Lead-back carry share and lead/trail-conditioned team rush attempts give the 28+ carry upper tail a 225-yard game needs.
Covers every non-rushing KXNFLGAMESPECIALS rung (passing, receiving, receptions, TDs, sacks, tackles, INTs, D/ST TDs, 100/100 combo), which previously had no inputs in this record.
KXNFLGAMESPECIALS lists quarter rungs (QPY250, QRY150, QREY150) whose window and overtime exclusion differ from the full-game rungs.

Detached-reference repair: this archetype's own record already relies on this input (stage s7) but its input list did not carry it; attached as context so the list supplies what the mechanism asserts.
Context for HIGHSCORE, which counts overtime: market-free OT probability and OT points by rule era (9-17 points possible under both-possess).

interactions.hypothesis: Backup-QB and rested-starter shocks on the weak side are sub-additive in rating loss, so the deepest margins need a mismatch compounded by availability loss without double counting the tail convexity.
Once a lead passes about 35 points, further margin growth depends on whether the leader keeps calling scoring plays, so the margin tail is switched by coach policy.
225 rushing yards needs both 25+ carries from a leading script and at least two long runs, a product of volume and tail that is concentrated in blowout wins.
More teams near the top of the weekly score distribution raise both the competition for the argmax and the chance of a dead-heat split.

A backup quarterback on the weak side and rested starters on the weak side are the same kind of rating loss and do not stack linearly: once the weak team already starts a backup, resting further starters adds less than it would for a healthy-QB team. The tail growth in expected margin is the separate GPD convexity already recorded as a nonlinearity, so this interaction is only the sub-additive stacking of availability shocks.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit margin exceedance above 35 points on a single combined weak-side availability index versus separate backup-QB and rested-starter indicators; test whether the product term is negative and whether it survives after the GPD convexity term.

interactions.hypothesis: Below a lead of about 28-35 points margin growth follows normal play; above it the process switches to a regime where the leader's coach policy and backup quarterback determine further points, so two games with equal mismatch can end 45 or 60 points apart.
interactions.how_to_test: Condition fourth-quarter scoring on lead >= 28 and compare coach-level points per drive; test whether coach identity adds explanatory power for final margin beyond the third-quarter margin.

interactions.hypothesis: A 225-yard game requires both upper-tail volume (often 28+ carries, usually in a winning script) and at least two runs of 30+ yards; a high-volume grinder without breakaway speed or an explosive back with 15 carries rarely reaches it.
interactions.how_to_test: On 2000-2025 rusher-games, model P(yards >= 200) with carries, per-carry tail and their product; check that the product term dominates.

interactions.hypothesis: Totals above 100 need both teams in their upper tail at once; shootouts are more likely to be tied late and go to overtime, so the OT increment is concentrated in exactly the games that approach the rung, raising the tail beyond the regulation fit.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare P(OT | regulation total >= 80) with P(OT) overall and the residual correlation of team scores in high-total bins.

interactions.hypothesis: With more teams playing and several teams projected near the top, a named team's argmax share falls and the probability of a tied maximum rises; in bye-heavy weeks the reverse holds, so the payout is conditional on the slate as well as the team.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress realised weekly-max shares and tie frequency on N_teams and on the number of teams within 3 projected points of the top.

interactions.hypothesis: When several outdoor games face wind or rain, the argmax mass concentrates on dome games and calm venues; in a uniformly mild week the mass spreads by team quality, so weather matters for the argmax mainly through its dispersion across the slate.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare dome-game share of weekly highest totals in weeks with high versus low cross-game spread of forecast wind.

interactions.hypothesis: Once a rung is reached the market settles and the next rung inherits the realised maximum, so the remaining-season probability of a higher rung depends on how far the current maximum is from it; the 17-reception rung settling YES removes it and leaves 20 as a far-tail event with a much lower hazard.
interactions.how_to_test: Backtest per-week remaining-season probabilities for each stat rung on 2010-2025 seasons conditioning on the realised maximum to date versus an unconditioned season product.

nonlinearities.shape: convex exponential-type tail in expected margin
nonlinearities.why: Per-game P(margin > 51.5) rises roughly exponentially in the expected margin of the mismatch, so a handful of extreme pairings carry most of the season probability.

nonlinearities.shape: saturating in games remaining with a jump to 1 on clearance
nonlinearities.why: P(YES) = 1 - prod(1 - p_g) grows concavely in the number of remaining games and jumps to certainty the moment one game clears the rung, so value decays non-linearly through the season.

nonlinearities.shape: convex in carry volume above about 25
nonlinearities.why: Each extra carry beyond about 25 adds another draw from a heavy right tail, so P(225+) accelerates with volume rather than rising linearly.

nonlinearities.shape: inverse in number of contenders
nonlinearities.why: Baseline argmax share scales like 1/N, so the drop from 32 to 26 teams lifts every team's share by about 23 percent, a non-linear effect for favourites near the top.

nonlinearities.shape: convex in play count
nonlinearities.why: A quarter with two extra possessions roughly doubles the chance of 150 yards because the tail needs several explosive plays, so exceedance rises convexly with quarter play volume.

mechanism_review.summary: Each contract reads one extreme over many games, so the contributing games are a small, identifiable subset. Margins above 50 arise only when a strong team meets a weak one, usually with a backup quarterback, and the game script snowballs through turnovers, short fields and non-offensive touchdowns while the leader keeps scoring rather than kneeling. Totals above 109.5 require two good offences in a dome or calm weather, weak defences and often overtime, with positively correlated team scores. A 225-yard rushing game needs a lead back with 25-35 carries in a winning script plus two or more long runs against a weak run defence. The weekly highest-scoring game or team is an argmax over 13-16 games or 26-32 teams with heterogeneous integer score distributions, so the slate size, weather spread and tie mass matter as much as a single matchup. For season thresholds, P(YES) = 1 - product over remaining games of P(not exceed), modified by shared rating error, and the realised maximum to date resolves the market early.

stages.name: Pairing strength and quarterback state across the slate
stages.description: Talent gaps between paired teams set where extremes can occur. The season schedule fixes about 272 pairings; market-free team ratings with their posterior uncertainty, quarterback status (backup or rookie starters) and late-season resting of starters determine which few games carry most of the blowout and shootout probability.
stages.distribution: Heterogeneous per-game means; rating errors shared within team across games; mismatch counts heavily right-skewed

stages.name: Per-game score distribution and environment
stages.description: For every game, a pair of integer team-score distributions is generated from offence and defence scoring rates, pace and weather, with positive covariance through shared tempo and conditions and overtime adding points to tied games. This stage produces the weekly argmax inputs and the bulk from which the season tails are drawn.
stages.distribution: Discrete team-score PMFs with key-number atoms; game totals right-skewed; OT adds a small mass of extra points

stages.name: Runaway script and tail generation
stages.description: Extremes come from cascades: early turnovers giving short fields, pick-sixes and return touchdowns, and a trailing team forced to pass into a strong rush. Whether the margin keeps growing past 35-40 points depends on the leader's policy after pulling starters and on backup quarterbacks; weather lowers totals but not margins (the 59-0 game in 2009 was played in snow), and very high totals need both sides to keep scoring rather than one side collapsing.
stages.distribution: Heavy upper tails (generalized Pareto above about 21 points of margin); totals tail thicker than normal

stages.name: Player single-game rushing extreme
stages.description: For the 225-yard contract, the relevant subset is lead backs and running quarterbacks in winning scripts against weak run defences. Yards are carries times a per-carry distribution with a long right tail, so the event needs high volume plus two or more explosive runs; late-lead clock carries add volume, while a starter pulled in a blowout caps it.
stages.distribution: Compound: negative-binomial carries times heavy-tailed per-carry yards; season max over about 64 starting backs per week

stages.name: Aggregation to slate extremes and tie handling
stages.description: Weekly contracts take the argmax over the games or teams actually playing, so byes, slate size and the integer-score tie mass at the top determine baseline shares and dead-heat payouts. Season contracts multiply non-exceedance across remaining games, adjusted for shared rating error, and condition on the realised maximum to date, which can end the market early. Weekly argmax contracts are also conditioned on scores already realised in earlier kickoff windows before the market closes.
stages.distribution: Order statistic over 13-16 games or 26-32 teams; ties with probability of several percent at common totals; season P saturating in games remaining

stages.name: Settlement wording and record verification
stages.description: Contract text fixes regular-season scope, strict over-rung strikes for margin and total, inclusive 225 for rushing yards, overtime inclusion and the 1/N rounding-down dead-heat rule. No source agency is named, and official rushing-yard corrections after the game can move a near-rung performance across the line before settlement.
stages.distribution: Deterministic given final official data; residual correction risk near the rung

stages.name: Other player single-game specials: passing, receiving, TDs and defensive counts
stages.description: The live KXNFLGAMESPECIALS list for 2026-27 has rungs on passing yards (475/500/525), passing TDs (6+), receiving yards (250/275/300), receptions (15/17/20), non-passing TDs (4+), sacks (4/5/6), tackles (20+), defensive interceptions (2/3), D/ST TDs (2+) and 100 rushing plus 100 receiving yards, besides rushing. Each is a season-long any-player tail with its own process: passing and receiving rungs need shootout scripts and a concentrated target tree, sacks need a dominant rusher against a trailing team, tackles need heavy opponent run volume and generous scorers, and interceptions need a turnover-prone passer. Rungs already reached (2 and 3 interceptions, 15 and 17 receptions) are settled and drop out.
stages.distribution: Per player-game exceedance probabilities from overdispersed counts and heavy-tailed yardage; season event = 1 minus product over about 9,000 relevant player-games, sensitive to tail calibration

stages.name: Quarter-window specials with overtime excluded
stages.description: Three rungs ask for 250 passing, 150 rushing or 150 receiving yards inside one regulation quarter. The window makes possession count and explosive plays dominate: end-of-half two-minute drills and fourth-quarter comeback passing create the high-volume quarters, and one long touchdown can supply most of a 150-yard quarter. The rules text excludes overtime from quarter-specific markets, so the fifth period never counts.
